author: kevinushey
body:
The vulnerability badge in the Packages pane was filtered per row (`pvItem.versions.has(version)`), but `onIconClicked()` passed the entire unfiltered, name-keyed vulnerability list to `PackageVulnerabilityModalDialog`, which does no filtering of its own. With the same package installed at multiple versions, clicking the badge on one row could show CVEs that only affect a different version, plus duplicates.

This extracts the version filtering into a shared `vulnerabilitiesForPackage(name, version)` helper used by both the badge/tooltip path and the click path, and only opens the dialog when the filtered list is non-empty (an empty list would throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException` in the dialog's `refresh()`). A package with vulnerability records under multiple repository keys now also gets a single combined icon and dialog instead of one per repository.

Verified with `ant javac`. Found by code review (roborev job 549).

Addresses #17970.

body: ## Summary Migrates `vertex/server/src/routers/manufacturing.ts` — the sole `prismaDirect.$transaction` in `generateSolid` — to `supabase.rpc("vertex_charge_manufacturing_hybrid")`. **Requires SQL deployment first** — run the `vertex_charge_manufacturing_hybrid` function in Supabase SQL Editor before deploying this code. ## Changes - Replaced 1 multi-table Prisma transaction with Supabase RPC call - Added supabase null-check before charge (matches `export.ts` / `ai.ts` pattern) - Preserved all `ctx.prisma` calls (license pre-check, design ownership, post-upload storage key updates, `getGcodeDownloadUrl`) - `prismaDirect` remains on ctx (unchanged) ## Deployment prerequisite ```sql CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION vertex_charge_manufacturing_hybrid( p_user_id uuid, p_cost integer, p_design_id uuid, p_export_format text, p_side text, p_file_name text, p_preset_id text, p_belt_angle_deg double precision, p_layer_height_mm double precision, p_is_gcode boolean, p_storage_key text, p_job_id text, p_ip text, p_metadata jsonb ) RETURNS json LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public AS $$ DECLARE v_balance integer; v_production_id uuid; v_export_id uuid; v_now timestamptz := now(); v_license_count integer; BEGIN SELECT COUNT(*) INTO v_license_count FROM licenses l WHERE l.status = 'active' AND ( l."ownerId" = p_user_id OR EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM license_seats ls WHERE ls."licenseId" = l.id AND ls."userId" = p_user_id ) ) AND (l."expiresAt" IS NULL OR l."expiresAt" > v_now); IF v_license_count = 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'NO_VALID_LICENSE'; END IF; UPDATE users SET "tokenBalance" = "tokenBalance" - p_cost WHERE id = p_user_id AND "tokenBalance" >= p_cost RETURNING "tokenBalance" INTO v_balance; IF NOT FOUND THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'INSUFFICIENT_TOKENS'; END IF; IF p_design_id IS NOT NULL THEN INSERT INTO productions ( id, "designId", method, "presetId", "beltAngleDeg", "layerHeightMm", material, "gcodeStorageKey" ) VALUES ( gen_random_uuid(), p_design_id, 'printing_solid', p_preset_id, p_belt_angle_deg, COALESCE(p_layer_height_mm, 0.3), 'TPU', CASE WHEN p_is_gcode THEN p_storage_key ELSE NULL END ) RETURNING id INTO v_production_id; END IF; INSERT INTO exports ( id, "designId", "userId", format, side, "tokenCost", "storageKey", "fileName" ) VALUES ( gen_random_uuid(), p_design_id, p_user_id, p_export_format::"ExportFormat", p_side::"Side", p_cost, NULL, p_file_name ) RETURNING id INTO v_export_id; INSERT INTO token_transactions ( id, "userId", type, amount, balance, reason, "exportId" ) VALUES ( gen_random_uuid(), p_user_id, 'deduct', -p_cost, v_balance, 'manufacturing:hybrid_gcode', v_export_id ); INSERT INTO audit_logs ( id, "userId", action, "targetId", metadata, "ipAddress" ) VALUES ( gen_random_uuid(), p_user_id, 'export_generated', COALESCE(v_production_id, v_export_id), p_metadata, p_ip ); RETURN json_build_object( 'productionId', v_production_id, 'exportId', v_export_id, 'balance', v_balance, 'jobId', p_job_id ); END; $$; ``` ## Remaining prismaDirect consumers 1. `stock.ts` — 4 transactions 2. `library.ts` — 1 transaction 3. `design.ts` — 1 transaction 4. `admin.ts` — 1 transaction 5. `trpc.ts` — `ensureAppUser` (non-transactional)

author: nicolasarthurdev
body:
**Bug:** clicar num slide só permitia editar o **título** — os bullets e textos aninhados não apareciam como campos editáveis.

**Causa:** a extração de texto era só de **nível superior** do frame. Mas o conteúdo real fica aninhado (`itemize`/`block`/`columns`), e o unified-latex anexa o texto do `\item` como **argumento do macro**. Então frames com bullets não tinham campos de Texto.

**Fix:** `collectTextRuns` agora **desce recursivamente** em environments, groups e nos args de macros de texto (`item`, `textbf`, `emph`, `alert`, …), pulando envs não-prosa (`tikzpicture`, `tabular`, …) e macros de título/layout. `listFrames` e `editFrameText` usam isso → bullets e prosa aninhada listados e **editáveis no lugar**.

## Verificação
- Testes de editing: listagem de `itemize` + edição de bullet aninhado (18 testes verdes no total).
- `/__outline` da Agenda agora retorna os 3 bullets; **Playwright** mostra o painel com Título + 1 campo de Texto por bullet (screenshot).
- `pnpm check` / `typecheck` verdes.

author: l3a0
body:
## What

The trend-gate pre-registration ([#12](https://github.com/l3a0/trading-strategies/pull/12), `docs/prereg_trend_gate.md`) is live, and its §10 ordering requires the §5–§6 analysis scripts to be committed **before any Stage 1 number is produced**. This PR is that commit. No stage has been run; the registration is still unburned.

- **`trend_gate.py`** — the registration, clause by clause: the §2.1 signal of record (`classify_regime` shifted one day, computed on the full unadjusted file), §3.1 spans, all four §4 arms (record, complement, vol-ablation diagnostic, baseline), the §5.1 placebo-sequence generator (single `default_rng(20260611)` stream, acceptance band [0.595130, 0.657776], fixed 10,000-pool with past-the-pool replacement semantics shared by both tests), Stage 1 Tests A/B + the §5.4 gate + the §9(a) MDE table at the expected record-arm n, and Stage 2: Family R (first 1,000 of the same stream, full engine re-runs with per-sequence complement statistics, fingerprint-guarded resumable checkpoints), Family S (seed 42, 500 circular shifts, checkpointed), the §6.3 pass rule with the vol-ablation binding clause, and every §6.4 mandatory secondary (LOYO with per-year placebo p, pooled stress windows, common-base Newey-West t, premium-normalized companion, same-sign tally, realized bull-day exposure).
- **`real_cc_backtest.py`** — the §10 seam: optional `suspended_dates` on `run_real_cc_overlay`. Entry-only (§2.3: the gate never triggers an exit), a suspended day behaves exactly like an existing no-entry day, default off and byte-identical.
- **`test_trend_gate.py`** — 21 always-run pure-logic tests (generator mechanics, statistic arithmetic, replacement semantics, the seam) plus 6 dataset-gated pins that reproduce the registration's §3.1/§3.3 tables exactly (spans 4,005/3,901/3,624; suspensions 2,506/2,207/2,510; episodes 69/86/85; F* = 0.626453; pairwise bull agreement 0.681/0.812/0.802) and a sha256 fingerprint locking the accepted-sequence stream. The gated layer touches **treatment-side data only** — no engine runs, no cycle P&L, no exceedance series.
- **`ci.yml`** runs the third suite; **`.gitignore`** adds `trend_gate_runs/` (checkpoints must not trip the CLI's clean-tree provenance guard); **README** CI claim + file-table rows.

## Reviewer notes

- **Verification:** full suite green — 188 passed, with all 161 pre-existing pins byte-identical under the seam. A 5-agent clause-by-clause adversarial panel reviewed the implementation against the registration and caught **two blockers before any number was burned**: (1) the real D_A/D_B tagging collapsed the three per-ticker §2.1 signals into one flat date→state map (last ticker wins — \~19% of MSFT/SPY observations would have been mis-tagged against a correctly-constructed placebo null, invalidating both Stage 1 p-values); (2) the §9(a) MDE table used the baseline cycle count where §9 specifies the expected record-arm count (\~325), overstating power \~1.6×. Both fixed; a fresh agent re-verified all eight fix items, including the direction-neutral LOYO flip detector, Family R replacement reporting, checkpoint crash-tolerance, and the price-file regeneration guard (constants verified against the committed CSVs).
- **Ordering discipline:** the prereg doc is byte-identical to its registration merge (no silent amendment, §11). The CLI refuses `stage1`/`stage2`/`placebo-mde` from a dirty tree so results carry an honest code provenance; `characterize` is exempt (treatment-side only, the §3.3 precedent).
- **Where the registration left implementation details open** (RNG call pattern per draw, per-test tail replay for replacements, Family S zero-exposure drops), the code documents the choice inline — those choices become the details of record at this commit, per the prereg's framing.
- **After merge,** the registered path is: `python trend_gate.py stage1` from the clean tree (re-tagging only — minutes), and only on a §5.4 pass does the expensive Stage 2 (Family R/S engine re-runs, checkpointed/resumable) run. Results land in a separate PR citing the registration merge commit and this analysis-code commit, per §10.

author: shonores
body:
## Root cause

The `Deploy to Vercel` step added in #830 assumed the Vercel CLI reads the `VERCEL_TOKEN` env var. **CLI 44.x does not** — it requires `--token`. Result: the step has failed on every execution since it shipped (`No existing credentials found`, both retry attempts — e.g. run 27413389659 on 2026-06-12, where the data PR landed but prod never redeployed). The site only stayed fresh because human PR merges kept triggering the Vercel GitHub-integration deploys; a weekend of pure bot data commits would have served stale data.

## Fix

- `vercel deploy --prod --yes --archive=tgz --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN"` — quoted interpolation also resolves the hyphen-rejection that originally motivated the env-var approach (#830 comment), which came from unquoted passing, not from `--token` itself.
- Empty-secret guard: fail fast with an actionable `::error` naming the secret, instead of two cryptic CLI retries.
- Comment block rewritten to document the CLI gotcha + incident reference.

## Verification

- YAML parse-validated; `tests/test_canary_validation_alignment.py` green (7 passed — workflow-parsing contract unaffected).
- Secrets confirmed present (`gh secret list`: VERCEL_TOKEN updated 2026-05-02).
- Real proof is tonight's 02:00 UTC nightly — being babysat; will report the deploy outcome.

author: saeedkolivand
body:
## Summary
Collapses the app's accent into a single user-customizable source and ships a picker. Pick **Default**, a **preset**, or **System** in Settings → Appearance and the whole app re-tints from one token — CTAs, focus rings, `brand-soft` text, progress bars, and glows — with auto-contrast labels, live preview, and persistence.

## How it works
- **One source of truth** — `--color-brand` (per light/dark scheme). `brand-soft`, `brand-dim`, `ring-brand`, `action-primary`, and the brand glows all **derive** from it (CSS `color-mix` / runtime). Semantic action colors (run/edit/delete) and status colors are intentionally **not** accent.
- **Runtime applier** in the theme engine (`packages/ui/src/lib/theme.ts` `applyAccent`): sets `--color-brand` + a derived `brand-soft` + an **auto-contrast** `--color-action-foreground` (dark label on pale accents), clears for Default, applies pre-paint via `restoreTheme`. Color math in new `packages/ui/src/lib/color.ts`.
- **Accent source** = `default | system | custom` on `ThemePrefs`.
- **System** = native OS read (`system_accent_color`): Windows `windows`-crate `UISettings::GetColorValue(Accent)` (new `UI_ViewManagement` feature; true accent, honours "Automatic accent color"), macOS `defaults read -g AppleAccentColor` → fixed macOS palette (dep-free, exact for macOS's named accents), Linux unsupported. The **System chip is hidden when unsupported** — no error UI.

author: thehammer
body:
## Problem

Whole files under Cargo `tests/`, `benches/`, and `examples/` directories were
classified as `origin_scope = production` because the extractor's scope derivation
only inspected `#[cfg(test)]` AST ranges.  It had no path-level rule.

Ground truth from the live index:
```sql
SELECT origin_scope FROM edges
WHERE to_entity_id = 'callimachus:make_source_meta' AND kind = 'defines';
-- → production  ← wrong; defined in .../tests/book_adapter.rs
```

Bug doc: `.claude/bugs/open/2026-06-12-origin-scope-misses-tests-dir-files.md`

## Fix

Add `path_is_in_tests_dir(path: &str) -> bool` — a **literal path-segment
match** (not a substring check):

| path | result |
|------|--------|
| `crates/foo/tests/integration.rs` | `true` |
| `crates/foo/benches/bench.rs`     | `true` |
| `crates/foo/examples/demo.rs`     | `true` |
| `src/contract_tests.rs`           | `false` |

When it returns `true`, `extract_structure` synthesises a full-file byte range
so every call to `scope_for_pos` returns `"test"`.  The path-level rule is
checked **before** the Rust structural rule (`#[cfg(test)]` ranges) — both
continue to work independently for `src/` files.

## Tests added (`edge_hygiene.rs`)

- `tests_dir_file_all_edges_tagged_as_test_scope` — fixture with a `tests/`-dir
  path asserts all edges carry `origin_scope = "test"`.
- `file_with_tests_in_name_but_not_in_tests_dir_is_production_scope` —
  `src/contract_tests.rs` stays `production`.

All existing `edge_hygiene` tests continue to pass (12/12).

## Operators: action required

- **Reindex** any corpus that contains `tests/`, `benches/`, or `examples/`
  directories for the fix to take effect on stored edges.
- Once reindexed, the client-side `/tests/` path workaround in calliope branch
  `fix/exclude-test-anchors` can be removed.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo build` ✅
- [x] `cargo test` — 0 failures across full workspace ✅
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` ✅

author: fryanpan
body:
## Summary
- Standalone `![alt](src)` lines had **no** handling in the server-side markdown parser/serializer (`packages/core/src/prose.ts`). They fell through to the paragraph path, where empty-alt images (`![](url)`) serialized to a bare `!`, and underscores in URLs (`/_images/DSC_1962_...`) were parsed as *italic* emphasis — mangling the `src` to `*images/DSC*1962...`.
- Root cause: links parse into a node with the URL in an attribute (so they round-trip), but images had no parser/serializer case at all. Images now get the same treatment.

## What changed
- **Parser** (`prose.ts`): a standalone image line becomes an `image` node with `src` / `alt` / `title` attributes. `src` is matched as a non-space run, so the URL never reaches inline emphasis parsing — **remote URLs and relative/local paths both work** (`![fork](./_images/fork.jpg)`).
- **Serializer** (`prose.ts`): `image` nodes serialize back to `![alt](src "title")`.
- **Editor** (`markdown-app/editor.ts`): registered `@tiptap/extension-image`. StarterKit v3 has no `image` node, so a synced `image` node would otherwise break the live doc.

## Answering "how do I indicate a local image?"
Standard markdown: `![alt](src)` where `src` is a remote URL **or** a relative/absolute local path. Both now round-trip losslessly.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run test:vitest` — 118 pass, incl. 6 new image tests (empty-alt, underscore-laden remote URL, relative path, title, block-placement)
- [x] `bun run test:server` — 50 pass
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `bun run build:markdown-app` — bundle builds
- [ ] **Not automated:** in-browser render of the image node in `/review/<id>` — needs the dev server + an MCP/server reload to pick up the core change.

OpenLibrary's ISBN-based cover endpoint serves an 'image not available'
placeholder JPEG with HTTP 200 when no cover exists — which then gets
saved as the book's cover.jpg.  Both OL cover URL forms now carry

- byte-size floor rejects blank stubs and 1x1 GIFs

A user-invocable skill — the design analog of `/code-review` — that runs the **DESIGN.md** rubric against UI.

## What it does

author: tas50
body:
## Summary

Closes #8056 with the rework discussed there: instead of bolting a lookup onto `auditpol`, this introduces `windows.auditPolicy` shaped like our modern resources, and deprecates `auditpol` / `auditpol.entry` in place.

```coffeescript
windows.auditPolicy {
  []windows.auditPolicy.subcategory
}

windows.auditPolicy.subcategory @defaults("name success failure") {
  init(name string)
  name string              // canonical English name, language-stable
  guid string
  category string          // e.g. "Logon/Logoff", from the built-in table
  localizedName string     // what the system actually reported
  success bool
  failure bool
  inclusionSetting string  // raw localized setting text
  exclusionSetting string
}
```

The checks from `mondoo-windows-security` collapse from a GUID + props pair to:

```coffeescript
windows.auditPolicy.subcategory("Logon") { success && failure }
windows.auditPolicy.subcategory("Process Creation").success
windows.auditPolicy.where(category == "Account Logon").all(success)
```

## Design notes

- **Language stability.** `auditpol /r` localizes subcategory names and settings to the OS display language (the class of bug #8286 fixed for the booleans). `name` and `category` are resolved from a built-in table of the 59 well-known subcategory GUIDs (MS-GPAC), verified 1:1 against the English real-system recording, so name-based queries behave identically on a German box. The lookup accepts the English name, the localized name, or a GUID (braces optional, case-insensitive).
- **The issue's `subcategory(name string)` field syntax** isn't expressible in the `.lr` grammar (field args are dependency refs), so the lookup is an `init` on the element resource — the `package(name:)` / `service(name:)` pattern.
- **Missing subcategory → explicit false, not null.** The issue asked for null settings so checks fail rather than error. It turns out `null && null` evaluates to **true** in MQL (`llx.boolAndOpV2` returns `v.Value == nil` when the left side is nil), so a null stub would make `subcategory("typo") { success && failure }` *pass*. A missing subcategory audits nothing, so `success`/`failure` are a real `false` (mirroring `package(...).installed`); the fields auditpol would have reported stay null.
- **Header-row parser fix.** `ParseAuditpol` parsed the CSV header as a 60th entry (`subcategory == "Subcategory"`), which `auditpol` has been emitting as a bogus row. Rows are now required to carry a GUID-shaped subcategory GUID, which drops the header in any display language. This is the one observable change to the deprecated resource.
- **Deprecation.** `auditpol` and `auditpol.entry` are marked `@maturity("deprecated")` and share the fetch path with the new resource; their `.lr.versions` entries are untouched. New entries land at 13.28.2.

## Testing

- `windows` package: parser header-skip case, GUID lookup forms, and a consistency test proving the 59-entry table matches the real-system recording name-for-name.
- `resources` package (English recording, shared runtime to exercise caching): list length, lookup by name / case-insensitive / GUID / braced GUID, category + category filtering, success/failure for all three inclusion settings, raw-field passthrough, and the miss behavior — `success == false`, `guid == null`, block check falsy, and no cache poisoning of subsequent good lookups.

author: nursedude
body:
## The crash

With a config whose `channels` contain only non-preset (private) channels — e.g. a single custom channel with `"meshtastic": true` — every received Meshtastic packet carrying an absent/zero channel hash (e.g. PKI direct messages seen on the LAN multicast) crashes the meshtastic receive path:

```
meshtastic recv: left-hand side expression is null
In decodePacket(), file meshtastic.uc, line 149, byte 72:
  called from function makeNativeMsg (meshtastic.uc:259:29)
  called from function recv (meshtastic.uc:331:45)
  called from function tick (router.uc:217:47)

 `                msg.decoded = crypto.decryptCTR(msg.from, msg.id, chan.symmetrickey, msg.encrypted);`
  Near here -------------------------------------------------------------^
```

## Root cause

`channel.uc` `getChannelsByMeshtasticHash(hash)` returns `[ meshtasticChannel ]` for a falsy hash — but `meshtasticChannel` is only assigned when a configured channel's namekey matches one of the stock `meshtasticChannelPresets` (`isMeshtasticPreset`). With only custom channels configured, the function returns `[ null ]`, which passes the caller's `if (hashchannels)` guard in `meshtastic.uc` and null-derefs at `chan.symmetrickey`.

## Fix

Return `null` when there is no preset channel, matching the unknown-channel-hash behavior. The sole caller (`decodePacket` in `meshtastic.uc`) already handles a null return and ignores the packet.

Observed several times a day on a long-running bridge (Raven ↔ meshtasticd on a Raspberry Pi over UDP multicast, private channel only) from ordinary direct-message traffic on the air; clean since patching. Reproduces on any platform — the code path is platform-independent.

Unrelated heads-up for installs on AREDN 4.26.x: the postinst's `restart-firewall` call trips an AREDN firmware bug (fw3 invoked on fw4 firmware) that wipes runtime firewall rules including WAN management access — filed as aredn/aredn#2762.

author: onder-akkaya
body:
## Summary

Closes #509 — audit 2026-06-10 finding #14 (High): `SyntheticVault` is structurally under-collateralized. Mint collateralizes at `collateralRatio` (120%) of the **mint-time** price, but `burn` pays full **current-price** value. Once the asset appreciates past the buffer (>20% at the default ratio), total redemption liability exceeds vault collateral: first redeemers extracted full value, later redeemers reverted with `InsufficientCollateral` against an emptied vault.

## Mechanism chosen: (b) pro-rata redemption haircut

Of the two options in the issue:

- **(a) Raise the collateral ratio — rejected.** Because collateral is keyed to the mint-time price, no finite ratio fixes the mechanism: 120% → 150% only moves the insolvency cliff from +20% to +50% appreciation, and beyond it the first-come-first-served drain is unchanged. It also worsens capital efficiency for every healthy-state user.
- **(b) Pro-rata haircut — chosen.** When available collateral `C` < total liability `L = totalSupply × price`, each redemption claim is scaled by `C/L`. This is **order-independent** in this exact code shape: a redeemer burning `s` of supply `S` receives gross `s·C/S`; collateral then falls to `C·(1 − s/S)` and supply to `S − s`, so the per-synth payout `C/S` is invariant across sequential redemptions. Early redeemers cannot extract more than their pro-rata share; the last redeemer is paid at the same rate instead of reverting. Integer division rounds the haircut down, so dust favors the vault. When the vault is healthy (`C ≥ L`) the scale factor is 1 and behavior is byte-identical to before. `previewBurn` mirrors the cap so `preview == actual` under stress. The old `InsufficientCollateral` check is kept as defense-in-depth (now unreachable: `s ≤ S ⇒ s·C/S ≤ C`).

Full rationale is also documented in the `@dev` comment on `burn()`.

## Changes

- `contracts/src/SyntheticVault.sol` — pro-rata cap in `burn()` + `previewBurn()`, mechanism doc comment. No signature/event/ABI shape changes.
- `contracts/test/SyntheticVault.t.sol` — 4 new tests:
  - `test_burn_total_supply_pro_rata_after_price_spike` — two equal holders, +50% price spike, **total issued synth redeemed**: no revert for the late redeemer, equal payouts regardless of order, early redeemer capped at her pro-rata share, vault stays solvent.
  - `test_burn_pro_rata_unequal_holders` — 3:1 holders, +100% spike, full-supply redemption: identical per-synth payout rate, total payouts bounded by collateral.
  - `test_burn_no_haircut_when_healthy` — healthy-path regression: full price value minus fee, unchanged.
  - `test_preview_burn_matches_under_stress` — preview parity while the haircut is active.

## Verification

```
forge test --match-contract SyntheticVaultTest
→ 20 passed; 2 failed (test_isFresh, test_revert_stale_price — pre-existing
  PriceOracle staleness-constant drift, owned by the parallel #508 PR)

forge test   (full suite)
→ 101 passed, 2 failed (same 2 known drift tests)
Baseline before this change: 97 passed, 2 failed → +4 new tests, no new failures.
```

Negative control: with the contract fix stashed, both stress tests fail against the pre-fix code with `InsufficientCollateral()` — reproducing the audited drain/strand behavior exactly.

## Redeploy required

`contracts/abis/` is deliberately **not** touched — it mirrors the live Arc testnet deployment. The deployed `SyntheticVault` instances still carry the FCFS bug; this fix requires a redeploy of `SyntheticVault` (and re-pointing `SyntheticFactory`/backend addresses). Note: the external ABI is unchanged (no signature/event changes), so consumers need only new addresses, not new ABI files.

## Review

Contract change — needs Chuan's review (live-funds surface, two approvals per convention). Cross-lane note: authored from Önder's risk-math lane; the solvency-invariant argument is in the `burn()` doc comment for review.

author: machjesusmoto
body:
Fixes #8076
Fixes #8051

## Issue Description

The `openclaw_gateway` adapter has two issues preventing it from working with current OpenClaw versions:

1. **Protocol version mismatch:** The adapter uses `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3`, but OpenClaw v2026.6.x expects protocol 4. Every connection attempt fails with "protocol mismatch" and all wakeups silently fail.

2. **Hardcoded API key path:** The adapter hardcodes `~/.openclaw/workspace/paperclip-claimed-api-key.json` for all agents. When a shared OpenClaw instance serves multiple Paperclip agents, they all load the same key file, causing auth boundary violations.

## What happened?

- Agent wakeup attempts connect to the OpenClaw gateway but get rejected: `protocol mismatch min=3 max=3 expected=4`
- Even if the protocol matched, all agents would load the same API key from the shared workspace path
- This makes the adapter non-functional with OpenClaw v2026.6+ in multi-agent setups

## Expected behavior

- Adapter connects successfully using protocol version 4
- Each agent loads its own API key from a configurable path

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw v2026.6.x (protocol 4)
2. Configure a Paperclip agent with `openclaw_gateway` adapter
3. Trigger a wakeup
4. Observe "protocol mismatch" in OpenClaw gateway logs
5. Wakeup silently fails

## Paperclip version or commit

Latest master (2026-06-12)

## Deployment mode

Local dev (pnpm dev)

## Agent adapter(s) involved

- [x] Custom / external plugin adapter (openclaw_gateway)

---

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - The `openclaw_gateway` adapter connects Paperclip to OpenClaw over WebSocket
> - OpenClaw v2026.6.x upgraded to protocol version 4, but the adapter still uses version 3
> - This causes "protocol mismatch" errors on every connection — the adapter cannot communicate with the gateway at all
> - Additionally, the adapter hardcodes the API key path for all agents, breaking multi-agent setups
> - This pull request bumps `PROTOCOL_VERSION` to 4 and adds a configurable `claimedApiKeyPath` field
> - The benefit is a working adapter with current OpenClaw versions and proper multi-agent support

## What Changed

- Bumped `PROTOCOL_VERSION` from 3 to 4 (required for OpenClaw v2026.6+)
- Added optional `claimedApiKeyPath` adapter config field
- Wired up existing `resolveClaimedApiKeyPath()` helper
- Added 5 test cases for the new config field

**2 files changed, 38 insertions, 3 deletions.**

## Verification

- TypeScript compiles cleanly (`tsc --noEmit`)
- 5/5 unit tests pass for `resolveClaimedApiKeyPath`
- Existing `resolveSessionKey` tests unaffected
- Adapter now connects successfully to OpenClaw v2026.6.x gateway (verified: no more "protocol mismatch" errors)

## Risks

- **Protocol bump (3→4):** Required for OpenClaw v2026.6+. Operators on older OpenClaw versions (< 2026.6) would need to upgrade. However, protocol 3 gateways are no longer maintained, so this is expected.
- **claimedApiKeyPath:** Low risk. Optional field, defaults to existing hardcoded path. No migration required.

## Model Used

- `openrouter/xiaomi/mimo-v2.5` (Zephyr agent on OpenClaw gateway)

session (removing a phantom `.claude/shared/` reference from `CLAUDE.md`), which the prior
execution-focused workflow did not capture.

- **Remove-vs-redirect decision rule** — remove the dead pointer under KISS/YAGNI when an adjacent
  surviving line already covers the same intent; redirect only when no surviving pointer covers it.
- **Confirm-then-fix audit sequence** — whole-corpus `grep -rn` → `ls` to prove absence →
  adjacent-line check → minimal single-line `Edit` → re-grep the whole corpus.
- **Reviewer-risk checklist** — ephemeral/worktree copies (`git ls-files`), drifting line numbers,
  MD022/MD032 regressions, memory-sourced external invariants.
- 4 new Failed Attempts rows; description trigger #11; planning When-to-Use bullet; 3 new tags;
  #1211 Verified On row.

## Verification Level

**verified-local.** The audit/verification *technique* was directly verified on disk (`ls .claude/`
proved `.claude/shared/` absent; `grep -rn` found one tracked occurrence). The **downstream PR
outcome is pending** — the plan that produced this learning had not been implemented or merged at
capture time. The skill section states this honestly.

## Key Findings

**What Worked**:
- Confirm-then-fix: prove the path is gone with `ls`, then check if an adjacent line already covers
  the intent before deciding remove vs redirect.
- Re-grep the whole corpus (not just the audit's `line:N`) to catch sibling stale copies.

**What Failed (now captured as anti-patterns)**:
- Patching only the cited line → sibling copies survive.
- Trusting the audit's reported line number → numbers drift after the audit date.
- Excluding an ephemeral copy without `git ls-files` → may miss a tracked occurrence.
- Adding a drift-guard for a single MINOR fix → YAGNI over-engineering.

author: wardix
body:
Resolves #121

This PR optimizes message and contact searches using PostgreSQL native Full-Text Search (FTS) with GIN indexes, replacing slow and CPU-heavy `ILIKE` pattern queries.

### Key Changes:
1. **FTS Database Migration**:
   - Dropped the legacy regular column and ad-hoc trigger/function `messages_search_trigger` on `messages.search_vector` from development/docker environments.
   - Added a `search_vector` column to the `messages` table as a generated `tsvector` using the `'indonesian'` dictionary.
   - Added a `search_vector` column to the `contacts` table as a generated `tsvector` concatenating `name`, `phone_number`, and `email` using the `'simple'` dictionary.
   - Applied GIN indexes (`messages_search_idx` and `contacts_search_idx`) on the `search_vector` columns to ensure fast search response times.

2. **Query Formatting Helper**:
   - Implemented `formatTsQuery` in `apps/main-api/src/utils/search.ts` to sanitize and transform user input into structured prefix-search tsquery expressions (e.g. `query:* & terms:*`). This prevents `to_tsquery` syntax errors while supporting search-as-you-type autocomplete matches.

3. **Backend Optimization**:
   - Updated search routes (`GET /`) to query `search_vector @@ to_tsquery(...)` and order results by relevance (`ts_rank`) for contacts, messages, and conversations.
   - Updated the CRM contacts route (`GET /api/contacts`) to execute FTS queries when the `q` query parameter is supplied.

4. **Integration Testing**:
   - Created `apps/main-api/test/search.test.ts` to cover name, phone, email, and message searches, verifying correct stemming (e.g., matching root word "bantu" to inflected word "bantuan").
   - Verified all 99 integration tests pass successfully in under 7 seconds.

body:
💡 What: Implemented short-lived (event loop boundary) caching via `queueMicrotask` for `collectLayoutPatterns` in `silcrow.js`.
🎯 Why: `collectLayoutPatterns` runs `document.querySelectorAll("[data-ps-layout]")`. This is called during high-frequency events like `mouseenter` (triggering `startPreload`). Repeatedly querying the DOM synchrononously in the same event tick is redundant and inefficient.
📊 Impact: Reduces repetitive synchronous DOM traversals to 0 during burst executions within a single event loop tick (e.g. rapid link interactions or batched prefetches).
🔬 Measurement: Verify by profiling `document.querySelectorAll` calls during a rapid sequence of mouseenter events over `[s-preload]` links. The first event will trigger a scan, and subsequent operations in the same tick will hit the microtask cache.

body:
## Task Proposal Agents are asked to write `/app/reconcile.sh`, a shell script that performs quarterly record reconciliation across four data files: an orders export (CSV), a bank transaction log (CSV), a shipping manifest (JSONL), and a product catalog (JSON). The records share no stable identifiers across systems, requiring multi-pass entity resolution using processor fee ranges (1.5–3.5%), partial merchant references, amount and date heuristics, installment payment grouping, refund linkage via transaction IDs, and consolidated shipment detection. The script must produce a `reconciliation.csv` with one row per order and a `summary.json` with aggregate statistics. The verifier checks both structural correctness and reconciliation quality against pre-computed golden files, requiring 90/100 to pass. ## Checklist This task meets the following criteria. If it doesn't match a criterion, I've explained why below. - [X] All behavior checked in `tests/` is described in `instruction.md`. - [X] All behavior described in `instruction.md` is checked in `tests/`. - [X] My `tests/` have informative docstrings that describe which behavior they check. - [X] My `instruction.md` was written by a human. - [X] My `solution/` was written by a human (with minimal help from a language model). - [X] I ran this task with a strong model (e.g. Claude Opus) using `harbor run -p tasks/ -m `. - [X] It is hard for the agent to cheat on my task. - [X] For failing runs (expected for hard tasks), I've added an [analysis below](#agent-run-analysis) to confirm the task itself is valid. ## Agent Run Analysis Tested with top performing models, including Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, and Codex gpt-5.5. 0 of 9 main trials passed the 90/100 threshold. Among the 6 trials that produced output, scores ranged from 34.1 to 71.3. **Failure pattern:** All output-producing trials fell short on the same algorithmic dimensions. Bank orphan detection was the most consistent failure: Jaccard scores ranged from 0.028 to 0.223 against a 0.30 threshold. Installment grouping was severely undercounted across every trial (agents detected 464–496 installment orders vs. the golden 801), because description-prefix grouping breaks when installment descriptions are generic and not tied to a specific order reference. Match status accuracy fell below the 98% threshold in most trials. **Non-output trials:** All three Codex gpt-5.5 runs scored 0. One agent spent its entire turn budget on data exploration without writing any implementation code. The other two were terminated by a 429 Too Many Requests error from the LiteLLM proxy after roughly 2 minutes of exploration each — an infrastructure issue unrelated to task design. **Adversarial trials:** None of the 3 cheat trials bypassed the verifier. The static golden file architecture proved robust: a Gemini trial explicitly attempted to empty all input files and produce zeroed outputs, confirming that the verifier compares against pre-computed static files rather than dynamically derived expectations. A Claude Code harness trial conducted a thorough filesystem-wide recon and correctly reported no viable bypass. The failures in main trials reflect genuine algorithmic difficulty. Agents correctly understood the problem structure and produced valid output schemas, but implementing accurate enough heuristics for installment-aware entity resolution and bank orphan detection at scale proved beyond what any trial achieved. The task is functioning as intended.

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a complete new benchmark task (`order-bank-reconciliation`) that asks agents to write a shell script performing quarterly financial record reconciliation across four files (orders CSV, bank transactions CSV, shipping manifest JSONL, product catalog JSON) with no shared identifiers, requiring multi-pass entity resolution and installment/refund/consolidation logic. - The test harness was redesigned from a lerp-based composite scoring system into explicit pass/fail gates: structural anchors (columns, row count, monetary format), deterministic-match fixture tests derived purely from public inputs, and calibrated threshold floors on fuzzy metrics (match status ≥97%, bank Jaccard ≥92%, orphan overlap floors). - Previously flagged issues have been resolved: `set -euo pipefail` removed from `test.sh`, `or ranked` double-assignment fallback removed from passes 2–3 of `match_bank`, pass 1 now checks `claimed` before assigning, per-status count exact gates replaced with the deterministic fixture, and `total_discrepancy` formula is now precisely specified in `instruction.md`. - Two minor hygiene issues remain: `test_script_exists_and_is_executable` only calls `os.path.isfile()` (not an execute-bit check), and the tests Dockerfile pre-installs pytest system-wide even though `test.sh` uses `uvx` isolation and never touches that install.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge; the task infrastructure is sound and the previously flagged algorithmic and structural issues have all been addressed in this revision. All prior double-assignment, set-e, lerp-threshold, and formula-specification issues have been closed. The remaining findings are a misleading test method name and a redundant Dockerfile layer — neither affects runtime behavior or scoring correctness. tests/Dockerfile (redundant install layer, unverified uv install) and tests/test_outputs.py line 113 (execute-bit check missing).

author: hamudl
body:
## Komplett-Redesign: Designsystem „Chromatogramm"

Löst das bisherige „Cinematic Lab"-Design (Gold/Amber, warmes Creme, Comfortaa) vollständig ab. Die neue Sprache übersetzt das Markenversprechen — unabhängig geprüfte Reinheit — wörtlich ins Design: Die Website liest sich wie ein hochwertiges **Analyse-Protokoll**.

### Designsprache
- **Farben:** kaltes Papierweiß, tiefe kalte Tinte, ein einziger Akzent in dunklem **Viridian** (Laborglas-Grün); dunkle Einschübe in kaltem Nachtblau (Ink). Dunkle Flächen rescopen die Akzent-Tokens automatisch auf helles Mint (AA-Kontrast ohne Sonderfälle).
- **Typografie:** Fraunces (Serif-Display mit echter Kursive) + Instrument Sans (UI) + IBM Plex Mono (Messdaten, Lots, Preise) — ersetzt Comfortaa/DM Sans/DM Mono.
- **Signatur-Details:** Mess-Lineal-Haarlinien mit Ticks (`tick-rule`), Index-Nummern (01/02/…), eckige Specimen-Tags, scharfe Radien (4/2/0 px), handgezeichnete Chromatogramm-Kurve als Marken-Visual im Hero. Keine Endlos-Animationen, kein Glassmorphism, kein Cursor-Glow (entfernt).

### Umfang (alle Kundenseiten strukturell neu)
- **Homepage:** asymmetrisches Editorial-Hero mit Chromatogramm-SVG statt Three.js-3D-Logo + Partikelnetz (beide entfernt → weniger JS), Protokoll-Sektionen, Kategorien als Index-Liste.
- **Katalog:** Produktkarte als „Probenblatt" (Mono-Kennzeile, Spez-Tabelle, `data-testid="product-card"`), neuer Seitenkopf, Filter/Pagination im Protokoll-Stil.
- **PDP + Qualitätskontrolle:** „Analyse-Dossier" — Spezifikationstabelle, COA als Laborbefund-Karte, Reviews neu.
- **Cart/Checkout/Order-Status:** „Bestellprotokoll" — Belegästhetik, nummerierte Checkout-Abschnitte, Status-Timeline als Mess-Strecke.
- **Auth + Dashboard:** Zugangs-Dossiers, Laborjournal-Dashboard, Bestelldetail als Beleg.
- **Wissen/FAQ:** Journal-Layout (asymmetrisches Lead-Stück, nummerierte Artikel-Listen, Protokoll-FAQ).
- **Über-uns/Kontakt/Versand/Zahlung/Rechtsseiten:** editoriales Manifest bzw. ruhige Protokoll-/Rechtstext-Layouts (Rechtstexte inhaltlich unverändert).
- **Systemzustände:** 404/Error/Loading als Protokollkarten; Cookie-Banner als Ink-Karte; OG-Images auf neue Marke; Header mit indexierter Mono-Navigation, Footer als Protokoll-Schlussblatt.
- Doku: `docs/design-system.md`.

### Kompatibilität
- Historische Klassennamen/Variants (`rule-gold`, `gold-underline`, `variant="gold"`) bleiben als Aliase erhalten und zeichnen die neue Sprache — kein Massen-Rename nötig.
- Alle Daten-Helper, Server-Actions, Routen, Caching, Rendering-Modi (`force-dynamic`/ISR) und der Server/Client-Split sind unangetastet.
- Keine neuen Dependencies; Three.js-Komponenten entfernt.

### Verifikation
- ✅ `next build` (Production)
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit`
- ✅ Vitest: 476/476 Tests grün
- ✅ ESLint: 0 Errors
- ✅ E2E-Kontrakte manuell verifiziert (Auth-Headings/Labels, Cookie-Dialog, Wissen-H1s/`.letter-link`/`.prose`/`#wissen-newsletter-email`, Warenkorb-Flow, Skip-Link, Nav-Links)

author: vikashaaryan1-code
body:
I have optimized the `getStats` methods across six backend services (`Ticket`, `Announcement`, `Meeting`, `Placement`, `Policy`, and `Attendance`). 

The optimization pattern involves:
1.  **Reducing Database Roundtrips:** Replacing multiple sequential `repository.count()` calls with a single `createQueryBuilder` query using conditional aggregation (`SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)`). This reduces the number of roundtrips from 2-3 down to 1 per request.
2.  **Efficient Data Processing:** In the `AttendanceService`, I replaced an in-memory aggregation of all records with database-side aggregation. This avoids the O(N) network transfer of fetching all historical attendance records for an employee just to calculate a monthly summary, resulting in significantly lower latency and memory usage.

These changes are non-breaking and improve the scalability of the dashboard features.

author: milotic3005-design
body:
💡 **What**:
1. Upgraded the `MemoryCache` class to enforce a maximum size limit (`maxSize` defaulting to 500) and implement an LRU eviction policy leveraging `Map` insertion order.
2. Implemented an in-memory caching layer on the `/api/v1/suggest` route to prevent repeated fetch requests to multiple external APIs (OpenFDA, RxNorm, NLM) for identical autocomplete prefixes.

🎯 **Why**:
1. In Next.js backend runtimes handling untrusted high-frequency input (like an autocomplete widget), unbound in-memory structures (like standard `Map` caching) without size limits inevitably lead to severe Out-Of-Memory (OOM) leaks.
2. The autocomplete endpoint performs expensive scatter-gather operations across multiple medical APIs per keystroke; failing to cache these results locally causes severe performance bottlenecks due to downstream network latency and API rate-limiting thresholds.

📊 **Impact**:
Eliminates redundant network traffic on repeat prefix queries (e.g. typing "van", pausing, backspacing and re-typing "van"), bringing the P99 latency on warm autocomplete searches from ~300ms+ down to <5ms. Additionally prevents potential production downtime from unbounded heap memory usage.

🔬 **Measurement**:
Start the dev server using `pnpm dev`. Open the UI and type "vanco" in the Search bar. The first fetch will incur normal network latency (observable in the Network tab). Backspace to "van" and immediately type "vanco" again—the second request will respond instantly from the new `MemoryCache` without firing outbound network requests. Check `.jules/bolt.md` for journal learning notes.

author: copilot
body:
Passing `undefined` into `doc.formText()` could serialize the literal token `undefined` into the field dictionary, producing an invalid PDF that breaks parsers such as pdf-lib and iText RUPS. This change normalizes explicit nullish text values to empty strings so AcroForm output remains valid.

- **AcroForm value normalization**
  - Treat explicit `value: undefined`, `value: null`, `defaultValue: undefined`, and `defaultValue: null` as `''` during field dictionary construction.
  - Preserve existing behavior for omitted options by only normalizing keys that are actually present.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Add unit coverage for `formText()` with `undefined` and `null` values.
  - Assert those cases serialize identically to an explicit empty string.

- **Example**
  ```js
  doc.formText('demofield', 10, 60, 200, 40, {
    value: undefined,
  });
  ```

  Before, this could emit an invalid object value like `undefined`. With this change, the field is serialized with an empty AcroForm value instead.

## What

## Changes (all under `src/Comet/`)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `global.json` | SDK `11.0.100-preview.3` → `11.0.100-preview.5.26302.115` |
| `Directory.Build.props` | Hardcode `MauiVersion` to `11.0.0-preview.5.26304.4` (with TODO to drop the override once `eng/Versions.props` moves to MAUI 11) |
| `sample/CometControlsGallery/CometControlsGallery.csproj` | Hardcoded `-macos` `MauiVersion` override `10.0.31` → preview.5 |
| `sample/CometMacApp/CometMacApp.csproj` | Hardcoded `MauiVersion` `10.0.31` → preview.5 |
| `NuGet.config` *(new)* | Comet-scoped `nuget.org` feed so Debug samples can restore `Redth.MauiDevFlow.Agent` (per `.squad/decisions.md` the team standard) — that package isn't mirrored on any dnceng feed the repo-root `NuGet.config` restricts itself to |

## Why scope to Comet only

A repo-wide bump of `MicrosoftMauiControlsVersion` to preview.5 would break every sibling on `net10.0-*` that uses CPM aliases without a `VersionOverride` — MAUI 11 preview 5 only ships `net11.0` / `netstandard` lib assets, no `net10.0`. Affected projects include the Linux.Gtk4 backend, the Windows.WPF backend, the EssentialsAI samples, the AIExtensions samples, and DevFlow.Sample. Keeping the bump local to `src/Comet/Directory.Build.props` leaves those net10.0 consumers untouched.

The `<Import Project="...eng/Versions.props" />` in Comet's `Directory.Build.props` is preserved so future repo-wide `MicrosoftMauiControlsVersion` updates flow through if the override is removed.

## Verified on macOS / preview 5

- `dotnet build src/Comet/src/Comet/Comet.csproj` (Debug, `net11.0-maccatalyst`): **0 errors** after `rm -rf obj/` clean restore.
- `dotnet build sample/Comet.Sample` (Debug, `net11.0-maccatalyst`): **0 errors** after clean restore.
- `project.assets.json` confirms `Microsoft.Maui.Controls/11.0.0-preview.5.26304.4` resolves (proves the localized version wins, not the repo-wide `10.0.41`).
- Comet.Sample launched on Mac Catalyst — visible UI, MauiDevFlow agent on port 9223, no startup errors, killed cleanly.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Re-enable `net11.0-macos` in `src/Comet/src/Comet/Comet.csproj` (the "workload not yet available" comment is obsolete in preview 5 — `microsoft.net.sdk.macos` ships).

body:
**Severity:** HIGH
**Vulnerability:** The `escapeHtml` and `formatMessage` functions in `chatInterface.js` only checked for truthiness (`if (!unsafe)`) before applying `.replace()`. This missed explicitly coercing the input to a primitive string, meaning a non-string object with a malicious `.replace` method could bypass sanitization (prototype pollution / type confusion). It also incorrectly suppressed valid truthy strings like `'0'`.
**Impact:** Potential XSS via injected objects, leading to arbitrary JavaScript execution in the browser. Functional bug where the user saying "0" resulted in no output.
**Fix:** Explicitly coerce input to string using `String()` and apply strict null checks (`!== null` and `!== undefined`). Added an entry to the `.jules/sentinel.md` security journal detailing the learning.
**Verification:** Added tests using Node.js and `jsdom` to verify valid strings, number types, and malicious objects are handled securely without bypass.

## What

The Docker image installed its dependency pins inline (`pip install 'mcp==…' 'beautifulsoup4==…' 'lxml==…'`), duplicating `pyproject.toml`. Dependabot's pip ecosystem cannot see inline Dockerfile pins (and the docker ecosystem only watches base images), so every pip bump silently broke the documented image/manifest lockstep.

## Change

- `Dockerfile`: install via `pip install .` — `pyproject.toml` is now the single pin source, already watched by Dependabot. `PYTHONPATH` hack dropped (package installs into site-packages).
- `.dockerignore`: `!README.md` exception — the package readme must reach the build (declared in `pyproject.toml`).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `[Unreleased]` entries for this change and the merged actions bumps (#10).

author: giswqs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #74, where image export fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'xee'` even though the user installed xee in a separate environment (pixi).

## Root cause

The plugin installs its Python dependencies into an isolated managed virtual environment (`~/.qgis_gee_data_catalogs/venv`) and prepends that venv's `site-packages` to `sys.path` at load time. However, `REQUIRED_PACKAGES` only listed `earthengine-api`, `geemap`, and `GeoAgent`.

The export code paths import additional packages that were never installed into the managed venv:

- Image / COG export: `xee`, `xarray`, `rioxarray`
- Feature / vector export: `geopandas`, `pandas`

So `import xee` failed at export time regardless of what the user installed elsewhere, because QGIS resolves imports against the managed venv's `site-packages`, not the user's pixi/conda environment (the reporter was also launching a standalone QGIS-LTR install, not their pixi QGIS).

## Changes

- Add `xee`, `rioxarray`, and `geopandas` to `REQUIRED_PACKAGES` so the managed venv provides everything the export features need (`xarray` and `pandas` are pulled in transitively).
- Update the export `ImportError` messages to direct users to the plugin's Dependencies panel (Install/Update) rather than a bare `pip install`, which does not help in the managed-venv model.
- Mention the export packages in the Dependencies panel info text. The package status list is generated from `REQUIRED_PACKAGES`, so the new packages appear there automatically.

Existing installs will report the new packages as missing via `get_venv_status()`, which surfaces the Dependencies panel and prompts a one-click update.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/test_ai_provider_config.py` (14 passed)
- `pre-commit run --all-files` (black, codespell, bandit all pass)

author: seanyao
body:
## Problem

`roll index --rebuild` silently downgraded already-merged-and-attested story pages — **143 in one real run** (incl. FIX-208): the green *"Merged to main — attested"* banner vanished and the Delivery spine node flipped done→incomplete.

## Root cause

`collectDossier` (`archive.ts`) let the backlog truth selector unconditionally overwrite `delivered`. The rebuild path passes **no live PR-evidence snapshot**, so the selector returns `unknown` for post-epoch cards → `delivered=false`, erasing pages that git proves merged.

## Fix

A durable, **offline merge-truth probe** (`storyHasMergeEvidence`): a HEAD-reachable commit whose subject names the story id (own work landed), or a `(#N)` PR commit referencing it. Fed into `collectDossier` from the run-cache git snapshot (one `git log`, no extra spawns).

- The selector may **promote** a card to delivered; durable merge evidence corroborates a backlog **Done** claim — but a confirmed-merged card is never **erased**.
- Gated on `status==="done"`: a Todo card a commit body merely references is **not** promoted, and a *premature done* (claimed Done but not merged) correctly stays not-delivered.

## Result

Recovers **113/143**. The 30 residual are legacy cards squash-merged under PRs that never named the story id → no HEAD-reachable proof → honest not-delivered (the merge-evidence-only model the owner chose; attest-presence is deliberately not a delivered signal per `dossier.test.ts:1033`).

## Tests

- `dossier.test.ts` — FIX-208 reproduction (delivered false without probe, true with merge evidence); Todo card stays not-delivered (Done-gate); `storyHasMergeEvidence` subject/`(#N)`/null cases.
- Full suite green (1066 passed). The pre-existing deliberate-stance test (`:1033`) still passes.

author: jeffmhopkins
body:
## Why

A long note (a pasted article, "dad's medical history") was extracted in **one** `note.extract` call with **one** fact budget — so its yield was capped by that budget *and* by the call's output-token ceiling (`EXTRACT_MAX_TOKENS`). The tail was clipped no matter how much durable content the note actually held. Raising the cap doesn't help: ~40 facts already approaches the output-token wall, so a single call can't scale.

This is the third item from the discussion thread (after #132 fact-cap scaling and #134 the paragraph-granularity fix this builds on).

## What changed

`analyze_note` now splits the note's paragraph chunks into token-bounded **groups** (`prompt.group_texts`, `GROUP_CHAR_BUDGET ≈ 6000 chars`), extracts each in its own call with its own length-scaled budget, and **merges** them (`extraction.merge_extractions`) into one note-level extraction before `_apply`. The yield scales with the note instead of clipping.

The reduce deliberately reuses the machinery that already reconciles facts **across notes**:
- union the mentions and tokens;
- **re-run the deterministic object binding over the full mention set**, so a relationship whose object entity was named in a *different* group still links instead of orphaning;
- dedup on the structural identity key, so a property restated across groups collapses to one;
- `dropped_facts` sums each group's own truncation, so the note-level `extraction_truncated` card (from #132) still reflects a hit budget.

**The common path is unchanged:** a note that fits one group makes exactly one call, byte-identical to before — every harness scenario (all single-chunk) and short note is unaffected. Groups run sequentially; a malformed group fails the note like any single extraction (the merge is in-memory, `_apply` runs once after in a single transaction).

## Tests
- Unit: `group_texts` partitioning (one group under budget; fan-out without splitting a block; lone-oversize isolation) and `merge_extractions` (single-part passthrough, metadata union, cross-group object rebinding, cross-group dedup, dropped summing). 636 unit tests pass.
- Integration: a two-group note makes two extraction calls and lands both groups' facts on the one note.
- `docs/ANALYSIS.md` marks the decision.

## Notes / future work
- Cross-group coreference is bounded by group size (several paragraphs per group); a small note-context header for later groups is possible future work, noted in the doc.
- Cost: groups × ~$0.01 — a few cents on a long note, negligible at personal scale.
- Backend integration test runs in CI (no Postgres in my environment).

body:
## Resumo

Implementa pagamento com cartão de crédito e débito via Mercado Pago Checkout API,
com todos os mecanismos de aprovação recomendados pelo MP, status correto e estorno
no CRM web.

## O que foi entregue

### Core (F0–F6)
- Bottom-sheet completo: cartões salvos, novo cartão, parcelas, revisão, resultado
- Tokenização no device (PCI-DSS: PAN/CVV nunca passam pelo backend)
- Split automático: taxa MP 100% do prestador, comissão da plataforma sobre o bruto
- Idempotência por tentativa (evita cobrança dupla)
- Flag `card_saved_cards` controlável pelo CRM web
- Cartões salvos via MP Customer (crédito, opt-in, CVV sempre exigido)
- Débito avulso sem salvar (regra de produto)

### Antifraude / Aprovação (recomendações do MP)
- Device fingerprint (`X-meli-session-id`) via WebView oculta + `security.js`
- Pagador completo: email, nome, sobrenome, CPF, telefone
- `additional_info` com itens e pagador
- **3DS 2.0** (`three_d_secure_mode: optional`): desafio na WebView com polling
  automático; timeout de 4 min → "em processamento"

### Status e notificações
- `in_process` → badge "Processando" (botão pagar some, evita cobrança dupla)
- `approved` → confirmado + split + notificação cliente e prestador
- `rejected` → badge "Recusado" + botão de nova tentativa
- Webhook MP resolve pagamentos pendentes (approved/rejected/cancelled)
- Auto-sync ao abrir o pedido (cliente e prestador): destrava SR travada em
  `processing` quando o MP rejeitou sem registrar

### CRM Web
- Coluna "Ações" na aba Pagamentos com botão **Estornar** (janela de 3 dias)
- Endpoint `POST /admin/payments/:id/refund`: valida 72h, chama MP refunds,
  reverte status, notifica cliente

### Infra
- Ambientes `staging` e `production` no `wrangler.toml`
- Rota `/v1/mp-public-key` pública (sem token)
- URL da API configurável por ambiente (EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL / VITE_API_URL)
- Runbook de rollout: `docs/rollout-cartao.md`

## Pendências pós-merge
- Aplicar migration `supabase/migrations/20260615_saved_cards.sql` em produção
- `wrangler deploy --env production` com credenciais de produção do MP
- Ligar flag `card_saved_cards` via CRM (PATCH /v1/admin/feature-flags)
- Chamado WCS-40518 no suporte MP (conta nova com `cc_rejected_high_risk`)

## Como testar
1. `wrangler deploy --env staging` (em `apps/api`)
2. `npx expo start -c` (em `apps/mobile-client`)
3. Ligar flag `card_saved_cards` no CRM → aba Pagamentos com cartão aparece

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements the requirements for Experiment 4 by introducing an SLR(1) parser generator and an automated documentation pipeline to generate the required submission artifacts.

### Parser Implementation (`lr.py`)
- **Grammar parsing:** Extracts context-free grammar productions from `g.in` and automatically augments the grammar.
- **DFA Construction:** Computes LR(0) item closures and `goto` transitions to build the state machine DFA.
- **SLR(1) Tables:** Computes `FIRST` and `FOLLOW` sets to populate the `ACTION` and `GOTO` tables, mitigating conflicts present in pure LR(0) parsers.
- **Parsing Controller:** Implements a table-driven, stack-based parser to track state and symbol transitions for input validation.

### Automated Reporting (`build_word_doc.py`)
- Uses `python-docx` to programmatically generate the assignment Word document.
- Embeds detailed explanations of the closure algorithms, DFA state transitions, table construction logic, and the full source code directly into the document.

**Example Usage:**
```python
from lr import Grammar, LR_Parser

# Parse grammar and target string
g = Grammar("g.in")

# Initialize parser, build DFA and tables
parser = LR_Parser(g)
parser.build_dfa()
action, goto_tbl = parser.build_slr1_table()

# Execute state-machine parser
if g.target:
    success, steps = parser.parse(g.target)
    for step in steps:
        print(step)
```

author: kennguy3n
body:
## Summary

Adds the **iOS build plane** under `plugins/xcode/**` (Phase 3), mirroring the Android/Gradle plane (WS-B): a SwiftPM/Xcode **build-tool plugin** that hardens an app at build time and registers a **build proof** with `RegistryService.CreateBuild`, plus an XCFramework packaging pipeline. Everything runs in the tenant's own CI — no per-build cloud compute. App Store safe by construction (public toolchain only; no private APIs, no dynamic code, no dyld/entitlement abuse).

The build-proof **manifest schema is canonical and shared with Android** so the control plane and runtime build-proof check validate either platform with one schema. New design doc: `docs/build-hardening-ios.md`.

## What's in the package (`plugins/xcode`, package `KsealHarden`)

| Product | Kind | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `KsealHardenCore` | library | Portable, **zero-dependency** hardening logic (unit-testable on Linux). |
| `kseal-harden` | executable | CLI the plugins invoke: `generate` / `register` / `harden-binary` / `version`. |
| `KsealHardenPlugin` | build-tool plugin | Build-time string hardening + proof emission. **No network** (sandboxed). |
| `KsealRegisterPlugin` | command plugin | Registers the proof (network-permitted) with offline fallback. |

Core modules: vendored SHA-256 (NIST-vectored), `PolymorphismSeed`, `StringHardener`, `SymbolHardener`, `BuildProofManifest`, `RegistryClient`, `HardenEngine`.

## Key design points (hard to see from the diff alone)

- **Per-build polymorphism.** Fresh CSPRNG seed per build (or pinned via `KSEAL_BUILD_SEED` for reproducible builds). All randomized material is derived as `block_i = SHA256(seed ‖ context ‖ i)` with a distinct `context` per use, so keystream is never reused. **Only the seed digest is published** — the raw seed is never logged/committed.
- **String hardening** emits a generated `KsealSecureStrings` enum compiled into the target; values are XOR-masked with seed-derived keys. The integration test asserts plaintext is absent from **both** the generated source and the **compiled binary**, and that two seeds produce different ciphertext (decay).
- **Wire format matters.** `CreateBuild` is Connect-JSON: field names camelCase, int64 `versionCode` encoded as a **string**, and the manifest carried as a JSON **string** field. Verified against a mock transport in unit tests and against a real local HTTP server.
- **`buildHash`** binds the proof to the build: `SHA256("kseal-build-hash/v1" ‖ platform ‖ sdkVersion ‖ target ‖ versionName ‖ versionCode ‖ protectionProfileId ‖ seedDigest ‖ sortedToolVersions ‖ generatedSource)`.
- **Offline fallback.** Registration never fails the build: if the registry is unconfigured/unreachable, the proof is written to a durable `*.offline.json` for later reconciliation.
- **Secrets from env only** (`KSEAL_API_KEY`, `KSEAL_REGISTRY_URL`, `KSEAL_TENANT_ID`, `KSEAL_APP_ID`) — never flags/files.

Usage:

```swift
.executableTarget(
    name: "App",
    exclude: ["kseal-secure-strings.json"],
    plugins: [ .plugin(name: "KsealHardenPlugin", package: "KsealHarden") ]
)
// then: KsealSecureStrings.apiBaseURL   (no literal in source/binary)
```

## Symbol/metadata stripping & XCFramework pipeline

`scripts/harden-binary.sh` runs `strip -x` (Mach-O + ELF), counts symbols via `nm`, and validates with `otool`. `scripts/build-xcframework.sh` builds `KsealFFI` + archives `KsealSDK` for device/sim, `-create-xcframework`, strips slices, then emits + registers the proof. Apple-only steps require macOS/Xcode and **skip cleanly** on non-Apple hosts; `strip`/proof logic still runs.

## Tests (all run locally)

`cd plugins/xcode && swift test` → **44 tests, 0 failures** on the Linux Swift 5.10.1 toolchain.

- Unit: SHA-256 vectors, seed determinism/keystream separation, string round-trip + plaintext-absence + polymorphism, manifest schema/serialization, registry wire format (path, bearer auth, int64-as-string, manifest-as-string), offline fallback, and a **real `strip`** run on a freshly compiled binary.
- Integration: builds `Fixtures/HardenedApp` with the plugin applied and asserts manifest fields, seed digest, and plaintext absence in the generated source + compiled binary.
- Apple-toolchain-dependent paths (`xcodebuild`, nested fixture build when no Swift toolchain is reachable) `XCTSkip` with a clear message rather than faking a pass.

## Scope / conflict-avoidance

body:
The bpm selector (#159) split each breath **evenly** (1:1), which silently dropped the **longer exhale** that makes resonance breathing parasympathetic — the actual point of the practice. This restores a **~2:3 inhale:exhale** ratio.

## Change
`phasesForBpm(bpm)` in `BreathePage.tsx`: `total = round(60/bpm)`, then `inhale = max(1, round(total·2/5))`, `exhale = total − inhale`. Inhale+exhale still equals `total`, so the **chosen bpm is preserved**; the out-breath is now longer.

Examples: 6 bpm → 4s/6s · 10 bpm → 2s/4s · 3 bpm → 8s/12s · 1 bpm → 24s/36s.

Ran the app: registered, drove the Breathe page at 6 bpm, started + finished a session → the **saved session stored `inhale_seconds=4`, `exhale_seconds=6`** (exact 2:3, longer exhale). `tsc` clean.

author: acedatacloud-dev
body:
## Problem

Reported from a live Coding Bridge session (`studio.acedata.cloud/coding-bridge`): after restoring a history conversation and sending a new query, the new message appeared **in the middle** of the transcript, with old content below it — and the new prompt was never actually answered.

Session `fa857047-8d2c-4b0d-9976-f9e3335502d3`, trace `f90ffc58…`.

## Root cause (confirmed via CLS + reproduction)

CLS (`platform-service-coding-bridge` relay) shows the failing turn:

```
09:54:50  history.get → history.detail            (browser renders the past transcript)
09:55:55  session.start (resume, trace f90ffc58)   ← the new query
09:55:56  79 node events in ONE second:
          thinking×5 text_delta×44 text×7 tool_use×11 tool_result×11 result×1
```

44 text-deltas interleaved with 11 *completed* tool round-trips in a single second is impossible for live generation — it is the claude CLI **re-streaming the whole resumed transcript** (some versions do this on `--resume --include-partial-messages`), terminated by the old `ResultMessage`. The node forwarded every replayed message as a live event, so:

1. The browser appended the replay **after** the just-added prompt bubble → the new prompt is buried mid-history.
2. `_turn()` used `receive_response()`, which stops at the first `ResultMessage` (the replay's) → the genuine new turn never streamed.

Reproduction: current CLI (2.0.1, 2.1.168) does **not** replay; the production node runs an older claude CLI/SDK that does.

## Fix

Guard the **first resumed turn** (`providers/claude.py`):

- Load the resumed transcript's ids — per-line `uuid` + assistant `message.id` (`history.claude_known_ids`).
- Iterate `receive_messages()` and drop any message that reuses those ids (the replay): replayed streaming messages (matched by `message_start.message.id`) and replayed complete messages (matched by `.uuid`).
- Swallow the replay's terminating `ResultMessage` once, so the genuine turn that follows still streams; end the turn on the genuine result.
- Keyed on stable ids → **no-op on CLIs that do not replay** (no id matches).
- Log the node's `claude_code_version` on resume so we can see which nodes are on a replay-prone CLI in CLS.

## Verification

- `tests/test_resume_guard.py` — deterministic unit tests: replay block + genuine turn → only the new turn's events emit; clean-CLI no-op; empty genuine turn still terminates.
- Live no-regression run through the gated path on CLI 2.1.168: gate arms (loads transcript ids), passes the genuine turn through unchanged (`GATE_OK`, one result).
- Full suite: 134 passed; ruff clean.

author: discreteds
body:
## Phase 3 of the unified profile→kwargs emission refactor

Replaces transport's duplicated `_core/auth` strategy/resolver engine with the `profile.emit(target)` primitive shipped in Phase 1 (mountainash-settings #46) and Phase 2 (mountainash-auth-client #5). Credential injection is now a single declarative call per leaf connection.

Governing spec: `mountainash-auth-client/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-unified-profile-kwargs-emission-design.md` (Phase 3 section). Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-13-unified-emission-phase3-transport.md`.

### What changed
- **Leaf connections are dict-only.** `HTTPConnection`/`S3Connection`/`SSHConnection` now take just `connect_kwargs` — the `auth_strategy.apply()` step is gone.
- **Factory emits per leaf.** `create_connection` / `create_tunnelled_connection` call `auth_profile.emit(family, base=profile.to_handler_kwargs())`, with `family` from `_family_for_provider` (http→HTTP; s3/r2/minio/b2/s3express→BOTO; sftp/ssh→PARAMIKO). `None`/`NoAuthProfile`/unmapped → kwargs pass through. S3 assume-role nested `{base_kwargs, role_arn, session_name}` shape layers credentials onto `base_kwargs` only (copy-on-write).
- **OAuth is flow-owned construct-and-emit.** `OAuth2Connection`/`OAuth1Connection` resolve tokens, then build a `TokenAuthProfile`/`OAuth1AuthProfile` and `.emit(TargetFamily.HTTP, …)`. Empty cached access token now fails closed (`if not access_token` → `AuthorizationRequired`).
- **Protocols survive, the engine dies.** `AuthStrategy`/`RefreshableAuthStrategy` relocate to `_core/http/auth_protocol.py` (the HTTP engine's 401-refresh seam — forward-looking, no concrete impl yet). `_core/auth/` (resolver + 8 strategies) and `tests/_core/auth/` are deleted.

### Scope note: absorbed a merged-dep API rename

author: chaliy
body:
## What
Add a `guardrails` capability that runs declarative, deterministic checks over
agent activity, plus a dry-run endpoint and a `specs/guardrails.md` spec.

- **Check engine** (`crates/core/src/guardrail_checks.rs`): typed, compiled,
  deterministic rules — `regex`, `blocklist` (case-insensitive by default),
  and `tool_pattern` (`*`-wildcard tool-name matching). Each check binds a rule
  to a **stage** (`output`, `tool_use`, `tool_output`) with an on-fail action
  (`block` or `log`) and optional replacement text. A config-level `advisory`
  mode downgrades every hit to log-only for false-positive tuning.
- **Capability** (`crates/core/src/capabilities/guardrails.rs`): compiles its
  per-agent config and contributes the matching runtime hooks — a streaming
  `OutputGuardrail` for `output`, a `PreToolUseHook` for `tool_use`, a
  `PostToolExecHook` for `tool_output`. Hooks are contributed only for stages
  that have checks; an empty/absent config contributes nothing.
- **Marker**: `is_guardrail` on `CapabilityInfo` (and a UI badge) groups
  guardrails in the capability picker; `prompt_canary_guardrail` is flagged too.
- **Dry run**: `POST /v1/capabilities/guardrails/dry-run` evaluates a config
  against sample text with no session and nothing persisted.

## Why
We have agents, harnesses, and capabilities; guardrails were the missing safety
layer. Modeling them as capabilities (rather than a top-level entity) reuses the
registry, per-agent config schema/validation, and harness/agent/session
composition, and fits the platform stance that guardrails are opt-in — an author
can build an agent with none, and a harness can ship them as soft defaults.
Design rationale and the deferred phases (model-based PII/profanity, `llm_judge`,
MCP-served checks, a gallery) are in `specs/guardrails.md`.

## How
Config-aware hook seams were added to the `Capability` trait
(`pre_tool_use_hooks_with_config` / `post_tool_exec_hooks_with_config`) and the
runtime now resolves tool hooks through them. Output guardrails already received
per-capability config. The engine compiles once and evaluates against accumulated
text (output), serialized arguments + tool name (tool_use), or the result payload
(tool_output). Invalid persisted config is logged and treated as no checks so a
bad config can never wedge a turn.

## Risk
- **Low/Medium.** Additive and opt-in; absent/empty config is a no-op with zero
  added latency. The streaming path runs only deterministic, linear-time checks.
- What could break: a misconfigured `block` check could suppress legitimate
  output/tool calls for that agent — mitigated by advisory mode and the dry-run
  tuning endpoint.

## Security
- **Threat categories reviewed:** TM-API, TM-DOS, TM-TOOL, TM-LLM.
- **Findings and resolutions:**
  - New authenticated input surface (dry-run, and persisted regex configs):
    added **TM-DOS-017** — regex compiled with `RegexBuilder::size_limit` (1 MB,
    linear-time engine), check/entry/replacement counts capped, dry-run text
    bounded to 64 KiB. Dry-run is gated by `capability.view`, persists nothing,
    and performs no DB/network I/O.
  - Tool-output `block` drops the original result/error/images/raw payload and
    substitutes a fixed notice, reducing (not adding to) the injection surface
    (TM-TOOL-005, TM-LLM).
  - No new auth/crypto/tenant surface — configs live in existing org-scoped
    per-agent capability config.

## Follow-ups
Deferred to later phases, documented in `specs/guardrails.md` (out of scope for a
deterministic phase-1):
- Model-backed checks (PII NER, profanity/toxicity, prompt-injection classifiers).
- `llm_judge` check type (natural-language policy, fast-model, parallel/at-end).
- `mcp` check type (third-party guardrail over scoped-MCP).
- Guardrail gallery via the harness-examples import pattern.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added or updated (42 core engine/capability unit tests; 6 HTTP
  integration tests run against real Postgres)
- [x] Backward compatibility considered (additive; no-op when unconfigured)
- [x] Security review performed against relevant threat model categories
- [ ] Final CI ran checks affected by this PR
- [ ] All review comments addressed (code change or written reasoning)

## Validation
- `cargo test -p everruns-core` (2342 passed) and `-p everruns-server` (1504 passed).
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean on
  touched crates.
- Regenerated `docs/api/openapi.json` (dry-run path + 3 schemas + `is_guardrail`).
- Smoke-tested end-to-end: brought up local Postgres, ran the 6-test
  `guardrails_integration_test` — guardrails appears in `/v1/capabilities` with
  `is_guardrail: true`, and the dry-run endpoint blocks, logs (advisory), matches
  tool patterns, and rejects invalid regex.
- UI lint/build deferred to CI (no local `node_modules`); changes mirror the
  existing `is_mcp` badge with a standard lucide `Shield` icon.

### Motivation
- Provide ISSUE-15: a non-destructive, structural sanitizer that prepares role/stage-scoped blind bundles without modifying the original bundle or doing any semantic/textual redaction.  Skills used: `tdd` (Red→Green→Refactor), `grill-with-docs` (ensure protocol/schema/policy adherence), and `diagnose` (investigate manifest/hash/policy/leak-checker edge cases). 

### Description
- Add a sanitizer module `generator/blind_bundle_sanitizer.py` implementing `BlindBundleSanitizeRequest`, `BlindBundleSanitizeResult`, `BlindBundleSanitizeError` and the public function `sanitize_blind_bundle(request)`, which: validates source/outputs, loads and schema-validates the source manifest, runs the structural leak checker on the source, applies policy per artifact (allow/warn/deny), performs only allowed transformations (`copy` and `normalize_filename` + structural `exclude_artifact`), recalculates SHA-256 hashes, builds a schema-compatible manifest (includes `parent_manifest_id`/`source_manifest_ids`, `transformations`, `integrity`, `visibility_policy`, `isolation_check`), runs final structural leak check on the sanitized bundle, and publishes the bundle atomically from a tmp dir. 
- Preserve originals byte-for-byte and write only into `output_root` tmp dir; ensure atomic publish/cleanup and overwrite semantics limited to the specific sanitized bundle directory. 
- Integrate with existing helpers/policy/leak-checker from `generator/*` without changing their public APIs. 
- Tests: add `tests/test_blind_bundle_sanitizer.py` covering expected behavior (non-destructive copy, neutralize paths, hash preservation, transformations recorded, policy deny/warn behavior, symlink/hash/undeclared failures, atomic publish/cleanup, determinism, and no textual sanitization). 
- Files added: `generator/blind_bundle_sanitizer.py`, `tests/test_blind_bundle_sanitizer.py`.

### Testing
- Ran the focused tests and full suite locally; key commands and results: 
  - `pytest tests/test_blind_bundle_sanitizer.py -q` → 10 passed.

author: cristulio
body:
Acts on the shrine/omen measuring sim (#607). The sim's headline finding for the owner's **principle 1 (chapter-relevance)**: event **gold** already ramps with depth (`eventGoldScale`, ×6 by Ch14) but **HP/temp-HP were deliberately flat** — so a +5 heal worth a quarter-bar in Ch1 is a rounding error against a Throne-era pool, and a −4 cost stops mattering.

**The tuning**
- New `eventHpScale` ramp with its own knob `EVENT_HP_CH14_MULTIPLE = 8` — hotter than gold's ×6 because HP pools climb ~×8–10 over the chain, set just *under* the pool curve so a scaled heal stays a worthwhile slice, never a full top-up.
- Same `minChapter` anchor as gold → deep-authored events don't double-count into a jackpot.
- `applyEventOutcome` takes an `hpScale` alongside `goldScale`; `EventRoom` computes it; `hp_delta` (heals **and** costs) and `temp_hp` both scale. The lethality floor (event costs never kill) is preserved.
- Qualitative rewards (blessings, run buffs, items, quirk rerolls) stay flat **by design** — a blessing is a blessing at any depth.

**Validated by the sim (re-run in this PR):**
| principle | reading | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — chapter-relevance | numeric value now scales: gold ×6 + **HP ×8** by Ch14 (was HP flat) | **fixed** |
| 2 — shrine ≈ omen | 165g vs 140g = 1.18× | under 1.3× — fine |
| 3 — risk pays | hard gates 164g vs easy 61g | ~2.7× — fine |

The sim's old "staleness 30/41" is reframed: that share is now correctly identified as *qualitative-reward* events (chapter-invariant by nature), not a bug. Further tuning rides the two `*_CH14_MULTIPLE` knobs.

`npm run build` green; delve + content + components suites **591 pass** (incl. new `hpScale` + `eventHpScale` coverage).
