author: hherb
body:
## What

Projects the four Rust-bridge **record-edit primitives** onto the **uniffi (Swift) + pyo3 (Python)** bindings, mirroring the existing `save_block`/`trash_block` projection pattern:

- `append_record`, `edit_record`, `tombstone_record`, `resurrect_record`
- a new `RecordContent` foreign input type (reuses the zeroize-typed `FieldInput`/`FieldInputValue` from `save_block`)

This is **Slice 1 of 2** for "iOS record editing" — it lands the FFI surface the native-iOS record-CRUD UI (Slice 2) will build on.

### Why it was needed
The bridge already had these CRDT-correct primitives, but the bindings exposed only block-level ops (`save_block` is **replace-semantics** — editing through it would re-stamp every field clock and drop forward-compat `unknown` data). This projects the granular primitives so edits go through the bridge's `edit_record` (preserving untouched per-field clocks, `tombstoned_at_ms`, and all `unknown` maps).

## Properties
- **CRDT clock-preservation proven at the binding boundary** (not trusted): the edit-test asserts an untouched field keeps its prior `device_uuid` while the changed field gets the new one — in **Swift, Kotlin, and pyo3**.
- **All three uuids length-validated** binding-side before the bridge call (→ `InvalidArgument`/`ValueError`); errors mapped, never swallowed; secrets in zeroize-on-drop carriers, never stashed past the call.
- **No new `FfiVaultError` variant** (`BlockNotFound`/`RecordNotFound` pre-existed) → **conformance harnesses stay 27/27**.
- **No `core` / on-disk-format / UDL-error / KAT change** — touches only `ffi/`.
- New code in dedicated `record_edit.rs` files (the 637-line `namespace/mod.rs` is not extended).
- pyo3 `FieldInputValue.inner` stays private (cross-module access via a `to_bridge()` accessor).

## Tests (all green)
- `cargo test --release --workspace` — pass; `clippy -D warnings` + `fmt --check` clean
- Swift smoke `run.sh` — **53/53**; Kotlin smoke parity — green
- Swift + Kotlin `run_conformance.sh` — **27/27 each, unchanged**
- pyo3 `pytest` — **83 passed** (incl. 5 new record-edit round-trips)

## Reviewer notes
- The `RecordContent` constructor arg order differs **intentionally** between bindings: uniffi UDL is `(record_type, tags, fields)` (matches the bridge struct); pyo3 `RecordContent(fields, record_type="", tags=[])` puts the required arg first for Python ergonomics (same shape as `RecordInput::new`). Not a transposition bug — each binding's tests construct it correctly.
- `read_block` surfaces tombstoned records via the per-record `tombstone()` flag (it does **not** filter them) — the tombstone tests assert the flag flips, and this is a documented input for the Slice-2 UI (which must filter live-vs-deleted itself).
- Includes a one-line bridge doc note that `append_record` does not enforce `record_uuid` uniqueness (mirrors `create_block`'s block-UUID contract).

body:
Two **distinct** OTA bugs found while proving #96 — both prod-gating, both fixed here as separate commits.

### Commit 1 — install silently fails on Android 14+ (`UpdateChecker.kt`)
The `INSTALL_COMPLETE` status PendingIntent was `FLAG_MUTABLE` + implicit, which API 34+ disallows → `getBroadcast()` throws, the catch swallows it, the session never commits. Every OTA silently fails to install on a 14+ device (download succeeds, version never changes). Fix: explicit intent (`setPackage`), keep `FLAG_MUTABLE` for status write-back.

### Commit 2 — no auto-relaunch after self-update (`Relauncher`/`PackageReplacedReceiver`, the #96 bug)
After install, `PACKAGE_REPLACED` killed the app and nothing relaunched it → screens dropped to the launcher. New `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED` receiver relaunches via a shared cascade (extracted from BootReceiver): **overlay-direct** `startActivity` → **FSI notification** (auto-launch <14; visible **tap-to-resume** prompt on 14+ — fail loud, never dark).

## Test status — honest
| Piece | Status |
|---|---|
| Install fix (FLAG_MUTABLE → explicit) | ✅ **emulator-proven** A16/API36 — `session committed`, update applies |
| Relaunch (MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED → overlay-direct) | ✅ **emulator-proven** A16 — `BAL_ALLOW_SAW_PERMISSION`, relaunches to new version |
| Accessibility **re-binds across the OTA** | ✅ **emulator-proven** — `Service connected` fires post-relaunch → **sequential OTAs safe** (the one real fleet-killer-class unknown; ruled out) |
| Onboarding flow (Enable buttons deep-link, grants stick) | ✅ **emulator-proven** A16 via the real on-screen UI |
| **Live hands-off auto-confirm** (one clean sequence) | ⏳ **deferred → strobe MAXHUB** — component-proven (accessibility binds + re-binds, config `typeAllMask`+`canRetrieveWindowContent`, logic targets the installer); the single live capture was blocked by Play-image noise (Play Protect / stale cross-UID file), not code |
| **A11 / A9 cross-version matrix** | ⏳ **deferred → strobe hardware** (first-OTA single-sequence behavior) |

## Operational notes
- **Unattended OTA requires accessibility (auto-confirm install) + overlay (relaunch)** — the setup wizard grants both. A device where they're **skipped** degrades to the visible tap-to-resume prompt, not a dark screen.
- **FireOS** untested (Amazon fork, no Play Services) — classify install-vs-relaunch on the next staging OTA via the #97 log signature: **#98**.
- **Known limitation**: Play Protect's dialog is `com.android.vending`, outside the auto-confirm's `packageinstaller` scope — a Play-Services device with Protect ON could stall even fully onboarded (MAXHUB/FireOS dodge it). Flagged, not chased.

## Planned regression guard (next session)
Tier-1 **pure onboarding-logic test** — a `canDeviceAutoUpdate(perms, sdk)` function + CI guard. The re-bind finding gives it a known-correct spec (accessibility + overlay → yes; either missing → fail-loud path).

Pairs with **PR #97** (server OTA logging). **Do not merge — gated on strobe confirming the live hands-off OTA on a real MAXHUB.** No deploy.

body:
## Contexto

No `Sidebar` (`src/components/Sidebar.tsx`):
- **Câmeras** (`#sidebar-cameras`, botão dropdown com a lista de câmeras) hoje fica na
  **seção inferior**, junto de Estatísticas/Configurações/Usuário. O navigator quer no
  **topo, logo abaixo do sino** de notificações (`#sidebar-notifications`).
- **Estatísticas** (`#sidebar-stats` → `/stats`; o navigator chamou de "status") hoje é
  um item na **seção inferior**. O navigator quer ele **dentro do flyout de
  configurações** (popup da engrenagem), **entre o color mode e "Sobre"**.

O flyout de configurações renderiza `settingsLinks`; antes do `/settings/about` injeta
`<ThemeModeNav/>` (color mode, `#theme-mode-nav`). Hoje a ordem final do flyout é:
color mode → Sobre. Alvo: color mode → **Estatísticas (/stats)** → Sobre.

## Solução

`Sidebar.tsx`:
- **Mover o bloco Câmeras** (botão + painel portal) da seção inferior para logo após a
  seção do sino, no topo. Ajustar o posicionamento do painel para abrir **ancorado ao
  topo** (`top: r.top`, como o sino) em vez de ancorado à base.
- **Remover** o `NavIcon` de Estatísticas da seção inferior; **renderizar um link
  `/stats`** dentro do flyout de configurações, logo após `<ThemeModeNav/>` e antes do
  link `/settings/about` (mesmo estilo dos demais itens do flyout).
- Adicionar `id="sidebar-bottom"` ao container inferior (para teste e referência).

author: ohah
body:
## 의도

사용자 요청 대응: **"사이드바 '+' 버튼으로 워크스페이스 생성 추가."** 세로 사이드바의 탭 목록 **바로 아래** 슬롯에 "+" 버튼을 그려, 클릭하면 새 워크스페이스(탭)가 열린다 — `⌘⇧T`의 마우스 버전. cmux가 워크스페이스 생성을 사이드바 UI로 하는 것을 따른다(이제 ⌘⇧T는 "임시"가 아니라 정식 단축키와 병행). 사용자 백로그 ③의 뒷부분(③a 폭 조절에 이어).

## 구현

`src/platform/macos/coretext_frame_builder.zig`, `src/platform/macos/app_dev_session.zig`.

**1) 렌더 — "+" glyph 행**
- `buildSidebarDrawList`에 **`plus_row: ?usize`** 추가: 그 행(= 탭 개수)에 '+' glyph를 가로 중앙(`col = cols/2`)에 그리고, `size.rows`를 그 행까지 포함하게 늘린다. 렌더러가 사이드바 셀을 **행 × 슬롯 높이**로 배치하므로 "+"가 마지막 탭 슬롯 아래에 놓인다.
- `buildSidebarTitleFrame`이 `plus_row = self.tabs.items.len`을 넘긴다(탭 제목 패스와 같은 glyph seam·atlas 재사용).

**2) hit-test + 클릭**
- 순수 `sidebarPlusSlot(y, slot_h, tab_count)`: `y ∈ [tab_count×slot_h, (tab_count+1)×slot_h)`. 렌더 "+"와 같은 슬롯.
- `mouse` down(1) 사이드바 분기에서 **슬롯 hit-test보다 먼저** `sidebarPlusSlot`을 검사 — 맞으면 `newTab()`(`createTab`이 새 탭을 활성으로). `⌘⇧T`(`new_tab` 액션)와 같은 경로.

**3) hover 커서**
- `hoverCursor`가 "+" 슬롯 위면 `link`(pointingHand) — 클릭 가능 affordance. 일반 탭 슬롯은 `arrow`(default). ②의 `CursorKind` 경로 그대로.

## 문서 정합성

- `docs/implementation-plan.md`: **③b 사이드바 "+" 버튼 완료** 항목 추가; 미정 폴리시의 "워크스페이스 생성을 사이드바 '+' 버튼으로(⌘⇧T 임시)" → 완료로 교체, "+" 슬롯 hover 밴드를 후속으로 남김.
- `docs/tabs-splits-layout.md`: 워크스페이스 생성에 사이드바 하단 "+" 버튼 추가(⌘⇧T와 병행).

## clean-room 근거

순수 UI — 외부 코드 미참고. "사이드바 하단 +로 새 탭/워크스페이스"는 보편 사이드바 UI(VS Code/cmux 등). "+" glyph 행·`sidebarPlusSlot`·`newTab` 배선은 기존 사이드바 렌더(`buildSidebarDrawList`)·슬롯 hit-test·`createTab`의 Maru 독립 재사용. VT/parser 변경 없음 → 명세 인용 **N/A**.

## 전략 영향 평가

- **기존 조각 재사용**: 사이드바 제목 렌더(`buildSidebarDrawList` 한 행 추가)·슬롯 hit-test 패턴·`newTab`(⌘⇧T와 같은)·② 커서 경로. 새 ABI/렌더 경로 없음. **ABI 무변경**(26).
- "보이는 = 클릭되는": 렌더 "+"(plus_row)와 hit-test(`sidebarPlusSlot`)·커서가 같은 슬롯(`tab_count`)을 공유.
- 방어 코드 없음. `plus_row`는 `?usize`(없으면 기존 동작 그대로), 슬롯 검사는 정확성.

## 테스트

```
zig build test               → 전체 통과(sidebarPlusSlot 순수 + buildSidebarDrawList '+' + ③b 통합 신설), exit 0
zig fmt --check / macos-app-host-swift-check / check-boundaries
  / test-macos-coretext-smoke / test-macos-metal-smoke / test-macos-app-pty-metal-smoke → 전부 PASS
```

테스트:
- 헤드리스(순수 `sidebarPlusSlot`): "+" 슬롯 안/아래 빈 영역/탭 슬롯/slot_h 0/음수/탭 0개(슬롯 0).
- 헤드리스(`buildSidebarDrawList`): `plus_row` 설정 시 '+'가 그 행 가로 중앙에·`size.rows`가 +1; `null`이면 '+' 없음·rows=탭 수.
- macOS 통합: "+" 슬롯 호버 = `link`; "+" 클릭 → `tabs` 2개·새 탭 활성·세션 유지.
- 기존 사이드바 테스트는 "+" 슬롯 밖(탭 슬롯·슬롯 10)을 클릭해 무영향(통과).

## E2E/관측 가능성

- 통합이 실 init→resize→"+" 슬롯 hover/click(실 셸 spawn) 경로를 돌아 탭 개수 증가로 검증한다.
- 실제로 "+"가 사이드바 하단에 보이고 클릭으로 워크스페이스가 늘어나는지는 dev 앱 수동 확인.

## 한계

- **"+" 슬롯 hover 밴드(시각 강조)는 없음** — '+' glyph + pointingHand 커서로만 표시. 호버 밴드는 후속 폴리시(탭 슬롯의 호버 밴드 머신리를 "+" 슬롯로 확장).
- 윈도가 짧아 "+" 슬롯이 화면 밖이면 안 보인다(스크롤 없음) — 탭이 아주 많은 극단.

## 사용자 논의 필요 여부

사용자 요청 직접 대응. 위치(탭 목록 바로 아래)·동작(=⌘⇧T)은 cmux 동작 비교 기준. 추가 논의 불요.

## 다이어그램

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RENDER["buildSidebarDrawList(plus_row=tabs.len): 탭 목록 아래 행에 '+' 중앙"]
    HOVER["hoverCursor: sidebarPlusSlot? → link(pointingHand)"]
    DOWN["mouse down(1) in sidebar"] --> PLUS{"sidebarPlusSlot(y)? (슬롯보다 먼저)"}
    PLUS -->|"예"| NEW["newTab() → createTab(새 워크스페이스, 활성)"]
    PLUS -->|"아니오"| SLOT["sidebarSlotAt → 전환/✕ 닫기/드래그(기존)"]
```

author: mcorbett51090
body:
## What & why

Research output for the **"identify 10 new plugins"** task. I surveyed the current ~99-plugin marketplace, identified 10 genuine, non-overlapping gaps, prioritized them by **demand × feasibility**, and built the **#1 priority (`email-engineering`)** to full gate-passing quality. The other 9 are scoped in [`docs/plugin-candidates-2026-06-13.md`](../blob/claude/eager-meitner-t24sxk/docs/plugin-candidates-2026-06-13.md) as the build queue.

### Why one plugin, not ten
Each plugin in this marketplace is ~30–60 files held to a strict bar (agents with the scenario-authoring frontmatter schema, Mermaid-tree knowledge banks, best-practices, templates, commands, hooks, scenarios, a stdlib script, plus the frontmatter/claims/layout/prettier/ruff gates). Shipping ten thin plugins would violate that discipline and produce slop. So this PR delivers **one complete, gate-passing plugin + a fully-scoped roadmap** for the rest — the honest split.

## The 10 candidates (prioritized)

| # | Candidate | Priority | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **email-engineering** | P0 | ✅ **built (this PR)** |
| 2 | llm-application-security (OWASP LLM Top 10, prompt-injection defense, red-teaming) | P0 | queued |
| 3 | developer-experience-build-systems (monorepo/Nx/Turborepo/Bazel, build caching) | P1 | queued |
| 4 | graph-knowledge-engineering (Neo4j/Cypher, knowledge graphs, GraphRAG) | P1 | queued |
| 5 | chaos-resilience-engineering (fault injection, game days) | P1 | queued |
| 6 | geospatial-gis-engineering (PostGIS, mapping) | P2 | queued |
| 7 | computer-vision-engineering | P2 | queued |
| 8 | developer-relations-devrel | P2 | queued |
| 9 | open-source-stewardship | P2 | queued |
| 10 | payroll-and-tax-operations | P2 | queued |

Each candidate in the roadmap doc states the gap, why it isn't already covered, the build approach (agents/skills/knowledge), dependencies/seams, and the demand×feasibility rationale.

## `email-engineering` v0.1.0 — what's built

Getting **legitimate mail to the inbox, not spam**:

- **2 agents** — `email-deliverability-architect` (SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment + staged `p=none → quarantine → reject` rollout, BIMI, warm-up, stream separation, spam triage, Gmail/Yahoo compliance) and `email-sending-engineer` (ESP integration, idempotent sends + verified idempotent webhooks, suppression, MJML templates).
- **5 skills**, a **3-doc knowledge bank** (3 Mermaid decision trees: auth setup / spam diagnosis / ESP choice + a dated 2026 ESP map), **8 best-practices**, **3 templates**, **4 commands**, a **scenarios bank** (2 dated narratives).
- **`scripts/email_auth_lint.py`** — stdlib SPF/DMARC record linter (lookup-count, `+all`, `p=reject`-with-no-`rua`, `pct` range). No DNS lookups, no deps, ruff-clean.
- **1 advisory hook** (`flag-email-smells.sh`).
- **Seams:** campaign strategy → `marketing-operations`; sending infra → `backend-engineering`; webhook contract → `api-engineering`; DNS/SES → cloud plugins; secrets/webhook verdicts → `security-engineering`.

## Shared-file changes
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — new plugin entry; metadata `0.86.0 → 0.87.0`.
- `README.md` — plugin count `101 → 102`.
- `docs/architecture.md` — roster row added.

## Gates (verified locally, all green)
frontmatter ✓ · marketplace-claims ✓ · JSON ✓ · prettier `--check .` ✓ · md-links ✓ · layout `--all` ✓ · ruff ✓ · `bash -n` hook ✓.

## Accuracy note
Email-auth mechanics are RFC-grounded (Tier 1). **Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender thresholds and BIMI/VMC requirements are volatile** — they carry `[verify-at-use]` riders + retrieval dates throughout the knowledge bank; re-verify against current provider guidance before a client commitment.

author: sfxdotcom
body:
Server-side wp_remote_get calls had no Referer header, so keys restricted to specific domains (Website restrictions in Google Cloud Console) were rejected with a 403 even when valid.

- Add Referer: home_url('/') to every API request so the call matches the site's own domain restriction.
- Switch validate_key() to use videos?part=id&id=<known ID> — a lightweight, universally-supported call that doesn't rely on the newer forHandle parameter.
- validate_key() now returns true|WP_Error so the AJAX handler can surface Google's actual error message (e.g. "Requests from referer are blocked") instead of the generic fallback string.

author: goultarde
body: # Add `-trust-keys` / `-just-trust-keys` to secretsdump: dump Trusted Domain Object secrets and derive inter-realm Kerberos keys ## Description This PR adds two options to `secretsdump.py`: - `-trust-keys`: in addition to the usual domain credentials, dumps Trusted Domain Object (TDO) secrets and derives, for each trust direction, the inter-realm Kerberos keys (AES256, AES128) and the RC4 (NT) hash, for both the current and the previous trust password. - `-just-trust-keys`: same extraction, but dumps **only** the trust keys. It implies `-trust-keys` and `-just-dc`, and skips the account enumeration entirely (no SAM/LSA, no NTDS account secrets). Useful when you only care about the trust keys and want a fast, quiet, minimal output. The feature lives entirely inside `impacket/examples/secretsdump.py` (`RemoteOperations` and `NTDSHashes`), so it reuses the existing DCSync engine and works through both code paths secretsdump already has: - **Online (DRSUAPI, default):** discovery is done over LSARPC (`LsarEnumerateTrustedDomainsEx`), each `trustedDomain` object is resolved to its `objectGUID` with `DRSCrackNames`, then replicated with `DRSGetNCChanges` (`EXOP_REPL_OBJ`) requesting only `trustAuthIncoming` / `trustAuthOutgoing`. The attributes are decrypted with the DRS session key. - **Offline (NTDS.dit, `-use-vss` or a local `.dit`):** the datatable is scanned for `trustedDomain` objects and the `trustAuthIncoming` / `trustAuthOutgoing` columns are decrypted with the PEK, exactly like `supplementalCredentials`. Both paths converge on the same parsing and key-derivation helpers, so the keys produced are identical regardless of the method used. ## Why this is useful and how it differs from `-just-dc` - `-just-dc` (DCSync) yields the **trust account** key, salted with the partner's NetBIOS (short) name. That is the key of the trust account object, not the key Kerberos actually uses on the wire for cross-realm referrals. - `-trust-keys` reads the TDO cleartext and re-derives the keys with the **inter-realm** salt (partner FQDN). These are the actual AES/RC4 keys used to sign and encrypt cross-realm referral tickets (the inter-realm ST issued by the TGS when a principal traverses the trust). - Practical impact: with these keys an operator can forge inter-realm referral tickets to move laterally across a trust, which the `-just-dc` output does not directly provide. The two also read different objects: `-just-dc` replicates the trust *account* (`CN=$,CN=Users`) and its stored key material, while `-trust-keys` replicates the *trustedDomain* object (`CN=,CN=System`) and decrypts its `trustAuth*` cleartext. On top of that, the salt fed to `string_to_key` differs. Both salts follow the same `{}krbtgt{}` shape, but with different names (example with local `SERVAL.INT` and partner `DEV.SERVAL.INT`): ``` account key salt (-just-dc, partner NetBIOS / short name): {SERVAL.INT}krbtgt{DEV} inter-realm salt (-trust-keys, partner FQDN): {SERVAL.INT}krbtgt{DEV.SERVAL.INT} ``` The two operands swap depending on the trust direction (Incoming uses `{LOCAL}krbtgt{PARTNER}`, Outgoing uses `{PARTNER}krbtgt{LOCAL}`), and everything is upper-cased. As we can see below, the AES keys differ (because of the salt) while the RC4 one is identical (it has no salt): ## Output One key per line, in the usual secretsdump colon-separated format, greppable and tooling-friendly: The `, previous` lines are the trust's old password (the `PreviousValue` of the `trustAuthInfo` structure), useful when the trust password has been rotated and the previous key is still accepted within the clock-skew / N-1 window. ## Credit The technique and the original tools I based this on are AlmondOffSec's [tdo_dump](https://github.com/AlmondOffSec/tdo_dump) by ThePirateWhoSmellsOfSunflowers (online extraction) and Synacktiv's [ntdissector](https://github.com/synacktiv/ntdissector) (offline `.dit` parsing). The `trustAuthInfo` structure is documented in [MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.9.1. On top of those, this PR contributes: LSARPC-based trust discovery (`LsarEnumerateTrustedDomainsEx`), so the online path needs no LDAP connection; a single integration of both the online (DRSUAPI) and offline (NTDS.dit) extraction into secretsdump's existing `NTDSHashes` engine, so both methods share the same parsing and key-derivation code and yield identical keys; dumping of the previous trust password alongside the current one; and the `-just-trust-keys` mode that outputs only the trust keys. This was first prototyped as a NetExec `ldap` module (Pennyw0rth/NetExec#1274); the maintainers and I agreed the feature belongs in impacket so it can be exposed through secretsdump (and through NetExec's `--ntds`) rather than as a standalone module. ## Testing Tested against a Windows Server 2022 (build 20348) Domain Controller in a domain with multiple trusts (incoming, outgoing, bidirectional, and a one-way external trust). Verified that the online (DRSUAPI) and offline (`-use-vss`) paths produce identical keys for every trust and direction, including the previous-password lines. Tested with NTLM and Kerberos (`-k`) authentication. ``` # online (DRSUAPI), NTLM secretsdump.py 'DOMAIN/user:password@dc' -just-dc-ntlm -trust-keys # offline, via a shadow copy of the live NTDS.dit secretsdump.py 'DOMAIN/user:password@dc' -just-dc-ntlm -use-vss -trust-keys # Kerberos auth secretsdump.py 'DOMAIN/user@dc' -k -just-dc-ntlm -trust-keys # only the trust keys, nothing else (online or with -use-vss) secretsdump.py 'DOMAIN/user:password@dc' -just-trust-keys ``` `-just-trust-keys` was verified to emit only the trust keys (zero account secrets) on both the online and the `-use-vss` paths, and the normal dump modes were confirmed unaffected. Privileges: an account with DS-Replication-Get-Changes rights (Domain Admin or equivalent), as for any DCSync. ## Notes - No new dependencies. - The inter-realm salt needs the local domain FQDN; secretsdump passes it automatically from the target you connect to. - A one-way trust only exposes one direction's `trustAuth*` attribute; the missing direction is skipped silently.

author: adam-dalloul
body:
## Summary

Adds a documented, runnable EmpirioLabs integration through Promptfoo's existing OpenAI-compatible chat, embedding, and transcription providers.

EmpirioLabs exposes OpenAI-compatible APIs, so the original dedicated wrapper was removed in favor of the generic provider path. This avoids a second, less-complete implementation while keeping the integration aligned with Promptfoo's existing request, credential, billing, and modality behavior.

## Final implementation

- Add EmpirioLabs documentation and a runnable `provider-empiriolabs` chat example.
- Document embeddings through `openai:embedding:*` and transcription through `openai:transcription:*`, including the literal audio-path contract and the five-minute synchronous limit.
- Make explicit `apiHost`/`apiBaseUrl` settings take precedence over ambient OpenAI endpoint variables.
- Isolate custom `apiKeyEnvar` credentials from `OPENAI_API_KEY` and suppress OpenAI-specific organization headers on third-party providers while preserving explicitly configured generic proxies.
- Preserve LiteLLM's documented `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback, prefer `LITELLM_API_KEY`, and propagate both context-level and provider-level key overrides.
- Support explicit `cost`, `inputCost`, and `outputCost` for compatible model IDs outside Promptfoo's built-in tables.
- Keep custom chat pricing fail-closed for incomplete or multimodal usage, support explicit zero-token sides, and price standard input-only embedding usage.
- Reject negative, non-finite, incomplete, or overflowed custom cost calculations.

## Simplifications

- Remove the duplicate `empiriolabs:` provider wrapper, schema additions, and static pricing table.
- Remove redundant Fireworks URL-resolution overrides now that the generic resolver honors explicit provider configuration first.
- Keep the runnable chat example single-purpose and move the complete transcription workflow to the provider documentation.

## Compatibility

- No new provider prefix, dependency, or required configuration is introduced.
- Existing OpenAI defaults remain unchanged when no custom endpoint or key variable is configured.
- Explicit custom endpoints and key variables now remain isolated from ambient OpenAI settings by design.
- OpenAI organization headers still work for the official endpoint, environment-selected OpenAI proxies, and explicitly configured generic compatible endpoints; provider subclasses can continue to veto them.
- LiteLLM's prior OpenAI-key fallback remains supported across chat, completion, and embedding providers.
- Custom pricing remains opt-in; built-in OpenAI model/tier/modal pricing is unchanged.

## Verification

- Final exact head: `8c1191e97918e4e9bcfb17704bfcce8c1d6aeb41`.
- Final focused provider verification: 7 files, 408 tests passed.
- Broader post-merge provider/example verification: 10 files, 2,150 tests passed.
- Formatting/lint hooks and `npm run architecture:check` passed.
- `SKIP_OG_GENERATION=true npm run build` passed in `site/`.
- Real CLI evals used `npm run local -- eval ... --no-cache` against a strict local OpenAI-compatible server and inspected exported JSON artifacts:
  - checked-in-equivalent two-model chat example: 2/2 passed;
  - chat plus embedding similarity: passed with custom chat cost `0.000028`;
  - multipart transcription: passed;
  - zero-input and zero-output pricing: both passed with cost `0.000014`;
  - LiteLLM OpenAI-key fallback and environment-selected OpenAI proxy organization: passed;
  - missing/total-only usage, modal usage, and a non-finite rate remained unpriced;
  - invalid credentials returned HTTP 401, a missing custom key failed before network access, and a missing audio file produced the expected result error.
- A real `OpenAiEmbeddingProvider` call using standard input-only usage returned cost `1.4e-7`; direct LiteLLM factory checks covered context keys and provider-over-context precedence.

## Remaining risks

- No paid EmpirioLabs credential was available, so wire behavior was validated with strict local mocks and the official [model](https://docs.empiriolabs.ai/models/deepseek-v4-flash), [embedding](https://docs.empiriolabs.ai/models/text-embedding-v4), and [transcription](https://docs.empiriolabs.ai/api-reference/api-reference/transcription/create-transcription) contracts rather than a production request.
- EmpirioLabs model availability and pricing can change; users should verify the live catalog.
- Files longer than five minutes use EmpirioLabs' asynchronous transcription flow, which Promptfoo does not currently poll. Per-minute transcription cost is not surfaced for these model IDs.

body:
## What

Adds `.github/workflows/deploy-dashboard.yml` so the dashboard publishes on merge instead of only via a local `deploy_pages.sh` run.

- **PR touching `viz/**`** → Cloudflare **preview** deploy (`--branch pr-<N>`)
- **Push to `main` touching `viz/**`** → **production** deploy to cpc.sahilashar.com
- **Actions → Run workflow** → manual production deploy

It wraps the existing `viz/deploy_pages.sh` wrangler direct-upload, so the `cpc-dashboard` project and the custom domain are reused unchanged.

## Inert until you opt in

A gate step skips the deploy when `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is unset and the run goes **green** — wiring this in does **not** start red-X'ing every push. Publishing stays manual until you add the secret.

To turn it on (one-time, your action — I never handle the token):
1. **Rotate** the Cloudflare token (it was leaked in transcript earlier).
2. Repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → add `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (scoped Pages:Edit + Zone DNS:Edit/Zone:Read).

From then on, merge-to-main auto-deploys. This deliberately reverses the prior "no GitHub secret" stance noted in CLAUDE.md.

## Notes / not in scope
- `build_visualizer.py` is stdlib-only; CI just needs Python + the preinstalled Node for `npx wrangler`.
- Data-refresh automation (Path B: scheduled eval runs → new `latest.json`) is still separate and not addressed here.

author: pablof7z
body:
## Summary

- New `ApprovedPeerStore` in Rust owns the approve/block allow-list (JSON-persisted, survives restarts)
- Trust predicate `(followed || approved) && !blocked` is enforced at both reception (responder gate) and projection (`trusted` flag on `NostrConversationDTO` / `AgentNoteSummary`)
- iOS wired end-to-end: four `KernelModel` dispatch shims → `podcast.social` host-op → kernel mutation → domain bump → reactive push; dead `NostrPendingApproval` / `NostrApprovalPresenter` scaffolding deleted

## Overview

### Rust (`nmp-app-podcast`)

**`store/approved_peer_store.rs`** (new) — `ApprovedPeerStore` with `approved: BTreeSet<String>` and `blocked: BTreeSet<String>`. JSON persistence with atomic tmp+rename write, D6 empty-on-missing load. `approve` clears any block; `block` clears any approval. Full inline test suite (round-trip, persist, corrupt-load, approve-clears-block, block-clears-approval, remove helpers, independent entries).

**`state/social.rs`** — `trust_predicate()` returns a closure implementing `(followed || approved) && !blocked`. Block is an absolute override — even a followed peer who is explicitly blocked is untrusted. Four mutation helpers (`approve_peer`, `block_peer`, `remove_peer_approval`, `remove_peer_block`). Both `agent_notes_snapshot` and `nostr_conversations_snapshot` switch to the composed predicate. Truth-table tests cover all seven predicate combinations.

**`ffi/actions/social_module.rs`** — four new `SocialAction` variants: `ApprovePeer { pubkey_hex }`, `BlockPeer`, `RemoveApproval`, `RemoveBlock`.

**`host_op_handler/social_actions.rs`** — match arms for all four variants: mutate `state.social` → `persist_approved_peer_store()` (atomic write) → `state.social.infra.bump()` (real Domain::Social re-emit path, lesson from #423) → `{"ok":true}`.

**`ffi/handle.rs`** — `approved_peer_store: Arc<Mutex<ApprovedPeerStore>>` added to `PodcastHandle`.

**`ffi/register.rs`** — construction and wiring of `approved_peer_store`; passed to `SocialState::with_approved_peers()` and `AgentNotesObserver::with_responder()`.

**`ffi/data_dir.rs`** — cold-load from `approved-peers.json` on startup, seeding both the `PodcastHandle` arc and `state.social`'s approved mirror.

**`agent_note_handler.rs`** — responder trust gate updated to composed predicate: `!blocked && (followed || approved)`.

**Five test-file `PodcastHandle` constructors** updated to include the new field.

### iOS (Swift)

**`App/Sources/Bridge/KernelModel+Social.swift`** (new) — four `KernelModel` dispatch shims routing to `podcast.social` namespace: `approvePeer(hex:)`, `blockPeer(hex:)`, `removePeerApproval(hex:)`, `removePeerBlock(hex:)`. Swift never re-implements the trust predicate.

**`AppStateStore+Nostr.swift`** — four access-control methods now dispatch through kernel for durable writes; local `nostrAllowedPubkeys` / `nostrBlockedPubkeys` sets retained as optimistic display mirrors. All `nostrPendingApprovals` management removed.

**`AppStateStore+Friends.swift`** — `addFriend` dispatches `approvePeer`; `removeFriend` dispatches `removePeerApproval`.

**`AppState.swift`** — `nostrPendingApprovals` field, CodingKey, and decoder line deleted. Optimistic-mirror comment added to allowed/blocked sets.

**`NostrPendingApproval.swift`** DELETED.

**`NostrApprovalPresenter.swift`** DELETED (auto-presenting trust sheet, now kernel-gated).

**`RootView.swift`** — `.nostrApprovalPresenter()` call removed.

**`AgentAccessControlView.swift`** — pending tab removed; two-tab view (Allowed / Blocked) routes through kernel-backed store methods.

**`AgentWhitelistRows.swift`** — `PendingApprovalRow` (depends on deleted type) removed.

**`AgentSettingsView.swift`, `SettingsView.swift`** — `pendingNostrApprovals.count` badge expressions removed.

**`whats-new.json`** — user-facing entry: "Agent access control now persists reliably."

## Validation

- `cargo test -p nmp-app-podcast` — **1291 passed, 0 failed**
- `xcodebuild build-for-testing -scheme Podcastr` — **zero Swift errors** (linker-only failure: Rust dylib not built for simulator in this worktree, expected)
- `git diff --check` — clean (no whitespace errors)
- `git grep` for all deleted symbol names — only comments remain, no live code

## Subjective decisions / tradeoffs

- **No pending-queue concept.** The original scaffolding auto-presented a "trust this person?" sheet. That UX is removed in favour of an explicit allow-list (`AgentAccessControlView`). Unknown senders are simply untrusted (kernel-gated) until the user adds them. This is simpler and avoids race conditions between the auto-presenter and kernel state.
- **Optimistic mirror retained.** `nostrAllowedPubkeys` / `nostrBlockedPubkeys` on `AppState` are kept as an optimistic display mirror for immediate UI feedback. The kernel's authoritative state arrives on the next `podcast.social` push; the mirror never diverges for more than one push cycle.
- **`addFriend` also approves.** Adding a friend through the Friends UI now also writes to the kernel allow-list, so friends are trusted by the agent without a separate approval step. This maintains the pre-existing behaviour (friends were auto-inserted into `nostrAllowedPubkeys`) through the new code path.

## Follow-ups (captured in BACKLOG.md)

- Bridge-decode fixture test: Rust-emitted JSON → Swift `NostrConversationDTO` decode, asserting `trusted:true` after `approve_peer` action
- Android access-control UI (no Kotlin changes in this PR)
- Re-emit test: dispatch `ApprovePeer` through `handle_social_action`, assert `build_social_payload` re-emits with `trusted` flipped

author: jeremyromerocarazo
body: # Pull Request ## Description Implements the `POST /jobs` endpoint for creating a new job of type `fixed` (fixed schedule with date, start time, and end time). Adds full request validation, error handling, and database schema synchronization via an initial migration. --- ## Related Issue Closes #IssueNumber --- ## Changes Included ### Backend Changes - [x] Added new endpoint(s) - [x] Added/updated DTOs - [x] Added/updated services - [ ] Added/updated repositories - [x] Added/updated database migrations - [x] Added validations - [x] Added exception handling - [ ] Other: ### Frontend / Mobile Changes - [ ] Added new screen(s) - [ ] Added ViewModel(s) - [ ] Added navigation - [ ] Added API integration - [ ] Added loading/error states - [ ] Added validation - [ ] Updated UI components - [ ] Other: --- ## Architecture Client → `JobsController` → `JobService` → `JobMapper` → `JobRepository` → `AppDbContext` → SQL Server --- ## API / Database Changes ### Endpoint - **`POST /jobs`** — Creates a new fixed-type job. ### Request Body (`CreateJobRequest`) - Required: `title`, `type` (must be `"fixed"`), `payment`, `companyId`, `date`, `startTime`, `endTime`, `paymentType` - Optional: `description`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `deliverables`, `skillsRequired` - `paymentType` accepts only `one_time` or `monthly` ### Validations Added (in `JobService.CreateJobAsync`) - `title` required - `companyId` required and must be a valid GUID - `payment` must be greater than 0 - `paymentType` must be `one_time` or `monthly` - `type` must be `fixed` - `date` required and must be a valid date - `startTime` / `endTime` required and must be valid times - `startTime` must be before `endTime` - Job date/time must be in the future - All validation errors are aggregated and returned in a single `400 Bad Request` ### Responses - `201 Created` — Job created successfully, returns `JobResponse` - `400 Bad Request` — Invalid job data (validation errors) ### Database - Generated and applied `InitialCreate` migration to synchronize the `jobs` table schema with the `Job` entity (columns: `IdCompany`, `WorkDate`, `StartTime`, `EndTime`, `StartDate`, `EndDate`, `PaymentType`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`, etc.) - `jobs.IdCompany` is a foreign key to `users.Id` (must reference an existing, active company user) --- ## Testing Performed - [x] Feature tested manually - [ ] Navigation tested - [x] Error handling tested - [x] Validation tested - [x] Backend integration tested - [x] No crashes detected ### Test Details - Tested `POST /jobs` with a valid payload and a valid existing `companyId` → returned `201 Created` with the expected `JobResponse`. - Tested with missing required fields (`title`, `companyId`, `date`, `startTime`, `endTime`) → returned `400 Bad Request` with aggregated error messages. - Tested with invalid `paymentType` (e.g. `"weekly"`) → returned `400 Bad Request`. - Tested with `startTime >= endTime` → returned `400 Bad Request`. - Tested with a job date/time in the past → returned `400 Bad Request`. - Tested with a non-existent `companyId` → triggered a foreign key constraint error (`FK_jobs_users_IdCompany`); confirmed this is expected behavior when the referenced company user does not exist. --- ## Evidence ### Screenshots / Videos --- --- ## Notes - The `Type` field is currently hardcoded to `"fixed"` in `JobMapper.ToEntity`, since this endpoint is scoped to fixed-schedule jobs only. Support for other job types (e.g. flexible/range-based) would require additional branching logic in `JobService`.

author: danielpballer
body:
Full UI/UX redesign per `design-brief.md` — a refined retro "Steel City WPA" aesthetic (night-shift-at-the-mill: warm iron grounds, poster-paper text, furnace gold for achievement). Built in 7 staged commits + refinements so any stage can be reverted independently.

## Stages
1. **Design tokens** — full iron/plate/paper/gold/rust/river/steel palette (WCAG AA verified), type scale, spacing/radii/motion; self-hosted **Oswald + Public Sans** (OFL, no CDN).
2. **Core chrome** — header, bottom nav, buttons, sheets/modals, toast, loading; **inline SVG icon sprite replaces all emoji**.
3. **Map layer** — framed-panel treatment, teardrop **patch pins** (lit gold / unlit), repaletted clusters, dark-chrome controls, redrawn check-in celebration. *(See map note below.)*
4. **Info cards** — bridge detail sheet with per-type **silhouette icons** (truss/arch/suspension/…), fun-fact rail, lit/unlit status.
5. **Badges** — the signature stage: collectible **patch medallions** (earned = lit gold, unearned = ghosted steel), monogram river badges, orchestrated unlock reveal.
6. **Share card** — Canvas regenerated in the new language (Oswald drawn in, bridge mark, three-rivers motif, flat fills).
7. **Empty/edge states + offline banner + SW fix** — invitational empty states, offline banner, About modal de-emoji'd, and **service worker switched to network-first for the app shell** (fixes stale JS/CSS surviving deploys).

## Verification
Each stage verified in-browser (Playwright screenshots): all flows — map, GPS check-in, info cards, badges, clustering, share card, export/import — work identically. 0 console errors throughout. 44px touch targets, safe-area insets, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected (Capacitor/iOS-bound).

## Open follow-ups (not blockers)
- **Tile licensing before paid release:** currently standard OSM tiles (for the black bridge casings, useful during dataset QA). OSM's policy forbids app use — swap to a licensed provider (Stadia/MapTiler/Thunderforest) that also renders casings, or CARTO w/ an account, before App Store release.
- **On-device map/filter tuning** for bright sunlight.

## Merge
Please **"Create a merge commit"** (not squash) to preserve the per-stage commits for independent rollback. `v0.1` tag marks the pre-redesign state.

body: Closes #35. ## Summary A minimal, fully in-app first-run onboarding wizard (styled to match the app / Cursor-like flow). Shown **once** via `userData/onboarding.json`; afterward a slim banner appears only if a hard blocker (no CLI / not signed in) or an app update exists. Flow: **Welcome → System check → Install CLI (skipped if present) → Sign in → Preferences → Done.** ## What it does - **Detects the machine** (sidecar `Environment.ts`): OS/arch, Node, droid CLI + version, package managers (brew/npm/curl/pnpm), editors, and auth (`~/.factory/auth.v2.file` + API key). - **One-click CLI install** (`CliInstaller.ts`): official script (`curl … | sh`), Homebrew (`brew install --cask droid`), or npm (`@factory/cli`), auto-detected, with streamed output. - **Sign in** via `droid login` (opens the browser) or API-key paste (safeStorage). Sidecar re-polls so the UI flips to signed-in automatically. - **Preferences**: default IDE from detected editors, CLI auto-update + app auto-update toggles; existing `~/.factory` settings imported automatically. - **Auto-updates**: silent CLI update on launch (`droid update`); app self-update via Electron autoUpdater (when a feed is configured) or a per-arch managed `.dmg` download, which relaunches the app. - **Settings**: new "Setup & updates" section (CLI status/update, sign-in, app version/update, toggles, "Run setup again"). ## Fresh-machine behavior On a clean PC the System check flags the missing CLI, the Install step appears and installs it, then `droid login` runs; the summary only turns green once each prerequisite is satisfied. ## Backend Protocol + `MissionManager` gain `env.detect`/`env.report`, `cli.install`/`cli.update` (streamed `cli.install.progress`/`done`); Electron main adds onboarding-flag, env, app-update, and open-external IPC. ## Testing - New unit tests: semver compare, channel selection, command building, onboarding gating. - `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run sidecar:typecheck`, `npm run sidecar:test`, `npm run electron:check`, and `npm run build` all pass. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a complete first-run onboarding (CLI install, sign-in, IDE setup) plus safe app/CLI auto-updates with a sidebar Update pill. Improves Windows CLI spawning and CLI probes, boosts auto-update reliability and feed handling, and tightens update security; aligns with #35. - **New Features** - In‑app wizard: Welcome → System check → Install CLI → Sign in → Preferences → Done; Install step has Re‑scan/Back/Skip so an empty manager list can’t trap users, and it auto‑advances if the step disappears mid‑flow. - Environment detection + runtime: OS/arch, Node, `droid` + version, package managers, editors, auth; checks executability; shared CLI resolver used by detection and runtime resolves PATH hits and routes Windows `.cmd` shims via `cmd.exe`; version and model‑catalog probes also wrap Windows shims; shell‑script channel omitted on Windows; Homebrew cask channel shown only on macOS. - One‑click CLI install via official script, Homebrew cask `droid`, or npm `@factory/cli` with streamed logs; script downloads to a temp file and aborts on failed `curl`; Windows spawns through a shell for `.cmd` shims; chosen channel is remembered; silent CLI auto‑update runs after env detection. - Sign‑in via `droid login` (browser) or API key; disabled until a runnable CLI is present; login spawn is guarded and runs through a shell on Windows; UI auto‑refreshes when auth completes and re‑detects once after a restored API key. - Preferences: pick a default editor (seeded from the saved preference), and toggles for CLI and app auto‑updates; existing `~/.factory` settings are imported. - Settings: new “Setup & updates” pane (CLI status/update, sign‑in, app version/update, toggles, “Run setup again”). - App updates: uses Electron autoUpdater when `DROID_UPDATE_FEED` is set (awaits feed outcome and relaunches; also checks the feed on launch even if the managed manifest is stale/absent, and reports “up‑to‑date” when nothing new), else downloads the manifest‑selected per‑arch `.dmg`; enforces HTTPS and an allowlisted host (download base, feed host, or `DROID_UPDATE_HOSTS`); auto‑download starts on launch when enabled; guarded so failures don’t crash; `shell.openPath` failures are treated as errors; “Couldn't check for updates” shown when manifest fetch fails; shared app‑update store powers a title‑bar “Update” pill and Settings; non‑http(s) links are refused. - Onboarding state: writes are serialized so rapid preference toggles can’t clobber each other. - **Migration** - Optional env vars: `DROID_UPDATE_FEED` (autoUpdater feed), `DROID_DOWNLOAD_BASE` (host for managed downloads), `DROID_UPDATE_HOSTS` (comma‑separated extra trusted hosts for updates). - Onboarding state stored at `userData/onboarding.json`; reopen via Settings → “Run setup again”. Written for commit 1727bd63b6260f314f20ec77d8ea005784993169. Summary will update on new commits.

author: kennethsinder
body:
Closes #3280.

## What

`pick_complementary_reviewer` already returned `fallback: bool` + a human-readable `fallback_reason`, but a caller could not branch deterministically on *why* the selector degraded to self-review without parsing prose. This adds a stable, machine-readable `fallback_code`:

- `unknown_author_family` — author family unresolved
- `no_diff_family_within_price` — a peer exists but exceeds `max_price_multiplier`
- `no_diff_family_serverless` — no active serverless cross-family peer cataloged
- `all_diff_family_excluded` — peers exist but were all excluded

It is `None`/absent on the success path. Surfaced through the serde-derived `llm_complementary_reviewer` builtin (no builtin-signature change) and documented in `catalog.harn`'s `complementary_reviewer`.

## Why

Lets a downstream private host that routes a second, independent reviewer model assert **structural independence** (reviewer family != author family) and hard-fail / disable a degraded review step, rather than silently degrading to self-review when the local catalog has no priced cross-family peer.

## Tests

- success path → `fallback_code == None`
- price-cap fallback → `no_diff_family_within_price`
- `ReviewerFallbackCode::as_code()` strings are append-only stable contract

`cargo test -p harn-vm --lib reviewer` (3 pass), `cargo clippy -p harn-vm` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean, builtin-registry-alignment unaffected.

> Draft until #1537 and #1538 (the SEO frontmatter gate) merge — this post depends on the title/description frontmatter those PRs enforce.

## What

A new blog post, `docs/pages/blog/posts/wildcard-class-patterns.md`, walking through wildcard class patterns in the inventory `classes:` list (the feature from #1457). It covers the before/after on a real target file, how to turn the feature on, what the glob patterns mean, the ordering and dedup rules, and a short note on how the temporary-materialization approach keeps every backend wildcard-unaware.

## Why

Long, hand-maintained `classes:` lists are a recurring pain in big inventories — add a class and you have to remember every target that should pick it up. The feature shipped, but it was opt-in and easy to miss. I wanted a practical post that shows people the flag exists and exactly when to reach for it (and when not to).

## Approach

I grounded every claim in the actual implementation rather than the PR summary, since the two drifted slightly on pattern semantics:

- `kapitan/inventory/wildcards.py` for the real matching rule (full dotted name via `fnmatch`, exact-match precedence, `${...}` pass-through, lexicographic sort, dedup, unmatched-pattern error, temp-tree materialization, symlink rewriting).
- `kapitan/cli.py` for the exact flag (`--enable-class-wildcards`) and its `.kapitan` key (`enable-class-wildcards` under `[inventory_backend]`), confirming it applies to both `compile` and `inventory`.
- The "Wildcard class patterns" section of `docs/pages/inventory/classes.md` for the opt-in rationale and the numeric-prefix ordering tip.

Voice follows the existing blog posts: first person, opinionated, concrete commands and YAML, no marketing filler.

## Verification

- Frontmatter parses as YAML; title is 50 chars and description is 126 chars, both inside the SEO gate's ranges.
- `<!-- more -->` separator sits right after the intro for the mkdocs blog plugin.

- Did not run pytest or build the docs, per the task scope.

author: mabry1985
body:
## What

The **second P1 concurrency-correctness port**. A long-running loop accumulates two kinds of cruft nothing reclaimed: features stuck `in_progress` after a drive died without finishing (holding a board slot forever), and `feat-<id>` worktrees left behind by a missed reap. A periodic sweep (`health_sweep_interval_s`, default **300s**; `0` disables) self-heals both:

- **stale `in_progress`** (not in `self._inflight_files` → no live drive) → reconciled the *same way boot recovery does* (adopt an open PR → `in_review`, else reset → `ready`). Boot recovery and the sweep now share `_reconcile_orphan`.
- **orphaned worktrees** — a `feat-<id>` dir whose feature is gone or already `done` → reaped. (`in_review` keeps its worktree for a CI-fail re-dispatch; a live drive's worktree is left alone.)

`worktree.list_feature_worktrees` enumerates the `feat-<id>` dirs under `worktrees_root`.

## Tests

**+6 (110 total), all green:** `list_feature_worktrees` (dirs only / absent dir); `_sweep` reconciles a driveless `in_progress` (and skips a driven one) and reaps `done`/missing worktrees (keeps `in_review`); `_maybe_sweep` rate-limit + disabled. `ruff` clean.

## P1 batch

- ✅ hot-file guard + review WIP (#10)
- ✅ periodic health sweep (this)
- ⏳ foundation merge-gate (review-vs-done)

author: com-junkawasaki
body:
## Problem
Every Python→Clojure tier port appended its test namespaces to ONE shared hand-maintained list in bb.edn (`test:stubs` + `test:pywasm`). Every feature branch edited the same region → guaranteed merge conflicts on sequential merge (observed across #1718–#1721, each needing a bb.edn union-rebase). Answer to 'can't bb.edn be file-separated?' — better: auto-discovery, so bb.edn stops changing at all.

## Fix
New `etzhayyim.tools.discovery/actor-test-nss` globs `20-actors` + `70-tools` for `test_*.clj(c)`, strips the longest classpath-root prefix, returns the sorted ns set, EXCLUDING:
- `mimamori.` / `yobel.` / `ibuki.` — owned by their dedicated bb tasks
- `etzhayyim.tools.*` — owned by `test:tools`
- any **hyphen-dir** path — SCI ns↔path munge can't load them (e.g. `kuni-umi`)

`bb.edn` is now **static**: drop a `test_*.cljc` and it is picked up — **zero bb.edn churn**, the merge-conflict class is eliminated for all future tier ports.

## Safety
- Verified discovered set **== prior test:stubs∪test:pywasm set exactly** (103 nss, zero diff both directions) before deleting the hand-lists.
- `test:actors` = **978 tests / 16878 assertions green** on current main (all merged tiers).
- `test:clj` :depends rewired to `[mimamori yobel tools ibuki actors]` (drops deleted test:stubs/test:pywasm).
- bb-task gotcha handled: project-ns fns can't resolve at task *analysis* time, so the task uses `(requiring-resolve …)` for runtime resolution.

> Land this AFTER #1719/#1721 merge — it replaces the same bb.edn block, so it conflict-resolves them to moot (their test files auto-discover). Once merged, future tier ports touch zero bb.edn.

author: kasianov-mikhail
body:
The `Server` workflow added in #571 could report a green run without testing anything: the contract suite is skipped unless `SCOUT_SERVER_URL` reaches the test process, so a broken environment hand-off — or an `-only-testing` identifier that matches nothing — would skip every test while `xcodebuild` still exits zero. The workflow now captures a result bundle and fails when no test actually ran, falling back to a warning only if the result-bundle schema turns out to be unreadable so it never blocks CI spuriously.

Alongside that it gains a `push` trigger on `main` so the merged state is contract-checked rather than only PR heads, widens its path filter to `Core/Database/Record` where the `RecordChunk` and `RecordCursor` pagination types that travel over the wire live, fails fast with a clear message when PostgreSQL never becomes ready instead of dying later on an opaque `psql` error, and documents that an API key must be passed as `TEST_RUNNER_SCOUT_SERVER_API_KEY` because `xcodebuild` forwards only prefixed variables into the test process.

`ServerContractTests` now writes a `params` bytes field and asserts it round trips, exercising the `bytes` wire coding that previously only unit tests covered even though real `Event` records carry `params` as bytes. The pagination loop is bounded so a server that never stops handing back a cursor fails an assertion rather than hanging until the job timeout, and the thrice-repeated `param_count` extraction is folded into a `paramCounts(in:)` helper.

author: eumemic
body:
## Summary

- **Bug:** `read_windowed_events` could return an **empty event list paired with a non-None `WindowOmission`**. `build_messages` relies on the inverse invariant — it reads `events[0].created_at` to anchor the omission marker — so it raised `IndexError`. Because `build_messages` is pure replay over the immutable window, the crash recurred on **every wake and permanently wedged the session**.
- **Root cause:** `select_window` guarantees a non-empty tail because it requires `min_tokens >= 1`. `read_windowed_events` loses that floor: when per-step overhead (system prompt + tool schemas) exceeds `window_min`, `events_window_min` clamps to **0**, the chunked snap drops in full-window chunks, and the asymmetric `ceil(drop_effective / ratio)` back-conversion can push `drop` up to `total`. The retained scan (`cumulative_tokens > drop`) then matches **zero** rows while the omission complement (`<= drop`) matches **every** row.
- **Reachability:** `window_min` / `window_max` are `Field(ge=1)` with no cross-validation, so a small-window agent is creatable, and overhead easily exceeds a small `window_min`.
- **Fix:** `drop = min(drop, total - 1)` so the most recent event (whose `cumulative_tokens == total`) always survives — restoring `select_window`'s retain-the-tail invariant and the producer→consumer contract that `omission != None` ⟹ non-empty window.

## Why this altitude

Fixed at the **producer**, not by guarding `events[0]` in `build_messages`: a consumer guard would silently return a **broken (empty) context** — the model called with only the system prompt, unable to see the user's latest message — trading a loud crash for a silent failure. The producer fix keeps the latest turn and the omission marker (graceful, visible degradation), matching how `select_window` retains an oversized tail.

## Verification

- Failing test written first (`test_overhead_clamp_never_drops_entire_window`), confirmed red: `drop_local=534 >= total=534`.
- The clamp is provably a **no-op in every healthy regime** (`drop <= total - 2` there); existing windowing tests' drop assertions (1000 / 667 / 7300) are unchanged.
- Adversarial review attacked 5 vectors (off-by-one/still-empty, prefix-cache/monotonicity regression, fires-when-it-shouldn't, omission-complement consistency, `remaining_effective <= window_max`) — none reproduced.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_overhead_clamp_never_drops_entire_window` (red→green)
- [x] windowing + window + context suites (178 passed); full unit suite 2607 passed
- [x] mypy clean · ruff check + format clean
- [ ] CI runs e2e / integration suites

body:
Fourth messaging slice per `docs/prd-messaging.md` §5 (M-4 ONLY — M-5+ not rolled in). Server-side; app screens are M-5. Built on merged M-1/M-2/M-3.

## 🧭 Storage pre-flight (the decision to confirm — D-#102)
Per AGENTS rule 3 (live repo wins over the PRD), I **reversed the PRD §9 proposal**:

- **PRD §9 proposed Oracle-VM-disk storage** for chat attachments, *because Atlas/GridFS can't hold 10 MB video*.
- **GP-A (D-#70/#71) already shipped a live binary store** — `DriveStore` (Google Drive on the school's own My-Drive quota) + `StoredFile` metadata + a server-streamed `/files` transport. Drive holds video fine, so the §9 reason is moot.
- **Decision: REUSE the Drive store; do NOT build the VM-disk path or a twin `Attachment` model.** I generalized the two existing primitives instead:
  - `DriveStore` — a `subfolder` param (`SCD-Hub-Files/<year>/chat/`), default `hw` (backward-compatible).
  - `StoredFile` — four `chat_*` kinds added to the `hw_*` enum + an optional `conversationId`.
  - The existing `GET /files/:id` server-streamed transport (the server-internal Drive id never reaches a client).

This is the "do NOT build a twin upload/transport" instruction taken literally. If you'd rather have a dedicated `Attachment` model or VM-disk, say so and I'll re-slice.

## What's in M-4
- **Upload** — `POST /files/chat` (multipart, gated `chat:write` + `assertChatMember(conversationId)`); MIME whitelist per `ATTACHMENT_KINDS` (image jpeg/png/gif/webp · pdf · video mp4/webm/quicktime · audio mpeg/mp4/aac/ogg/wav/webm) + a **10 MB** (10,485,760-byte) hard cap; Bangla 422; **Drive-first** (a Drive failure ⇒ 503 + nothing persisted, GP-J8 posture). (J-M6)
- **Read gate** — `ChatFileService.assertChatFileReadAccess`: the caller must be a member of SOME conversation holding a **LIVE (non-deleted) message** referencing the file. So a **deleted message's attachment becomes inaccessible** (the M-4 acceptance) while its refs stay in the `MESSAGE_DELETED` audit. `GET /files/:id` **dispatches the gate by the file's OWN kind** (hw → HomeworkFile, chat → ChatFile) so neither plane can re-expose the other's files.
- **Send binding** — `sendMessage` gains `attachmentIds`; `resolveSendAttachments` admits an id ONLY if it is a CHAT `StoredFile` the **sender** uploaded **for this conversation** (blocks attaching another user's file or a file from another conversation/module). **Attachment-only messages** (no body) are now allowed. `ChatMessage` GraphQL gains an `attachments` field (batched per page).

## Vocab-free, as instructed
`shared/vocab.ts`, the schema, and the verifier are **untouched** (verifier still PASS). One new audit kind `CHAT_ATTACHMENT_UPLOADED` lives in `platform/models/Audit.ts`. (`ATTACHMENT_KINDS` already existed in vocab since M-1 — I only *read* it.)

## Executed gate (base was jest 684/684 on main)
- vocab verifier **PASS** (untouched)
- `npm run build --workspace=shared` + shared/server `tsc --noEmit` clean
- **jest 710/710** (43 suites; 26 new in `chatAttachments.test.ts`; firewall green; the `homeworkFiles` `StoredFile` mock was extended for the generalized kinds — note for review)
- app `tsc --noEmit` clean + `expo export --platform web` green

Not verified live (needs the Drive credential D-#70/#71 + DEP-3). **Next = M-5** (app screens).

author: randallanjie
body: Two issues hitting moments.randallanjie.com: 1. /api/files/upload returns: {"success":false,"message":"上传文件失败: Fetch API cannot load: jSofCawJJqvx7rK8Li1Lfm.png","filename":""} Root cause: workerd's Service Binding RPC semantics treat every property access as an RPC method call. When the host plane hands us a raw Fetcher instead of an R2Bucket-shaped wrapper, `env.UPLOADS.put(key, data)` becomes `fetch(key)` — and `key` isn't a valid URL, so workerd throws "Fetch API cannot load: ". Real Cloudflare Pages binds UPLOADS as a proper R2Bucket so this never triggers there. Self-hosted edge planes that pass us a raw Fetcher + a sibling `_ID` text binding (the convention bigrandall.io uses) hit it on every upload. Fix: lib/r2-shim.ts adds a minimal R2Bucket-compatible class that wraps the raw Fetcher and proxies put/get/delete/list through `service.fetch('http://r2proxy/v1/objects//', ...)`. lib/cf-env.ts detects the raw-binding case (presence of `UPLOADS_ID`) and applies the wrap on the fly. Real Cloudflare Pages doesn't ship `UPLOADS_ID`, so the wrap is a no-op there — both deployment shapes keep working without conditional code at call sites. 2. Favicon still points to `/upload/.png` after avatar-style migration. layouts/default.vue feeds userinfo.favicon directly into the href, and pages/config.vue shows a raw preview. Both bypass the R2 rewrite. Route them through getImgUrl() like the rest of the uploaded-image surface so they hit the R2 public hostname directly instead of round-tripping through /upload/[filename] Worker route.

author: bunsdev
body:
## Problem
In a narrow bookmarks panel, distinct rows all rendered as an identical truncated **`DeepWi…`** + `deepwiki.com` — you couldn't tell four entries apart (see report screenshot).

## Root cause
The bookmarks table used `table-layout: fixed` with the **Title as the only width-less (leftover) column**. The Title is the row's identity but had the *lowest* width priority, so as the panel narrowed it was sacrificed first. And once the responsive rules hid Saved/Tags (≤520px), fixed-layout wouldn't let the Title re-claim that freed width — it collapsed to ~content-min while a repetitive **150px Domain** column held its space.

## Fix
- `.library-bookmarks-table` → **`table-layout: auto`** with the Title as a fluid `max-width:0; width:100%` clipping column, so it absorbs all leftover space and truncates *last* — at every width, including when columns are hidden.
- Domain cell now **ellipsizes** (`min-width:0` + overflow) and its column trimmed **150→112px** (only ever holds a short host); Tags **128→96px**.
- Base `table-layout: fixed` for other library tables and the responsive ladder are untouched.

## Validation (standalone CSS harness, real board.css+library.css, across shell widths)
| shell | Title width | cols | title collapses? |
|------:|------------:|-----:|:----------------:|
| 820 | 615px | 5 | no |
| 520 | 402px | 3 (domain shown, saved/tags hidden) | no |
| 440 | 414px | 2 (domain hidden) | no |
| 280 | 254px | 2 | no |

Title now gets **254–615px** and never collapses (was ~70–150px in the narrow band). Also measured in the live app: at shell 827 Title 429→**533px**.

`pnpm typecheck`, the library `*.test.ts` suite, and `pnpm build` all green.

body:
## Summary

- Persist each session created by `aco session start` to `~/.aco/sessions/<sessionId>.json` (sessionId, serverUrl, platform, pid, startedAt, deviceName, app). Unlinked on graceful teardown; left in place on crash so `session list --prune` can surface it.
- `--session`, `--server-url`, and `--platform` are now **optional** on all consumer subcommands. A new `resolveConnection()` layer consults the store when flags are omitted (latest live local session by default; explicit `--session <id>` looks up the matching record). Explicit flags always win, so existing CI / remote-grid scripts keep working unchanged.
- Add `aco session start --detach`: re-spawns the same `aco` binary in the background, relays the JSON envelope, and exits. Detached output is teed to `~/.aco/logs/aco-detach-<parent-pid>.log`. Guarded in dev mode (tsx) with a clear error.
- Add `aco session list` with `--json` (machine-readable annotated records) and `--prune` (delete records for dead servers or crashed pids). Liveness uses `process.kill(pid, 0)` for local-host records and an HTTP `GET /status` probe (2s timeout) for the row's overall `alive` column.
- Add `aco session stop` (`--session <id>` defaults to the latest live record, `--all` iterates all stored records). Calls `deleteSession` on the W3C server, SIGTERMs the recorded Appium child pid, then unlinks the record. Resilient to network errors.
- Documentation: README walkthrough rewritten around zero-arg defaults plus the new `--detach`/`list`/`stop` commands; CLAUDE.md "subcommands are stateless" paragraph rewritten as a "convenience layer for default resolution" caveat (explicit flags keep everything stateless).

You were right to question this — `includeHiddenNodes` is a real, working option in `@xyflow/system` (and RF/SF expose it), not a dead one to remove. It was just **silently broken** in vue-flow.

## The bug

`fitView` declares `includeHiddenNodes` in `FitViewParams` and even defaults it to `false`, but the `fitViewport(...)` call built its options object with `padding`/`duration`/`minZoom`/`maxZoom`/`nodes` and **omitted `includeHiddenNodes`** — so the user's value was dropped and hidden nodes were always excluded.

System's `getFitViewNodes` gates each node on `measured.width && measured.height && (options?.includeHiddenNodes || !n.hidden)`, so forwarding the flag makes hidden (but measured) nodes participate.

## The fix

Forward `includeHiddenNodes` into the `fitViewport` options. There's a system types-vs-runtime quirk worth noting: `fitViewport`'s options type is `Omit<…, 'nodes' | 'includeHiddenNodes'>`, yet at runtime it forwards `options` straight to `getFitViewNodes` which reads both. The existing `nodes` forwarding already works around this with a conditional **spread** (a direct property trips the excess-property check; a spread doesn't), so I used the same pattern for `includeHiddenNodes`.

## Verification

Guard added in `fitView.cy.ts`: a far-away hidden node (seeded with `measured` dims, since a truly hidden node has no DOM and is never measured) widens the fit — and thus lowers the zoom — only when `includeHiddenNodes: true`. Verified it **fails against the dropped-option behavior** (stash/rebuild) and passes with the fix. Full suite 149/149; `vue-tsc` clean.

author: copilot
body:
`train.js` had several runtime bugs and was missing test coverage. This PR fixes the bugs and adds a full unit test suite.

## Bugs fixed

- **`calculateTraining`** — `newStats[stats]` used the stats object as a key (typo for `stat`). The proxy's `train` method is now `(stat, amount = 1n) => trainStat(newStats, stat, amount)`, matching the pattern in `training.js`. Gold is now passed in as a starting value and accumulated correctly via `let newGold = gold`, returned alongside `stats` as `{gold, stats}`.
- **`determineSkillsUsed`** — missing guard for an empty enabled-skills list caused a crash on `skills[skills.length - 1]`. Added early `if(!skills.length) return []`.
- **`updatedFighter`** — `skillIDs.some(s.id)` passed a value instead of a predicate to `Array#some`; changed to `skillIDs.includes(s.id)`. Fired skills were filtered out of the regimen but never re-inserted with their updated `lastUsed` values; they are now added back (deduplicated via `Set` for skills that fired multiple times). Gold earned during training was silently dropped; it is now written back to `fighter.details.gold`.

## Style

- Removed double blank lines between function declarations.

## Tests (`train.test.js`)

10 new cases covering: empty regimen, no enabled skills, insufficient elapsed time, stamina training, vitality multiplier, gold accumulation, multi-skill round-robin cycling, `lastUsed` update in regimen, skill retention after firing, and disabled-skill preservation.

> Draft until #1537 and #1538 (the SEO frontmatter gate) merge — this post depends on the title/description frontmatter those PRs enforce.

## What

A new blog post, `docs/pages/blog/posts/sharing-generators-oci.md`, walking through publishing reusable Kapitan generators as OCI artifacts and consuming them as an `oci` dependency. It covers the full loop: package a bundle, `oras push` it to a registry, reference the image in inventory, and `kapitan compile --fetch`.

author: snds
body:
Adds a second baked **aux texture** (R cloud density, G ocean/specular mask) and composites clouds directly in the surface shader — no shell, no extra draw call ([docs §3](docs/planet-visual-realism.md)).

## Pipeline
- **Baker**: aux bake path renders data channels into a **linear** RT; Romulus aux = ocean mask (mirrors albedo elevation) + clouds (ITCZ band + mid-latitude systems). Material set to `NoBlending` (raw overwrite).
- **Two bugs found & fixed**: (1) alpha-0 data pass was alpha-composited into the cleared target → `NoBlending`; (2) the readback `<canvas>` backing store is **premultiplied**, so alpha-0 zeroed the RGB data — fixed by forcing alpha=1 (A is reserved). Clouds baked black until this was found.
- **Surface shader**: differential-rotation drift (pure phase shift of the bounded wall clock ⇒ **zero smearing at any warp**), sun-offset cloud shadow (cotangent frame from `dFdx/dFdy`, stretches toward the terminator), per-channel terminator scattering (**warm cloud limb**), and **ocean-masked specular** (sea-glint × ocean mask × (1−cloud) — land/clouds stop glinting).

## Verification (live)
- Romulus aux confirmed by texture scan: **cloud 13% / ocean 82%**.
- Day side renders as a blue marble with composited white cloud systems; warm terminator visible; **no console errors**; `TEXTURE_VERSION` 6→7; build + vitest 7/7.

**Deferred** (fold onto this aux pipeline next): emissive B channel (city lights / lava cracks) and gas-giant flow-map band rotation. (Headless FPS is rAF-throttled — not representative.)

body:
Fixes a node stuck "thinking 108s" on an idle bot. The canvas (`pipeline.js`) runs its own paced state machine and, unlike `Story.Reducer`, had no decay — so a thinking/waiting node never returned to idle (no engine turn-complete event exists to clear it) and the elapsed counter just grew forever.

The canvas now decays on its existing 1Hz timer: thinking → idle after 60s of silence, waiting after 300s. `lastAct` refreshes on every agent event (including a held-`since` ask), so a genuinely long turn with recent activity survives — only silence decays. Mirrors `Story.Reducer` so the canvas and the in-flight strip below it never disagree.

- [x] `node --check` + `mix assets.build`
- [x] browser-verified: thinking→idle on 60s silence, survives recent activity, a 200s-but-active turn stays thinking, zero console errors

author: vjpixel
body:
## Resumo

Lote de 4 fixes coesos em `workers/poll/src/index.ts`, todos no mesmo arquivo — sem deps externas.

### #2188 (P1, BUG) — backfill re-pontua `vote.correct===false`

O guard em `handleAdminCorrect` usava `vote.correct === null || vote.correct === undefined`, pulando entradas com `correct===false` ao corrigir o gabarito. Resultado: votos já-pontuados-como-errados ficavam permanentemente errados após correção do admin.

**Fix**: guard expandido para incluir `=== false` — re-pontua TODAS as entradas não-confirmadas-como-corretas contra o novo gabarito.

### #2189 (P2, BUG) — nickname form acessível no retry após "já votou"

Branch `existing` (voto já gravado) hardcodava `nicknameForm = null`. Se o request original commitou o voto mas falhou depois (500 na leitura do score), o retry caía no branch "já votou" sem o form — nickname form inacessível para sempre.

**Fix (abordagem escolhida)**: tornar o branch "já votou" capaz de servir o form. Lê `score:${email}` no branch e gera `nicknameForm` se o subscriber não tiver nickname.

### #2190 (P2, perf) — `score:${email}` lido no máximo 1x por request

A chave era lida na checagem de nickname (~linha 316), dentro de `updateScore` (~linha 518) e condicionalmente em `updateScoreByMonth` (~linha 420). **Fix**: leitura consolidada ANTES do `put(voteKey)` — aproveita o mesmo valor pré-commit para as 3 funções via parâmetro opcional `preloadedScoreRaw`. Callers do admin backfill (sem preloaded) fazem get normalmente, semântica preservada.

### #2191 (P3, cleanup) — `renderLeaderboardHtml` usa `htmlEscape()`

O replace inline `/[<>&"]/g` omitia `'` — nicknames com apóstrofe (ex: "D'Artagnan") apareciam crus no HTML da tabela do leaderboard. **Fix**: substituído por `htmlEscape()` de `lib.ts`, que cobre os 5 caracteres HTML especiais incluindo `'`.

---

## Testes

9 novos casos em `test/poll-hardening-2188-2189-2190-2191.test.ts`:

- **#2188**: 3 casos — voto `false` re-pontuado; `true` idempotente; cenário completo null+false+true
- **#2189**: 2 casos — retry sem nickname recebe form; retry com nickname não recebe form
- **#2190**: 1 caso — contagem de KV gets ≤1 para `score:{email}` no caminho feliz
- **#2191**: 3 casos — apóstrofe escapada como `'`; 5 chars cobertos; votePageHtml com email com apóstrofe

Todos os 195 testes do poll passam (worker-poll, poll-snapshot-2152-2129, poll-snapshot-2123, worker-poll-brand + 9 novos).

Closes #2188, closes #2189, closes #2190, closes #2191

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

## CI (LiteLLM team)

- [ ] **Branch creation CI run**
       Link:
- [ ] **CI run for the last commit**
       Link:
- [ ] **Merge / cherry-pick CI run**
       Links:

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The gate is deterministic, so the proof is the gate itself, run two ways. First, the codebase as-is passes the new ceiling:

```
$ uv run python scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py --base HEAD
OK: every strict rule is within its codebase ceiling (base HEAD)
```

The clean gate is untouched and still at zero, so `make lint-ruff` is unaffected:

```
$ cd litellm && uv run ruff check .
All checks passed!
```

And the ratchet update is idempotent against the committed baselines (no diff), confirming the budget matches the current tree:

```
$ uv run python scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py --update && git diff --stat ruff-strict-budget.json
Re-captured per-rule baselines from the current tree
(no change)
```

To see it actually catch a regression, add a single new banned-`Any` or a `UP006`-style legacy annotation on a fresh line, rerun `python scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py`, and the gate fails pointing at the new line.

## Type

🚄 Infrastructure

## Changes

This turns on ruff's preview rule set, but only in the budgeted strict lane, never in the clean gate.

Ruff has two lanes here: `ruff.toml` drives `make lint-ruff` (`ruff check .`) which must stay at zero, and `ruff-strict.toml` drives `scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py`, which counts violations against a `baseline + slack` ceiling in `ruff-strict-budget.json`. Preview belongs in the second lane because that is the only one with a grandfathering mechanism; flipping preview on in the clean gate would surface ~48k violations with no way to absorb them.

Enabling `preview = true` with non-explicit selection makes ruff pull in its broad preview catalog (415 rules enabled on this tree), which is both noisy and liable to shift on every ruff upgrade. Instead the config sets `explicit-preview-rules = true` and enumerates the exact 118 codes that fire today, so the gate is deterministic and a ruff bump never silently adds or drops a gated rule.

The 58438 existing violations across those 118 rules are grandfathered into `ruff-strict-budget.json` as per-rule baselines. The original ten rules keep their hand-tuned slack; each newly tracked rule gets slack 10 when its baseline is 50 or more and 3 otherwise, so there is a little headroom for churn while net-new violations still fail CI. Two pre-existing rules drifted up by one (`ANN401` 1885 -> 1886, `TID251` 2404 -> 2405) and are re-captured at their current counts.

No script or Makefile changes were needed; `ruff_strict_gate.py` already reads the rule set from `ruff-strict.toml` and the budget from the JSON, so `make lint-strict-budget` and `make lint-strict-budget-update` pick this up as-is.

author: richard-burhans
body:
## What

Two related artifacts, surfaced by the real-world featureCounts PR work:

**1. `version-suffix-shape` standing measure** (with synthetic-fixture tests). Per tool with a `version=` attribute, it classifies the attribute *shape* and, for the `@TOOL_VERSION@+galaxy@VERSION_SUFFIX@` two-token form, resolves whether both tokens are **imported from a macros file** vs **defined inline** (via tier-1 `token_definitions`).

Corpus result (combined, 9,373 unique tools; 8,903 with a `version=`):
- two-token form `@A@+galaxy@B@`: 2,248 (25.2%), of which 1,973 use the canonical names;
- of those, **73.9% import both tokens from a macros file** (20.1% inline, 5.9% mixed);
- most common shape overall is still literal-no-suffix (47.9%, the older ToolShed long tail).

So the "both tokens imported from `macros.xml`" hypothesis holds for tools that tokenize at all, which supports a single shared `@VERSION_SUFFIX@` token for a suite.

**2. `docs/iuc_conference_questions.md`** — a running list of policy questions to raise with IUC maintainers *in person*, each with our provisional behavior and the corpus data to bring. Seeded with three:
1. per-tool vs **suite-wide** version-suffix for a shared-macros suite (provisional: suite-wide; the measure above backs it);
2. blanket vs **behavior-preserving** text-parameter quoting (provisional: behavior-preserving);
3. whether `<param>` **attribute-order normalization** is actually wanted (provisional: keep it, per the documented standard).

This is groundwork for the upcoming `vg` PR (which needs the suite-wide suffix decision).

## Verification
- New tests for `version-suffix-shape` (classes + provenance + empty corpus).
- Full QA gate green; corpus measure run (numbers above).
- All docs are em-dash-free per project style.

author: doo-nothing
body:
A render whose output path's parent directory was missing failed silently: the tape writer's `WavWriter::create` returned an error that was swallowed, so the render only ever reported *"mixer never started recording — is the audio device available?"* and waited out its 30s boot deadline.

This made every render look like a dead/busy audio device when the real cause was a **missing `tmp/` directory** (it gets removed after gitignoring it and switching branches). Cost a long detour chasing a phantom CoreAudio problem.

## Fix
- `render()` now `create_dir_all`s the output path's parent directory up front (with context on failure)
- the mixer's `tape_writer` creates the parent and logs a forensics line instead of silently returning if `WavWriter::create` still fails

A missing directory can no longer be mistaken for an unavailable audio device. Verified: rendering to a missing nested path (`tmp/sub/probe.wav`) now creates the dirs and records.

author: stormer78
body:
## P1.3 — Keyspace-name registry

vta-service named its ~17 keyspaces with bare string literals across ~230 call sites (server, offline CLIs, backup, tests). That already produced a **live test-vs-production divergence**: tests opened keyspace `"imported"` while production writes `"imported_secrets"`, so the test `imported_ks` was an empty keyspace disjoint from what prod populates — masking any bug in that path.

### Change
- **New `crate::keyspaces` module** — one `const` per keyspace, the single source of truth. Every `.keyspace(..)` call (and the `contexts` test helper's `k(..)`) now names its keyspace through a const.
- **`"imported"` → `IMPORTED_SECRETS`** fixed at all three test sites.
- `operations::protocol::snapshot::KEYSPACE_NAME` re-points to `keyspaces::SNAPSHOT`.
- **Backup**: the registry partitions every keyspace into `BACKED_UP` (`{keys, acl, contexts, audit, imported_secrets, webvh}` — exactly what `export_backup` reads) vs `EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP` (with `did_templates` + `vault` flagged as **known gaps**, not silent drops). A guard test keeps the partition total, so a new keyspace can't be silently dropped from the backup decision.

### Acceptance
- ✅ **Zero bare keyspace string literals** outside the registry — enforced by the `no_bare_keyspace_literals` guard test (the "CI grep": scans `src/`, asserts no `.keyspace("literal")` outside `keyspaces.rs`).
- ✅ **Backup enumerates keyspaces from the registry** — `backup_partition_is_total` asserts `ALL == BACKED_UP ∪ EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP` (disjoint), forcing a backup classification when a keyspace is added.

### Deferred
Typed per-keyspace key-format constructors (`Key::Acl(did)`, `Key::PathCounter(base)`, …) — a separate, much larger surface. The P1.3 acceptance criteria are keyspace-scoped and met here; the key-format registry is a good follow-up.

### Verification
fmt + clippy clean (default & tee); vta-service lib **716** (default) / **749** (tee) + bin **45** + all integration suites green; vta-enclave checks. 66 files (mostly mechanical literal→const).

Phase 1 item P1.3 of the VTA architecture simplification plan.
