## E20-T2 — Settings tree

Builds the full Settings tree (FR-E20-4): **Workspace, Identity, Devices, Sync, Export (stub)**. ("Skill mappings" stays with the recommendation module, E17.) Completes the v0.1 trust surface alongside the Inbox.

### What's here
- **Web:** `routes/Settings.tsx` restructured into a five-node tree (Members / My Agent / Telemetry nested under Workspace / Identity), plus `routes/settings/{Workspace,Identity,Devices,Sync,Export}.tsx`.
  - **Workspace** — name + id.
  - **Identity** — member, role, token scopes, and capability grants (revocable via the existing grants path).
  - **Devices** — the workspace's verify-key trust roots, with a Maintainer+ **decommission** that cascade-revokes the device's grants. The runtime's **own active device is marked "this runtime" and cannot be decommissioned** (disabled in the UI, 409 on the server) — re-key is not a v0.1 flow and self-decommission would strand grant issuance.
  - **Sync** — configured backend + local event-log counts. **Read-only on purpose:** push/pull is unwired until the next sprint, so there is no "sync now" action rather than a button that no-ops.
  - **Export** — a disabled stub for the future portable export.
- **Runtime (read surface, no migration / no schema / no role-matrix change):** `GET /v1/me` (self-scoped identity), `GET /v1/devices` + `POST /v1/devices/{id}/revoke`, `GET /v1/sync/status`. OpenAPI document + generated TS schema regenerated; drift pins extended.
- **Core:** `revoke_device` / `revoke_grants_for_device`, mirroring the member-keyed revocation.
- **Taste pass:** `Layout` unified onto the single `lib/ui` palette (one gray family); a ~25-line framework-free `index.css` adds the hover / active / `:focus-visible` / transition states inline styles can't express (zero specificity; `filter`/`transform`/`outline` so it never overrides an inline background). Visually QA'd against the production build.

### Golden rule (reuse)
The settings-UI / tree-view / headless-component candidates — Radix UI (~15k★), shadcn/ui, react-arborist (~3k★), react-hook-form (~42k★) — were evaluated and rejected against the framework-free shell (RISK-08). Built on the in-stack React + react-router + the `lib/ui` inline-style vocabulary, identical to every prior web epic. Recorded in `docs/stack.md` (§E20). No standard claimed.

### Permissions / security
Every Settings read is gated by the existing bearer-token auth; the only write (device decommission) requires `tokens.rotate` (Maintainer+). Devices expose **verify keys only** — the private seed never leaves the keychain (no-seed-leak test-pinned). No new §11 action.

### Tests / gates
`make lint && typecheck && test && coverage` all green: **pytest 751 passed, 56 skipped**, **Vitest 81 passed** (18 new), coverage **97.04%** (gate ≥90%); `tsc` + `vite build` clean. New tests cover identity self-scope + no-secret, device read authz + no-seed-leak + decommission cascade/audit/self-device-409/403/404, sync counts/mode/authz, the core revoke helpers, and the five web pages (render, guards, grant revoke, device decommission + 403, sync counts, export stub).

author: rygel
body:
## Brain Export/Backup System

Export the user's entire Chalie state (SQLite DB + local files) into a single encrypted `.chalie-backup` archive, with optional upload to GitHub as a recoverable backup.

### Features
- **Export** — snapshot SQLite DB via backup API, collect document files, build zip, encrypt with AES-256-GCM (PBKDF2 key derivation, 600k iterations)
- **Import/Restore** — decrypt, validate checksums, pre-restore backup of current brain, replace DB + files
- **GitHub Integration** — upload encrypted backups as GitHub Releases to a private repo (one release per backup, tagged by timestamp)
- **Self-contained** — passphrase-derived encryption, no dependency on the vault; restore only needs the passphrase
- **Unencrypted mode** — optional; backup still has the CHALIEBACKUP header for format consistency

### New Files
- `backend/services/brain_export_service.py` (215 lines) — snapshot, zip, encrypt
- `backend/services/brain_import_service.py` (183 lines) — decrypt, validate, restore
- `backend/services/github_backup_service.py` (149 lines) — GitHub REST API: create repo, release, upload asset
- `backend/api/brain.py` (155 lines) — Flask blueprint: `GET /brain/info`, `POST /brain/export`, `POST /brain/import`, `POST /brain/export/upload`, `POST /brain/github/test`
- `frontend/brain/brain.js` (305 lines) — Brain tab panel with export/import dialogs and GitHub config

### Modified Files
- `frontend/brain/sidebar.js` — Brain nav entry in system group
- `frontend/brain/app.js` — route/label/panel/command palette registration
- `frontend/brain/index.html` — script tag
- `frontend/brain/style.css` — Brain tab styles (cards, forms, layout)
- `frontend/brain/icons.js` — Download, Database icons

### File Format
`.chalie-backup` binary format:
```
CHALIEBACKUP (12B magic) | version (2B) | PBKDF2 salt (16B) | iterations (4B) | AES-256-GCM nonce (12B) | ciphertext+tag (variable)
```

### Test Results
- Encrypted round-trip: PASS
- Unencrypted round-trip: PASS
- Wrong password rejection: PASS

## Reporting tab

A new Reporting page under **Intelligence & Insights** with four report types and a context-aware period selector.

**Report types**
- **Performance** — marketing P&L: spend → sessions → calls → intakes → matters → revenue funnel, spend efficiency (CPA/ROI), traffic & search visibility, reputation, daily call volume, and the open recommendation queue. Operating layout for short windows, full strategic layout (funnel + channel table) for longer ones.
- **Production** — content shipped by type, published-by-channel, pipeline health, and a recently-produced table (from `content_drafts` + the pipeline board).
- **Trends** — Claude ranks the biggest wins and risks across keyword rankings, organic search (GSC), and AI search visibility (AEO), plus raw mover tables.
- **Custom** — free-text prompt + scope-filter chips; Claude assembles a tailored report from the metric set.

**Periods**
- Performance / Production / Custom: **Last week** · **Last month** (calendar) · **Last 30 days**
- Trends: **Last 7 days** · **Last 14 days** · **Last 30 days**

Each window compares against the equally-long prior window, matching `/api/metrics/overview`.

**New endpoint** — `POST /api/reporting/ai-digest` powers Trends and Custom, reusing the shared Anthropic client (`KEYWORD_RESEARCH_MODEL`), `getFirmContext()`, and the structured-JSON extraction pattern from `recommendations/generate`. The client gathers metrics (it holds the session) and the endpoint reasons over them.

All reports print clean (white sections, hidden controls) for Save-to-PDF.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` clean across the new files.
- Verified all four tabs render in the dev preview; period sets swap and reset correctly between report types; calendar windows resolve correctly (e.g. "Last month" → May 1–31). Trends and Custom AI generations confirmed end-to-end against live data.

author: acoshift
body:
The DO-NOW tier from the performance + send-failure review.

## 1. HTTP failure taxonomy — stop retrying permanent 4xx forever (the important one)

`flush()` treated **every non-200 as retryable**, so `retryFlush(false)` retried forever. A single misconfiguration — wrong index (404), expired token (401), or a schema-rejected batch (400/422) — parked a worker in the infinite-retry loop. With the **default 2 workers, a couple of poison batches froze all ingest** and blocked every `Ingest` caller. There was no permanent-failure path.

Now `flush()` classifies the status:
- **Permanent** (`400/401/403/404/409/422`): settle tracked items with a new `*IngestError{Reason: ReasonServer}`, invoke `OnDiscard` for fire-and-forget items, drop the batch, and keep draining.
- **Retryable** (5xx, 408, 425, 429, transport errors): unchanged. `413` keeps its own auto-reduce/re-chunk path.

Tracked (`IngestSync`) callers now get a **definitive Nack/dead-letter verdict** instead of an ambiguous context timeout.

## 2. Drop a per-flush allocation

`flush()` built a fresh `encoded := make([]ingestItem, 0, len(batch))` (~48 KB + a full 1000-element copy at the default batch size) **every round-trip**, only to replay the settle list. Removed — on HTTP 200 we settle over `batch` directly. Identical behavior, because encode-failure and fire-and-forget items have `ack==nil`, so `settle(nil)` is a no-op for them.

## 3. Recover a 413-reduced batch size on the ticker

The post-413 batch-size reset only ran on a *successful flush*, but `flush()` never runs on an empty buffer — so after a transient 413 spike followed by quiet traffic, the batch could stay shrunk (down to 10%) indefinitely. The reset now also runs in the worker's ticker branch, firing within ~one `maxDelay` of the 10-minute window expiring. Gated on `SetAutoReduceBatchSize`, off by default.

## Invariants preserved
Fire-and-forget batching, ordering, the 413 split, and the `IngestSync` at-least-once / exactly-once-settle guarantees are unchanged. The permanent path settles each item exactly once and drops the batch, so nothing is re-flushed or double-settled.

## Tests
5 new (`ingest_reliability_test.go`): permanent 400 → prompt `ReasonServer`; permanent 404 doesn't wedge a single worker (second call still gets a verdict); 5xx still retried to success (guards against over-classifying); fire-and-forget 422 → `OnDiscard` + Close returns promptly; worker-side encode failure still discarded with the `encoded` slice gone (good docs delivered, poison discarded). Full suite green, `go vet` clean, race-clean across `-count=2`.

## Reviewed but deferred (not in this PR)
429/Retry-After, backoff jitter, `ResponseHeaderTimeout`, ingest-response-body inspection (silent reject loss), `SetCloseTimeout`, and `commit=wait_for` — all from the "with care" tier, to be decided separately.

## Summary

Add a curated, deterministic golangci-lint configuration to the Go GTS engine, enforce it in CI, and complete godoc coverage for exported identifiers and non-trivial unexported helpers.

## Scope

- `go/gts` only.
- No GTS wire-format, API behavior, or runtime behavior changes.
- Minor public API rename: `codec.CodecError` -> `codec.Error` (eliminates package-name stutter).

## Constitution principles

- **Principle 4** (canonical source): linter config lives in `go/gts/.golangci.yml`; CI consumes it; no hand-edited generated artifacts.
- **Principle 6** (greenfield quality): the new lint gate runs in CI alongside `go vet` and `staticcheck`.
- **Principle 15** (every module earns its consumer): the consumers are downstream Go users of `go.blackcatinformatics.ca/gts` and the monorepo CI gate.

## What changed

1. Added `go/gts/.golangci.yml` (v2 format) enabling `errcheck`, `gocritic`, `gosec`, `govet`, `ineffassign`, `misspell`, `revive`, `staticcheck`.
2. Fixed all surfaced lint findings:
   - `staticcheck`: tagged switches, `fmt.Fprintf` vs `WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(...))`.
   - `revive`: `CodecError` stutter, missing/malformed godoc on constants.
   - `gocritic`: append-assign in `compact/compact.go`.
   - `gosec`: resolved with targeted `//nolint` comments for intentional CLI I/O, test scaffolding, files-profile permissions, and bounded int->uint64 conversions.
3. Completed godoc for every exported identifier and added comments to non-trivial unexported helpers across `go/gts`.
4. Added a `golangci-lint` step to the Go job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
5. Updated `go/gts/README.md` and the root PR template to mention the new gate.

## Validation

- `cd go/gts && golangci-lint run ./...` -> 0 issues.
- `cd go/gts && go vet ./...` -> pass.
- `cd go/gts && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...` -> pass.

author: pchang388
body:
Part of the Prometheus best-practices breaking batch (3.0.0). Final code phase (P3.4) before migration notes + release. Stacked behind #88/#89/#90/#92/#93/#94 (all merged to `main`).

## Changes
- Removed the `library_name` label from every `tdarr_library_*` metric. Library metrics now key on the stable `library_id`.
- Added `tdarr_library_info{library_id, library_name}` (value always 1), emitted once per library — the id→name mapping to join against.
- Collector: stripped `library_name` from 11 desc label-sets + emit sites; `emitPieSlices` lost its `libName` param.
- Tests/golden: added the `tdarr_library_info` block, stripped `library_name` from value metrics, `wantCollectorDescs` 27 → 28.
- Dashboard (`examples/dashboard.json`):
  - `$library` template variable repointed to `label_values(tdarr_library_info, library_name)`.
  - 4 overview panels join `* on (library_id, tdarr_instance) group_left(library_name) tdarr_library_info` to display the name.
  - 13 per-library panels move the `$library` selector onto `and on (library_id, tdarr_instance) tdarr_library_info{library_name=~"$library"}`.
- Alerts (`examples/alerts.yaml`): `TdarrTranscodeFailed` expr joins `* on (library_id) group_left(library_name) tdarr_library_info` so the `{{ $labels.library_name }}` annotation still resolves.

## Motivation
A library rename churned every `library_name`-labeled series (id stable, name changes → new series, broken continuity). Moving the name to an info metric keyed on `library_id` makes the value series rename-stable and follows the Prometheus info-metric pattern (mirrors the worker `_info` split in #89).

## Decisions
- Joins use `on (library_id, tdarr_instance)` (both labels) for multi-instance safety — internally consistent across all P3.4 joins. The alert rule uses `on (library_id)` only (no `$tdarr_instance` template there).
- `node_name` on `tdarr_node_info` has the same churn pattern but is out of scope (node renames rare).

## Test plan
- `go test ./... -race`, `go vet`, `gofmt` — all green. Golden fixture updated by hand.
- Live-verified on Tdarr v2.77.01: 7 `tdarr_library_info` series, no `library_name` leak on other `tdarr_library_*`, `library_id` sets match between info and value metrics (every series joins to a name), `size_diff_bytes` sign/scale intact.
- Dashboard/alerts: JSON + YAML parse; join counts verified (4 group_left, 13 `and on`, 13 `library_name=~` all on the info side, 0 stale template refs).
- **Pending (manual):** Grafana visual import — PromQL render correctness of the joins can't be proven from a static `/metrics` dump.

## In-depth
Two join idioms, intentional: `* … group_left(library_name)` where the name must appear in output (multiplies the value by the info metric's `1`, preserving it incl. negative `size_diff`); `and on(...)` where `$library` is only a filter (set intersection, no value math, mirrors #89). Release-please PR stays gated until the whole batch + consolidated migration notes land on `main`.

## Why

`eslint-plugin-vitest@0.5.x` introduced a circular reference in its `recommended` config object (`configs.recommended.plugins.vitest` → self). ESLint 8's legacy `@eslint/eslintrc` calls `JSON.stringify()` during config validation, which crashes with:

```
TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON
    property 'configs' -> 'recommended' -> 'plugins' -> 'vitest' closes the circle
Referenced from: @dvcol/eslint-plugin-presets/lib/index.js
```

This blocked Dependabot dev-dependencies group PR #8 from passing lint CI.

## What

Add an `ignore` entry for `eslint-plugin-vitest` so Dependabot excludes it from the group and stops trying to bump past 0.4.x until we migrate to flat ESLint config.

- The other 7 deps from PR #8 (homebridge 2.1, prettier 3.8, husky 9.1, nodemon 3.1, homebridge-config-ui-x 5.24, @dvcol/eslint-plugin-presets 1.3.11, eslint-plugin-prettier 5.5.6) are unaffected and will be re-picked up by Dependabot in the next scheduled run.

body:
## What

Adds `crossorigin="use-credentials"` to the `<link rel="manifest">` tag in `apps/web/src/index.html`.

## Why

Non-prod hostnames (`staging.aecintegrations.com` and `*.aec-integrations.workers.dev` previews) sit behind Cloudflare Access. Browsers fetch the web app manifest without credentials by default, so the Access cookie wasn't sent — Access then 302-redirected the manifest fetch to its cross-origin login page, and that redirect failed CORS, throwing a console error on every staging/preview page load. Sending credentials lets Access recognize the session and serve the manifest directly; it's harmless in production, which has no Access gate. Staging-only — can't be reproduced on localhost (no Access), so this verifies once deployed.

author: leopenausa
body:
Follow-up to #53, implementing the two highest-value fail-safes the [2026-06-13 legacy-vs-pyladcp fidelity audit](../tree/main) flagged as un-ported (`p.soundcorr` was the audit's single material catch).

## 1. Sound-speed correction — `p.soundcorr` (ON by default)

Legacy `prepinv.m:35,419-444` multiplies the water velocities `ru/rv/rw` by `c_in-situ / c_firmware` on every cast (default ON). RDI computes Doppler velocity with the single fixed sound speed configured at deployment; when that value is wrong, **every cell carries a proportional scale error**. pyladcp read the PD0 `sound_speed` but never applied it.

This wires the correction per ensemble:
- `c_firmware` from the PD0 variable leader
- `c_in-situ` at each ping's **package depth** from the CTD (TEOS-10 `gsw.sound_speed`), interpolated and clamped to the profile range
- applied to `merged.ru/rv/rw` **after** bottom-track acquisition (legacy `getbtrack` precedes `prepinv`, so BT keeps the firmware sound speed) and **before** super-ensemble formation
- clamped to ±15% as a bad-header guard; falls back to no-op if the CTD lacks salinity/pressure
- toggle with `--no-soundcorr`

**Evidence (MORIA-80 golden ladder):** firmware ran a fixed **1450 m/s** vs in-situ median **~1492** → a ~2.9% scale. The fix moves ūbar **−6.31 → −6.47 cm/s** (golden **−6.50**) and bias **+0.20 → +0.04 cm/s**, with u-correlation held at **0.9988**. (rms 0.64 → 0.78 reflects the small methodological difference vs golden's ADCP-temp/S=34.5 estimate — pyladcp uses real CTD T/S/P; the near-zero bias and ūbar match confirm the physics.)

## 2. Shear-vs-inverse consistency WARN

Legacy `getshear2.m:143-158`: the inverse and the shear method independently estimate the baroclinic shear; when they disagree by more than the formal error, legacy inflates the delivered `uerr` and warns. pyladcp computed both but never compared them.

- compute `uvds = sqrt(std(u_inv_baroclinic − u_shear)² + std(v...)²)`
- if `uvds > mean(uerr)`: inflate `vp.uerr` so its mean = `uvds/1.5` (shape kept), matching `getshear2.m:156`
- new `shear_vs_inverse_consistency` QA metric WARNs when `uvds > 1.5·mean(uerr)` **and** `> 0.1 m/s`
- inverse solver only (for `solver=shear`, `vp` *is* the shear product). On clean MORIA-80 the two agree (uvds 0.017 < formal err 0.035) → OK, no spurious WARN.

## Tests
`tests/test_qa_soundcorr_shear.py`: sound-speed scale ratio, ūbar-toward-golden, `--no-soundcorr` disable, no-salinity fallback; shear-inverse helper (identical/different/grid-mismatch), metric presence, uerr inflation. `test_session_config.py` updated for the new `inv_opts` key + round-trip. **Full suite green (405 passed), ruff clean.**

author: tu11aa
body:
## Problem

`cockpit crew spawn --worktree` creates an isolated worktree and sets `spawnCwd` to it, but the crew's cmux pane is created in the captain's workspace cwd (main checkout). `cmux new-surface`/`new-pane` have no `--cwd` flag, so the shell never enters the worktree — the agent's git ops run against the main checkout, dragging the captain's HEAD onto the crew branch.

Proof: a `--worktree` crew's status line shows `⎇ develop` (main checkout branch), not `crew/<name>`.

## Fix

Prepend `cd '<spawnCwd>' && ` (POSIX single-quoted) to the `sendToPane` launch command for both **claude** and **opencode**. For non-worktree crews `spawnCwd === proj.path`, so the `cd` is a harmless no-op — behavior is unchanged.

**Codex** is unaffected — it dispatches through the daemon with `cwd: spawnCwd` and launches `cockpit crew attach` in the pane (not the agent CLI directly). Confirmed by reading `runCodexInteractiveSpawn`.

## Changes

- `src/commands/crew.ts` — add `shellQuote()` helper; prepend `cd` on both the claude (L398) and opencode (L448) `sendToPane` lines
- `src/commands/__tests__/crew.test.ts` — 3 new tests:
  - `--worktree` claude crew: launch starts with `cd '<worktree>'`
  - non-worktree claude crew: launch starts with `cd '<proj.path>'` (no-op)
  - `--worktree` opencode crew: launch starts with `cd '<worktree>'`

## Tests

```
npm test → 1028/1028 passed
```

## Manual verification

To verify after merge: spawn a `--worktree` crew and check its status line shows `crew/<name>` (not `develop`), and that the captain's main checkout `git status` does not show a branch switch. This requires a live cmux environment — the unit tests cover the mechanism and are the primary regression guard.

Closes #279

body:
## Summary
Normalizes human-friendly time inputs to the **unix epoch seconds** Quickwit
expects for `start_timestamp` / `end_timestamp`. Required by `search_logs` (#8)
and `aggregate_logs` (#9).

## Linked issue
Closes #4

## Changes — `src/quickwit_mcp/timeparse.py`
`to_epoch_seconds(value, *, now=None) -> int`, accepting:
- `"now"` and relative `"now-<N><s|m|h|d>"` (e.g. `now-1h`, `now-7d`) — case-insensitive
- ISO-8601: `2026-06-01T12:00:00Z`, explicit offsets, naive (treated as UTC), bare dates (midnight UTC)
- raw epoch as `int` / `float` / numeric string

`now` is injectable so relative offsets are deterministic in tests. Bad strings
raise `ValueError`; bad types raise `TypeError` (incl. `bool`, to avoid `True -> 1`).

### Notes
- `datetime.fromisoformat` in Python 3.10 rejects a `Z` suffix, so it's normalized to `+00:00` first (keeps the 3.10 floor working).
- Relative offsets are minus-only by design — log ranges look backward; `now+1h` is rejected.

author: heeyunlee
body:
## Problem

Cross-locale text animations don't play on the deployed site — the language toggle swaps the text but nothing animates.

**Root cause:** Switching locales is a **soft client navigation**. The `[locale]` param changes and `AnimatedText` receives a new `text` prop *in place* — the instances are **not** remounted (verified with a headless browser: a `window` flag set before the switch survives it). But the animation was gated on a **mount-only** effect (`useIsomorphicLayoutEffect(..., [])`), whose comment wrongly assumed *"locale switches remount."* Since the effect never re-ran when `text` changed, the text swapped with no animation.

(My first commit on this branch chased a hard-reload theory and added `sessionStorage` — that was wrong; this amended commit replaces it with the actual fix.)

## Fix

- Run the effect on `text` change (`[text]` deps) instead of mount-only.
- Source the previous string from a per-instance `useRef` (the in-place case), falling back to the registry for any instance that does remount (e.g. a page swap).
- `locale-transition.ts` keeps its original module-state design (soft nav preserves it); only its comments were corrected.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅
- `npm run build` ✅
- Headless-browser test against the static export (`out/`): roll cells render mid-switch (`rollCells` 194→210), settle cleanly to plain text (`rollCells` back to 0, no artifacts), and animate in both directions (EN→KO, KO→FR).

## What

Drops the carried keystone CVE backport patches `0001`–`0005` for
2025.1. They were added in #731 and have since merged upstream on
`stable/2025.1`, so they now apply as "already applied"/reversed (and
`0001` has context-drifted hunks too) against the
`keystone-27.0.2.dev20` tarball. `patch --dry-run` exits non-zero, so
`container-images-kolla-push-2025.1` aborts at *Run build script* every
nightly run.

## Why now

This is the 2025.1 analogue of the 2025.2 drift already resolved in the
`#736`/`#737`/`#738` series. First surfaced on the 2026-06-13
periodic-midnight build:

- https://zuul.services.osism.tech/t/osism/build/6b20bdb9f17540fcac88ee175f59baad

## Verification

Checked each patch against the current `stable/2025.1` source
(`HEAD 5613a37d4`, = tarball `keystone-27.0.2.dev20`):

| patch | fix | upstream? | action |
|-------|-----|-----------|--------|
| 0001 | Enforce delegation project boundary (bug #2150089) | yes | drop |
| 0002 | Fix user impersonation (CVE-2026-42998) | yes | drop |
| 0003 | Forbid trust ops via app credentials (CVE-2026-43000) | yes | drop |
| 0004 | Preserve expires_at when rescoping (CVE-2026-44394) | yes | drop |
| 0005 | Prevent RBAC policy bypass (CVE-2026-42999) | yes | drop |
| 0006 | Block app credential token rescoping (bug 2144966) | no | **keep** |

(merge commits for each CVE); `0006`/`0007` are absent upstream and still
apply cleanly (forward, no fuzz) at their existing numbers. Same
keep-numbering approach as `b769eb1` (#648) / the 2025.2 series.

CVE coverage is preserved — the fixes now live in the upstream tarball
instead of local patches.

author: zachshallbetter
body:
The product rebrand from **field-ui** to **Fundamental**, as one clean cutover. Keeps the *field primitive* (`<field-root>`, `--field-*`, `field:*`, `FieldHandle`) and the *forces concept* (the `FORCES` catalog / token names); removes every trace of the old product names and the forces-ui→field-ui migration compat.

### Rename
- All packages `@field-ui/*` → `@fundamental-engine/*` (core, platform, elements, react, vanilla, three, kit) + the bare `fundamental-engine` umbrella; imports, READMEs, configs, `field-ui.com` → `fundamental-engine.com`.

### Clean break — forces-ui alias window purged (#432)
- **Registration protocol** collapsed to `field:*` only (`field:register-body` etc.); dropped the `forces:*` twins, `FIELD_*` duplicates, and the dual dispatch/listen across `shadow.ts` / `field.ts` / `platform-runtime.ts`.
- **`--forces-*` CSS vars** removed (density, heatmap-density, interaction `--forces-pull-*`/`--forces-attention`) incl. the platform FeedbackRegistry mirror.
- **`forces:*` events** removed (event-agent + platform mirror + DataConsole).
- **`<forces-field>`/`<forces-cell>`/`ForcesField`/`ForcesCell`/`ForcesController`/`useForcesField`** removed (`forces-cell.ts` renamed to `field-cell.ts` — it *is* the `FieldCell` primitive — keeping the primitive, dropping only the alias).
- Freeze gate: dropped the alias-window entry (14 frozen entries intact). Migration test suites removed; `shadow.test.ts` rewritten to the single `field:*` dispatch. Doc consumers updated off `--forces-*`.

### Verification
- typecheck · build · test (0 failures: core 628 / platform 124 / three 19 / react 7 / vanilla 26 / elements 25 / site 45) · check:api (14 frozen) · check:cem — all green.
- e2e `home.spec.ts` chromium: boots-clean (particleCount > 50) + the body-interaction/accretion tests pass — **proves the `field:*` registration protocol still registers bodies**. (One Contour Charge poll-to-0 flake under suite contention; passes in isolation, unrelated to this change.)
- Sanity grep: no `forces-*`/`forces:`/`Forces*` symbols remain except the `FORCES` catalog + force-token names.

Follow-ups (separate): publish 0.4.0 + deprecate `@field-ui/*`/`@forces-ui/*`; repo rename + domain 301; Swift `FieldUI*` → `Fundamental*`; reconcile the one historical paper (`writings/05-host-driven-runtime.md`) that documents the now-removed mirror.

author: rajatvarna
body:
## Summary

This PR enhances the stock screener with new comparison and analysis features, plus a light theme option. Users can now compare multiple stocks side-by-side, see top daily gainers/losers, view dividend information, and toggle between dark and light themes.

## Key Changes

- **New ComparisonChart component**: Allows users to add up to 2 comparison symbols alongside the primary stock. Displays normalized percentage returns from the earliest common date, limited to the last 252 trading days. Includes interactive symbol management and a clean SVG-based chart with gridlines and labels.

- **New TopMovers component**: Displays top 5 gainers and losers in a horizontal scrollable strip. Users can click any stock to select it for detailed analysis.

- **New ThemeToggle component**: Adds light/dark theme toggle button. Theme preference is persisted to localStorage and applied via CSS custom properties.

- **Dividend and Beta data**: Extended StockData type and API responses to include:
  - `dividendYield` (trailing annual)
  - `exDividendDate` (Unix timestamp)
  - `beta` (volatility measure)
  - These are now displayed in the Fundamentals tab, table columns (optional), and CSV export

- **Split view mode**: New "Split" view button that displays the screener table and chart panel side-by-side for simultaneous browsing and analysis.

- **Light theme CSS**: Added `html.light` class styles to globals.css for a light color scheme with proper contrast.

- **API enhancements**:
  - `/api/batch` now fetches and returns dividend yield, ex-dividend date, and beta
  - `/api/fundamentals` now includes summaryDetail module for additional dividend data
  - `lib/yahoo.ts` updated to request new fields from Yahoo Finance API

- **UI improvements**:
  - Dividend badge in ChartPanel header showing yield and ex-dividend date
  - New "Compare" tab in ChartPanel for the comparison chart
  - Sortable columns for dividend yield and beta in the screener table
  - CSV export includes dividend yield and beta columns

## Implementation Details

- ComparisonChart normalizes all series to percentage change from the earliest common date to enable fair visual comparison across different price scales
- Chart uses SVG for crisp rendering and includes dynamic Y-axis scaling based on data range
- TopMovers filters stocks with valid daily performance data and sorts to extract top 5 gainers/losers
- Theme toggle uses document.documentElement class manipulation for CSS-in-JS style application
- Split view uses flexbox with sticky positioning for the chart panel to remain visible while scrolling the table

body:
## Summary

Sprint 3 後半 PR-6（F-CAM-004 写真編集フル実装）。写真詳細画面から編集画面に入り、トリミング/回転・明るさ/コントラスト/彩度調整・プリセットフィルタ 11 種を適用して Storage に上書き保存できる。PR #24（PATCH の width/height/file_size 拡張）が前提。

- `ColorMatrix`（domain）: 4x5 カラーマトリクスの合成・brightness/contrast/saturation 生成（純 Dart、テストの主対象）
- `FilterPresets`: 11 種（オリジナル/モノクロ/ノワール/セピア/ヴィヴィッド/ウォーム/クール/フェード/ヴィンテージ/フィルム/ドリーミー）
- `PhotoEditRenderer`: `PictureRecorder` + `Canvas`（`Paint()..colorFilter = ColorFilter.matrix`）で焼き込み → JPEG q80。プレビューと同一フィルタパス
- `PhotoEditRepository`: image_cropper でトリミング/回転、編集後を **同パス upsert 上書き** + サムネ再生成（既存 `ImageProcessor.generateThumbnail`）+ PATCH で width/height/file_size 更新
- `PhotoEditNotifier`（family）: フィルタ選択・スライダー・合成マトリクス算出・保存。保存成功でフィード refresh
- `PhotoEditScreen`: 上部にライブプレビュー（`ColorFiltered`）、下部にフィルタカルーセル + トリミングボタン + スライダー 3 本
- 詳細画面に編集アイコン（`Icons.tune`）。戻り時に `reloadAfterEdit` で署名 URL に `&v=<epoch>` を付けて cached_network_image のキャッシュを更新
- `/photo/:id/edit` ルート、AndroidManifest に `UCropActivity` 登録

## Design notes

- **トリミング/回転は image_cropper（uCrop/TOCrop）**。自由比率 + 1:1/4:3/16:9 + 90 度回転をネイティブ UI で標準サポート。`lockAspectRatio: false` で比率自由
- **調整/フィルタは ColorFilter.matrix + Canvas 焼き込み**。プレビューと保存が同一行列なので見た目が一致。`image` パッケージ依存を増やさない。原寸は前処理済み ≤1024px でメモリ負荷小
- **上書き保存**（編集前画像は保持しない＝ユーザー承認済み）。寸法が変わるため PATCH で width/height/file_size を更新
- **キャッシュ更新**: 署名 URL は再発行ごとにトークンが変わるが、同一秒の再発行で同一になり得るため `&v=<epoch>` を付加。実機で Storage が余剰クエリを無視するか要確認（NG なら CachedNetworkImage の cacheKey 方式へ）

## Test plan

- [x] `dart run build_runner build` / `dart format` / `flutter analyze`（No issues）
- [x] `flutter test`（ColorMatrix/FilterPresets 13 ケース追加 = 計 35 passed）
- [ ] 実機: 詳細 → 編集 → トリミング 4 比率・回転 → 保存 → 詳細/一覧が新画像に更新
- [ ] 実機: フィルタ + スライダー → プレビューと保存結果が一致
- [ ] 実機: `&v=` 付き署名 URL が 200 を返すか（NG 時は cacheKey フォールバック）

## Out of scope

- 編集前画像の履歴保持（上書きのみ）
- カバー写真の手動選択 — v1.1

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

S11 ACT on **descartes-rule-of-signs-oq-02-oq-01-oq-02** (Sturm's Theorem: exact root count). Lands the **B.1** building block of Step B toward discharging the lone axiom `sturm_exact_count_axiom`:

`squarefree_root_has_nonzero_derivative` — for a squarefree `p : ℝ[X]`, at any root of `p` the derivative is non-zero.

Proof: `Squarefree p → p.Separable` (`PerfectField.separable_iff_squarefree.mpr`, `[PerfectField ℝ]` auto from `[CharZero ℝ]`) → `∃ a b, a*p + b*p' = 1` (`Separable` is defeq `IsCoprime p p'`) → evaluate at `r`, contradict the proposed double root.

## Bearer-name corrections

The S10 PREP "paste-ready recipe" did **not** compile as written — both named bearers were wrong at Mathlib v4.26.0 (the S10 audit was GitHub-raw, not compiled). A baseline Docker build surfaced this:

- `Polynomial.separable_def'.mp` (does not exist) → destructure `hsep` directly, since `Polynomial.Separable p` is definitionally `IsCoprime p (derivative p) = ∃ a b, a*p + b*p' = 1`.
- `Polynomial.PerfectField.separable_iff_squarefree` (wrong namespace) → `PerfectField.separable_iff_squarefree` (verified against the actual v4.26.0 `Mathlib/FieldTheory/Perfect.lean:280`).

## Counts

`lineCount` 513→538, `theoremCount` 28→29; axiom count unchanged (still 1, `sturm_exact_count_axiom`), sorries 0.

## Test plan

- [x] `./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.DescartesRuleOfSignsOQ02OQ01OQ02` → **Build completed successfully (3058 jobs)**, 0 errors, 0 sorries.
- [x] meta.json validated; counts synced.
- [x] B.1 is a standalone building block (used by future B.2/assembly); no existing proof depends on it, so no regression risk.

author: pari-dubey1
body:
## Pull Request Description

This pull request introduces the classic, high-performance **Animated Hamburger Menu Toggle (`ease-hamburger`)** navigational utility component to the repository suite. It transforms a standard 3-line horizontal hamburger icon smoothly into a crisp 'X' close state on hover, completely synchronized via pure CSS transition paths.

Fixes #6296

---

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New animation / hover effect
- [ ] 🧩 New component
- [ ] 📝 Documentation improvement
- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix in an existing submission
- [ ] Other (describe below)

---

## Submission Checklist

- [x] All changes are inside `submissions/examples/ease-hamburger-toggle/`
- [x] Includes `demo.html` — self-contained, opens in browser with no server
- [x] Includes `style.css` — raw CSS for the proposed feature
- [x] Includes `README.md` — what it does, how to use it, why it fits EaseMotion CSS
- [x] **No changes to `core/`**
- [x] **No changes to `components/`**
- [x] One feature per PR (no bundled unrelated changes)

---

## Feature Description

**What does this add?**
It adds a fully synchronized navigational micro-interaction component layer. When a user hovers anywhere over the component display block, the three standalone horizontal vector elements morph seamlessly. The top and bottom lanes execute calculated vertical translations (`translate3d`) along with contrasting angular rotations (`45deg` / `-45deg`) to lock into a clean intersection 'X', while the middle vector collapses horizontally (`scale3d(0, 1, 1)`) and fades away.

**State Synchronization UI:** The component status label text content is directly tied to the parent container's hover state via CSS pseudo-elements (`::before`). This triggers an instantaneous text swap from `"Menu State"` to `"Active Open"` at the exact microsecond the icon morphs, maintaining absolute logical consistency without JavaScript execution latency.

**Why does it fit EaseMotion CSS?**
It abstracts advanced multi-element layout morphs and text injection rules into an elegant, human-readable helper utility setup. By relying 100% on hardware-accelerated compositor parameters (`transform` and `opacity`) bound to a `will-change` layer, it bypasses heavy main-thread paint loops to run at a locked, stutter-free 60fps.

---

## Browser Testing

- [x] Chrome
- [x] Firefox
- [x] Edge
- [ ] Safari

---

## Notes for Maintainer

- **Strict Path Isolation:** Built 100% within sandbox boundaries, ensuring absolute zero overlap with primary core framework stylesheets.
- **Pure CSS Core Mechanics:** Completely independent of runtime script timers or external layout bundles, preventing runtime bottlenecks or paint layer shifting.
- **High Com-posability Scope:** Designed as a layout-agnostic component that fits fluidly into navigation headers, floating control widgets, responsive banners, or collapsible sidebars.

## Summary

Closes #1036.

Three loops RQ2 opened but left dangling — each closed with data already in hand.

### 1. Arrows name their risks

The risk-matrix movement overlay (RQ2-9) deduplicates identical inherent→residual paths into one `×N` arrow but collapsed identity: hover said "three risks moved", not _which_ three. The `movementArrows` memo now retains `titles: string[]` per path; each arrow renders a native SVG `<title>` composed by a new bounded pure helper `movementArrowTitle(titles)` — **top 8 + "+N more"** so a path shared by 40 risks stays readable. > **Update (이번 세션 추가 승격분):** 이 PR은 원래 **v1.5.0** 승격용이었고, 그 위에 v2.0 로드맵 **M12(피드백 루프)**·**M11 Phase A(측정 인프라)**가 추가됐다. 아래 "추가분" → 원본 v1.5.0 설명 순. 버전 범프·태그 push(비가역 릴리스 단계)는 미포함.

## 추가분 — v2.0 M12 + M11 Phase A

### M12 — 피드백 루프 / closed loop  `9101db1`
M10 텔레메트리 → 설계 제안의 닫힌 고리(measure → suggest → 사용자 결정).

### M11 Phase A — 비교·증명 벤치 측정 인프라  `e43de3a`
- `bench/collect.mjs`(ccusage·/context 순수 파서)·`gen-fixture.mjs`(대형 fixture 결정적)·`test-trigger.sh`+시드(트리거 **17/17**·오발화 **0/5**)·`report.mjs` 축 3·4 열(하위호환).
- **Phase B(A~E n≥5 라이브 실측)는 API·타 하네스 필요 → 코드 외, 인프라만 완료.**

### 문서  `b2cf39e`
M11/M12 플랜, MS7 로드맵·인덱스 상태 갱신, 벤치 결과 현재 스냅샷(라이브 표는 v1.1.0 역사 라벨), CHANGELOG.

**게이트(추가분 반영):** `npm run check` clean · `npm test` **287/287** · 커버리지 **88.31%** · `npm run score` **100/100** · 런타임 의존성 불변 · 네트워크 없음.

---

## What

v1.5.0 — the final fade-out stage. Deletes the **7 faded-out components** from the catalog + assets, and adds a one-time **orphan cleanup** so existing installs are tidied on `carve update` (no uninstall/reinstall).

Removed (catalog entry + `assets/skills/<id>/` + `assets/commands/carve-<id>.md`):
- **4 hidden** (built-in slash collision, v1.4.1): `memory` · `verify` · `pr` · `review`
- **3 deprecated** (squad delegation, v1.4.0): `changelog` · `security-scan` · `coordinator`

Replacements: built-in `/memory`·`/verify`·`/pr`·`/review`; `squad-gitops`·`squad-audit`·`parallel-agents` (deep review `squad-review`).

## Orphan cleanup (the new behavior)

`installer.removeOrphanedComponents()` runs in `carve update`:
- Scoped by an **explicit tombstone** (`REMOVED_COMPONENTS`), NOT "any unregistered id" — this is the key safety choice: `byId('clean-html')` is also `undefined`, so the naive approach would wrongly delete the anti-slop `clean-html` pack skill.
- **Hash-guarded**: deletes only carve-owned, unmodified files; **preserves user-modified** ones (with a notice); syncs the manifest.
- So existing users upgrade with just `npm i -g carve-harness@latest` → `carve update` — no uninstall needed.

## Staged delivery (each step 100% green)

1. Migration added with an empty tombstone (no-op) + unit tests — existing behavior untouched.
2. 7 components deleted + tombstone filled + tests reshaped (subjectless deprecated/hidden integration tests removed; e2e Scenario E **repurposed** to the orphan-cleanup flow).
3. docs/lifecycle.md (Wave 2 + cadence exception), bench config, version, CHANGELOG, README/README.en.

## Side-effect-free

- Lifecycle machinery (`statusOf`/`deprecationNotices`/filters) kept for future fade-outs — only the components and their now-subjectless tests were removed.
- Regression tests lock the oversafety guard (clean-html untouched) and user-modified preservation.
- No dangling references (remaining mentions are test fixtures, historical CHANGELOG/lifecycle, or built-in `/slash` pointers).

## Verification

`npm run check` clean · `npm test` **268/268** · `npm run test:cov` **~88.0%** (≥80) · `npm run score` **55/55** (gate 50 PASS).

## Notes

- **Cadence exception** (documented in docs/lifecycle.md): the 4 hidden components were faded out only in v1.4.1 (1 day prior), short of the "hidden ≥1 minor" rule. The collision-bug fast-track + update orphan cleanup (replacing the grace period) justify immediate deletion; the 3 deprecated skipped the hidden stage.
- Release is published by CI on a `v1.5.0` tag push (not done here).

author: hollow
body:
zup was printing hundreds of lines per run from chatty tools that all default to verbose. Each tool needed a different lever; the goal was to keep signal (what actually changed, errors) and drop the rest.

## brew

- `HOMEBREW_NO_ASK=1` — skips the "Do you want to proceed?" confirmation prompt that `brew upgrade`/`install` added in 4.4+ (this was breaking `zup` non-interactively).
- `HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS=1` — drops the "Disable this behaviour by setting `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_CLEANUP=1`" hints that print after every step.
- Both as `local -x` so they only apply during `:brew-update`, not in the rest of the shell.
- `--quiet` on `brew update`, `upgrade`, `bundle install`, `cleanup`.

## git pulls

- `git pull --ff-only --quiet` on the dotfiles repo in `zup` — silences "Already up to date." and the fetch progress on no-op runs; real fast-forwards still show their diff stat.
- Same `--quiet` plus `git switch --quiet` in `zsh/clone` — kills "Already on 'master'" + "Your branch is up to date with 'origin/master'." + the `remote: Enumerating objects…` block whenever `clone` is invoked on an already-cloned repo (every `:tmux-update`, etc.).

## zi update

`-q` alone only suppresses messages for plugins **without** new versions — curl `--progress-bar` frames from snippet downloads, per-plugin git commit logs (`* hash - msg <author>`), `Updating <hash>..<hash>`, `Fast-forward` and the diff stat still leak through. Worse, `-q` also drops the `Updating: <plugin>` headers, so for plugins that **did** update you only see the commit, not which plugin it belonged to.

Instead: drop `-q` and pipe through `sed` + `awk`.

- `sed -E 's/\r/\n/g'` converts the `\r`-overwritten curl progress frames into separate lines so the anchored awk patterns can match them.
- `awk` buffers each `Updating: <plugin>` line and only emits it when a real `* <hash> - msg <author>` commit line follows. Everything else (the commit line itself, `Updating xxx..yyy`, `Fast-forward`, diff stats, curl bars, `From github…`, `* branch … -> FETCH_HEAD`, blank lines) is dropped. Anything that doesn't match a noise pattern (e.g. `Compiling: …`, real errors) passes through, with the pending header flushed first.

Result: one `Updating: <plugin>` line per plugin that actually moved, plus errors and `Compiling:` lines. Plugins with no updates stay silent.

`setopt local_options pipefail` is added at the top of `zup` so the new pipeline still trips `set -e` when `zi` itself fails — without `pipefail`, awk's `0` exit would mask zi failures.

## tpm

`tpm/bin/install_plugins` has no quiet flag and prints `Already installed "<plugin>"` for every plugin on every run. Piped through `grep -v '^Already installed' || :` — the `|| :` absorbs grep's exit 1 when every line was filtered (the common case). Real install/update lines still pass through.

No Jira ticket.

author: mfwolffe
body:
## What

A production linear-scan register allocator for the x86_64 backend, replacing the naive spill-everything allocator at O1+. Default at O1+ is now linear-scan; naive stays at O0 (compile speed) and behind `ARMFORTAS_USE_NAIVE_REGALLOC` as the bisection reference (mirrors arm64).

**Liveness** (`x86/liveness.rs`): backward-dataflow live intervals, ported arch-neutrally from arm64.

**Allocator** (`x86/linearscan.rs`): interval walk with two-tier (caller/callee-saved) selection, eviction, and spill. Uses the **full register file** via fixed-interval modeling:
- `implicit_phys_effects` — the registers isel encodes in the opcode, not the operand vector: Cltd/Cqto (use rax, def rdx), Idiv (use+def rax/rdx), Call/CallReg (clobber all caller-saved). Without this a wide pool miscompiles instantly.
- `build_phys_occupancy` + `phys_free_over` — a vreg never takes a register isel references over its live range. This makes rax/rcx/rdx/rsi/rdi/r8/r9 + xmm0-7 safe to allocate and **subsumes call-crossing** (a call occupies all caller-saved, so crossers fall to callee-saved or spill).
- Spill scratch r10/r11/xmm14/xmm15 reserved out of the pool; spilled operands reuse the naive allocator's proven spill helpers, preserving the 32-bit-def full-quad store rule, Xmm/Xmm128 widths, address-in-vreg/FP-store-to-address forms, and flags adjacency.
- Callee-saves saved to frame slots at block-0 entry, restored before each Ret (emit's epilogue untouched).

This is x10a (baseline + audit + hardening) and x10a-1 (full-register-file). The MirView-vs-fork decision (fork) and a full code/architecture audit informed the design.

## Validation

- **FreeBSD x86_64**: full run_programs matrix 120/120 at all six opt levels; lib 1256; all 14 i128 suites; multifile; clippy; deterministic asm.
- **Linux glibc (hasu)**: full matrix 120/120 all six levels; **valgrind clean (0 errors) on all three class_star select_type fixtures** at O1 (X64-O1-002 class).
- **arm64**: byte-identical by construction — the diff touches zero arm64 source (x86-only).
- **Benchmark gate**: passes, no regressions (size flat; spill traffic on a pressure probe 10→4).
- New high-register-pressure fixture (16 non-foldable simultaneous live values) with OPT_EQ across naive-O0 and linear-O1+.

## Follow-ups (specced, separate sprints)

x10a-2 (move coalescing + live-range splitting), x10b (peephole round 2), x10c (SSE2 synthesis). The allocator is correct and competitive now; those are further code-quality layers.

author: rhynis
body:
Closes #183

## Bug
User (right-side) chat messages wrapping to 2+ lines rendered with the text right-aligned, so the second line sat oddly to the right (e.g. "…phường bình lợi trung ck" → "trung ck" shifted right).

## Cause
The inner content container used `text-right` for user messages, which right-aligns the wrapped text. The bubble's right placement actually comes from `flex-row-reverse` on the message row — not from `text-right` — so the alignment class was unnecessary and caused the ragged-left wrapping.

## Fix (`components/chat/message-bubble.tsx`, CSS only)
- Drop `text-right`/`items-end` from the user content container (bubble stays right-aligned via the row's `flex-row-reverse`).
- Left-align + wrap the **plain-text** (user/staff) bubble: `whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-left` — long words break (no horizontal overflow), newlines preserved, multi-line reads left→right.
- **Assistant** markdown branch and its container are untouched.

No chat logic changed.

## Acceptance — verbatim output

```bash
$ npm run type-check
> tsc --noEmit
(no errors)

$ npm run lint
> eslint . --max-warnings=0
(no errors)

$ npm run build
⚠ The "middleware" file convention is deprecated. Please use "proxy" instead.   # pre-existing Next warning, unrelated
✓ Compiled successfully in 2.7s
```

## Manual verification
- A long user message wrapping to 2-3 lines: bubble right-aligned, text reads left→right cleanly with no right-shift, no horizontal scroll at mobile widths.
- Assistant (left) bubbles unchanged.

author: joelepper
body:
## Context

INCIDENT 2026-06-12: model-less sessions default to `claude-fable-5` (unavailable on this account) on `--resume`. Coordinator + evaluator sessions silently died; workers survived only because their cwd `.claude/settings.json` already pinned sonnet. `settings.json` `"model"` does NOT fix `--resume`'s persisted model selection — only the env-var path reaches the subprocess reliably.

## What this PR does

**`cli/treadmill_cli/commands/team.py`** — `_env_contents()` now emits `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=<model>` per role via a new `_ROLE_MODEL` dict:
- coordinator / evaluator → `claude-opus-4-8`
- worker → `claude-sonnet-4-6`

The launcher already sources each session's per-label `.env` with `set -a` on every team-role start, so the var reaches the subprocess with no further launcher changes needed for team roles.

**`tools/cc-channels/launch-session.sh`** — adds:
```bash
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="${ANTHROPIC_MODEL:-claude-opus-4-8}"
```
after all `.env` sourcing, covering orchestrator labels (`treadmill-alan` etc.) which carry no per-label `.env`. The `${var:-default}` form preserves any value already set (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-6` from a worker's `.env`), so team-role sessions are not affected.

## Scope

Does NOT backfill existing live `.env` files — that one-time backfill was alan's hotfix lane (consistent with the canonical per-role values this render defines).

## Tests

- `TestModelPin` (4 tests) in `cli/tests/test_cli_team_up.py`: coordinator=opus, evaluator=opus, worker=sonnet, cross-role distinct.
- `test_orchestrator_label_carries_opus_model_fallback` in `tools/cc-channels/tests/test_coordinator_launch.py`: strips host `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, verifies opus fallback for treadmill-alan.
- `test_team_role_env_model_not_overridden_by_launcher`: worker .env carries sonnet, verifies launcher fallback doesn't clobber it.

All three suites green: CLI 281 passed, cc-channels 101 passed, team-templates 63 passed.

author: kirillmachuk
body:
## Проблема

При async-эмбеддинге (RAG_ASYNC_EMBED) файл, отправленный в file_search, может быть `embedded: false` пока `embeddingStatus: 'pending'`. Категоризатор вложений (`BaseClient.processAttachments`) пропускал инлайн только при `embedded === true`, поэтому pending async-документ проваливался в ветку инлайна → большой скан кодировался в base64 в запрос к LLM → **413 у анонимайзера/провайдера**, и документ уходил за суверенный периметр (ровно то, что RAG-маршрутизация и должна предотвращать). Это и есть источник «Something went wrong» на больших документах.

## Фикс

Добавлен `file.embeddingStatus != null` в условие пропуска инлайна → любой RAG-маршрутизированный файл (pending/processing/ready/failed) не инлайнится, а ищется через file_search. Для легаси/синхронных файлов (`embeddingStatus` undefined) поведение не меняется.

## Проверка

Тесты BaseClient — 62/62 зелёные. Правка изначально сделана другим агентом; проверена и оформлена.

author: chuanseng-ng
body:
Implements the foundation of the parked post-M6 visualization-scalability
work (docs/viz-scalability.md), removing the two worst bottlenecks for large
designs: client-side layout time and per-frame draw cost.

Phase 1 — renderer hygiene (viz/template.html): batch edges into one Path2D
per (dash, width-bucket) instead of one stroke per edge; cull off-screen
nodes and edges against the transformed viewport; cap labels per frame
(MAX_LABELS); draw a weight-prioritized edge sample above MAX_DRAWN_EDGES with
a "showing X of Y edges" note. No new deps, no API change.

Phase 2 — precomputed layout: new viz/layout.py computes a community-stacked
layout in Python (quotient-graph spring_layout, then per-community subgraphs
offset by sqrt(size)) so the client paints the first frame immediately. New
[layout] extra (numpy/scipy, BSD-3); render_html returns a RenderResult and
takes layout=auto|live|static; tier thresholds are module constants; the
payload carries the resolved mode plus integer x/y; the template's STATIC
branch skips the simulation and picks via d3.quadtree. Missing numpy falls
back to the live tier — the command never fails for a missing extra.

Small designs are unaffected (live tier, plain JSON), so the existing
template/payload tests hold by construction.

author: agentx-asaf
body:
## Symptom

Tab tear-off is fast (the warm window pool makes the window appear instantly), **but it flashes** during the bootstrap. The user asked for the same pulsing-brain splash to cover it.

## Root cause

The brain splash `#startup-loading` (a full-cover overlay: `position:fixed; inset:0; bg; z-index:99999`) was removed **mid-mount** inside `initWave` (`app-init.ts`). But the content-reveal gate (`tab-reveal.ts::scheduleRevealLift`) holds the tab content hidden until "settled" (80ms clean frames / 800ms cap), and `initWaveWrap` un-hides the body immediately. So in the gap between brain-removal and gate-lift, the window showed **bare chrome → empty pane → piecemeal mount, uncovered** — the flashing. Most visible on tear-off: a pool window is shown instantly *with* the brain, then the brain died before the torn-off content had rendered.

## Fix — tie the splash to the reveal gate

- **Don't remove the brain in `initWave`** — let it survive past mount.
- **`tab-reveal.ts`:** new `liftGate()` calls `setTabSwitching(false)` **and** `fadeOutStartupSplash()` at every gate-lift site (settled, hard-cap, and the no-`PerformanceObserver` fallbacks).
- **`startup-splash.ts`** (new): idempotent cross-fade + remove (adds `.fading`, removes on `transitionend` with a timeout safety net). No-op once gone, so ordinary tab switches don't re-trigger.
- **`index.html`:** `#startup-loading.fading { opacity: 0 !important; transition: opacity 200ms }`.
- 30s body safety net also drops the splash as a last resort.

Result: **brain → (cross-fade) → settled content**, nothing uncovered in between. Applies uniformly to all window-init paths (main / new / pool), since they all funnel through `initWaveWrap` → `scheduleRevealLift`.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean on touched files.
- `tab-reveal.test.ts` + `error-display.test.ts` — 10/10 pass.
- Live: HMR-applied; verify by tearing off a tab — brain should hold over the whole bootstrap, then fade to ready content with no bare-chrome flash.

## Note

Also lands `docs/analysis/ANALYSIS_TEAR_OFF_PERF_2026_06_13.md` — the pane-vs-tab tear-off perf/flash analysis. This PR is the shared **P0** (brain coverage). The pane-specific blank-window flash (P0a: show-after-paint) and the floating-pane pool (P0b) are separate follow-ups.

author: leon180
body:
## Slice D2 — step 2 (issue #69): FTS5 on nodes

Additive. Gives the node layer full-text search, mirroring the entries_fts pattern (0007).

### Migration `0015_nodes_fts.sql`
- `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE nodes_fts USING fts5(node_id UNINDEXED, title, body)` — own-content, no triggers.
- Backfills from live (`is_current=1`) nodes so search works the moment it applies.

### Repository
- **CreateNode** now writes the node row + its `nodes_fts` row in one tx (was a bare exec) — atomic.
- **SupersedeNode** drops the retired version's FTS row and indexes the new live one, inside its existing tx → the index always mirrors the live version (node analogue of `TestSupersede_FTSMirrorsLatest`).
- **SearchNodes(query, limit)** — bm25-ranked full-text search over live nodes. `ftsMatchQuery` sanitises arbitrary user text into a quoted-token FTS5 `MATCH` expression, so hostile input (operators, quotes, parens, unterminated quotes) can't trigger a syntax error or inject query logic. Empty query → empty result, not an error. `limit<=0` → default 50.
- `nodeColumns` is now `n.`-qualified (the FTS join makes bare `title`/`body` ambiguous); all node reads alias the table as `n`.

### Tests
search finds created node (title + body) · supersede mirrors live version only · bm25 ranking + limit honoured · hostile-input sanitisation (6 nasty queries) · empty-query nil · backfilled-node searchable. 306 tests pass.

### Notes
Hand-written SQL (sqlc.yaml stops at 0011) → no sqlc drift. `SearchNodes` is wired but the read/UI path still reads entries — switching the UI over to node search lands in the read-path-flip sub-PR (D2f).

author: dandi007
body:
## 问题：legacy e2e 套件整体腐烂，且 self-hosted runner 长期不可用，从未真正跑过

排查发现 desktop/mobile/key-conformance e2e 全部失效，**两个独立根因**（都在 `main` 上，与终端模拟器无关）：

1. **桌面 UI 重构**：sidebar + `session-list` → `tab-bar`（每个 managed session 一个 tab）。测试仍点击早已删除的 `.desktop-shell__sidebar-toggle` / `.session-list__item`。残留的死 CSS 掩盖了这一点。移动端同样漂移：rename/kill/quick-launch 迁到 `.header-action`，底部输入栏改成 inline-expand textarea，特殊键收进可折叠 `.mobile-keys-panel`。

2. **managed-only 过滤**（registry 只展示记录在 managed db 里的 session）：测试用裸 `tmux new-session` 旁路造 session 当 fixture——**这种 session 永远不会出现在任何客户端**。fixture 策略本身从根上就是错的。

两者叠加 + self-hosted runner 长期排队 24h 被 cancel（e2e 从没真跑），所以无人发现。

## 修法：端到端测试只用真实用例

- **fixture 走真实 managed 路径**：`ctx.createSession()` 改为 `POST /templates/:id/run`（UI 的 `+` / quick-launch 按钮走的同一条路），返回服务端分配的名字，409 自动重试（ts14 同秒撞名）。裸 tmux 只保留作 instrumentation（capture-pane / send-keys / kill）。
- **按真实 DOM 重写三套**：desktop 打 `.tab-bar__tab[data-session]` / `__close` / `__new` / 右键 context-menu 改名；mobile 打真实 picker + 输入栏 + keys-panel；key-conformance 经 tab-bar 选中后走 xterm.onData 真键路。
- **SSE 测试按 managed-only 语义重构**：managed session 创建后经 SSE 出现；**unmanaged 外部 session 必须保持隐藏**（锁住该行为）。
- echo/按键敏感用例用 `kb-cc`(plain sh) 模板，输出确定（无 zsh autosuggestion ghost）。
- **fail-fast**：CI 下 `maxFailures:1` + `retries:0` + webServer boot 收紧到 20s——坏测试快速挂掉，不拖到 job 超时上限。

## 验证

本机全套 **36 passed (1.7m)**：desktop 12 + key-conformance 3 + pwa 5 + mobile 16。`bun run lint:tests` OK，tsc 无 e2e 类型错误。

author: adrianwedd
body:
## Why
The `deploy.yml` audit gate (`npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev`, line 32) is a **hard gate** and has been **failing on every push since 2026-06-12**. The last green deploy was PR #463 — **everything since (incl. the 6 Dependabot merges from today) is NOT live.**

## Root cause
Two HIGH advisories, both **build-time only** (not shipped in the static GitHub Pages output):
| Advisory | Package | Source |
|---|---|---|
| GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr | esbuild <0.28.1 (RCE via Deno module install) | astro + vite transitive |
| GHSA-5375-pq7m-f5r2, GHSA-99f4-grh7-6pcq | @grpc/grpc-js <1.14.4 (crash) | GA4 analytics client |

`npm audit fix` only "resolves" these by **downgrading astro to v2** — unacceptable.

## Fix
Force-patch both via npm `overrides` (precedent already exists for fast-xml-parser/yaml):

body:
## Summary

Adds the image + Helm-chart **publish pipeline**, modeled on `jacaudi/cloudflare-operator`, so the operator can be deployed and tested for real. Replaces the build-only `ci.yml`.

- **`pr.yml`** — PR validation: the full `task ci` gate (build/vet/gofmt/`-race` envtest/helm-lint/**CRD+RBAC drift gate**) + a no-push multi-arch image build (Dockerfile breakage protection).
- **`ci-cd.yml`** — on push to `main`: `task ci` → `release` (conventional-commit semantic-release) → `container` (push `ghcr.io/jacaudi/towonel-operator:vX.Y.Z` + `:latest`) → `helm` (push chart to `oci://ghcr.io/jacaudi/charts/towonel-operator`). Image/chart only publish when a new version is cut.
- **`test-build.yml`** — on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`) alpha image+chart from any non-`main` branch (`test-<slug>-<sha>` tags).
- **`.releaserc.json`** — semantic-release config: conventional commits → version, CHANGELOG, and `chart/Chart.yaml` version/appVersion bump.

Uses the shared `jacaudi/github-actions@v0.20.3` reusable workflows (same as cloudflare-operator). The Dockerfile already accepts the `VERSION`/`COMMIT`/`DATE` build-args, and the chart's empty `image.tag` defaults to `.Chart.AppVersion`, so the published chart always references a published image tag.

**Deviation from a pure copy (intentional):** validation uses towonel's `task ci` instead of cloudflare's split `component-lint`/`component-test`/`envtest` jobs — `task ci` additionally runs the generated-artifact **drift gate** (which caught the P2/P3 bugs) and the gofmt/build/vet bundle.

## ⚠️ Prerequisite before the release job can succeed
The `release` job uses semantic-release via a **GitHub App** — it needs repo (or org) secrets **`APP_ID`** and **`APP_PRIVATE_KEY`** configured on this repo. Until those exist, `ci-cd.yml`'s `release` job will fail (the `validate`/PR jobs are unaffected). Set these up, then the first push to `main` will cut the initial version (the accumulated `feat:` commits from P1–P6) and publish the first image + chart.

## Test Plan
- [x] All three workflow YAMLs parse; jobs + reusable-workflow refs (`@v0.20.3`) resolve
- [x] `.releaserc.json` valid; `Chart.yaml` bump `sed` matches only the top-level `version:`/`appVersion:` (not the indented dependency `version:`)
- [ ] (post-secrets) first `main` push cuts a release and publishes image + chart
- [ ] (manual) `helm install ... oci://ghcr.io/jacaudi/charts/towonel-operator` deploys the operator

body:
# Pull Request: Implementation of Phases 1 to 4 (Schema, Auth, UI Shell, Applicant Intake)

## Overview
This PR introduces the foundational implementation for the first four phases of the project. It sets up the core database schema, the complete authentication and RBAC workflows, the reusable RTL-ready UI design system, and the first major business workflow (Applicant Intake). 

The repository has also been cleaned up and is production-ready, passing all CI gates (`typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`).

---

## 🎯 What's Done So Far (Phases 1-4)

### Phase 1: Schema, Domain Constants, Tenant Foundation
- **Milestones**: 
  - Baseline PostgreSQL migration system initialized.
  - Tenant, role, permission, and status constants finalized as strict single sources of truth. 
  - Required schema gaps addressed and repository transaction helpers created for reliable data handling.

### Phase 2: Authentication, RBAC, User Management, Settings
- **Milestones**: 
  - `Better Auth` seamlessly integrated with custom session lifecycles.
  - Internal user CRUD and permission enforcement matrix implemented. 
  - Tenant settings API and Next.js auth client completed, allowing protected routes, identity provisioning, and access revocations.

### Phase 3: UI Shell, Design System, RTL, Tables, Forms
- **Milestones**: 
  - Built out the reusable `@zellforce/ui` library from scratch, preventing tight coupling of UI into logic.
  - Implemented the core UI shell with full **RTL (Arabic/English)** support, local persistence, and density preferences.
  - Deployed shared operational data patterns (tables, forms, drawers, dialogs) and system-wide status visual mappers.

### Phase 4: Applicant Intake Import, Review, Recruitment
- **Milestones**: 
  - Google Sheets applicant sync Adapter completed.
  - Applicant intake logic (mapping, validation, dedupe hashing, and import summaries) built. 
  - Applicant decision, screening, and interview flows connected to the frontend review queue.

---

## 🏗️ Code Architecture Practices Followed

To maintain strict discipline and scalability, all implementation adhered to the following constraints defined in our execution gates:

- **Test-Driven Development (TDD)**: Absolutely no production code was introduced without a failing test first. The `RED` -> verify `RED` -> `GREEN` -> `REFACTOR` cycle was strictly adhered to.
- **Layered Architecture & Separation of Concerns**: We strictly separated **Actions** (which orchestrate product, roles, and business rules) from **Modules** (which own reusable operational mechanics) and **Adapters** (handling provider IO/infrastructure like Google Sheets and Postgres).
- **DRY Principle**: Avoided premature abstractions but rigorously kept roles, statuses, permissions, environment variables, and schemas to a single source of truth to avoid state drift.
- **Deep Modules**: Operational complexities were encapsulated behind simple, highly-leverage Interfaces.

---

## 🚀 Remaining Phases & Milestones

- **Phase 5: Staff Profiles, Filtering, Skills, Groups**
  - *Milestones*: Complete person profile CRUD, skills management, and build high-scale filtering algorithms.
- **Phase 6: Clients, Events, Event Roles, Workspace**
  - *Milestones*: Event creation lifecycle, tenant job roles, and event workspace tabs to assign and lock event parameters.
- **Phase 7: Budget, Wage, Lateness rules**
  - *Milestones*: Budget engine implementation with precise wage calculations and lateness tiers.
- **Phase 8: Assignment and Roster**
  - *Milestones*: Staff assignment pipeline, stage state transitions, roster approvals.
- **Phase 9: WhatsApp and Token pages**
  - *Milestones*: Messaging templates, WhatsApp send logs, webhook idempotency, and worker confirmation tokens.
- **Phase 10: Contracts and Files**
  - *Milestones*: File storage mapping, upload flows, and signed URLs.
- **Phase 11: Supervisor Attendance, Backup, Ratings**
  - *Milestones*: Mobile roster views, attendance locks, backup standby outcomes, and event-day tracking.
- **Phase 12: Payment Review & Export**
  - *Milestones*: Batching, automated calculator integration, and payment approval exports.
- **Phase 13: Reports, Dashboards, Audit views**
  - *Milestones*: High-level reporting and analytics views.
- **Phase 14 & 15: Hardening & Deployment Handover**
  - *Milestones*: Final performance testing, deployment runbooks, security audits, and UAT.

---

## 📅 When Will the App Be Usable & Operationally Useful?

- **Current Status**: The structural and infrastructural foundations are completely laid. The UI shell, secure routing, DB, and the initial applicant recruitment flow are fully working.
- **First Useful Business Value**: The application will begin delivering its first core operational utility at **Phase 6** (Events), allowing you to actively track events.
- **Deep Operational Usefulness**: The app crosses the threshold into a highly valuable, day-to-day tool at **Phase 8** (Assignment and Roster). This milestone connects the recruited staff with the configured events, transforming the app from a simple registry into a living operational pipeline.
- **Full Automation Attained**: By the completion of **Phase 11 & 12**, the loop is closed entirely—bringing workers in, assigning them, tracking attendance via supervisors, and securely outputting payroll exports.

author: johanneslichtenberger
body:
Resolves the long-standing blocker that made GraalVM native images **unusable for writes** (`UnsupportedFeatureError: Support for Arena.ofShared is not active`). **First working native write path for the project** — create / shred / commit / reopen / append-remap / time-travel, all in a native binary.

## Root cause confirmed (reproduced on 25.0.3+9-LTS, byte-identical to 25.0.1)

GraalVM's restriction is on shared-arena **close**, not creation: `Arena.ofShared()` + map + cross-thread read all succeed in a native image; only `close()` throws. And `-H:+SharedArenaSupport` is not a viable workaround — it's rejected outright alongside `+VectorAPISupport` (which we need for the SIMD kernels), and crashes the builder (`SubstrateOptimizeSharedArenaAccessPhase`) when vector code is reachable without it.

## Fix: pluggable arena strategy (`SharedArenas`)

JVM keeps the deterministic `Arena.ofShared()`+`close()` path unchanged. In a native image (detected via `org.graalvm.nativeimage.imagecode`) the allocator uses `Arena.ofAuto()`: identical cross-thread access semantics, but reclamation moves from explicit `close()` to GC (a `Cleaner` unmaps once unreachable) and `close()` becomes a no-op. **Safe because sirix never relies on synchronous unmap for correctness** — superseded generations are immutable, the OS reclaims the mapping, and the on-disk file is fsync'd at commit independently of the mmap.

## Native query perf (measured, -O3 -march=native, same on-disk DB)

Warm steady-state native wins **7-17×** even with the predicate-codegen fallback (AOT: 71% retiring vs 53%, IPC 3.18 vs 2.90): filterCount 17×, sumAge 11×, groupByDept 4.8×.

The real native cost is the **runtime predicate codegen fallback**: `compileToClass` uses `defineHiddenClass`, impossible in AOT, so the first query on each distinct predicate interprets a full cold mmap scan (filterCount cold native ~43 s vs JVM ~12 s; pure-aggregate queries with no codegen are already optimal cold). Cheap mitigation included: default the codegen path off in native images so the executor skips the doomed build + throw/catch + stderr dump — **zero result/behavior change** (verified: identical query results, JVM codegen path unchanged, the 89-case differential gate still green). Deep fixes (build-time predicate kernels; AOT-friendly parallel ingest — native shred is ~8× slower, single-threaded tokenizer) documented as out-of-scope in `docs/NATIVE_IMAGE.md`.

## Verification

Native write smoke: create+commit rev1 → append+commit rev2 (mmap remap) → reopen + time-travel read rev1/rev2 — **passes** (~51 ms). `:sirix-core:test` 9,213/0 (incl. new `SharedArenasTest` 7/7), JVM behavior unchanged. Rebased onto current main (#1034/#1035/#1036); the executor codegen-skip merged cleanly into the post-#1036 `resolveCompiledPredicate` and the differential gate (89 cases) re-confirmed green.

author: henrigeorge
body:
## P4 Nightboard

Realises locked program decision #3 — a **full-bleed canvas mode** the workbench swaps into, visualizing the set/transition analysis the engine **already produces**. No new analysis math, **no new backend endpoint**, no LLM. Local-mode only, behind the workbench gate; the legacy vertical `#setbuilder-section` stays reachable (parity-retired later).

Built entirely on existing REST: `POST /api/setbuilder`, `POST /api/transitions/score`, `GET /api/setbuilder/alternatives`, `GET /api/tracks/{id}/energy`, `POST /api/playlists`.

### What it does
- **Mode, not a place** — `body.nb-active` hides rail + grid + inspector (grid **hidden, never detached** — TASK-033/037) and the canvas owns the body, keeping the global topbar. Entered by the `#nb-open-btn` toolbar verb + `open-nightboard`/`build-set` ⌘K commands.
- **Canvas** — stats strip (mono), four **zone bands** proportioned by `category` duration, a duration-weighted **set-wide energy arc** (NaN-guarded), and a timeline of **tiles** (green-wash mono BPM/key/category chips, sparkline, duration + cue-status, `relaxed` tag) + circular **joints** banded ≥85/≥70. Initial joint scores reuse `transition_score` — zero round-trips.
- **Joint popover** — lazily fetches `/api/transitions/score` for the 3 real `explanation` strings + a tip + ≤2 swap alternatives. **Swap in** replaces the incoming track and re-scores **only** the ≤2 touched joints (`rescoreJoints`), never a full rebuild.
- **Gravity tray** — ranked next-track candidates for the focused/last tile; **Add** inserts after the anchor. **Tile click** re-hosts the **existing P2 inspector** (mode 'track') for in-context cue prep — no second cue engine.
- **Export** — delegates to the shared `_createPlaylist` write path (409-honest), no new write.

### Architecture
New ES modules under `docs/js/v2/nightboard/`: `set-model.js` (pure state + fetch), `canvas.js`, `joint-popover.js`, `tray.js`, `mode.js`. body: ## Bug and impact - `peak_to_ema` could not start from a clean checkout because runtime imports referenced missing `dedup`, H1 context, and market gateway modules. - Ready trade signals were marked as deduplicated before Telegram delivery succeeded, causing alerts to be silently lost on transient send failures. - Soft-mode signals used live entry/stop prices in the dedup key, so one setup could generate repeated Telegram alerts as prices drifted. - The M15 detector reported `local_low_break=True` even when soft mode fired without that break, inflating signal scores. - Moy Arbitr Parser-API document lists were treated as complete and skipped browser/KAD discovery, causing partial Parser-API responses to lose documents. - Year-filtered Parser-API PDF discovery dropped undated URLs, silently losing materials whose dates were unavailable in the Parser-API JSON. ## Root cause - Parser-API court document results were used as a short-circuit rather than merge candidates, and date filtering treated missing event dates as exclusion. ## Fix - Restore the missing `peak_to_ema` runtime modules. - Move dedup marking to the Telegram-success path and use stable M15 setup fields for dedup identity. - Preserve the computed M15 local-low-break flag and require `m15.ready` for final readiness. - Merge Parser-API Moy Arbitr documents with browser/KAD-discovered documents. - author: jegabyte
body:
## Summary

Draft design doc for the **Finding aggregation redesign** — replaces per-turn `Finding`s with one Finding per `(probe_id, asi)` key, with successful attempts collapsed into a nested `attempts: list[Attempt]` field. Confidence becomes Wilson lower bound of `success_count / attempt_count`.

This is a **design artifact for review** before PR #185 (the implementation) lands. No code changes in this PR — just the doc at `docs/_design/finding-aggregation-redesign-2026-06.md`.

## Motivation (live evidence)

A live rc28 scan against the finbot testbench (`cli-397b6d788333`) produced **24 raw Findings across only 16 unique `(probe_id, asi)` keys**:

- `ASI03-PII-001` emitted **4 separate Findings**, all `severity=high`, all `verdict_v2=exploited`, all `confidence=1.0`. That's 4 mirrors of one vulnerability — not 4 distinct bugs.
- 5 other probes emitted 2 findings each. The remaining 10 probes emitted 1 each.
- Every finding has `reproduced_n_of_m=null` because fast mode doesn't N-fold replay — so rc28's `_is_band_eligible` gate falls through to the legacy band-eligible path on every finding.

Same pattern reproduces in the original #159 evidence (`cli-f7ba6f2f7d9a`): 5 HIGH findings on `ASI08-fallback-02`, all mirrors of the same probe. Under aggregation those collapse to 1 finding with `confidence ≈ 0.575` — which becomes the structural fix for the band-flip that rc28 currently bandaids with arbitrary 0.5/0.7 thresholds.

The user's UX direction was explicit: *"findings should be more clear and inside that we need to have all the individual probe attempts and its turns. The finding should [show] individual attempts and clicking [on those] we can see the turns?"*

## What's in the doc

- **§I — Why** (live evidence + user direction)
- **§II — Data model** (Finding changes, new `Attempt` class, deterministic `Finding.id = f"f-{sha256(probe_id:asi)[:12]}"`, aggregation key + edge case decisions locked)
- **§III — Run-loop changes** (`_build_finding` → `_build_attempt`, aggregator in `agent.run()` before `AgentReport`, verify-turn dedup, cross-category dedup contract)
- **§IV — Output surfaces** (`scan.json` schema-v2 bump, SARIF one-result-per-Finding, CLI summary, dashboard nested Attempts section)
- **§V — UX mocks** (Findings tab, slideover with Attempts section, per-attempt turn drill)
- **§VI — Backward compatibility** (`Finding.schema_version` field, legacy v1 compat reader, downstream consumer impact matrix)
- **§VII — Test plan** (cli-* replay assertions + regression guard that no per-turn Findings are written in parallel)
- **§VIII — Rollout** (rc29 lands the redesign; rc28 `_is_band_eligible` gate stays until rc29 live-scan data picks the rc30 confidence threshold via documented decision tree)
- **§IX — Open questions** (6 design choices for Syed + Linus to sign off)
- **§X — PR #185 implementation outline** (files, LOC ≈ 2,220, commit sequence)

## Adversarial review

An adversarial verifier passed the synthesised draft and flagged 4 blocker + 4 major spec ambiguities — all closed inline before commit:

| Gap | Fix |
|---|---|
| SHA-256 hash formula unspecified | Locked to `f"f-{sha256(f'{probe_id}:{asi.value}').hexdigest()[:12]}"` + 48-bit collision bound documented |
| `attempt_count` semantics flip breaks consumers | Added `Finding.schema_version: Literal["finding-v1", "finding-v2"]` + compat reader |
| Verify-turn marker propagation unenforced | Added `Attempt.is_verify_turn: bool` sourced from `metadata.get("verify")` |
| Cross-category dedup interaction prose-only | Locked contract in code: dedup compares aggregated Findings via `representative Attempt.trigger_response` |
| Representative-Attempt selection ambiguous | Locked: `max(bucket, key=lambda a: (a.success, -a.sequence))` |
| Run-loop lifecycle unclear | `_attempt_records` init in `__init__`; no cross-run reuse; documented invariant |
| Regression test wouldn't catch parallel per-turn writes | Added explicit assertion in `test_cli_f7ba6f2f7d9a_aggregation_replay` |
| rc30 threshold speculative | Decision tree in §VIII based on rc29 live-scan distribution |

## What's still open (6 design questions)

1. `Finding.summary` — representative Attempt's summary, or synthesised rollup?
2. SARIF: `attempts[]` in `properties` vs one SARIF result per Attempt?
3. `schema_version` bump — also on SARIF emitter?
4. Dashboard legacy per-turn view as a toggle?
5. Wilson `z` value — lock at 1.96 (cite arXiv:2410.03492)?
6. rc30 threshold — `0.5` default vs `0.6` strict vs data-driven?

## Test plan

- [ ] Syed + Linus review the doc
- [ ] Open questions 1-6 resolved before PR #185 starts
- [ ] PR #185 (implementation) builds against this doc; any design change amends this doc first

cc @as-glac — this is the architectural follow-up to the #159 fix discussion. The rc28 `_is_band_eligible` gate stays in place until the redesign lands; this doc is what PR #185 builds against.

author: joamag
body: ## Summary Fixes the accent long-press picker being hidden / clipped when long-pressing a key on the **first (top) row** of the on-screen keyboard. The **O** key is a good example to reproduce it. Closes #59. ## Root cause The accent popup was a child of `.keyboard-container`, which carries `overflow: hidden` (used for the preview-mode collapse animation). The popup renders above the pressed key via `transform: translate(-50%, -100%)`, so for top-row keys it lands entirely above the container's top edge and gets clipped away. Lower rows worked because the popup stayed inside the container box. It is therefore primarily an overflow-clipping problem (compounded by the popup's stacking order). ## Fix - Anchor the accent popup to the document `body` and position it from the key's viewport rect (`getBoundingClientRect`) instead of container-relative offsets, so it escapes the keyboard container's `overflow: hidden`. - Switch the popup to `position: fixed` and raise its stacking order so it always paints above surrounding elements. - Regenerated `bundle.css` / `bundle.js` via `node scripts/build.js`. ## Testing - `npm test` — 144 passing. - `eslint` on the changed JS — passes. - Not visually verified in a running browser (the keyboard view requires an authenticated session/config that isn't available headlessly); the change is a standard overflow-escape fix. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Fixed an issue where the accent picker appeared hidden behind other elements when long pressing top row keyboard keys. The accent picker now displays correctly with improved layering and visibility. * **Documentation** * Updated release notes to document the accent picker visibility improvement.
