| 4 JSON 读改写原子性 | 🟡 | `$transaction` 只防半写、**未防并发 lost-update** | ⏸ 见「已知残留」 |
| 5 allowedModels 白名单 | 🟡 | **已彻底修复** | 无需改 |
| 6 删组恢复配额 | 🟡 | **已彻底修复** | 无需改 |
| 7 前端全选同步 | 🟡 | **实为无效修复**，原 Bug 仍复现 | ✅ 真正修复 |
| 8 存储小时浮点 | 🟢 | 后端已修，前端 `parseInt` 仍截断 | ✅ 改 parseFloat |
| 9 前端静默失败 | 🟢 | **已彻底修复** | 无需改 |

## 本 PR 修的 4 项

### Bug 7（前端全选同步）— 最关键，原修复无效
`usePermissionsForm` 加的 `useEffect` 修在 `selectAll === true` 的**死状态窗口**里：此时 `selected` 既不参与渲染（UI 走 `selectAll ||` 短路 + `disabled={selectAll}`），也不被 `buildPermissions` 读取（`selectAll ? '*' : ...`）。原 Bug 的真正根因是 `handleToggleAll` 取消全选时**无条件 `setSelected(new Set())` 清空**，保存即塌缩成 `'local'`。
**改法**：取消全选时预填为当前全部 provider，让用户在全集基础上逐个取消。

### Bug 8（存储小时浮点）— 后端修复触达不到前端
后端已去 `Math.floor` 保留小数，但前端 `buildPermissions` 仍 `parseInt(storageLimit)`，`2.5h→2` 在到达后端前就被截断。
**改法**：`storageHoursLimit` 改 `parseFloat`（`minutes`/`concurrent` 保持 `parseInt`），并给存储输入框加 `step="0.5"`/`min="0"` 使小数可输入。

### Bug 3（PUT 空名）— 与 POST 不对称
PUT 改名分支的空名/保留名校验包在 `if (name !== undefined && name.trim())` 内，传 `name:""` 会绕过校验，并在赋值处把组名覆盖成空串。POST 有 `if (!name)` 拦截，PUT 缺对等。
**改法**：`name !== undefined` 时空名直接返回 400。

### Bug 1（系统组同步）— 健壮性
系统组 PUT 的 `SiteSetting.upsert` 与 `user.updateMany` 是两次独立 `await`，半成功会导致「后台显示配额」与「用户表实际配额」不一致（自定义组分支已用事务）。
**改法**：两步包进 `prisma.$transaction`，与自定义组分支对称。

## 已知残留（本 PR 不处理，建议另行跟进）

- **Bug 4 并发 lost-update**：`$transaction` 仅防半写；两个管理员并发改组仍会互相覆盖（无行锁/版本号）。正解需 `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`（含首次创建竞态处理）或乐观锁，属更大、更易引入新失败模式的改动，宜单独评审。低频管理操作，风险可控。
- **编辑组不传播 `storageBytesLimit`**：字节配额恒由 role 派生（`resolveRoleStorageBytesLimit`），编辑组不改 role，常态下无漂移；仅当管理员中途改了 `chat_files_quota_*_mb` 才有滞后，属较小边界。
- **GET 系统组默认值用 `DEFAULT_GROUP_PERMISSIONS`，与 `getDefaultQuotasForRole` 双源**：当前数值一致，但会随演进漂移。统一需处理 `maxConcurrentSessions` 语义，单独重构更稳。

## 验证

- `type-check`：仅 `pdf-parse`/`exceljs` 缺包的**既有假错**，不在本改动文件内。
- `lint`：仅既有 warning，本改动零新增。
- 相关单测：`quota` / admin page / 角色到期 共 **50 passed**。
- **浏览器实测**（admin 登录 → 用户组）：Bug 7 取消全选后 provider 复选框**保持勾选+可用**（旧代码会变未勾→塌缩成 `local`）；Bug 8 存储输入框可输入 `2.5`（`stepMismatch:false`）；面板渲染无 console 报错。

author: frawau
body:
## Summary
Fixes an artificial 1-lap gap created at a red flag. Two nose-to-tail karts could end up a full lap apart purely because one crossed S/F just *before* the flag (lap counted) and the other just *after* (crossing was during suspension → dropped).

**Server** — `classify_red_flag_crossing()` unifies the cases. The lap a kart is *on* when the flag falls counts whichever side of the flag it completes, with its time voided:
- in-flight (crosses during suspension, previous crossing before the flag) → counts, time void
- a whole extra lap done under suspension → dropped
- straddling (completes after resume) → counts, time void (already shipped)

So both cars keep the lap; only the (meaningless) time is voided.

**Simulator** — adds `inflight_window` (default 3 s). On pause the sim now keeps firing for that window so cars already at the line cross before the field is held — modelling a real decoder (which reports every crossing, including post-flag ones) and making the in-flight case deterministic to test.

## Test Plan
- [x] `classify_red_flag_crossing` unit tests (in-flight / extra-lap / straddling / no-previous / count-during-suspension) — 14-test suite green on toulouse
- [ ] **Live (pending):** switch toulouse to this branch, `rebuild` + `deploy-timing`, run MAIN with a pause; confirm two nose-to-tail cars stay on the same lap and the in-flight laps show as counted-with-voided-time (no `during`/dropped cascade)

- Implement server-side flow to expire notified reservations, notify next in queue, and allow users to fulfill or cancel reservations when a copy becomes available.

author: jonatanghub
body:
## `/metrics` endpoint (Prometheus)

Completes the metrics item of the observability milestone (the one bullet not
covered by #18). A `/metrics` endpoint in Prometheus text-exposition format.

### Why this design

The worker writes `audit_log` (one row per cycle: `emails_processed`,
`drafts_saved`, `error_count`). The endpoint **aggregates from that table** (plus
`email_accounts`), so the counters are accurate **across the api/worker process
boundary** — no shared in-process state or pushgateway needed.

### Exposed metrics

```
mailflow_up                       1 if the API can read the DB, else 0
mailflow_cycles_total             cycles recorded
mailflow_emails_processed_total   emails processed across all cycles
mailflow_drafts_saved_total       draft replies saved
mailflow_errors_total             per-email errors
mailflow_accounts_total           configured email accounts
```

On a DB read failure the scrape still returns **200** with `mailflow_up 0`, so
Prometheus can alert on the target being unhealthy.

### Security

Unauthenticated like `/health`; exposes only **deployment-wide totals** (no PII,
no per-org). Documented to restrict to the scraping network at the reverse proxy.

### Verification

- Tests: aggregates from a seeded `audit_log` (+ `HELP`/`TYPE` headers present);
  DB-down path → `mailflow_up 0`.
- api suite **104 passed**, coverage **80%**; `ruff` + format clean.

## Summary

Adds a second entry path to the AI Assistant tab. Authors can now paste or upload a `.docx` of an outline they already wrote, instead of generating from scratch.

## The 3 modes

| Mode | Flow | AI involvement |
|---|---|---|
| **Build full course** | parse-outline → OutlineEditor review → existing `/generate` → LOAD_COURSE | AI writes prose from author's structure |
| **Shells only** | parse-outline → OutlineEditor review → empty `contentBlocks` → LOAD_COURSE | AI only structures the outline |
| **Convert finished docx** | mammoth → headings→sections, paragraphs→`text.content` verbatim → LOAD_COURSE | No AI rewrite — prose preserved exactly |

## Architecture

All three modes feed the **existing** outline→generate→LOAD_COURSE pipeline. Nothing saves until the author hits Save (existing `/save` → `InteractiveCourse.save()`, fires word-count hook).

## Backend additions — `courseBuilder.js` (surgical, before `export default router`)

- `parseOutlineText()` — Anthropic converts author text → outline JSON, preserves their section titles verbatim
- `buildShellsFromOutline()` — builds course with `contentBlocks: []` per section
- `buildCourseFromDocxProse()` — maps headings → section titles, paragraphs → `text` blocks (field: `content` per BLOCK_FIELD_REFERENCE.md). **Never rewrites prose.**
- `POST /parse-outline` — paste path, modes 1 & 2
- `POST /import-docx` — multer memory + mammoth extraction, all modes

## Frontend additions — `AIAssistantTab.jsx` (surgical)

- Entry-mode toggle: "Generate from topic" (existing, untouched) / "Import my outline" (new)
- Mode selector (radio): full / shells / convert + descriptions
- Large textarea (paste) + `.docx` file picker (ref-driven, overrides paste if both provided)
- CE hours / category / level fields reused from existing params
- `handleImportSubmit` — routes to `/parse-outline` or `/import-docx` per input type + mode
- `handleBuildShells` — client-side: builds shell course from reviewed outline → LOAD_COURSE
- `OutlineEditor` gains `actionLabel` prop → shows "🗂 Build Shells →" for shells mode, "✨ Generate Full Course" otherwise

## Constraints honored
- ✅ BLOCK_FIELD_REFERENCE.md read: `text` block prose field = `content`
- ✅ Convert mode never rewrites author prose (ACEP Gold Standard)
- ✅ `interactive-course.html` not touched

Implements the missing #722 canary prerequisite found before live activation: scheduler enablement alone can create `runtime=unconfigured` queue work. author: eugendimant
body:
Cut fresh from `main` (post-#21). Three feedback items in one round. Version **1.5.2.2** (app/core in lockstep).

## 📖 Word definitions on played rows
> *"Sometimes I (or the bot) plays a word I don't recognise."*

**Hover or tap any played row — yours *or* the duel bot's — to learn what that word means.** A faint **ⓘ** hints the row is interactive; a one-line gloss appears as a native hover tooltip (desktop) **and** a tap-to-reveal card (mobile, via CSS `:focus`/`:hover` — no JS needed, survives Streamlit's sanitizer).

- New **`avoidle/definitions.py`** fetches best-effort from **Wiktionary's public REST API**, which covers all four languages (en/de/es/ru) and returns the definition *in the word's own language*. One network call per unique `(word, language)`, cached process-wide.
- **Fully offline-safe — definitions can never break a game.** No network, a 404, junk JSON, or a slow host all resolve to a quiet *"no definition found"*, and a small **circuit breaker** stops trying after a few consecutive failures so a no-egress deployment never eats repeated timeouts.
- Glosses are session-cached and **cleared on new-game / language switch**, so a spelling never carries a stale meaning from another language.

> Note: the lookup needs outbound HTTPS to `*.wiktionary.org` (Streamlit Cloud has it). On a locked-down host the feature simply shows *"no definition found"* — everything else works unchanged.

## ⏱️ "Time crunch" is now a *choice*, not a fixed 3:00
> *"Give a few suggested options for time per move instead of imposing 3 minutes."*

The turn timer is still **off by default** and still **locks before your first word**, but now you pick the pace from a tidy selector that appears only when the timer is on:

**⚡ 30 sec · 🏃 1 min · 🚶 2 min · 🧘 3 min · 🐢 5 min** — default **2:00**.

Every deadline (new game, each play, and the duel reset after the bot replies) honors the chosen length; the existing overtime ladder (eat a hint → a peek → an undo → forfeit) is unchanged.

## ⌨️ Your physical keyboard works in either input mode (desktop)
> *"On the computer, can I just type with my keyboard no matter which input option is selected?"*

Yes — new **`inject_keyboard_bridge`**:
- **Clickable mode:** a keydown listener on the parent document maps real keystrokes onto the on-screen keys — a letter clicks its key, **Enter** submits, **Backspace** deletes — reusing every existing button callback, so the buffer, clue colours and rules behave exactly like tapping. Language-agnostic (matches keys by their label, so Cyrillic works too).
- **Typing mode:** the text box **auto-focuses** when nothing else is, so you can just start typing — and again after each submit — without clicking in first.
- A **single handler** is kept on the parent `window` and replaced every rerun, so listeners never stack up and double-type. Harmless no-op on touch devices.

## Verification
- **205 tests pass** (+18 new): Wiktionary parsing / caching / circuit-breaker (`tests/test_definitions.py`), board-definition embed states incl. the bot's word, timer-length choices + lock-after-first-move, and the keyboard-bridge script (routing, single-handler guard, type-mode autofocus).
- **pyflakes clean**; headless boot returns **HTTP 200** with a clean log.
- `avoidle/__init__.py` and `_EXPECTED_CORE_VERSION` bumped together to **1.5.2.2** (hot-redeploy guard intact); README changelog updated.

body:
## What
Adds a `CONTRIBUTING.md` and links it from the README header (a `PRs welcome` badge). The guide collects the conventions already used across the repo into one place, organized by the four contribution types: a new **skill**, a new **LLM gateway**, a **community skill pack** listing, and **core fixes**.

It documents:
- **Skills** — the frontmatter contract (`requires:`/`mcp:` two-tier semantics), the scaffolding commands (`./new-from-template`, `./add-skill`, `create-skill`, `ai-build` issues), the sandbox-fallback requirement, and the `./generate-skills-json` regen step the CI gate enforces.
- **Gateways** — the existing five-file checklist (native vs sidecar tiers), linking to the README's `#adding-a-gateway` section.
- **Skill packs** — the README-row + `skill-packs.json` + `skills-pack.json` manifest requirements.
- **CI gates** — what `ci-skills-json` and `ci-capabilities-parity` enforce and how to satisfy them locally.
- PR conventions: branch from main, one change per PR, squash-merge expectations.

## Why
A 510-star repo with 170 forks and active external contributors (e.g. the open BEAMR gateway PR #418) had **no CONTRIBUTING.md**. Every contributor was reverse-engineering branch naming, the CI gates, the skill-submission flow, and the gateway pattern from existing PRs. Surfaced as the top community-health gap in yesterday's `repo-actions` audit. Lowering fork/contribution friction is a direct lever on ecosystem growth.

## Changes
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (new): full contributor guide, anchored to real files and README sections — every internal link verified to resolve.
- `README.md`: added a `PRs welcome` shield linking to `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the header badge block.

## Notes
- Docs-only — touches no `skills/**`, `aeon.yml`, or taxonomy paths, so neither CI gate is triggered; no `skills.json` regen needed.

全ステージ共通で、ステージ開始時に黄色い玉（`LogTrigger` = ストーリーログ収集アイテム）が重力で落下し、床をすり抜けて画面外へ消えていくバグを修正しました。

## 原因

`LogTrigger` 自身は生成時に `setAllowGravity(false)` / `setImmovable(true)` を設定していましたが、`GameScene.buildLogTriggers()` で `this.logTriggers.add(trigger)` によりグループへ追加した瞬間、Phaser Arcade の `Group.add()` がグループ既定値（重力ON・可動）でボディ設定を**上書き**していました。

これは砲台敵の落下バグ（既存コミット `6ea5022`）と同系統の問題です。

## 修正内容

- `src/entities/LogTrigger.ts`: 物理ボディの静止設定を `configureBody()` に集約し public 化（コンストラクタからも呼ぶ）
- `src/scenes/GameScene.ts`: `buildLogTriggers()` でグループ追加**後**に `trigger.configureBody()` を再適用（既存の `Enemy.configureBody()` と同パターン）
- `tests/unit/entities/LogTrigger.test.ts`: 静止不変条件を守る回帰テストを追加（グループ上書き → 再適用ケースを含む）

これにより、玉は本来の位置に静止し、ストーリーログ収集アイテムとして正しく機能します（落下現象のみが解消）。

author: simons-plugins
body:
Surfaced commissioning a multi-sensor Matter node (HomePod mini: temperature + humidity).

## 1. Readings showed 6 decimal places
Sensor handlers rounded the value, but it reached Indigo as a bare `{key, value}` — and Indigo renders a `Number` state at full float precision without a `uiValue`/`decimalPlaces` (a `round(x, 2)` still displays as `21.340000000001`). The plugin set neither anywhere.

- New `ClusterHandler.format_kv()` hook converts a `{state: value}` dict into an Indigo `updateStatesOnServer` kvlist. The sensor base overrides it to attach `uiValue` + `decimalPlaces`.
- `device_sync` now routes **every** handler-produced state write (live updates, node events, node-scoped battery fan-out, create-time priming) through `handler.format_kv()`.
- Precision/units: Temperature `21.5 °C`, Humidity `47.5%`, Illuminance `123 lux`, Pressure `1013 hPa`, Flow `2.5 m³/h`, CO₂ `ppm`, PM2.5 `µg/m³`. Boolean sensors (motion/contact) pass through untouched.

## 2. Devices named "(endpoint 1)"
- A node's devices now read `{name} - {role}` (e.g. **HomePod - Temperature** / **HomePod - Humidity**) via a device-type → role map. Endpoint-number naming is kept only as a fallback (unmapped type) or to disambiguate genuinely identical siblings (a 4-outlet strip → `- Switch 1..4`). Bridged children with their own identity are unaffected.
- `dev.model` is stamped with the product name on every device, so a node's siblings share one **Model** column value.

## 3. Master device + children — investigated, kept standalone
Indigo's only master/children mechanism is the **Device Factory** (shared `model` + `subType`, tabbed editor), which is dialog-driven and fights the automated Domio-commission + WebSocket-reconcile creation path — and the children stay independent devices for triggers/control-pages/Domio regardless. Standalone devices + role naming + shared model column deliver the grouping without the factory machinery.

## Notes
- **Existing** devices: the display self-heals on the next reading; names only change on a commission (authoritative) pass, so re-commission or delete+reload to pick up the new names.
- Tests: +sensor formatting, +role naming/model stamping, updated Patio multi-endpoint naming. **773 pass.**

body:
Scope = design system, Header, Footer, and a real homepage. No calculators, content engine or data files (those are later tasks).

Follows the `frontend-design` skill process: plan tokens → self-critique against generic defaults → build.

## Concept — "Modernist Grid, Electric Charge"
Chandigarh's planned-city modernism (Le Corbusier's sector grid, béton-brut concrete, signage) meets EV energy. Editorial publication, not a brochure.

## What's in this PR
- **Tokens** (`src/styles/global.css`, wired into `BaseLayout`): the brief's palette + a few derived tokens (`--charge-ink` so blue text passes AA on concrete, dark-footer tones), a fluid type scale, focus styles and a `prefers-reduced-motion` floor.
- **Type (3 roles, self-hosted via `@fontsource` for CWV):** *Space Grotesk* (geometric display), *Source Serif 4* (editorial serif **body** — inverts the serif-display cliché, signals "real publication"), *Space Mono* (data/labels, geo-coordinates).
- **Signature — `ChargeBar.astro`:** a segmented EV charge indicator whose modules echo Corbusier's brise-soleil/formwork. Used as brand mark (full = "charged"), section marker, and an **animated hero gauge**; hub markers **fill to full on hover**.
- **`Header.astro`** (sticky; charge glyph + mono nav) and **`Footer.astro`** (dark "foundation" band; About / Editorial Policy / RSS placeholders + `30.73°N 76.78°E` meta).
- **Real homepage** (`index.astro`, genuine copy): hero thesis → the four hubs (Guides / Comparisons / Calculators / News) → trust strip → soft CTA to `evchandigarh.com`.

## Self-critique vs the three AI defaults
Not look #1 (serif is *body* not display; accent is electric-blue not terracotta) · not look #2 (light concrete base, no acid-green) · hairlines kept spacious/modular to avoid look #3's dense broadsheet. Boldness spent only on the charge motif + grid.

## Quality floor
Skip link, semantic landmarks, `:focus-visible` (charge on light, signal on dark), `aria-hidden` decorative motif, reduced-motion respected, responsive 4→2→1 columns.

## Verification
`npm run build` passes; SEO head intact; 15 font files + design CSS bundled; gauge renders animated. Note: couldn't screenshot — the Playwright browser CDN is blocked by this environment's network policy, so visual review was code-level.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact **1. Remote tasks stuck after single-node restart (critical)** When Semaphore restarts while remote runner tasks are still executing, `TaskPool.GetTask` only hydrated from the database in HA mode. On a single-node deployment the in-memory pool is empty after restart, so `UpdateRunner` silently dropped all progress reports. Tasks remained stuck in `running` in the database even after the runner completed successfully. **Trigger:** Restart the Semaphore server (upgrade, crash, deploy) while one or more remote runner tasks are actively executing. **2. History page crash on websocket events (high)** `History.vue` called `this.items.some()` without a null guard when handling websocket updates. If an update arrived before the first paginated load finished (or after a failed load), the History view threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. **Trigger:** Open project History while tasks are actively updating; websocket event arrives before `/tasks/last` returns. ## Root cause - HA work added `HydrateTaskRunnerFromDB` behind an `util.HAEnabled()` guard in `GetTask`, leaving single-node restarts without the same recovery path already used across HA nodes. - Task pagination added websocket reload throttling to `History.vue` but omitted the null guards already present in `TaskList.vue`. ## Fix and validation - Always hydrate from DB in `GetTask` when a task is not in the in-memory pool (same behavior HA already relied on). - Mirror `TaskList.vue` null guards and throttle state initialization in `History.vue`. - Added `TestUpdateRunner_RunningTaskInDBButNotInPoolAccepted` covering post-restart runner completion. ``` go test ./api/runners/... ./services/tasks/... -count=1 ```

author: spacebass11
body:
## Problem

`scripts/build_iso.ps1` validates that `-UnattendFile` exists but never checks whether it's well-formed XML. A malformed answer file gets staged into the ISO without complaint. The failure only surfaces later:

- Pre-2026-05-17: Windows Setup at first boot silently ignored the bad XML and dropped through to manual OOBE.
- Post-2026-05-17 (per the existing routine entry): `unified_winpe_deploy.ps1`'s `Start-Deployment` runs `[xml](Get-Content $UnattendFile -Raw)` and aborts pre-flight, so the end user gets a deploy failure on their hardware.

Either way, the admin packaging the ISO never sees the parser diagnostic on the workstation where they could fix it — they ship a broken ISO and hear about it from the field.

## Root cause

The build step trusts `Test-Path -PathType Leaf` plus `Resolve-Path` and copies the file straight into `staging\configs\`. The runtime guard in the deploy script is defence in depth, not the right layer to fail at.

## Files changed

- **`scripts/build_iso.ps1`** — added a `try { [xml](Get-Content -Path $UnattendFile -Raw) } catch { throw ... }` block immediately after the existing existence check. Error message names the file, the parser's `Exception.Message`, and points at `docs/UNATTEND.md` section 6.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — `## Unreleased / ### Changed` bullet at the top describing the new build-time guard.
- **`docs/claude-routine-log.md`** — routine entry with investigation notes, verification, and outstanding-backlog snapshot (so the next routine run doesn't re-investigate this area).

## Verification

`pwsh` installed once per session per the CLAUDE.md note (PowerShell/Releases v7.4.6 tarball into `/opt/pwsh/`).

- `pwsh -NoProfile -File ./tests/test_parse.ps1` → **48 passed / 0 failed** both before and after the edit. No regression in `build_iso.ps1` syntax or required-functions list.
- Behavioral check: extracted just the new `if ($UnattendFile)` block into a standalone test script and exercised three inputs:
  - Well-formed `<unattend xmlns="...">...</unattend>` → exits 0.
  - Malformed (missing `</unattend>` closing tag) → throws with the full parser diagnostic naming the file and a docs reference; exits 1.
  - Non-existent path → throws the existing `"UnattendFile not found"` error; exits 1.
- The `[xml]` cast is a PSv5.1-safe core .NET cast and matches the pattern already shipping in `unified_winpe_deploy.ps1`, so it imposes no new dependencies and won't fail on any input the runtime guard already accepts.

## Risks / follow-ups

Minimal. The change is build-time-only and additive — it fails a build that would have produced a broken ISO. No destructive code paths (diskpart, DISM apply, BCDBoot) touched. No new parameters, no new dependencies.

The matching runtime guard in `unified_winpe_deploy.ps1` stays in place as defence in depth (someone could hand-edit a `deploy.args` to point at a malformed XML staged outside the ISO build, or replace the file on the USB after the fact).

Follow-ups recorded in the routine log but not taken this pass:

- A Pester row in `tests/validation-gates.Tests.ps1` asserting that `Start-Deployment` returns `$false` when handed a malformed `-UnattendFile`. Open PRs #69 / #75 are already in flight on adjacent Pester gates and may have conventions worth aligning with.
- `Show-ImageList` / `Show-ImageSelection` listing-render factoring — open PR #56 already chasing this.

body: ## Bug and impact - Inference startup extracted MODEL_ARTIFACT_URI tarballs unsafely on Python 3.11, allowing malicious artifact archives to write outside MODEL_DIR. - Manual workflow_dispatch inputs were interpolated directly into shell scripts/heredocs, allowing command execution or malformed release metadata from crafted dispatch inputs. - Training handoff metadata could point at mutable latest artifacts, and failed-quality models could still publish artifacts. ## Root cause - tarfile.extractall() only used Python 3.12's filter path and fell back to unfiltered extraction on the Docker image's Python 3.11 runtime. - Workflow inputs were embedded as expressions in run blocks instead of being passed as environment data and serialized safely. - Manifests used latest paths and train.py did not enforce the quality evaluation before artifact publication. ## Fix - Validate tar members before extraction, rejecting path traversal, links, and special files; preserve legacy regression_model.joblib loading. - Pass dispatch inputs through env, validate newline-sensitive values, and generate workflow JSON with json.dump. - Emit run-scoped manifest paths and fail training before publication when quality evaluation fails. ## Validation - python3 -m pytest -q - python3 -m ruff check .

author: stefan-burke
body:
## What

Adds a new code-quality check to `test/lib/code-quality.test.ts` that detects the smell you described: a function where a given positional argument is **always** passed the same constant literal across every call site.

> e.g. if every call is `fooMethod("foo", bar)` / `fooMethod("foo", baz)`, the first argument is redundant and should be a default parameter or constant.

## How it works

- A small hand-written lexer scans `src/` (`.ts` + `.tsx`), skipping comments and string/template literals, and extracts every `name(...)` call site with its top-level arguments. This matches the regex-driven style of the existing code-quality checks (no AST dependency added).
- Call sites are grouped by callee name. For any callee with **3+ call sites**, each argument position present in *every* call is checked — if all calls pass the *same constant literal* there, it's flagged.
- Only literal arguments count (strings, numbers, booleans, `null`, `undefined`, template literals). Variables/expressions are ignored, since identical *names* rarely mean identical *values*.

## Tuning knobs (all near the top of the new `describe` block)

- `MIN_CALL_SITES` (default `3`) — how many calls before a constant argument is suspicious. At `2` the check also surfaces idiomatic/intentional cases (e.g. crypto `extractable` flags, a fixed role), so `3` keeps it low-noise.
- `IGNORED_CALLEES` — builtin methods whose constant literal args are idiomatic, not redundant (`padStart`, `toFixed`, `lastIndexOf`, …).
- `ALLOWED_CONSTANT_ARGS` — per-`callee#position` allowlist for intentional cases (currently empty).

## Real finding it caught

The check immediately flagged `editPushResult(...)` in `features/admin/built-sites.ts`, which was passed the same `"Deadline could not be pushed to the site"` failure string at all three call sites. That argument is now a default parameter and the redundant argument removed from the call sites.

author: chrisrackauckas-claude
body:
## Problem

The Downgrade job (LTS Julia 1.10, strict `allow_reresolve: false`) pins every direct dependency to its declared `[compat]` lower bound, then builds and tests. The test suite loads **MethodOfLines** (a `[extras]` test dependency with no `[compat]` entry).

At the old floors, the downgrade resolve was **Unsatisfiable**:

```
ERROR: LoadError: Unsatisfiable requirements detected for package MethodOfLines [94925ecb]:
 MethodOfLines log:
 ├─restricted by compatibility requirements with SymbolicUtils to versions: [0.8.3-0.8.4, 0.9.0-0.11.0]
 └─restricted by compatibility requirements with ModelingToolkit to versions: uninstalled — no versions left
   └─ModelingToolkit restricted to versions 9.0.0 by an explicit requirement
```

### The conflicting pins (why the old floors were impossible)

1. `ModelingToolkit = "9, 10, 11"` floors MTK at **9.0.0**. But **no published MethodOfLines version supports MTK 9.0.0** — the lowest, MethodOfLines `0.11.0`, requires `ModelingToolkit = "9.7.1 - 9"`. So at MTK 9.0.0, MethodOfLines is uninstallable. (Older MethodOfLines only support MTK 8.)
2. Raising the MTK floor to **9.7.1** lets MethodOfLines `0.11.0` install, but MTK 9.7.1 requires `OrdinaryDiffEq = "6.73.0 - 6"`, while the old `OrdinaryDiffEq = "6, 7"` floor pins **6.0.0** — too low.
3. `OrdinaryDiffEq 6.73.0` itself still fails: it requires `FastBroadcast = "0.2"`, whereas `OrdinaryDiffEqSDIRK` (floor 1.2.0) requires `FastBroadcast = "0.3.5 - 0.3"` — **no overlap**. `OrdinaryDiffEq 6.80.0` is the first version that admits `FastBroadcast = "0.2 - 0.3"`, which overlaps SDIRK's `0.3.5`. So **6.80.0 is the smallest co-installable OrdinaryDiffEq floor**.

`OrdinaryDiffEqSDIRK` (1.2.0) and `SciMLBase` (2.69.0) floors are left unchanged — they co-install fine once MTK = 9.7.1 and OrdinaryDiffEq = 6.80.0.

## Fix

Raise two `[compat]` lower bounds to the smallest versions that resolve at the downgrade minimum:

| Dep | Old floor | New floor | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ModelingToolkit` | `9` | `9.7.1` | lowest MTK any MethodOfLines (0.11.0) supports |
| `OrdinaryDiffEq` | `6` | `6.80.0` | MTK 9.7.1 needs ODE ≥ 6.73.0; 6.80.0 is the first that shares a `FastBroadcast` with the SDIRK floor |

This raises only lower bounds; no upper bound is touched, no test logic or tolerance is changed.

## Resolve verification

Reproduced locally on Julia 1.10 (the LTS downgrade floor):

- **Old floors** (`ModelingToolkit = 9`, `OrdinaryDiffEq = 6`): pinning every direct dep to its floor → `Unsatisfiable requirements detected for package MethodOfLines` (matches CI).
- **New floors**: pinning every direct dep to its floor, and separately running `julia-downgrade-compat`'s `downgrade.jl` in the real `deps`/LTS configuration, both **resolve successfully** — manifest pins MTK 9.7.1, MethodOfLines 0.11.0, OrdinaryDiffEq 6.80.0, OrdinaryDiffEqSDIRK 1.2.0, SciMLBase 2.69.0.

Master's non-downgrade CI is unaffected (the package already resolves at the top of its compat ranges; the master CI red was only a Codecov upload-auth error, not a test failure).

Ignore until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.

author: jankr02
body:
## Summary

Bugs found while end-to-end testing the booking flow (manual API + Stripe CLI test-mode + real browser checkout). Seven focused commits across the NestJS backend and Angular frontend.

## Fixes

- **A — Post-payment redirect 404 + missing verify endpoint** (`stripe.service.ts`, `bookings.controller/service`): Stripe `success_url`/`cancel_url` pointed at non-existent `/booking/*` routes with a mismatched query param, and the `verify-payment` endpoint the success page calls didn't exist → customers hit a 404 after paying. Now point at the real `/buchung/bezahlung-*?bookingId=` routes and add a public `GET /bookings/:id/verify-payment`.
- **B — Full-course confirmation/cancellation mails crashed** (`payments.service.ts`, `booking-email.service.ts`): full-course bookings have no session, but the side-effects + email loader dereferenced `booking.session`, throwing a `TypeError` that suppressed the confirmation mail (7/9 courses). Null-guard the reminder + fall back to the course/earliest session.
- **C — Full-course courses unbookable in the UI** (`courses.service.ts`, `course-detail-response.dto.ts`, `booking-form`, `schedule-section`, shared types): the booking modal forced session selection for every course. Expose `bookingMode`, skip the session step for full-course (book without `sessionId`), render a course-level schedule view.
- **D — Button labels touched the border** (`button.component.scss`): raise content horizontal padding 8 → 16 px.
- **E — `truefalse` in cancellation/refund mails** (`template.service.ts`): `eq`/`gt` were value helpers used as block helpers; make them dual block/value.

## Review follow-ups (in this PR)

- **Security + code-review — verify-payment fail-closed**: replaced a blacklist trim with an explicit whitelist projection so no future booking field can leak on this public, owner-check-less endpoint (GDPR data minimisation).
- **Code-review — success-page payment race**: the page declared success on the first response without checking payment status; the `checkout.session.completed` webhook can lag the browser redirect (always for async SEPA), so it now re-polls until paid/confirmed (2 s interval, 30 s timeout) with a "Zahlung wird verarbeitet" state on timeout.

## Testing

- **Backend (API + Stripe CLI):** happy path, free course, checkout expiry, idempotency, real refund roundtrip, full-course mail (no crash), verify-payment whitelist (pending → paid, no PII leak).
- **Browser (end-to-end):** paid single-session + full-course booking → Stripe test card `4242…` → webhook → CONFIRMED → success page; abort path; full-course modal session-skip; schedule-section.
- **Email:** all 14 templates rendered via Ethereal.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact **FD_CLOEXEC regression (f560cb5 / #14):** When migrating `daemon` from `libc::fcntl` to `redox_syscall`, `F_SETFD` was passed `CallFlags::FD_CLOEXEC` (`0x8000`) instead of `O_CLOEXEC` (`0x0100_0000`). The kernel only checks `O_CLOEXEC` for `F_SETFD`, so close-on-exec was never set on `INIT_NOTIFY` pipe fds handed to scheme daemons (`logd`, `randd`, etc.). **Trigger:** Normal boot — every scheme daemon calls `get_fd("INIT_NOTIFY")` during startup. **Impact:** Security hole — the notify pipe fd can leak to child processes if a daemon later `exec`s without closing it. **Bootstrap spawn sync:** Parent `spawn()` in `bootstrap/exec.rs` ignored pipe read failures and could continue with `new_fd == usize::MAX` if a bootstrap child (initfs/procmgr/initns) crashed before sending its capability fd. **Trigger:** Bootstrap child panic/OOM before capability handoff. **Impact:** Boot corruption / confusing late panics instead of an immediate, actionable failure. ## Root cause - Conflated `CallFlags::FD_CLOEXEC` (syscall message flags, bit 15) with `O_CLOEXEC` (fcntl descriptor flags, `0x0100_0000`). - Bootstrap `spawn()` used `_ => break` on pipe sync instead of checking `call_ro` result like `init/service.rs`. ## Fix and validation - Use `syscall::flag::O_CLOEXEC` in `daemon::get_fd`. - Mirror `init/service.rs` error handling in bootstrap `spawn()` (panic on `Ok(0)`, wrong fd count, or syscall error). - `cargo check -p daemon` passes.

body:
## 概要

親 #1478（番号参照排除）の Sub-Issue。`CHANGELOG.md` / `CHANGELOG.ja.md` の旧エントリ（`[0.1.x]` / `[0.2.x]` 系統）に残存していた 1-2桁の `(#NN)` 形式 Issue/PR 番号参照を除去する。PR #1486（#1483）は 3-4桁のみを対象としていたため取り残されていた分。

Closes #1488

## 変更内容

| ファイル | 除去件数 | 形式 |
|---------|---------|------|
| `CHANGELOG.md` | 42 | 末尾 `(#NN)` / `(#39, #41)` / `(#18, #20)` |
| `CHANGELOG.ja.md` | 42 | 同上 |

いずれもエントリ末尾の純粋な PR provenance 括弧で、散文中の裸参照・アンカーリンクはなし。機能レベルの説明文は番号なしで自己完結する。

## 受入基準

- 検証は `rg '#[0-9]+' CHANGELOG.md CHANGELOG.ja.md` で（3-4桁限定ではなく）**全桁が 0 件** ✅
- diff は末尾括弧の純粋な suffix 除去のみ（行数不変、説明文不変）

## 判断: 番号参照検出 lint の閾値拡張について

**結論: `number-reference-check.sh` の検出 band は 3-4桁（`#[0-9]{3,4}`）のまま維持し、1-2桁へは拡張しない。**

評価（誤検知リスクとのトレードオフ）:
- 現状の number-free surface（CHANGELOG×2 + lint.md）に 1-2桁 `#N` は 0 件で、拡張しても**現時点の誤検知はゼロ**。
- しかし 3-4桁 band は `number-reference-check.test.sh` の **TC-003 / TC-005 / TC-011 で意図的に pin されたテスト済み契約**（`#42` / `#99` を「下限未満で非検出」と明示）。拡張は script + 3 テストケース + lint.md doc（#1481/#1482 のマージ済み領域）への波及を伴う。
- 1-2桁 `#N` は本質的に曖昧性が高い（テスト自身が `#42` を task-list ref と注記）。
- CHANGELOG の number-free 維持は、新規参照の混入を防ぐ release ワークフロー側の制御で担保する方が適切。
- シンプルさ優先（既存のテスト済み機構を必要性なく変更しない）。本 Issue の主目的（既存 1-2桁参照の除去）は本 PR で達成済み。

## 検証

- `number-reference-check.sh`（lint Phase 3.19）: 0 findings
- `rg '#[0-9]+'`（全桁）: CHANGELOG.md / CHANGELOG.ja.md ともに 0 件

## Summary

15 `.catch(() => {})` handlers across the frontend and 1 backend handler were silently discarding errors, making failures invisible during debugging.

**What changed:** Every silent catch now logs a descriptive `console.warn(...)` with the error message. The app behavior is unchanged — these are all non-critical fetches (auth config, song versions, corrections, settings preferences, OCR model) that gracefully degrade on failure. The only difference is that failures now leave a diagnostic trail in the browser/server console.

**Backend:**
- `routes/songs.js` — import error handler now includes `e.stack` alongside `e.message`
- `lib/auth.js` — empty `catch {}` in `optionalAuth` documented with comment (intentionally silent — invalid token = unauthenticated)

**Frontend files touched:** `App.tsx`, `AuthView`, `SongView`, `SongEditView`, `AdminView`, `SettingsView`, `OcrModal`, `lib/setlists.ts`

Example before/after:
```diff
- .catch(() => {});
+ .catch((e) => {
+   console.warn('Failed to load song versions:', e.message);
```

author: markus-lassfolk
body:
## Summary

Closes #1897 (Phase 1 Option 1a only).

The `/memory-diagnostics` route was always JSON-only. Operators had no
way to capture a V8 heap snapshot without restarting the gateway with
`--inspect` and racing the lifecycle. Issue #1897 documents a residual
\~62 MB/h `old_space` growth with `reuse-databases` that we cannot
root-cause without an actual heap snapshot.

## What this PR does

Adds three pieces of behaviour, all behind existing auth/permission
checks, all safe to leave enabled in production:

1. **`?heapSnapshot=1` query parameter.** When set, the route calls
   `v8.writeHeapSnapshot()` to
   `<workspace>/memory/heap-snapshots/<ISO-timestamp>-<pid>.heapsnapshot`
   and returns the path, file size, pid, and duration in a new
   `heapSnapshot` field on the response. The rest of the diagnostics
   JSON is unchanged.

2. **`OPENCLAW_HEAP_SNAPSHOT_AUTO=critical`** env var. When this is
   set and the live leak verdict is `likely_leak` (heapUsed \>= 1.5 GB),
   the route auto-fires a snapshot on every diagnostics call. The
   verdict helper mirrors the bounds used by `buildLeakHints` so the
   public-facing `leakHints` block and the auto-fire decision stay
   in sync. `critical` is the only value the var currently accepts;
   adding more modes is a follow-up.

3. **`OPENCLAW_HEAP_SNAPSHOT_DIR`** override. Default is
   `memory/heap-snapshots` under the workspace root.

## Failure mode

Snapshot write failures are caught and logged via `pluginLogger` but
do not break the diagnostics response. A failing snapshot returns
`heapSnapshot: null`; the operator still gets the full JSON.

## Tests

- 19/19 pass in `tests/public-api-routes.test.ts`
  (16 pre-existing + 3 new)
- 3/3 in `tests/gateway-memory-diagnostics.test.ts`
- 2/2 in `tests/memory-diagnostics.test.ts`
- 0 new TypeScript errors (pre-existing errors in unrelated files
  are not touched by this PR)

New tests cover:
- `?heapSnapshot=1` writes a real `.heapsnapshot` to the configured
  directory and returns the path/bytes/pid
- omitting the param returns the unchanged JSON (no `heapSnapshot`
  field)
- `?heapSnapshot=1` is rejected with 403 when unauthenticated
  (no privilege escalation)

## Diff size

`2 files changed, 201 insertions(+)`. Pure additive; no existing
behaviour changed.

## Phase 2 (separate PR)

Phase 2 (root-cause fix for the leak itself) is **not** in this PR.
We need an actual snapshot to analyze. Once a snapshot is captured
from a live gateway in the leaked state, the follow-up PR will target
the real culprit (likely candidates: cumulative cache maps, listener
accumulation, or mmap retention).

## Acceptance criteria mapping (from #1897)

1. ✅ `/memory-diagnostics?heapSnapshot=1` returns a path to a valid
   V8 `.heapsnapshot` file.
2. ✅ Tested in the test suite (vitest uses a real `v8.writeHeapSnapshot`
   in a tmpdir; passes).
3. ⏳ Phase 2 — separate PR after analysis.
4. ⏳ Phase 2 — separate PR after analysis.
5. ⏳ Phase 2 — separate PR after analysis.

## Out of scope

- Phase 2 (root-cause fix)
- Wire `vm-memory-collect-diagnostics.sh` to use `?heapSnapshot=1`
  (lives in openclaw-maeve, not this repo; will update in a follow-up
  once this lands)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New production behavior writes large heap files on demand and can add latency/IO on every diagnostics call when auto-critical fires; mitigated by existing auth on the route and non-fatal snapshot errors.
> 
> **Overview**
> Authenticated **`/memory-diagnostics`** can now write a **V8 `.heapsnapshot`** and return a **`heapSnapshot`** metadata block (path, bytes, pid, duration, trigger, verdict) while leaving the rest of the diagnostics JSON unchanged.
> 
> **Manual:** `?heapSnapshot=1` calls `v8.writeHeapSnapshot()` under the workspace (default **`memory/heap-snapshots`**, overridable via **`OPENCLAW_HEAP_SNAPSHOT_DIR`**). **Auto:** when **`OPENCLAW_HEAP_SNAPSHOT_AUTO=critical`** and leak hints imply **`likely_leak`** (e.g. repeated Lance/SQLite teardown), a snapshot is taken without the query flag. Write failures are logged and surfaced as **`heapSnapshot: null`** without failing the route.
> 
> **Tests** in `public-api-routes.test.ts` cover manual snapshot, omitted param, auto-critical path, and **403** when unauthenticated. Unrelated diffs are largely line-wrapping/formatting.

> **Stacked on #434** (`feat/composing-runbooks`). Review/merge #434 first; GitHub will auto-retarget this PR's base to `main` once #434 lands. The diff below is iterate-and-delegate's own commits only.

## Summary

Adds the **iterate-and-delegate** pattern: FOR loops that fan out per-item delegated child runbooks, with the supporting core resolution semantics, static checks, spec language, and a worked-example runbook (the `#435` work).

### Core / CLI
- **FOR-source static analysis helper** (`for-source-analysis.ts`) shared by launch validation and `rd check`, so the two cannot disagree (spec §8.2).
- **Typed FOR `IterationBinding`** captured on the delegation snapshot and surfaced to children, gated on declared `inputs` (spec §10.4).
- **Deferred launch validation** for self-produced FOR sources — a runbook may iterate a source it produces itself, with no seed required (C1).
- **`rd check` warnings** for unsatisfiable FOR sources and multi-ref (shared-binding) data-source FOR steps. SHOULD-level, never errors.

### Spec / docs
- Define FOR data-source resolution timing and iteration bindings (§8.2, §10.4).
- Document `Index` inheritance across delegation.
- Promote iterate-and-delegate to a dogfooded pattern.

### Review follow-ups (last two commits)
- Direct `IterationBindingSchema` rejection coverage via `ContextSnapshotSchema` (item-without-value, non-positive index, unknown kind).
- CLI-layer assertion pinning the multi-ref shared-binding warning (+ exit-code on PASS-with-warnings); confirms the unsatisfiable-source warning does not co-fire for a declared input.
- Removed dead `PayloadFor<T>` (zero consumers after the emitter moved to `RunbookEventInput`).
- Tightened a delegation fixture (honest branding, no blanket cast) and split FOR-clause guard assertions for clearer failures.

author: sagnik7896
body:
﻿This PR introduces 4 new filesystem extractors for discovering container image references in CI/CD and Kubernetes configuration files. All extractors emit PURL type `docker` and use the standard `parseName` helper to split image references into `(name, version)` pairs, handling both digest (`@sha256:...`) and tag (`:tag`) formats.

### New extractors

| Extractor | Package | Files scanned | Fields extracted |
|-----------|---------|---------------|------------------|
| Cloud Build step images | `language/cloudbuild` | `cloudbuild.yaml` / `cloudbuild.yml` | `steps[].name` |
| Skaffold build images | `language/skaffold` | `skaffold.yaml` / `skaffold.yml` | `build.artifacts[].image` |
| Kustomize transformed images | `language/kustomize` | `kustomization.yaml` / `kustomization.yml` | `images[].name` / `images[].newName` + `newTag` / `digest` |
| GitHub Actions container images | `containers/githubactionsimage` | `.github/workflows/*.yml` / `*.yaml` | `jobs.*.container.image`, `jobs.*.services.*.image` |

### Implementation details

- **YAML parsing:** Cloud Build, Skaffold, and Kustomize use struct-based `yaml.v3` decoding. GitHub Actions uses `yaml.v3` Node tree walking, matching the existing `githubactions` extractor, to handle dynamic job and service IDs.
- **Image parsing:** All extractors use `strings.LastIndex(name, ":")` for tag splitting, which correctly handles `registry:port/image:tag`, and `strings.SplitN(name, "@", 2)` for digest splitting.
- **Deduplication:** All extractors deduplicate extracted images with a `map[string]struct{}` keyed by the raw image string.
- **Variable skipping:** Extractors skip image references containing unresolved `$` variables, such as `$PROJECT_ID` or `${IMAGE_NAME}`.
- **No Metadata:** All extractors omit the `Metadata` field to avoid the `metadata.Protoable` interface requirement, keeping the implementation minimal and self-contained.
- **No custom proto configs:** Each extractor uses the generic `PluginConfig` with `MaxFileSizeBytes` only.

### Shared changes

- `extractor/filesystem/list/list.go`: Added imports and registered all 4 extractors in the `Containers` InitMap, making them discoverable via `--extractors=containers`, `--extractors=all`, and `--extractors=artifact`.
- `docs/supported_inventory_types.md`: Added documentation for all 4 extractors in the Container inventory and Misc sections.

### Test coverage

- Each extractor has a comprehensive `_test.go` file with 5-7 YAML test fixtures covering basic extraction, digest format, duplicate deduplication, empty configs, invalid YAML, port-in-registry names, and unresolved variable skipping.
- Verified with targeted package tests, list package tests, `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `git diff --check`.

### Related / prior art

- `containers/dockercomposeimage`: Similar container image extraction pattern from Docker Compose files.
- `containers/k8simage`: Similar container image extraction pattern from Kubernetes manifests.
- `misc/githubactions`: Complements this PR by extracting `uses:` action references from GitHub Actions workflow files. This PR adds container image extraction from `container:` and `services:` fields without overlap.

### Checklist

- [x] Tests added for all new extractors
- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] `go vet` passes
- [x] `gofmt` applied
- [x] Documentation updated (`docs/supported_inventory_types.md`)
- [x] Extractors registered in `extractor/filesystem/list/list.go`
- [x] No duplicate extractors found during pre-submission duplicate check

This PR is a combined submission because all 4 extractors modify the same shared files (`list.go` and `docs/supported_inventory_types.md`). If maintainers prefer smaller PRs, I am happy to split this into separate branches from current upstream `main`.

author: johannesjo
body:
Fixes #8304.

## Problem

The upload path persisted `lastServerSeq` covering piggybacked ops **before** those ops were applied. `processRemoteOps` runs in the caller (`OperationLogSyncService`), after the upload lock releases — so a crash, or a cancelled piggybacked SYNC_IMPORT dialog, in that window advanced the server cursor past unstored ops, and the next download skipped them **forever** (silent data loss across devices). The download path already maintained the inverse invariant ("persist `lastServerSeq` AFTER ops are stored"); the upload path did not.

## Fix

`OperationLogUploadService` now **defers** persisting `lastServerSeq` once it collects piggybacked ops, returning the planned value as `UploadResult.lastServerSeqToPersist`. `OperationLogSyncService` persists it **only after `processRemoteOps` succeeds**, and skips it on the cancel / USE_REMOTE / USE_LOCAL early-returns. The non-piggyback path still persists in-loop — verified safe against the server: `operation-download.service.ts` returns ops in `(sinceSeq, latestSeq]` **excluding the requesting client**, so when no piggyback is returned the gap to `latestSeq` is only our own just-uploaded ops (no loss risk).

## Tests

- **Unit** — `operation-log-upload.service.spec.ts`: the upload service defers (no in-loop `setLastServerSeq`) and returns `lastServerSeqToPersist`. `operation-log-sync.service.spec.ts`: caller persists after `processRemoteOps` (ordering), and does **not** persist on the cancel path or when the apply throws (crash window).
- **Cross-service integration** — `operation-log-upload-piggyback-seq.integration.spec.ts`: wires the **real** upload + sync services over one in-memory provider seq; cancel/crash → seq unchanged, success → seq advances strictly after apply. All fix-discriminating specs were confirmed to **fail without the fix**.
- **E2E** — `supersync-import-conflict-dialog.spec.ts`: real-server multi-client guard for the cancel → re-offer → reconverge contract. It routes through the (already-correct) download path, so it is **not** a fix regression for #8304 — documented in-file; the upload-piggyback manifestation is reachable only via a timing race a deterministic E2E can't force, and is covered by the unit + integration specs.

## Risk

Sync-critical. The deferred persist now runs outside the upload lock — as the download path already does — so the worst case in a rare multi-tab race is an idempotent re-download, never loss. No reducer/effect/vector-clock changes: only *when* a durability marker is written. An adversarial sync-correctness review across multi-chunk uploads, both other direct callers, the `hasMorePiggyback` follow-up, and the out-of-lock race found no defect.

A leaked or logged refresh token could be used against protected endpoints for the full refresh-token TTL, bypassing the intended short access-token lifetime and revocation expectations from logout/password reset. ## Root cause `SecurityConfig` used the default JWT resource-server converter, which validated signature/expiry but did not enforce the `token_type=access` claim that `JwtService` already emits. ## Fix Configure a JWT authentication converter that rejects bearer JWTs unless `token_type` is `access`, while leaving the shared decoder unchanged so refresh endpoints can still parse refresh tokens from request bodies. ## Validation - `mvn test -Dtest=SecurityConfigTest,JwtServiceTest` - `mvn test`

## What this PR does

Adds a GitHub Actions workflow that automatically reviews newly opened issues using an LLM (DeepSeek V4 Flash).

### Workflow steps:
1. **Extract input** — parses the issue type prefix (`[Bug]`, `[Installation]`, `[Usage]`, `[Doc]`, `[Misc]`) from the issue title
2. **Prepare template** — loads the matching YAML issue template from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`

- `.github/workflows/scripts/robot/` — modular Python scripts for each step

- Tested against 100 real issues from the repository with 100% success rate
- All 100 issues received AI-generated reviews via DeepSeek V4 Flash

No — this is a CI automation change only.

author: copilot
body:
This change addresses two auth gaps: login/session handling could break because the UI and API disagreed on the session user shape, and the system had no durable audit trail for successful or failed logins. It aligns the auth contract and adds end-to-end login auditing with admin visibility.

- **Auth contract alignment**
  - Unified the session user model on `authMethod` so UI logout/session logic matches the API token payload.
  - Corrected related auth/OpenAPI shapes to reflect the actual request/response payloads and enum values.

- **Login audit persistence**
  - Added a login audit service that writes auth events to a dedicated Cosmos container when configured, with bounded in-memory fallback for local/disconnected environments.
  - Captures outcome, method, user/email context, reason, IP, and user agent for both successful and failed sign-in attempts.

- **Audit coverage in auth flows**
  - Added audit writes for:
    - OTP verification success/failure
    - Entra ID login success/failure
    - Guest login success
  - Failed login paths now record a reason code/message instead of silently returning only HTTP status.

- **Protected audit API**
  - Added `/api/auth/audit` for recent login history.
  - Restricted access to authenticated users with `users:read`.
  - Added lightweight auth route throttling to reduce brute-force and abuse risk on login-related endpoints.

- **Admin UI visibility**
  - Extended the Users page with a recent login audit view.
  - Displays outcome, timestamp, auth method, user/email metadata, and failure reason in a scan-friendly format.

- **Targeted coverage**
  - Added API coverage for failed and successful OTP login audit records.

```ts
await loginAuditService.record({
  method: 'otp',
  outcome: 'failure',
  email,
  reason: 'invalid_or_expired_otp',
  ipAddress: request.ip,
  userAgent: request.header('user-agent') ?? undefined
});
```

author: deanmarano
body:
## What

Closes the `set-operations-cte-eager-ast` story (RFC 0022, cluster `set-ops`).

The headline scope — removing `_toSqlSetOperationConcat` / `_setOpOperandUsesStringFeatures` and folding CTE/annotate onto the composed `Union*` AST — already landed with `set-operations-bind-threading` (#3149). This PR closes the remaining acceptance-criteria gap (operand-feature coverage) and fixes a latent correctness bug that surfaced while writing it.

### Eager-load operands must stay arity-compatible

`#3149` compiled an eager-load set-op operand through its JoinDependency manager, emitting the wide `t0_r*` alias list + `LEFT OUTER JOIN`s. That breaks a UNION two ways:

1. **Arity** — the operand's column count no longer matches the other side, so the DB rejects it: `SELECTs to the left and right of UNION do not have the same number of result columns`.
2. **Instantiation** — the compound executes through the `_eagerLoadBypassesJoinDependency` branch and reads rows as **plain models**, so the JD aliases would be instantiated as bogus attributes.

Confirmed both `eager.union(plain)` and `plain.union(eager)` raised the arity error. `_buildSetOperationOperandManager` now always uses the plain `_buildSelectManager()` projection: both operands stay arity-compatible, and the left-operand's eager association still loads via the bypass branch's preload. Rails has no `Relation#union`, so there is no JoinDependency-through-union path to mirror.

### Coverage

SQL-generation + execution tests for CTE, annotate, and eager-load set-op operands — each composes a single statement, stays arity-compatible, and returns correct records (acceptance criteria #1 and #3).

## Test plan

- `relations.test.ts` set-operations group (CTE/annotate/eager operands) + with.test.ts + eager-load tests pass on SQLite locally; CI green (PG/MySQL).

author: caiogn-dev
body:
## O que foi alterado e por quê

Dois endpoints críticos geravam um número de queries SQL proporcional ao volume de dados, causando degradação de performance conforme o uso cresce.

---

### Fix 1 — Order Stats endpoint: 21 queries → 1 query

**Arquivo:** `apps/stores/api/views/order_views.py`

**Problema:** O endpoint `GET /api/v1/stores/orders/?action=stats` chamava `.count()` separadamente para cada janela de tempo (hoje, semana, mês) e para cada status de pedido (~13). Com agregações de receita, totalizava ~21 queries SQL por requisição ao dashboard.

**Solução:** Substituição por um único `queryset.aggregate()` com filtros condicionais (`Count('id', filter=Q(...))` e `Sum('total', filter=Q(...))`). O banco resolve tudo em um único `SELECT` com `CASE WHEN` expressions.

**Ganho:** 21 queries → 1 query para o endpoint de estatísticas do dashboard.

---

### Fix 2 — Universal Conversation Service: 2N+1 queries → 3 queries

**Arquivo:** `apps/conversations/services/universal_conversation_service.py`

**Problema:** `_build_whatsapp_rows` iterava todas as conversas e, para cada uma, fazia:
1. `conv.messages.order_by("-created_at").first()` — última mensagem (N queries)
2. `conv.messages.filter(direction="inbound", read_at__isnull=True).count()` — mensagens não lidas (N queries)

Com 50 conversas ativas: 101 queries. Com 200 conversas: 401 queries.

**Solução:**
1. Anotação `unread_inbound=Count('messages', filter=Q(...))` — elimina todas as N queries de contagem
2. Subquery `last_message_id=Subquery(...)` — obtém o ID da última mensagem por conversa no banco
3. Bulk fetch `WhatsAppMessage.objects.filter(id__in=msg_ids)` — busca todas as últimas mensagens de uma vez

**Ganho:** 2N+1 queries → 3 queries independente do número de conversas.

---

## Como testar

```bash
# Habilitar query logging no Django e verificar contagem:
# settings.py: LOGGING['loggers']['django.db.backends'] = {'level': 'DEBUG'}

# 1. Order stats
GET /api/v1/stores/orders/?action=stats

# 2. Conversations hub (inbox unificado)
GET /api/v1/conversations/

# Antes: N+1 queries vistas nos logs
# Depois: número fixo de queries independente do volume
```

## Prioridade

**P1** — Performance: o dashboard de pedidos e o inbox unificado são as telas mais acessadas. Com crescimento de volume (dezenas de conversas simultâneas), o tempo de resposta crescia linearmente.

author: mgcohen
body:
## Why

The API boundary was wired by **convention** — a `static class XxxEndpoint` with a `static Map(group)`, chained through `Module.MapX()` + `MapGroup`. Nothing makes a slice *have* an endpoint, register it, or sit on the right route; with 20+ features planned, that convention is a drift surface, and drift only surfaces as a missing route at runtime.

For an agent-first repo whose strictest rule is **structure over convention**, the API boundary should be compiler-enforced: an endpoint is a class whose abstract members you *must* implement to compile. After surveying the validated .NET VSA references (Milan Jovanović, Anton Martyniuk, SSW, RiverBooks), we picked **FastEndpoints** (the REPR-pattern library SSW uses).

## What

Converts the **Projects** slice as the canonical example and wires the Host; Flows/Git/Tasks stay on Minimal API and migrate as a follow-up (FastEndpoints coexists with them).

body:
## What

Closes the last open test gap from the new-machine-readiness audit (event-bus events 4152 / 4159). `sysload-writer` and the LaunchAgent installer had **zero tests** despite both being prior confirmed-failure surfaces (the sysload zjstatus widget flicker, the launchctl `|| true` crash on re-bootstrap).

The bus repeatedly flagged that `tests/test-bootstrap.sh` was mostly `grep -q 'fn_name'` presence checks — proving functions are *named*, not that they *work*. These four are behavioral.

## Tests added

| Test | Exercises |
|------|-----------|
| `sysload-writer writes cache from top output` | stubs `top`, asserts `~/.cache/sysload` gets computed CPU% (`100 - idle`) and RAM% (`used/(used+unused)`) — verified `85% idle → 15%`, `20G/2949M → 87%` |
| `sysload-writer tolerates top failure` | `top` exits 1 → writer exits 0 and writes **no** cache (KeepAlive sanity / widget keeps last good value) |
| `launch agent substitutes __HOME__ and reloads` | real `install_launch_agent` expands `__HOME__` in the plist, leaves no placeholder, calls `launchctl bootstrap` |
| `launch agent idempotent on unchanged plist` | second run on identical plist does **not** reinstall or re-call launchctl (the `cmp -s` guard) |

## Note on `install_launch_agent`

It derives `dotfiles_dir` from `BASH_SOURCE`, which `eval` can't satisfy — so the loader redirects *that one line* at a fixture tree (same pattern as the existing `_load_is_gateway_host` helper). Everything actually under test — the `__HOME__` sed, the `cmp`-based idempotency guard, the launchctl reload — is the genuine bootstrap code.

## Verification

`make check` green (lint, **39** bootstrap tests, hooks). All four **mutation-verified**: removing the `__HOME__` sed, the `cmp` guard, or the writer's failure guards each flips the corresponding test red; the broken-writer assertion was confirmed to discriminate against the real writer.

author: rogeriochaves
body:
## The board now snaps to the room you just spawned

When a room spawns, the gateway brings the KanbanCode board forward, but it did not auto-**select** the room's channel, so you still had to click into it to watch the agents self-organize. That channel auto-select was dropped earlier when we removed the `kanbancode://` deep link (the deep link relaunched a stale registered build and tripped KanbanCode's quit-protection dialog mid-demo).

This restores it without a deep link. `focusChannel` now writes the channel slug to `~/.kanban-code/focus-channel` before bringing the app forward. The KanbanCode app reads and drains that marker in `applicationDidBecomeActive` and selects the channel. A plain marker file needs no relaunch, so the quit dialog stays gone.

### Contract (paired with the KanbanCode app-side watcher)
- File: `~/.kanban-code/focus-channel`
- Content: the bare channel slug (`room.channel`, e.g. `dark-mode`), no `#`, no newline. The app-side read trims whitespace and strips a leading `#`, so either form is tolerated.
- The app **drains** (deletes) the marker on read, so each spawn writes a fresh one and nothing accumulates.
- Written before the System Events activate, so it is on disk when `applicationDidBecomeActive` fires.

### Safety
Best-effort: the write is wrapped so a failure (missing dir, permissions) just means no auto-select, never a broken board-focus. The two halves are independent and harmless alone (the watcher no-ops with no marker; the marker no-ops with no reader).

### Verification
- Drove `focusChannel("marker-probe-xyz")` headless: the marker file held exactly `marker-probe-xyz` (bare slug, no newline).
- Typecheck clean; gateway hot-reloads cleanly.
- Joint test with the rebuilt app: spawn a room, board snaps to its channel.

author: paul-krug
body:
Adds C-API surface for component-level access to the backend, plus
three pre-existing memory/correctness bug fixes found along the way.
Structured as three commits — easiest reviewed commit-by-commit.

## Commit 1 — correctness fixes (small, ~20 lines)
- **`Tube::operator=`** copied the 93 sections plus three scalars but
  silently dropped `staticPartsInitialized`, the subglottal/nasal
  cavity lengths and both piriform fossa dimensions, so a copied
  `Tube` could disagree with the original on static geometry.
- **`vtlGetTransferFunction`**: the fallback `TransferFunctionOptions`
  was declared inside the `if (opts == NULL)` block but used through
  the `opts` pointer after the block ended (dangling pointer; under
  `-O3` the stack slot was reused, corrupting the options). Also
  `opts->staticPressureDrops` was never copied into `TlModel::Options`,
  so that option was silently ignored.

## Commit 2 — new C-API surface (the bulk; mechanical)
21 new `vtl*` functions exposing backend internals for component-level
use from language bindings (driving individual models step by step,
reading intermediate values) without full synthesis runs:
- **Glottis:** `vtlGlottisCalcGeometry`, `vtlGlottisIncTime`,
  `vtlGlottisResetMotion`, `vtlGetGlottisStaticParamInfo` (also added
  to the Windows export table).
- **Time-domain simulation** on a caller-supplied tube:
  `vtlTdsSetTubeAndRun`, `vtlTdsSetOptions`, `vtlTdsResetMotion`.
- **Anatomy scaling:** `vtlGetAnatomyParams`, `vtlSetAnatomyParams`,
  `vtlSetAnatomyFromAge`, `vtlSetFossaDims`.
- **Geometry export:** `vtlGetSurfaceVertices`, `vtlGetCenterline`,
  `vtlGetOutlines`, `vtlGetCrossSections`, `vtlGetCuts`,
  `vtlGetProfiles`, `vtlGetTongueRibData`, `vtlGetTongueWidthBounds`,
  `vtlTractToFullTube`.
- **TL introspection:** `vtlGetTLIntermediateValues`, backed by new
  read-only `TlModel` accessors (`getMatrixProduct`,
  `getFossaInputImpedance`, `getNose-/getMouthRadiationImpedance`).

Supporting changes: `VocalTract::getRawCuts()`, the outline line
strips made public, 4 entries in the Windows export table.

This commit also folds in one small **correctness fix** (bundled here
because it's consumed by the new `vtlTractToFullTube`):
`Tube::getVelumOpening_cm2()` returned `noseSection[0].area_cm2` — the
nose-section area *after* shaping and the `MIN_AREA_CM2` clamp —
instead of the velopharyngeal opening the caller requested. It now
returns that raw value, stored in a new `rawVelumOpening_cm2` member
set in `setVelumOpening()` (and copied in `operator=`). The two agree
for any normally-open velum and differ only at/near a closed port —
e.g. a requested opening of `0.0` previously read back as `0.0001`
(the clamp floor), now reads back as `0.0`. Affected readers: the
`velumOpening_cm2` output of `vtlTractToTube` / `vtlFastTractToTube` /
`vtlTractToFullTube`, tube interpolation, and the Synthesizer text
export.

## Commit 3 — off-by-one array overruns found with AddressSanitizer
- **`AnatomyParams::adaptArticulation()`** scaled four tongue-side
  params but the model has three (`TS1..TS3`); `TS1+3 == NUM_PARAMS`,
  so the loop read and wrote one element past the `oldParams`/
  `newParams` stack arrays per call. The stray write can crash the
  process later (malloc abort in `~VocalTract()` during `vtlClose()`
  after using the anatomy API, depending on stack layout). Loop bound
  is now derived from the enum.
- **`VocalTract::calcTongueRibs()`** right-edge scan started at
  `k = NUM_PROFILE_SAMPLES`, reading `upperProfile`/`lowerProfile` one
  element past the end (read-only; rejected by the `INVALID` guards in
  the normal case → no behavior change expected). Now starts at the
  last valid index.

## Testing
Builds clean on macOS arm64 (cmake Release). `VtlApiTests` 19/19 and
`VtlBackendTests` 1/1 pass. Each commit compiles standalone; new API
paths exercised under AddressSanitizer.

## Known pre-existing issue (NOT addressed here, for the record)
AddressSanitizer shows `EmaPoint::name` strings sharing buffers with
XML-parser strings freed at the end of `VocalTract::init()`
(`XmlNode.cpp`); using the anatomy API then makes `vtlClose()`
double-free, so a process can abort at exit (work/results unaffected).
Pre-dates this PR (reproduces on current `main` + these additions) and
lives in the XML/EMA ownership code — worth its own issue/fix.

body:
## Summary

Ships the **Linear half of Phase 7 Track B's "Linear / Jira" item** — read-only sync of your assigned Linear issues, surfaced alongside GitHub on the dashboard. Follows the proven GitHub-PAT pattern end to end. (Jira stays open.)

## How it works

- **Auth** (`auth:connect-linear`): paste-once **personal API key**, validated against the GraphQL `viewer` before storage and encrypted via the standard `saveToken`/`safeStorage` path. Linear personal keys go in the `Authorization` header **verbatim** (not as a `Bearer` token — that form is OAuth-only); a test pins this.
- **Sync** (`electron/integrations/linear.ts`): fetches the viewer's assigned issues, drops completed/canceled and malformed nodes via the **pure `normalizeLinearIssues` transformer**, and upserts the active ones into a new `linear_issues` table (migration **0011**). Issues no longer returned are pruned so the dashboard list can't accumulate stale rows. Same insert-on-conflict integration-row + `sync_events` bookkeeping as the other integrations (a first-ever failure still surfaces).
- **Wiring**: `sync:trigger`, `sync:trigger-all` (joins only when connected), `SUPPORTED_SYNC_SERVICES`, and the per-integration cron; `linear:get-items` IPC via the 3-file pattern.
- **UI**: a Linear card on the Dashboard (shown once synced, so it doesn't add a permanent empty card for non-users) mirroring the GitHub card; the Integrations card is promoted from "Upcoming" with a PAT form.
- **Security**: Linear calls are main-process-only, so the renderer CSP is untouched (the #166 review lesson).

## Tests

10 new unit tests: the pure transformer (active vs done/canceled, malformed nodes, partial/empty responses, optional-field defaults) and `syncLinear` bookkeeping (upsert, prune-on-next-sync, GraphQL-error + 401 surfacing) on real in-memory SQLite, plus the `auth:connect-linear` handler (format validation, auth-failure-stores-nothing, encrypt-and-persist, verbatim Authorization header).

author: allyblockcast[bot]
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - The in-review evidence gate (`shouldBlockUnreviewableInReview`) gates agent transitions from any status → `in_review` by checking whether the computed evidence verdict indicates something reviewable exists
> - `warn` is the intentionally lenient verdict for unlabeled / doc-only issues — it is returned when no required evidence shapes are registered (see `DEFAULT_UNLABELED_REQUIRED` in `evidence-shapes.ts`) and means "no PR required, proceed"
> - The old predicate used `verdict !== "pass"`, which erroneously treated `warn` the same as `block`, freezing all unlabeled issues at `in_review` even when the gate was designed to let them through
> - This pull request narrows the predicate to `verdict === "block"` and adds a targeted unit test asserting `warn` is not blocked, plus a regression test for `request_checkbox_confirmation` as a valid review-path interaction kind
> - The benefit is that agents working on unlabeled or doc-only issues can transition to `in_review` as designed, and the gate still correctly blocks `block`-verdict transitions

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**What happened?**

Agents on unlabeled issues receive a `warn` verdict from the evidence evaluator (the intentional lenient fallback path in `evidence-shapes.ts` when `DEFAULT_UNLABELED_REQUIRED` applies). The gate predicate `verdict !== "pass"` treated `warn` identically to `block`, causing the transition to fail with `invalid_issue_disposition / missing: review_path` even though the design explicitly allows `warn` through.

**Expected behavior**

Only `block` verdicts should be blocked. `warn`, `pass`, and `null` (evaluation failure) should all allow the transition to `in_review`. The gate was designed with `warn` as a lenient fallback that lets through unlabeled issues without a PR requirement.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create a Paperclip issue with no labels assigned
2. Have an agent work on the issue and attempt to PATCH `status: "in_review"`
3. Observe the 422 error: `invalid_issue_disposition / missing: review_path`
4. The evidence evaluator returns verdict `warn` (not `block`), yet the gate predicate `verdict !== "pass"` evaluates to `true` and blocks the transition

**Paperclip version or commit**

`c044e0471` (Blockcast/paperclip master before this fix)

**Deployment mode**

Self-hosted server

**Affected code**

`server/src/services/in-review-gate.ts` line 48 — predicate was `verdict !== "pass"`, fixed to `verdict === "block"`.

**Regression note**

`request_checkbox_confirmation` was missing from `REVIEW_PATH_INTERACTION_KINDS` in a prior commit; this PR adds a test confirming it is present and accepted.

## What Changed

- `server/src/services/in-review-gate.ts`: Change `verdict !== "pass"` → `verdict === "block"` so `warn` verdicts (unlabeled fallback) are not blocked
- `server/src/__tests__/in-review-gate.test.ts`: Update base fixture to use `verdict: "warn"` and assert it returns `false` (not blocked); retain `"block"` test asserting `true`
- `server/src/__tests__/issue-execution-policy-routes.test.ts`: Add PAP-1008 regression test confirming `request_checkbox_confirmation` as a valid review-path interaction (avoids collision with existing PAP-1006 `background_liveness` test)

## Verification

```
pnpm --filter server test in-review-gate
pnpm --filter server test issue-execution-policy-routes
```

- 7 unit tests in `in-review-gate.test.ts` — all green
- 17 route tests in `issue-execution-policy-routes.test.ts` — all green including new PAP-1008
- Post-deploy probe: PATCH `status: "in_review"` on an unlabeled fixture issue should return 200

## Risks

Low risk. The predicate change is strictly narrowing: it only removes the erroneous blocking of `warn` verdicts; `block` verdicts are still blocked; `null` and `pass` verdicts are still allowed through. No schema or migration changes.

## Model Used

- Claude Sonnet 4.6 (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) via Paperclip Release Engineer agent
- Tool use mode (no extended thinking)

author: martijnarts
body:
The WebdriverIO end-to-end suite has never passed on the Linux CI job, and it turns out it cannot. The embedded WebDriver server from `tauri-plugin-webdriver` drives the app's webview, which on Linux is WebKitGTK, and that engine refuses to marshal any JavaScript result back across its process boundary under the CI runner. Every script result — a string, a boolean, an object, it does not matter — fails with `WEBKIT_JAVASCRIPT_ERROR_INVALID_RESULT` ("Unsupported result type"), and the same happens through both of WebKitGTK's JavaScript-evaluation APIs, so no `execute` call or element lookup can complete. I confirmed this with a probe that ran `navigator.userAgent` (a plain string) four different ways on the runner; all four came back "Unsupported result type". It is not specific to our setup either: the plugin's own Linux CI is red for the same reason, while its Windows (WebView2) job passes.

That leaves no headless platform to run it on. Windows works but cannot use our Flox toolchain, and macOS runners are a cost the original workflow deliberately skipped. So this drops the Linux workflow and keeps the suite as the local, macOS-first dev tool it already is — CI keeps gating on the fast unit tests in `ci.yml`. TESTING.md now explains the constraint so nobody has to rediscover it.

Left as a draft; mark ready when you are happy with it.

author: pos-ei-don
body:
## Problem

When `huggingface_hub` downloads models into LocalAIs models directory, it creates a `CACHEDIR.TAG` file. This file shows up in `/v1/models` because the suffix skip list contains `.tag` (lowercase), but `strings.HasSuffix` is case-sensitive — `CACHEDIR.TAG` (uppercase) is therefore not matched.

Additionally, backup files like `model.yaml.bak-pre-gpumem072` appear in `/v1/models`. These are created e.g. when LocalAI backs up YAML configs before modifying them.

## Fix

1. **Case-insensitive suffix matching**: The filename is lowercased once with `strings.ToLower` before comparing against entries in `knownModelsNameSuffixToSkip`. This makes `.tag` match `CACHEDIR.TAG` and similar variants.
2. **`.bak` detection via contains-check**: Backup files with suffixes like `.bak-pre-gpumem072` do not end exactly in `.bak`, so an additional `strings.Contains(lowerName, ".bak")` check is added.
3. **Cleanup**: The duplicate `.MD` entry is removed (now redundant via case-insensitive `.md` matching). `.DS_Store` is replaced by lowercased `.ds_store`.

## Reproduction

```
$ curl http://localhost:8080/v1/models | jq '.data[].id'
"CACHEDIR.TAG"
"coder.yaml.bak-pre-gpumem072"
"gemma4-12b.yaml.bak-pre-gpulayers"
...
```

Affects any installation that uses `huggingface_hub` for model downloads or has YAML backup files in the models directory.

author: dhananjaysable
body:
💡 What: The application executed `SELECT * FROM table` queries just to count the number of rows using `$result->num_rows` inside `admin/dashboard.php` and `company/index.php`. This has been optimized to use `SELECT COUNT(*) as count`.
🎯 Why: Fetching complete tables into PHP memory solely to get a record count is a severe anti-pattern that causes excess database I/O, heavy network traffic, and massive application memory spikes. Using `SELECT COUNT(*)` reduces the network payload to a single scalar value.
📊 Impact: Considerably reduces memory consumption and database load for the admin dashboard and company index page, likely yielding faster load times.
🔬 Measurement: Verified via custom PHP CLI mock scripts running `dashboard.php` and `index.php` to ensure the correct mock database counters are displayed.

author: iouzy
body:
## A5 · Bottom sheets on phones

`ui/PautaSheet.kt` was a centred `Dialog` (440dp, a 30dp × top-right, no enter/exit animation, no drag-dismiss) — a desktop-web idiom that's hostile to one-handed use. This makes the sheet **responsive to width** while leaving every call site untouched.

### What changed
`PautaSheet(title, onClose, content)` now dispatches on screen width:

- **Phone (`screenWidthDp < 600`) → `ModalBottomSheet`.** Drag handle, drag-to-dismiss, scrim-tap and back gesture all dismiss; opens fully expanded (`skipPartiallyExpanded = true`); the scrolling body carries `imePadding()` so the keyboard never covers a field. The mono uppercase eyebrow keeps the sheet's identity; the desktop × is dropped because the drag handle is the dismiss affordance (and Material's drag handle carries the a11y dismiss action).
- **Wide screen (`≥ 600dp`, tablet/landscape) → the existing centred dialog**, unchanged (title + × header, 440dp, 18dp radius).

The `content` slot is byte-for-byte the same lambda in both modes, so the ~dozen sheets that call `PautaSheet` (Start/Pause/Conclude, Manual time, habit add/edit, week-ahead, insights, trend, habit detail, Marés remove, previous blocks…) **don't change internally**.

### Look & feel (guardrails)
- **Theme tokens only:** bottom sheet is `containerColor = paper`, `contentColor = ink`, `tonalElevation = 0` (flat paper, no M3 tonal tint), top-only `RoundedCornerShape(18.dp)` to match the app's radius, and a quiet `ink4` drag handle.
- **No new deps:** `ModalBottomSheet` ships in the Material3 already on the BOM (2024.09.03 → 1.3.0).
- **i18n:** no new user-facing strings.
- **600dp** is Material's compact→medium width breakpoint, matching the task spec exactly; chosen with `LocalConfiguration.screenWidthDp` (no extra window-size-class dependency).

### Why `imePadding()` works here
The activity is `windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"` and edge-to-edge (`decorFitsSystemWindows=false`), so `WindowInsets.ime` resolves inside the sheet's window. `imePadding()` is placed **before** `verticalScroll` so it shrinks the scroll viewport above the keyboard — the focused field is brought into a visible region rather than parked behind the IME. Verified there are no `LazyColumn`/`fillMaxHeight` inside any sheet body, so the bounded-scroll behaviour is identical to the old dialog.

### Notes
- Gesture-dismiss now animates out before `onClose` (a real improvement); programmatic closes (e.g. tapping *Concluir*) still leave composition instantly, exactly as the old dialog did — callers are unchanged.
- **Backup:** no data-model or `pauta.v4` change; the unit-test gate (domain math + backup converter) is untouched.

### Build / tests
No Android SDK in this environment (Gradle can't resolve AGP), so compilation/tests are deferred to CI. The change is UI-only and doesn't touch the tested domain/backup code.

Roadmap **Status + Log** for A5 in `docs/NATIVE_IMPROVEMENTS.md` follow in a commit on this branch once the PR number is known.
