author: dataders
body:
## What

A four-tab operational dashboard for the Gooners stack — in the spirit of [`dataders/fusion_issue_analysis`](https://github.com/dataders/fusion_issue_analysis) ([dashboard bakeoff](https://dashboard-bakeoff.anders.omg.lol/)) — built from the **existing dbt marts in MotherDuck** with [`prefab-ui`](https://pypi.org/project/prefab-ui/) and served **only to the signed-in owner**.

| Tab | Marts | Highlights |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Engineering / CI** | `gooners_engineering.*` | open issues/PRs, time-to-merge, CI failure rate, per-workflow reliability + run-time, failure-rate trend, scraper throughput |
| **Operations & Cost** | `gooners_operations.*` | Supabase host load & DB reliability, per-source scrape SLA + silent-failure watch, API spend (cumulative + 30-day burn) |
| **Resale Intelligence** | `gooners.fct_enrichment_coverage` / `fct_ebay_comp_coverage` / `fct_price_accuracy` | enrichment coverage, eBay comp coverage, comp accuracy vs realised hammer price |
| **Product & Users** | `gooners.fct_posthog_engagement` / `fct_user_engagement` / `fct_item_engagement` | PostHog DAU/searches/opens, users by engagement tier, top items by net favorites |

Every section degrades to an **"awaiting first refresh"** note if its mart isn't populated yet, so the dashboard never breaks — it fills in as upstream pipelines come online. Today the **Engineering** tab is fully live (1,000 CI runs, 20.3% failure rate, etc.); resale/product/scrape marts populate once the workflow's `dbt build` runs; the Supabase-platform metrics + PostHog tabs need their existing pipelines (`supabase_stats/`, `posthog_export.py`) to have run first.

## Access model — real auth, not obscurity

`prefab export` bakes the data **inline** into the HTML, so a public URL would leak it. Instead the data stays behind Supabase auth, mirroring the existing "members-only resale intelligence" gates (0008):

1. The workflow uploads `admin.html` → a **private** Supabase Storage bucket (`admin-dashboard/latest.html`) with the service key.
2. A Storage RLS policy (`0020_admin_dashboard.sql`) lets **only the owner's email** read it. **Verified at the DB:** owner reads 1 object, any other user reads 0.
3. The SPA's `/admin` route (a separate Vite entry → `dist/admin/index.html`) signs the owner in, downloads the object with their session, and renders it in an iframe. **The data never ships in the public bundle.**

Live at **`/admin/`** once merged + deployed.

## Files

- `dashboard/app.py` — queries marts → prefab HTML (defensive; a missing mart → "awaiting refresh", never a crash)
- `dashboard/upload.py` — upload to the private bucket
- `.github/workflows/admin-dashboard.yml` — hourly: posthog export → `dbt build` → render → upload (refresh steps best-effort)
- `supabase/migrations/0020_admin_dashboard.sql` — private bucket + owner-only Storage RLS *(already applied to `gooner_jr`)*
- `src/admin-entry.jsx`, `src/components/AdminDashboard.jsx` — gated `/admin` route
- `vite.config.js` — second HTML entry; `dbt/profiles.yml` — `SUPABASE_DB_ATTACH` so CI drives the Supabase attach from the pooler URL (back-compatible fallback)

## Rollout

Per the repo's data-backed-migration pattern: migration is applied; after review I'll run `admin-dashboard.yml` from this branch to populate the marts + storage, then merge.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint` + unit tests (pre-push hook) green
- [x] `npm run build` — both entries emitted (`dist/admin/index.html`)
- [x] prefab renders live engineering data (screenshot below)
- [x] Storage RLS verified: owner = 1 object, others = 0
- [x] `/admin` gate renders at desktop + mobile
- [ ] Run `admin-dashboard.yml` from branch to populate ops/resale/product marts

Screenshots posted in the session for review.

author: mjdwitt
body:
Experiment, **not for merge**. Builds on #2 (the shared-RpcWriter fix) to land enough of the batching ideas from `research.md` to clear challenge 3d (and stretch goal 3e).

The change moves all of (2) — per-peer outbox + envelope batching — into the maelstrom crate. `broadcast/src/main.rs` is untouched. See `research.md` for context.

### Results per row of the table

| # | Config | Test | msgs/op | median (ms) | max (ms) | Pass? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | Baseline (poke + 500ms timer, msg_id on envelope) | 3d | 23.24 | 76 | 107 | ✓ all three thresholds |
| 4 | Same config | 3e | 23.11 | 76 | 105 | ✗ msgs/op (target ≤20) |
| 5 | + 150ms sleep **before** snapshot on poke (coalesce window) | 3d | 24.43 | 224 | 266 | ✓ but msgs/op got *worse* (spurious resends during sleep window) |
| 6 | + 250ms sleep **after** send (throttle) | 3e | 24.16 | 75 | 310 | ✗ msgs/op |
| 7 | Drop poke; pure 350ms timer | 3d | 22.49 | 243 | 458 | ✓ |
| 7 | (same) | 3e | 22.36 | 255 | 455 | ✗ msgs/op |
| 8 | Restored: poke + 500ms timer (final) | 3d | 24.10 | 77 | 104 | ✓ |
| 8 | (same) | 3e | 23.27 | 75 | 104 | ✗ msgs/op (everything else 13–19× under budget) |

(Row numbers retain their original meaning so they line up with the commits on the branch; rows 1–2 — the initial implementation crash and msg_id fix — were stepping stones to the baseline at row 3 and aren't load-bearing for the experiment's conclusion.)

### Headline

Envelope batching + per-peer outbox passes 3d cleanly. 3e's ≤20 msgs/op is unreachable by transport-level batching at this workload rate — the per-node broadcast rate (~2/s) means you'd need ~1s coalesce windows to average 2 broadcasts per envelope, which blows 3d's 400ms latency budget. The remaining levers all live in `broadcast/src/main.rs` (sparser topology + onward forwarding, anti-entropy, cumulative acks).

### Files changed

- `rust/maelstrom/src/node/rpc.rs` — per-peer outbox, envelope batching, send_replies
- `rust/maelstrom/src/node.rs` — batch dispatch on receive (hoist itself is in #2)
- No changes to `rust/broadcast/src/main.rs`

## SD-LEO-INFRA-WORKER-INBOX-PUSH-DELIVERY-001

Closes the RCA-confirmed (conf 0.95, corroborated by session 32925831) structural blindness: the canonical worker `/checkin` loop surfaced ONLY `WORK_ASSIGNMENT`, so COACHING / advisory INFO / coordinator_reply / directive push targeting a worker were never seen unless it manually queried `session_coordination`. Secondary: callsign lived only in `claude_sessions.metadata` and went null after a release/sweep.

### Deliverables
- **FR-1** — `resolveCheckin` attaches `base.coordinator_messages[]` (surfaces on EVERY return path: resume / idle / self_claimed). `isCoordinatorPush` surfaces COACHING + all self-targeted INFO; excludes OUTBOUND friction (`signal_type && !signal_resolved`), own roll_call, WORK_ASSIGNMENT, SET_IDENTITY.
- **FR-2** — `rehydrateCallsign` re-hydrates the callsign from the durable SET_IDENTITY row when metadata lost it (survives release/sweep) + persists it back.
- **FR-3** — `/checkin` is the AUTHORITATIVE non-draining bounded delivery point. The PostToolUse hook now read-only-drains coordinator push (`read_at`=DELIVERED, ack WITHHELD) instead of full-draining it, so `/checkin` (filters `acknowledged_at IS NULL`) delivers it. First delivery stamps `read_at` only (re-surfaces once = missed-render guard); a 2nd advisory delivery stamps `acknowledged_at` (bounded). DIRECTIVE_KINDS never auto-acked.
- **FR-4** — `worker-status.cjs` `getMessagesForSession` gains an `unackedOnly` read.

### Adversarial review (7 agents) — both findings fixed before merge
1. The hook default-drained COACHING/plain-INFO → acked them before `/checkin` saw them (would have left the headline case still broken). Fixed with the read-only-drain branch.
2. **SIGNAL_RESOLVED** notifications (echo `signal_type` as context) were dropped by the bare `signal_type` guard on BOTH seams (double-blind) — an exact recurrence of the bug. Both now exclude only outbound friction.

author: nextocompany
body:
## Summary
Wires the expired-auth-row cleanup (follow-up **#60**) into the existing scheduler→worker infrastructure as a new `auth:cleanup` job. Batch-deletes expired/consumed `email_otps` and expired/revoked `candidate_sessions` so those tables don't grow unbounded.

Closes #60.

## Design
- Mirrors the **retention sweep** pattern: the single-replica `scheduler` enqueues an asynq task on a cron; the `worker` handles it. No new process.
- **Separate task** (not folded into the retention sweep) so this benign housekeeping isn't gated behind the destructive, default-OFF PDPA anonymization job.
- **Enabled by default** (`AUTH_CLEANUP_ENABLED=true`) — it only removes already-dead auth artifacts (no user data), so it should run wherever the scheduler is deployed. Cron defaults to `03:15` (offset from retention's `03:30`).
- Batched DELETE (`LIMIT`, bounded loop) drains a backlog over a few iterations without an unbounded query.

## Changes
- `pkg/queue/tasks.go` — `TypeAuthCleanup` task (retry/timeout/unique policy mirroring retention).
- `internal/candidateauth/cleanup.go` — `CleanupService` (pool-based, like `pdpa.RetentionService`) with `CleanExpired` + asynq handler.
- `pkg/config` — `AUTH_CLEANUP_ENABLED` / `AUTH_CLEANUP_CRON` / `AUTH_CLEANUP_BATCH`.
- `cmd/scheduler/main.go`, `cmd/worker/main.go` — register the job/handler.
- `.env.example` — documented.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` — clean
- [x] `go test ./...` — pass (new config-default tests)
- [x] **Integration test** (`-tags integration`, build-tagged like the PDPA tests) run live against the dev DB: 2 expired OTPs + 2 dead sessions deleted, the 1 live OTP + 1 live session survive
- [ ] Confirm on prod after deploy: scheduler logs `auth:cleanup registered`; worker logs `auth cleanup complete` with counts

## Notes
- The `scheduler` and `worker` images must be rebuilt + redeployed for this to take effect (see `docs/career-membership-provisioning.md`). The job is harmless if the membership tables are empty.

In parallel Agent Council turns or when users reply to a message generated by an agent council, the virtual `agentCouncil` message has a composite concatenated ID (e.g. `agentCouncil-parentMessageId-memberIds`). When submitting subsequent messages or executing sequential rounds, this virtual ID is passed downstream as `parent_id` (via the last message selector). This PR modifies the `findLastMessageIdRecursive` selector to handle `node.role === 'agentCouncil'` nodes by recursively finding the message ID of the last member in the `members` array (the last real message generated in the council) or falling back to `extra.parentMessageId` if there are no members.

author: thykel
body:
### Pre-requisite PR(s) 
* https://github.com/opf/commonmark-ckeditor-build/pull/120

# Ticket
https://community.openproject.org/work_packages/STC-645

# What are you trying to accomplish?

When a user drags or pastes an image of an unsupported type (e.g. WebP) into the CKEditor description field on an instance where WebP is not on the attachment allowlist, the backend already returns a clear 422 error:

> "The file was rejected by an automatic filter. 'image/webp' is not allowed for upload."

However, that message was silently discarded by the frontend. The upload progress toast dismissed itself on failure without ever surfacing the error text, and a generic CKEditor indicator was shown instead — leaving the user with no actionable explanation.

This PR ensures the specific backend error message is shown to the user in an OpenProject error toast whenever an attachment upload is rejected (by file-type filter or any other server-side validation).

## Screenshots

N/A

# What approach did you choose and why?

**Root cause:** `toast.component.html` bound the `(uploadError)` output of `UploadProgressComponent` to `remove()`. The `HttpErrorResponse` carrying the backend message was emitted but never passed to `ToastService.addError()`, so the only thing that happened on failure was that the upload toast silently disappeared.

**Fix — two-part:**

1. **`ToastComponent` (`toast.component.ts` + `toast.component.html`):** Added an `onUploadError(error: HttpErrorResponse)` method that calls `this.toastService.addError(error)` — which already knows how to extract HAL error messages — and then removes the upload toast. The template binding was changed from `(uploadError)="remove()"` to `(uploadError)="onUploadError($event)"`.

2. **`AttachmentsResourceService` (`attachments.service.ts`):** Added a `catchError` pipe in `uploadAttachments()` that converts the opaque `HttpErrorResponse` into a plain `Error` with the human-readable message before re-throwing. This ensures that callers further up the chain (such as the CKEditor upload plugin) receive a meaningful string rather than an unreadable object when calling `loader.reject()`.

**Why not only fix the service layer?** The `ToastService.addUpload()` and the `UploadProgressComponent` are the natural point where per-file upload errors are observed; fixing the component handler is the minimal, targeted change that guarantees the message is shown exactly once without interfering with other callers. The service-layer `catchError` is a complementary improvement for CKEditor's own error path and does not duplicate the toast display.

No backend changes are required — the error message (`not_allowlisted`) already exists and is translated in all supported locales.

# Merge checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] Added/updated documentation in Lookbook (patterns, previews, etc)
- [ ] Tested major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, ...)

body:
## Summary

Third updater-parity workstream. Until now the updater could only read the GitHub API token from the `UPDATER_GITHUB_TOKEN` env var. This adds an admin UI to configure it, stored **encrypted at rest** in the settings table — a convenience for hosts without env access, without weakening Cimaise's "no plaintext secret at rest" posture.

- **`app/Support/SecretBox.php`** — libsodium authenticated encryption (`sodium_crypto_secretbox`, XSalsa20-Poly1305). The key is derived from the existing `SESSION_SECRET` via a fixed-purpose `generichash`, so **no new env var** is introduced. When `SESSION_SECRET` is unset / still the shipped placeholder, or libsodium is missing, encryption reports unavailable and the feature falls back to env-only — it never writes a plaintext token. Wire format: `ENC:` + base64(nonce ‖ ciphertext).
- **`Updater::githubToken()`** — `UPDATER_GITHUB_TOKEN` still wins; otherwise the encrypted `updater.github_token` setting is decrypted on demand. Decrypt failure yields no token, never a leak. Token remains scoped to `api.github.com` (unchanged).
- **`UpdateController::saveToken()` + `POST /admin/updates/token`** — admin-only, CSRF-verified, rate-limited (5/600s). An empty submission clears the token. The token value is never echoed back or logged.
- **`updates.twig`** — a "GitHub token" card with a masked input, save/clear actions, and state notices (configured / overridden-by-env / encryption-unavailable). en + it strings added.

## Testing

- 8 SecretBox unit tests: round-trip, fresh nonce per encryption, tamper rejection (auth tag), and refusal under wrong key / placeholder / empty secret.
- Integration check on the dev DB: a token saved via the controller path round-trips through `SettingsService` into `Updater::githubToken()` with no plaintext at rest, and clears correctly.
- `updates.twig` parses; full PHPUnit suite green (71 tests).

author: jamubc
body:
## Why

The baseline `app.css` flagged that the full M4 visual language was still unbuilt, and the app shipped one hard-coded palette with no way to restyle it or share a look. A Claude Design handoff settled on four dark-first, near-monochrome directions; this change turns them into a data-driven theme system so the look is owned by the user, portable between users, and extensible without touching code. A keyboard-first command palette is added alongside so actions and theme switching are reachable without hunting through menus.

## What Changes

- Runtime CSS-variable theme engine: a theme is a typed token set (colors, fonts, metrics) for light and dark, applied to `:root` via `style.setProperty`, with Manuscript dark as the first-paint fallback in `app.css`. Existing tokens are kept; `--font-body`, `--font-meta`, `--accent-text`, and `--density` are added.
- Four built-in themes (Manuscript default, Graphite, Terminal, Paper Dark), each with light and dark variants.
- A rune-based theme store persists the active theme and light/dark/auto mode to the settings store and applies to both the library and capture windows.
- Sidebar ThemePicker: theme swatches, a light/dark/auto toggle, and import/export buttons.
- Portable theme sharing as `.intheme.json` files: a native open/save dialog (tauri-plugin-dialog), two thin `std::fs` shell commands, typed client wrappers, and an import validator that sanitizes untrusted values before any token is applied.
- A command palette: a fuzzy-filtered overlay with keyboard navigation and recents, covering note actions, theme switching, light/dark toggle, and theme import/export; filtering and ranking are isolated in `command-filter.ts` for unit tests.
- Capture, editor, and status surfaces adopt the body and meta fonts; the capture window reapplies the active theme on show; the library gains a live word count.

## ADDED Requirements (RFC 2119)

- The app SHALL apply a theme as runtime CSS custom properties on the document root, and MUST fall back to Manuscript dark on first paint before the store loads.
- A theme SHALL define token sets for both light and dark, and the app SHALL resolve the active variant from a light/dark/auto mode where auto follows the system appearance.
- The app SHALL ship four built-in themes (Manuscript, Graphite, Terminal, Paper Dark), with Manuscript as the default.
- The active theme and mode SHALL persist across launches via the settings store, and SHALL apply to both the library and capture windows.
- The app SHALL export the active theme as a portable `.intheme.json` file and SHALL import one through a native file dialog.
- Imported themes MUST be validated against the token allow-list and value patterns, and the app MUST NOT apply any token from a theme that fails validation. (Previously: no theme format existed, so external styling could not be loaded at all.)
- The command palette SHALL open on its shortcut and MUST support keyboard navigation (up, down, enter, escape) over a fuzzy-filtered command list.

## Scenario

#### Scenario: switch theme and persist across restart

- GIVEN the library open in the default Manuscript dark theme
- WHEN the user picks Terminal in the sidebar ThemePicker and sets the mode to light
- THEN the library, capture panel, and inline `#tag` color all retheme to Terminal light AND the choice survives an app restart

#### Scenario: import a shared theme file

- GIVEN a valid theme exported to `Graphite.intheme.json` on another machine
- WHEN the user chooses Import in the ThemePicker and selects that file
- THEN Graphite appears in the picker and applies, AND a malformed theme file is instead rejected with a message and no token is applied

## Verification

- [ ] 1.1 `npm test` passes (theme validate, theme apply, and command-filter unit tests)
- [ ] 1.2 `npm run check` passes with 0 errors
- [ ] 1.3 `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --workspace` passes
- [ ] 2.1 Cycle all four themes across light/dark/auto from the sidebar picker; the library, capture panel, and empty states retheme and the inline `#tag` color tracks the accent
- [ ] 2.2 Export a theme to a `.intheme.json` file, then re-import it: it appears in the picker and applies
- [ ] 2.3 Import a malformed theme file: it is rejected and no token is applied
- [ ] 3.1 The command palette opens on its shortcut; up, down, enter, and escape navigation works and the theme and light/dark commands act

body:
## Contexto

Categoria **A** da revisão de bugs. Auditoria de segurança identificou 7 mutations DML (UPDATE/DELETE) em tabelas multi-tenant que **NÃO filtravam por brand_id** no WHERE — deixando RLS como única defesa.

**Cenário de ataque mitigado**: se RLS quebrar amanhã por bug em migration, ou um admin esquecer `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, esses pontos vazariam. Defesa em profundidade evita isso.

## Mudanças (8 arquivos, +62/-10)

| Arquivo:linha | Mutation | Guard adicionado |
|---|---|---|
| `OffersPage.tsx:90` | UPDATE offers | `.eq("brand_id", currentBrandId)` quando não-root |
| `OffersPage.tsx:98` | DELETE offers | Idem |
| `StoresPage.tsx:96` | UPDATE stores | Idem |
| `StoresPage.tsx:104` | DELETE stores | Idem |
| `OperatorRedeemPage.tsx:65` | UPDATE redemption EXPIRED | `.eq("brand_id", data.brand_id)` |
| `RedeemPinInput.tsx:70` | Idem (duplicado) | Idem |
| `VoucherForm.tsx:105` | UPDATE vouchers | `.eq("branch_id", branchId)` |
| `StoreVoucherWizard.tsx:220` | UPDATE offers | `.eq("brand_id", brandId)` |
| `customerService.ts:64` | UPDATE customers | `.eq("brand_id", form.brand_id)` |
| `VoucherRedeem.tsx:87` | UPDATE voucher uses | `.eq("branch_id", voucher.branch_id)` + TODO race |

## Padrão usado

```ts
// Pra mutations em pages admin
let q = supabase.from("X").update(payload).eq("id", X);
if (!isRootAdmin && currentBrandId) q = q.eq("brand_id", currentBrandId);
const { error } = await q;
```

```ts
// Pra mutations com brand_id do registro recém-fetched (operator panel)
.update({...}).eq("id", data.id).eq("brand_id", (data as any).brand_id)
```

## Comportamento

- **root_admin** (impersonando brand): mesmo behavior, mutations funcionam em qualquer brand
- **brand_admin / branch_admin**: mutations bloqueadas se ID for de outra brand. Antes só dependia de RLS; agora além disso o WHERE falha (returns 0 rows updated, error não é lançado mas resultado vazio).
- **operator panel** (token + CPF auth): defense-in-depth contra colisão de token + RLS misconfig.

## NÃO incluído (follow-ups)

- `voucherService.toggleVoucherStatus` — function recebe só ID, precisaria mudar contrato + atualizar 1 teste. Marcar como tarefa futura.
- `VoucherRedeem` race no increment — anotado com `TODO(perf/race)`. Fix correto é RPC atômica.

## Verificação

- ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` passa (1 erro pré-existente em `ProductRedemptionOrdersPage.tsx`, não relacionado)
- ✅ Build verde
- ✅ Comportamento idêntico pra root_admin
- ✅ Sem mudança de contrato API

- **D** — useImpersonatingBrand não reativo
- **E** — Heap exhaustion em import-drivers

author: ferponse
body:
## Summary

execd already implements interactive PTY sessions — the `/pty` REST endpoints (create / status / delete) and the `/pty/{sessionId}/ws` WebSocket — but the Kotlin SDK had no way to reach them. This PR exposes the PTY session lifecycle in the SDK and builds the WebSocket URL clients connect to.

Adds a **`Pty`** service, accessible via **`sandbox.pty()`**:

- `createSession(cwd?, command?)` → `POST /pty` (the shell starts on first WebSocket attach).
- `getSession(sessionId)` → `GET /pty/{id}` (`running`, `outputOffset` for replay).
- `deleteSession(sessionId)` → `DELETE /pty/{id}`.
- `webSocketUrl(sessionId, mode = PTY, since?, takeover?)` — derives the `ws`/`wss` URL with the `pty=0` / `since=` / `takeover=1` query params, no network call.

```java
PtySession session = sandbox.pty().createSession();
String wsUrl = sandbox.pty().webSocketUrl(session.getSessionId()); // attach with any WS client
```

### Notes / scope

- The PTY routes are **not part of the OpenAPI specs** (the interactive channel is a WebSocket), so `PtyAdapter` is **handwritten OkHttp transport**, mirroring the existing SSE command stream. No spec/server/generated-code changes.
- This lands the **session lifecycle + URL**. Driving the binary WebSocket protocol (stdin/stdout frames, resize, takeover handling) is intentionally left to the caller for now; a follow-up can add an in-SDK WebSocket client if maintainers want it.
- This is the first client SDK to surface PTY — happy to align Python/Go/JS/C# in follow-ups if you'd like parity.

## Testing

- `./gradlew spotlessCheck :sandbox:test` — green (full `:sandbox` suite: 184 tests, 0 failures).
- New `PtyAdapterTest` (MockWebServer) covers create/get/delete request shape and parsing, error status mapping, endpoint-header forwarding, and the `webSocketUrl` builder (params + `wss` for https). `SandboxTest` covers the `pty()` accessor.

## Breaking Changes

None for SDK consumers (additive API). Note: the internal `Sandbox` constructor gains a `ptyService` parameter — it is `internal`, not part of the public surface.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional Commits
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Java interop preserved (builders/accessors, no coroutines, `java.time` unaffected)
- [x] No generated code edited
- [ ] Open to adding the `/pty` paths to `specs/execd-api.yaml` + an E2E in `tests/java/` if preferred

- **`unik3d-large-nyuv2`** (new): UniK3D-Large (CVPR 2025) on the NYUv2 Eigen test, **metric depth, no scale/shift alignment**. Reproduces the paper's zero-shot NYUv2 row out of the box on UniK3D's default inference bounds (no `resolution_level` tuning):

  | Metric | Observed | Paper (Table 18) | Δ |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | AbsRel | **0.0749** | 0.074 | +1.2% |
  | δ₁ | **0.9656** | 0.965 | ≈exact |
  | RMSE | **0.2632** | 0.259 | +1.6% |

  654/654 frames on a GTX 1080 Ti.

- **Fix: UniK3D now loads for inference.** The vendored inference subset prunes `unik3d.ops.losses`, but `UniK3D.build_losses` (run via `__init__` → `from_pretrained`) imported it unconditionally → `ModuleNotFoundError`, so the model could not be instantiated at all. `build_losses` now no-ops when the pruned module is absent (the loss dict is read only on the training path, never in `infer`).

## Paper provenance

Target PDF-verified against **arXiv:2503.16591, Appendix C.2 Table 18** ("zero-shot evaluation for NYUv2"), UniK3D-Large row, **metric** columns (δ₁ 96.5 / A.Rel 7.4 / RMSE 0.259) — *not* the δ₁^SSI scale-shift column. See `reproductions/AUDIT.md`.

## Matrix impact

Verified-cell count **38 → 39** (32 mono-depth), and UniK3D is added as a new model family (models 13 → 14). Docs, site, and queue updated to match.

body:
## Summary

Phase 1, slice 2: routes the three game-identity facades through `EffectiveManifest.Current` and adds the `SetRemote` hook the App will call at startup once a feed exists. This is the integration seam — the point a verified remote manifest plugs in to override/extend the embedded one. **Ships inert** (nothing calls `SetRemote` in production yet) with **zero observable behavior change**, proven by the parity tests passing with their files byte-for-byte untouched.

- `EffectiveManifest` gains `Current` (= `Merge(embedded, remote)`), `SetRemote(GameManifest?)`, and a monotonic `Generation` counter. `Merge` unchanged. Lock-free reads (`volatile` remote ref + `Interlocked` generation); `SetRemote` is a startup-time single-writer op.
- `KnownEngines` / `NexusDomains` / `PopularGames` now read `EffectiveManifest.Current` through a **generation-checked cache** — rebuild only when `SetRemote` bumps the generation. Public signatures unchanged; consumers untouched.

## Why inert is correct here

`Merge(embedded, null)` returns the embedded manifest by reference, so with no remote set `EffectiveManifest.Current == EmbeddedGameManifest.Current` and every facade answers identically. The `SetRemote` hook exists and is fully tested, but its first production caller — the App-side `RemoteManifestSource` (HttpClient fetch → on-disk cache → `SetRemote` at startup) + settings toggle — is the next slice. Seam first, proven inert, then plug in the source (same order as the trust core).

## Test isolation (how the parity files stayed untouched)

`SetRemote` is process-global mutable state, which would otherwise race the parity tests under xUnit's default parallelism. The new state-mutating tests live in a `[CollectionDefinition("ManifestState", DisableParallelization = true)]` collection and reset `SetRemote(null)` via `IDisposable` — so they never run concurrently with, nor leak into, the parity tests. The three parity test files are **not edited** (empty `git diff`), so the zero-behavior-change proof is as strong as the prior slices.

## How it was verified

- **Full Core suite:** `Failed: 0, Passed: 1125, Skipped: 2` (pre-existing env-gated 7z/rar skips). Re-run by hand.
- **Parity files untouched:** `git diff master..HEAD` on `KnownEnginesTests.cs`/`PopularGamesTests.cs`/`NexusGameDomainTests.cs` is empty.
- **Scope:** `git diff --name-only master..HEAD -- src/` lists only `EffectiveManifest.cs` + the 3 facades. No `src/ModManager.App`, no `HttpClient`/`System.Net`. `CorePurityTests` green (only `System.Threading` added to Core).
- New `FacadeRemoteWiringTests` proves each facade reflects a `SetRemote`'d remote game; `EffectiveManifestStateTests` covers the state/generation/revert behavior.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI green on the Core suite
- [ ] Confirm the 3 parity test files are unchanged in the diff
- [ ] Sanity-read the generation-checked cache + `EffectiveManifest` thread-safety

> Deferred per your call, unchanged by this slice: signing keypair, the `626-game-manifest` feed repo, and the pre-publish licensing sign-off (spec §11 #6). None are needed here.

## Summary

When a channel-specific `beforeDeliver` existed, the composed hook chain only included the channel hook + `reply_payload_sending`, silently bypassing global `message_sending` hooks. This meant `{ cancel: true }` and content rewrite from `message_sending` hooks were ignored for channel-agent replies.

## Root cause

Both `dispatchInboundMessageWithBufferedDispatcher` and `dispatchInboundMessageWithDispatcher` had:
```
const composed = beforeDeliver
  ? combine(beforeDeliver, replyPayload)     // missing message_sending!
  : combine(replyPayload, messageSending)     // correct
```

## Fix

Both paths now always include `message_sending` in the composed chain:
```
const composed = beforeDeliver
  ? combine(beforeDeliver, replyPayload, messageSending)
  : combine(replyPayload, messageSending)
```

Updated existing test that asserted the old (buggy) behavior to verify message_sending runs.

## Files changed
- `src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts` — 2 composition sites (+6 lines)
- `src/auto-reply/dispatch.test.ts` — updated test expectations (+12 lines)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Global `message_sending` hooks were silently bypassed when any channel had a configured `beforeDeliver`. The `{ cancel: true }` return and content rewrite from plugin message_sending hooks were ignored.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at PR head, macOS/Darwin arm64, Node v22.22.0.

**Exact steps run after this patch:**
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/dispatch.test.ts
```
All 19 tests pass, including updated test "composes custom beforeDeliver with reply_payload_sending hooks" which now correctly asserts `runMessageSending` is called 2 times (was previously asserting NOT called — the buggy behavior).

Closes #92374

JAXPXPathEngine's Source-based xpath methods bypassed the secure parser:
- selectNodes(String, Source) and evaluate(String, Source) handed Convert.toInputSource(s) to javax.xml.xpath.XPath.evaluate, which parses with JAXP's own default factory, so a DOCTYPE declaring an external SYSTEM entity in the source was resolved during evaluation
- the Node-based overloads and the HasXPathMatcher/EvaluateXPathMatcher matchers already route through Convert.toNode, which uses DocumentBuilderFactoryConfigurer.Default
- both Source methods now do the same and delegate to those overloads
Added a regression test that feeds an external entity through both methods.

author: duynhne
body:
Cache review (code-review-and-quality + doubt-driven-development) found real bugs that surface under outage / slow DB / concurrency / punctuated input. This fixes the critical + correctness ones; docs updated in `homelab` (`docs/caching/caching.md`).

## Changes
- **🔴 Fail-open on cache errors** — `GetProductOrSet` now treats a Valkey `GET`/`SETNX` error as a miss and degrades to the DB, instead of returning the error (a cache outage previously 500'd every `GET /products/:id`; the list path was already fail-open).
- **🟠 Safe lock release** — the stampede lock carries a per-acquisition random token and is released via `DeleteIfEqual` (Lua compare-and-delete). A fetch that overran the 5s lock TTL can no longer delete a successor's lock. (New `DeleteIfEqual` on the `CacheClient` interface.)
- **🟠 Collision-safe list keys** — `generateProductListKey` hashes the normalized filter tuple (sha256) instead of concatenating raw values, removing the `search="a:b"` collision class. `product:list:` prefix kept so `product:list:*` invalidation still matches.
- **🟡 TTL jitter** — list/detail TTLs get ≤10% jitter to avoid synchronized expiry waves.

## Out of scope (documented as limitations, not fixed here)
Negative caching, waiter-timeout tuning, uncancellable lock-release context, cross-service invalidation hook, Update/Delete invalidation. See the caching doc's *Resilience* and *Ownership & Invalidation Boundary* sections.

## Tests / verification
- New unit tests: fail-open (failing client still returns DB value), compare-and-delete (wrong token can't release), key non-collision, jitter bounds. `go test ./...` green.
- local-stack: list/detail/aggregation work; Valkey now shows hashed list keys (`product:list:<sha256>`); 404 returns `{"code":"NOT_FOUND",...}`.

author: julesseg
body:
## What

Adds the **maps branch** to the Share Capture classifier (#108), governed by **ADR-0007**. A Google Maps (`maps.app.goo.gl`, `google.*/maps`, `maps.google.*`) or Apple Maps (`maps.apple.com`) link now becomes a **Place** Item (`category: location`) with the original link kept in `notes` so it stays tappable, the address taken from the shared text, and coordinates resolved best-effort in layers.

## Coordinate resolution (ADR-0007 layers)

1. **Parse the URL offline** — `@lat,lng` / `?q=lat,lng` / `!3d…!4d…` are read with no network call (`classifyShare` → `parseMapsUrl`).
2. **Follow a short link's redirect** and parse the resolved URL (`resolveShareCoords` → `resolveMapsUrl`).
3. **Photon geocode** of the shared name/address when the redirect yields no pin.
4. **Total failure → address-only Place, no pin** — the capture is never dropped.

The Share editor resolves the pin *before* opening (instant for full URLs, a network hop for short links) so the editor mounts exactly once with its final location rather than re-seeding mid-edit. The user still confirms the draft before it's saved.

## Interface

- `classifyShare` gains a maps-link branch and `ShareDraft` gains an optional `location` (layer 1, sync/offline).
- New async `resolveShareCoords(payload, { fetchImpl?, geocode? })` encapsulates the network layers + fallback; `fetchImpl` and `geocode` are injectable for unit tests.

## Tests

Built test-first, one behavior per cycle:
- `lib/share-capture.test.ts` — host detection across all maps variants (and look-alike hosts staying generic), address/coords extraction, and each resolution layer including the offline total-failure fallback.
- `__tests__/share-screen.test.tsx` — the editor seeds a Place with resolved coordinates, and falls back to an address-only Place when no pin resolves.

Full suite: **474 passing**, typecheck clean, no new lint warnings.

Closes #109

author: bjmorgan
body:
## Summary

`DefectSystem.site_percentages` computed each species' occupancy from the unbounded dilute Boltzmann expression (`DefectSpecies.get_concentration` divided by `nsites`), which ignores site-exclusion statistics and `site_pools`/`element_pools` competition. A near-saturation or pooled species could therefore report occupancies far above 100% (for example ~2.5e10% for a low-energy species), contradicting the concentrations reported by `report` and `concentration_dict`.

The occupancies are now taken from `_global_defect_concs` at the self-consistent Fermi level -- the same source of truth the rest of the class uses -- and each species' total is divided by the sites available to it: its own `nsites`, or, for a species in a `site_pools` entry, that pool's total site count (so a pool's members together occupy at most 100% of it). A species' concentration cannot exceed its available sites -- a fixed concentration over the site budget is rejected at construction rather than being reported -- so every reported occupancy is at most 100%.

The method signature and return type are unchanged.

author: colbymchenry
body:
Follow-up to #845: the reporter had no clean way to shut down a runaway daemon (`kill -TERM` did nothing, resorted to `kill -KILL`). This adds first-class daemon control.

## Commands

- **`codegraph stop [path]`** — stop the daemon for the current project (no arg → resolves the root from cwd, walking up exactly like the daemon does), or a given path. SIGTERM → wait → SIGKILL fallback, then sweeps the lockfile / socket / registry record.
- **`codegraph stop --all`** — stop every running daemon on the machine (the "it's eating my machine" case from #845).
- **`codegraph list`** (alias `ps`) — show running daemons (root, pid, version, uptime); `--json` for scripts.

## Discovery — a small global registry

There was no central record of running daemons (each only writes a per-project lockfile). So each daemon now drops a tiny record under `~/.codegraph/daemons/` on start (`Daemon.start`) and removes it on graceful shutdown (`Daemon.stop`). Readers **prune any record whose pid is dead**, so a `kill -9`'d daemon self-heals — the registry is a discovery index, never the source of truth (the live pid is). Every read/write is best-effort; a registry hiccup can't break the daemon or a command.

Cross-platform by construction: only files + `process.kill` (which behave the same on macOS/Linux real-signals and Windows TerminateProcess). `stopDaemonAt` sweeps artifacts itself, so the forceful-SIGTERM-on-Windows path still leaves no lockfile/socket behind.

## Validated live on all three platforms

Registry unit tests (`__tests__/daemon-registry.test.ts`, 6) + a real-daemon end-to-end script (spawn a `serve --mcp` daemon → `list` shows it → `stop` → process dead, lockfile cleaned, `list` empty):

| | registry unit | live stop/list |
|---|---|---|
| **macOS** | 6/6 | 6/6 (+ `stop --all` with 2 daemons, `list --json`) |
| **Linux** (docker `--init`) | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| **Windows** (VM) | 6/6 | 6/6 |

A settled daemon stops gracefully in ~100ms (measured); a daemon still warming up (engine init) exceeds the 3s SIGTERM grace and gets the SIGKILL fallback — honest and always reliable. Full suite green (77 files, 1516 passed / 2 skipped).

author: mgfv2r2mpv-hash
body:
## Summary

Fixes the cold-launch persistence bug and tightens schedule-password handling.

### Bug: schedule didn't reopen after PIN unlock (root cause)
`clientCrypto.encryptString` ended with `btoa(String.fromCharCode(...combined))`. Spreading a large `Uint8Array` (a whole encrypted `ScheduleData`) overflows the JS argument-count limit and throws `RangeError`. Since `saveSchedule` is fire-and-forget (`void`), the throw was swallowed — so the at-rest schedule blob was **never written**. The tiny PIN verifier still encrypted fine (hence the PIN screen persisted), but unlock found no schedule and the app came back blank.

Fix: convert to base64 in 32 KB chunks. Verified with a 300 KB round-trip (the old path threw on the same input); wrong-PIN still rejects.

### Imported encrypted schedule → default export password
After successfully decrypting an imported encrypted file, its password becomes the session's schedule password, so exporting re-encrypts with the same password automatically (no re-entry on a round-trip).

### Schedule password is write-once-then-guarded
- The set password is **never re-displayed** in Settings.
- Changing it now **requires the current password** — a wrong/forgotten one would orphan already-exported encrypted files, so the change is gated and verified.
- Includes a warning that files exported under the old password still need the old password.

`tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` pass.

author: fkeijzer
body:
## Summary
Improves Obsidian startup time when a calendar view is restored from the previous session, and fixes the sidebar calendar only filling half its height.

## Changes
- **Defer heavy work to `onLayoutReady`**: cache population and FullCalendar rendering are deferred until Obsidian finishes its own layout, so the plugin no longer blocks startup. A lightweight "Loading calendar…" placeholder is shown in the meantime.
- **Responsive layout after deferred render**: re-apply `onResize()` once after a deferred render (height + day/week view), since Obsidian's own `onResize` has already fired by then.
- **Deterministic height**: give FullCalendar an explicit `height: '100%'` + `expandRows` and a full-height container, so it fills the available space instead of falling back to a too-short, width-based height in a narrow sidebar.
- Bump version to `1.0.1` and add `versions.json`.

## Testing
Verified in the user's vault: startup is noticeably faster, the sidebar calendar opens in day view at full height, and event loading happens after the rest of the UI is ready.

This is only factory-dispatch assembly. It does not read runtime state, compile packets from stores, aggregate packets, execute transactions, call models, or generate narration.

author: eddie-knight
body:
Does what it says on the tin.

## Potential pitfall

There is currently no mechanism for steps to send evidence back up the chain.

We don't pass the payload in as a pointer (allowing modification which can be read later) and we obviously don't return evidence at the end of a step. So as this presently stands, it will be incumbent on the user to incorporate global state management to move evidence gathered during a step back up to the assessment that invoked it.

The alternative is to tolerate a breaking change to support Evidence — which will impact every step in any scanner that is already using this part of the SDK.

Leaving this in draft until we figure out what solution we're going to recommend / produce.

Complete overhaul of power-up system and game UI for v1 release. Addresses three core areas: (1) turn ownership clarity on mobile/desktop, (2) notification spam reduction, (3) power-up mechanics to make them feel strategic and scarce.

### Key Changes

**A. Turn Ownership Clarity**
- Central countdown timer between player avatars (turns red ≤5s, amber ≤10s)

author: komediruzecki
body:
Bundles several 3D-editor and data-management UX improvements. Version bumped to **0.9.4**; `pnpm check` and the full test suite (147 tests, incl. new smart-affine math tests) pass.

## Camera & shortcuts
- **Fix: right/middle-click drag-to-pan in 3D did nothing.** The 3D camera routed middle/right-button drags to its pan handler, but the shared `createDragHandler` silently ignored every button except left, so mouse panning never started (only WASD/arrow pan worked). The helper now accepts an optional `button` set; the 3D camera pans on middle (1) / right (2) and keeps orbit on left. Right-click still suppresses the canvas context menu.
- **Theme toggle moved `D` → `Ctrl/Cmd+D`.** Plain `D` is part of the WASD pan set, so it double-fired (panned *and* flipped the theme). The 3D camera now ignores modified movement keys, and the About panel's shortcut list is updated with a dedicated **3D Camera** controls section (orbit / pan / WASD / scroll-zoom).

## Fly mode (3D)
- First-person navigation **toggle in the action widget's second row** (3D only): `W`/`S` fly along the view direction, `A`/`D` strafe, `Q`/`E` descend/ascend, **left-drag looks around** (turn in place instead of orbiting). Reuses the existing spherical camera by keeping the eye fixed and moving the target.
- **Movement speed via scroll** while flying, plus a **Speed** scrub in the View Controls next to the camera options (persisted).

## Randomizer — Smart vs Full affine mutation
- The Flame Randomizer's *Mutate* gains an **Affine Mode** toggle. **Smart** composes the existing affine with random, well-defined rotate / scale / flip / translate operations (2D **and** 3D) so mutations stay recognisable instead of collapsing into degenerate maps; **Full** keeps the previous per-coefficient randomization. Remembered between sessions, default Smart.

## Share dialog
- Notes that short `?s=` links **expire after 60 days** (matches the Worker's `SHORTEN_TTL`) and adds **Copy full link** for the self-contained `?flame=` link, which carries all data inline and never expires.

## About panel — Storage & Data
- **Usage breakdown** per group (settings, recent flames, generated history, logo/favicon history) with item counts and a total.
- **Danger Zone:** two separate, confirm-gated actions — *clear all settings* and *delete all stored flames* — each listing how many items / how much space will be recovered.
- **Backup/export as ZIP** (built on `fflate`): individually selectable groups exported as JSON descriptors + PNGs with the flame embedded (from stored history thumbnails), plus a `manifest.json`. Fresh high-res batch renders are a planned follow-up — any flame can already be loaded and re-exported at full quality.

## Notes
- New dependency: `fflate` (^0.8.3) for ZIP creation.
- New files: `utils/flameBackup.ts`, `utils/storageUsage.ts`, `components/DataManagement/*`, `flame/randomize.test.ts`.

author: edrejta
body:
Two fixes (bundled to merge together).

## 1. `fix(security):` clear query cache on account switch
Switching accounts showed the previous restaurant's metrics for a few seconds. The generically-keyed TanStack Query caches survived the identity change. `AuthCacheReset` in `AppProviders` now `queryClient.clear()`s when the signed-in user id changes away from a known user (logout / account switch).

## 2. `fix(devops):` restore the GHCR pull secret on project-05 pods
**This is what's hanging the current deploy.** The dedicated ServiceAccounts added in #159 (for `automountServiceAccountToken: false`) moved the app pods off the namespace `default` SA — which carries the `ghcr-pull` imagePullSecret. The pods stopped inheriting it and failed to pull the **private** GHCR images with **401 → ImagePullBackOff**, so `helm --atomic` hangs every deploy (the old pod keeps serving, so no outage).

Fix: set `imagePullSecrets: [ghcr-pull]` explicitly in the project-05 overlays for backend/frontend/aiops. The secret already exists in the namespace; local/minikube is unaffected. Verified: all three charts render `ghcr-pull` and lint clean.

> Once this merges, the next CD deploy gives the pods their pull credential → images pull → deploy succeeds → `development` tip goes green.

## Descrição

Implementa o mapa interativo (RF05 / US 2.2.2): ao acessar `/mapa`, o usuário vê um mapa em tela cheia, centralizado no Distrito Federal, totalmente explorável (zoom e arraste). O cabeçalho e o menu ficam sobrepostos ao mapa, sem faixa de separação, e o rodapé é ocultado nessa rota. Por enquanto, nenhuma ocorrência é exibida no mapa — marcadores serão adicionados em uma feature futura, após a pesquisa no dashboard.

A implementação foi feita seguindo TDD: testes escritos primeiro (red), depois o código necessário para passá-los (green), com refatoração ao final.

## Tipo de mudança

- [x] Nova funcionalidade
- [x] Testes

## Issue relacionada

RF05 / US 2.2.2 — Mapa interativo (`frontend/Specs/Specs_mapa_interativo/spec.md`)

## Como testar

1. `git checkout feat/frontend-mapa-interativo`
2. `cd frontend`
3. `npm install`
4. `npm run dev`
5. Acesse `http://localhost:3000/mapa`
6. Verifique:
   - O mapa ocupa a tela inteira, centralizado no DF
   - É possível arrastar e dar zoom (controles de zoom no canto inferior esquerdo)
   - O cabeçalho/logo/menu aparecem sobrepostos ao mapa, sem barra de pesquisa
   - O rodapé não aparece nessa rota
   - Nenhum marcador é exibido no mapa

Para rodar os testes automatizados:
```powershell
npm test
```

## Evidências

- Print do mapa renderizado em `/mapa` (enviado anteriormente no chat)

## Impactos e riscos

- Novas dependências adicionadas: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`
- O componente `Header` recebeu uma prop `overlay` opcional; o comportamento padrão (outras rotas) não é afetado
- O `Chrome` agora detecta a rota atual para decidir o layout (overlay apenas em `/mapa`)
- Sem impacto em backend, autenticação ou dados sensíveis (tiles do OpenStreetMap, sem chave de API)

## Checklist

- [x] Código segue os padrões do projeto (TypeScript, CSS Modules)
- [x] Testes novos/atualizados cobrindo o comportamento implementado
- [x] `npm test` passa localmente
- [x] Documentação da spec (`spec.md`/`plan.md`/`tasks.md`) atualizada

## Observações adicionais

Esta é a primeira etapa do mapeamento de ocorrências (Épico 2). A exibição de marcadores/ocorrências será feita em uma feature futura, após a pesquisa no dashboard (RF04/RF06).

body: Adds a **TVL adapter** for [T3tris Finance](https://app.t3tris.finance) — an ERC-4626 vault protocol with async deposit/redeem flows and silo-based strategies routing into underlying yield sources. The protocol is deployed at a deterministic CREATE3 address (`0x0000000000CC53b5Fd649b80f08b05405779cC71`), identical on every EVM chain. The adapter enumerates all vaults via the protocol factory and sums each vault's `getGrossTVL()` breakdown per underlying token. author: adrianthedev
body: ## Problem External sidebar links can incorrectly receive the `active` class and `aria-current="page"`. Given a custom menu like: ```ruby group do link_to "Avo", "https://avohq.io", target: :_blank link_to "Google", "https://google.com", target: :_blank end ``` with Avo mounted at `/avo`, the **Avo** link renders as active while **Google** does not. ## Cause `Avo::Sidebar::LinkComponent#is_external?` decided externalness with a raw substring check: ```ruby return !@path.include?(helpers.mount_path) if URI(@path).scheme.present? ``` `"https://avohq.io".include?("/avo")` is `true` — the `//avohq.io` portion contains the substring `/avo`. So the link was classified as *internal*, routed through `active_link_to`, and matched as active. `google.com` has no such collision, so it was correctly treated as external. ## Fix Parse the URL and compare its **path component** against the mount path, so only links whose path is genuinely mounted under Avo count as internal: ```ruby def is_external? uri = URI(@path) return false if uri.scheme.blank? !uri.path.start_with?(helpers.mount_path) rescue URI::InvalidURIError true end ``` | URL | before | after | |---|---|---| | `https://avohq.io` | internal ❌ | external ✅ | | `https://google.com` | external | external | | `/avo/resources/users` | internal | internal | | `https://demo.example.com/avo/x` | internal | internal | ## Tests Adds `spec/components/avo/sidebar/link_component_spec.rb` covering relative paths, internal full URLs, external hosts, the `avohq.io` collision regression, and invalid URIs. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Localized sidebar link classification and test timing; no auth, data, or API behavior changes. > > **Overview** > Fixes sidebar links like `https://avohq.io` being treated as internal when Avo is mounted at `/avo`, which routed them through `active_link_to` and incorrectly marked them active. > > **`LinkComponent#is_external?`** now parses the URL and treats scheme-less paths as internal; for absolute URLs it compares `uri.path` to `helpers.root_path_without_url` (prefix + mount), treats invalid URIs as external, and no longer uses `String#include?(mount_path)` on the full URL. > > Adds **`spec/components/avo/sidebar/link_component_spec.rb`** for relative paths, internal full URLs (including `prefix_path`), external hosts, the `avohq.io` regression, and bad URIs. > > **`manual_loading_memory_spec`** waits for `tabindex='-1'` on the turbo-frame after “Load Comments” so the manual-frame cookie is written before the next `visit`, reducing flake on return-visit auto-load assertions. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 06ac2d6657501d29de2f047b140f3b3d4260aa8b. author: zanip23
body:
## Summary
This PR adds a virtual joystick control system for touch input, enabling mobile players to steer the ship using an on-screen joystick instead of relying solely on keyboard or mouse controls.

## Key Changes
- **Virtual Joystick Input Handler**: Added touch-aware pointer event handling that detects touch input and initializes a joystick when the user touches the screen
- **Joystick Rendering**: Implemented visual joystick feedback with a circular base and draggable knob that displays in the UI layer
- **Joystick Movement Logic**: Added `handleJoystick()` method that converts joystick input into ship navigation targets, with proper clamping to map boundaries
- **Touch Detection**: Implemented `_isTouchPointer()` helper to distinguish between touch and mouse/pointer input
- **Joystick State Management**: Added joystick lifecycle methods (`_joyStart`, `_joyMove`, `_joyEnd`) to track touch position, calculate angle and distance, and clean up when touch ends
- **Input Event Refactoring**: Updated pointer event handlers to route touch input to joystick and mouse input to existing sea pointer logic

## Implementation Details
- Joystick radius is configurable via `JOY_RADIUS` constant (70 pixels)
- The joystick knob is clamped to the radius boundary while tracking full distance for angle calculation
- Touch input is ignored if UI elements are present or if the ship is wrecked
- Joystick graphics are rendered at depth 201 to appear above game elements
- When joystick is active, it sets `sailTarget` to guide the ship toward the joystick direction

author: scottopell
body:
## Summary

Eliminates a recurring React perf problem: **completed markdown content being re-parsed through `ReactMarkdown` on every re-render of a component that re-renders frequently** (per streaming token, or per tool-result arrival). `StreamingMessage` already solved this for its own tail via a memoized per-block component; these changes apply the same pattern everywhere else the class occurs.

Most of the UI's hot paths were already well optimized (virtualized message list, streaming isolation, memoized handlers). This PR targets the three places that were missing per-block / per-row memoization.

## Changes

**1. `AgentMessage` prose blocks (`MessageComponents.tsx`)**
The historical agent message rendered each prose block with an inline `<ReactMarkdown>`. During an active turn the `toolResults` Map gets a new identity each time a tool result lands, re-rendering `AgentMessage` and re-parsing **every** prose block even though the text is unchanged.
- Extracted a memoized `AgentTextBlock`. `remarkPlugins` is a module constant and `components` is the memoized `markdownComponents` map, so a shallow prop compare bails for unchanged prose.
- `markdownComponents` also allocated a fresh `fileClickHandler` closure **and** a `new Set()` per code/paragraph/list node on every render — now one shared handler + a shared `EMPTY_LINE_SET`.

**2. Sub-agent transcript (`MessageComponents.tsx`)**
`SubAgentTranscript` re-renders per token while a sub-agent streams. It rebuilt a `toolResults` Map every render and re-rendered every (completed) step, re-parsing their markdown.
- Memoized `ChildAgentActivity`.
- Derived `toolResults` / `agentMessages` / counts with `useMemo` keyed on `atom.messages`. `sse_token` preserves that array's identity (only `streamingBuffer` grows), so finished steps bail instead of re-parsing.

**3. Chain Q&A list (`ChainPage.tsx`)**
`ChainPage` re-renders the whole Q&A list on every inflight token, re-parsing every persisted answer's markdown.
- Memoized `PersistedPairCard`.
- Made `handleReask` referentially stable (reads `draft` via the existing ref) so `onReask` no longer breaks the memo.

The actively-streaming tail in each case (the streaming buffer / inflight answer) still re-parses, which is intrinsic and matches how `StreamingMessage` handles its growing tail.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm test` (76 files / **945 tests**) all pass.

## Context

Go-live hardening (BACKLOG): _verify graceful shutdown + health checks under load_. The shutdown sequence and `/health` + `/health/ready` probes already existed; this closes the drain gap and adds the missing test coverage. **Safe items only** — Astro 5→6 major, `npm audit` major bumps, and Sentry DSN are deliberately left to separate PRs / Franck.

## Changes

**Graceful drain**
- New `utils/shutdown.ts` (`isShuttingDown` / `beginShutdown`). `GET /health/ready` now returns **503 `shutting_down`** the moment shutdown begins, so the load balancer stops routing to this instance *before* the HTTP server closes connections — the piece that was missing for clean draining under load.

**Shutdown robustness**
- `gracefulShutdown` guarded against double signals (SIGTERM → SIGINT) via the idempotent `beginShutdown()` (was previously runnable twice → workers stopped twice).

**Tests (were none for health)**
- Liveness returns healthy without touching dependencies.
- Readiness: 200 when DB+Redis up; 503 when DB down; 503 when Redis ≠ PONG; 503 `shutting_down` during drain (and skips dependency probes).
- Unit test for the idempotent double-signal guard.

## Verification
- `nx typecheck api`: pass.
- Full API suite: **751 passed, 8 skipped** (+8 new).

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)
- Astro 5 → 6 (landing) — risky major, own PR.
- 15 `npm audit` vulns — Dependabot security PRs / deliberate major bumps.
- Confirm Sentry DSN configured in prod (ops / Franck).
- Real under-load drain test belongs in a load-test/staging run, not unit tests.

author: jsakkos
body:
## Summary
Episode promotion was capped at ~75–106 contributions/run by the per-group D1 write path, and had **no `ORDER BY`**, so recent shows (e.g. The Wire, `tmdb_id 1438`) starved and never appeared in the catalog browser (which reads only `episode_canonical`). Full investigation + evidence in the spec below.

- **Oldest-first + bounded:** `runPromotion` selects groups `ORDER BY MIN(received_at) ASC LIMIT PROMOTION_BATCH_LIMIT` (100) — longest-waiting contributions promote first; per-run work is bounded so a run never depends on draining the whole backlog.
- **Fewer D1 round-trips:** `promoteOne` folds the flagged-contributor check into the main read (`LEFT JOIN contributor`) and batches the canonical `INSERT` + mark-promoted `UPDATE` into one atomic `env.DB.batch()` — ~4 → ~2 D1 ops/group.
- **Own cron:** episode promotion moved from the shared `0 3 * * *` to its own `30 * * * *` (hourly, isolated from disc promotion and the sketch builder). ~2,400/day capacity vs ~90/day intake.
- Removed the diagnostic `_dev/run` route used during investigation.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-promotion-throughput-fix-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-13-promotion-throughput-fix.md`

body:
The main change here is to make any variables defined in the C++ base classes accessible via the interface in C#/Java when they were just completely lost before. For Java, any nested classes defined in these base classes are exported from the interface as well, but this is not done for C# because:

1. This is "only" available since C# 8 and so would require an option allowing to generate code requiring it.
2. Unlike Java, C# doesn't allow to refer to the nested classes defined in an interface using the derived class scope, which makes this much less useful, at least for my purposes.

Seeing that most of the recent changes in SWIG have been done by Claude, I've decided to use it for these changes too. FWIW I've reviewed all the changes in the first 3 commits but made only minor corrections to them, i.e. LLM-generated code looks fine to me.

author: jensmunkhansen
body:
Foundations for `KHR_materials_transmission` (glass), plus a validation fix that
makes the hand-written sync in this and future passes verifiable. The refraction
draw pass + shader are intentionally **not** in this PR — see *Not included*.

## Validation backstop (essential fix)
- **Re-enabled validation layers.** A stray unconditional `set(VKWAVE_DEBUG OFF)`
  after the auto-enable block left `VKWAVE_DEBUG` always undefined, so the
  validation layer and debug messenger were compiled out of **every** build — no
  validation ran at all.
- Wired `VKWAVE_DEBUG` as a **per-config compile definition**
  (`$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:VKWAVE_DEBUG>`). Required under the Ninja Multi-Config
  generator: `config.h` is generated once and shared across configs, so a
  `#cmakedefine` cannot vary Debug vs Release. Debug gets validation; Release
  stays clean.
- **Enabled synchronization validation**
  (`VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_SYNCHRONIZATION_VALIDATION_EXT` via
  `VkValidationFeaturesEXT` on the instance `pNext`). Standard validation catches
  API/state misuse but not GPU sync hazards; this flags missing/too-narrow
  barriers (it would have caught the earlier pbr→composite wait-stage bug).
  Verified by a deliberately-removed mip barrier producing a `READ_AFTER_WRITE`
  hazard with no env-var override.

## Transmission groundwork
- **Slice 1 — detect + gate.** `SceneData::has_transmission()` scans materials;
  when a scene has glass, a per-slot `transmission_snapshot` color resource is
  registered in the graph's `FrameResourcePool` (`eSampled | eTransferDst`).
  Gated at **build time**, so non-glass scenes pay no VRAM and keep the
  opaque-only DAG.
- **Slice 2 — snapshot the opaque HDR.** `record_transmission_snapshot_copy()`
  (`app/transmission.{h,cpp}`) does an exact `vkCmdCopyImage` from the opaque HDR
  into the per-slot snapshot, recorded at the **tail of the opaque command
  buffer** — same submission, no extra `vkQueueSubmit`. Fine-grained barriers on
  exactly the two images (never a global barrier): HDR
  `ShaderReadOnly→TransferSrc→ShaderReadOnly`, snapshot
  `Undefined→TransferDst→ShaderReadOnly`. Merged into the pbr group's existing
  post-record (screenshot copy) rather than overwriting it.
- Added the `TransmissionTest` conformance asset (fetch + `model_paths`);

As the Palette agent, I identified a micro-UX improvement across the standalone visual analyzer HTML files. 

Interactive elements like the "Analyze Chat" button and the "Select User" dropdowns were initialized in a `disabled` state without any explanation. This can be confusing for standard users and completely opaque to screen readers. 

I added explicit `title` attributes (e.g., `title="Upload a file first"`) to these elements. I then updated the JavaScript event listeners to dynamically remove the `title` attribute when the elements become active (after a file is uploaded/parsed), and restore them if an error occurs. 

Additionally, while making these changes, I noticed and fixed a logical bug in `visual_2.html` and `visual_3.html` where a failed file read (`FileReader.onerror`) would incorrectly re-enable the user select dropdown.

Finally, I updated the `.Jules/palette.md` journal with this critical accessibility learning and fixed a few minor test/environment configuration issues in the Python backend to ensure the full test suite could run and validate no regressions were introduced.

author: snuffy2
body:
## Summary
Updates the release flow so published stable releases move a real Git `latest` tag that ESPHome configs can track directly. It also simplifies local builds by removing GitHub API release lookup from `scripts/build` and improves workflow behavior with safer release serialization and ESPHome/PlatformIO caching.

## What Changed
- Added release workflow handling to move the `latest` tag after stable published releases.
- Skipped release tag mutations for prereleases so prerelease publication does not move version tags or `latest`.
- Serialized release workflow runs through a shared `release-latest` concurrency group to avoid older releases moving `latest` backward.
- Added ESPHome and PlatformIO cache steps to validation and release workflows using `actions/cache@v5`.
- Added validation workflow concurrency so superseded branch runs are canceled.
- Changed the default ESPHome external component refresh from `never` to `1h` so the moving `latest` ref can be rechecked.
- Simplified `scripts/build` to pass `rtl433_esphome_ref` directly to ESPHome instead of resolving `latest` through the GitHub API.
- Updated script tests and removed brittle repository-shape assertions that did not exercise runtime behavior.

## Why
ESPHome treats `external_components.source.ref` as a literal Git ref. Publishing and moving a `latest` tag gives the default config a stable ref name while keeping updates tied to stable release publication. Moving that responsibility into the release workflow keeps local builds offline-friendly and avoids requiring GitHub API access just to compile firmware.

The release workflow now serializes runs that mutate shared tags, which prevents overlapping stable releases from racing over the `latest` pointer. The added PlatformIO and ESPHome caches reduce repeated dependency downloads during validation and release builds without caching generated compile output.

body:
## Summary

Closes two gaps a live test against the real go-study-mcp ext-apps server surfaced after the 109a–e wave. **Gap A:** a `ui://` App document at/above the 32 KiB heavy-content threshold (D-026) is correctly offloaded to the ArtifactStore by reference by 109a's `mcp.servers.read_resource`, but the 109b renderer treated the resulting `artifactRef` as a fatal "server bug" and refused to render — which hits nearly every real App (go-study-mcp's `studio/index.html` is **86.4 KB**; Svelte/React bundles routinely exceed 32 KiB). The renderer now fetches the offloaded artifact's bytes and loads them into the same sandboxed iframe. **Gap B:** a host-side operator "expand ⤢" affordance on the inline app frame pops the app to the 109c side-by-side (`pip`) / fullscreen layout without the app asking.

## Phase / RFC reference

Phase 109f (Console MCP Apps) — RFC §6.4, §6.5, §7. Decision **D-217**. Plan: `docs/plans/phase-109f-heavy-app-doc-render.md`.

## What changed

**Gap A — heavy App documents render (the offload is correct; only the renderer's content source changes):**
- `MCPAppHostClient` gains `resolveArtifact(artifactID): Promise<string>` (injected seam, chat module stays dependency-injected — D-091).
- `mcp-app.svelte::preload()`: when `readResource` returns an `artifactRef`, resolve it to a presigned URL, fetch the bytes at the iframe edge, and feed the SAME `wrapAppDocument` + CSP + sandbox (no `allow-same-origin`) + origin guard the inline path uses. The wrong "server bug" comment is corrected; a non-2xx fetch fails loud.
- The real `resolveArtifact` impl lives OUTSIDE the chat module, in `makeMCPAppHostClient` (over `artifacts.get_ref` → `presigned_url`).

**§17.6 bug-twin (same PR):** the playground `ChatProtocolClient.resolveArtifact` read the absent `resp.url` (the Go wire field is `presigned_url`), silently breaking every chat-bubble artifact preview. Fixed.

**Gap B — operator "pop to side-by-side":** an expand/fullscreen overlay on the inline frame dispatches `onDisplayModeRequest({requested, granted})` through the EXISTING injected seam → `MessageBubble` → `ChatPanel` → `+page.svelte::onInlineAppDisplayModeRequest` → the 109c layout reducer. No parallel display-mode path; tokens-only; accessible (`aria-label`). Shown only while inline + only for advertised non-inline modes.

## Tests

- `mcp-app-discovery.spec.ts` — **Gap A** real-component guard: mounts the real `MessageBubble` → `McpAppRenderer` with a client whose `readResource` returns an `artifactRef` (not inline) + an artifact-fetch stub returning a realistic **>32 KiB** App document (Vite single-file-build shape, §17.8); asserts the iframe `srcdoc` is populated from the fetched bytes and the error is gone. Verified it FAILS (times out on the error path) if the artifactRef branch reverts. Inline-path regression kept. **Gap B** test: the expand button dispatches a `pip` request through the injected callback and the real reducer moves the app to pip.
- `mcp-app-host-client.spec.ts` — `resolveArtifact` routes to `artifacts.get_ref` and returns `presigned_url` (not the absent `url`).
- `scripts/smoke/phase-109f.sh` (static-only) — 11 OK / 0 FAIL.

## Checklist

- [x] `make vet test build` passes locally — N/A Go (Console-only); `cd web/console && npm run check && lint && test && build` all green.
- [x] `make lint` is clean — Console: `npm run lint` clean.
- [x] `make preflight` passes locally (pre-commit hook + manual run).
- [x] `make check-mirror` clean.
- [x] If new endpoint/method/CLI subcommand: smoke check added — no new Protocol surface; `scripts/smoke/phase-109f.sh` covers the Console seams.
- [x] Coverage on touched packages ≥ phase target — the new branches are guarded by the always-on component + adapter specs.
- [ ] If multi-isolation code: cross-session isolation test passes — N/A, no identity-scoped storage path changed (the renderer drives the already-scoped injected client).
- [ ] If Protocol types changed: all references compile — N/A, no Protocol type changed.
- [ ] If config schema changed — N/A.
- [ ] If migrations added — N/A.
- [x] No new TODO without issue link.
- [x] No new dependency without rationale — no new dependency.

## Risk / blast radius

Console-only, scoped to the MCP Apps renderer + its adapter. The security envelope (sandbox tokens, CSP, `wrapAppDocument`, postMessage origin guard) is byte-identical on both the inline and heavy paths — only the document source differs. The §17.6 `resp.url` → `presigned_url` fix also repairs chat-bubble artifact previews that were silently broken. No Runtime/Protocol/migration surface touched, so `make protocol-docs-gen-check` is clean and no `protocol.ts` hand-sync is needed.

- Chat-module encapsulation confirmed: `grep -rEn "from ['\"]\$lib/" web/console/src/lib/chat/ | grep -v '\$lib/chat/'` is empty; the artifact fetch is injected via `MCPAppHostClient`, not a `$lib/protocol` import.

author: enochlev
body:
## What & why

The legacy `/voice/b/0/` HTML/XML endpoints this library scraped are gone, so
login — and therefore everything — has been broken for years (#8). This is a
ground-up rewrite against the JSON API that voice.google.com actually uses
today: `https://clients6.google.com/voice/v1/voiceclient/...`.

## Authentication (no more passwords)

Google's login is JavaScript-heavy and bot-protected, so scripted password
login isn't viable. Instead:

- `python -m googlevoice.auth login` opens a real (undetected) Chrome via
  `nodriver`; you sign in normally — 2FA, passkeys, and captcha all work.
- It harvests the Google cookies into a portable `~/.googlevoice/session.json`.
- Each request is signed with a `SAPISIDHASH` derived from those cookies — no
  OAuth, no token refresh. **Copy `session.json` to any machine and reads work
  there with just `requests`, no browser.**

This keeps the browser dependency optional and minimal — addressing the concern
about heavy Selenium-style setups raised in #8.

## What works (verified end-to-end against a live account)

- **Read — pure `requests`, portable:** `Voice().number`, `.inbox()`,
  `.thread(number)` return clean `Thread`/`Message` objects.
- **Send SMS:** Google gates sending behind reCAPTCHA + BotGuard anti-abuse
  tokens that can only be produced in a browser, so `BrowserSender` drives the
  real web app (which mints them). Handles both new and existing conversations.
- **CLI:** `python -m googlevoice {login,check,number,inbox,thread,send}`, with
  `--json` output and lenient number parsing (`+1 (208) 555-0123`,
  `208-555-0123`, `2085550123` all accepted; `+1` assumed by default).

## Notable changes

- New modules: `googlevoice/auth.py` (session + SAPISIDHASH), `googlevoice/browser.py` (`BrowserSender`).
- Rewrote `voice.py` and `util.py` (JSON wrappers; the old `XMLParser` is gone),
  plus `__init__.py`, `__main__.py`, `interact.py`.
- Removed dead legacy code (`conf.py`, `settings.py`, `setup-asterisk.py`) and
  stale examples; added `examples/read_inbox.py`, updated `examples/sms.py`.
- `nodriver` is an optional `[browser]` extra (needed only for `login`/`send`);
  dropped `oathtool` and `bs4`.
- Refreshed README + docs; added towncrier news fragments.
- Tests rewritten with mocked HTTP (`responses`); `pytest`, `ruff`, and
  `pytest-checkdocs` all pass.

## Limitations / not yet ported

- **Sending requires Chrome** (browser-minted anti-abuse tokens); reading does not.
- Calls, MMS, and voicemail download are not yet implemented.

## Testing

- `pytest` (mocked, no network) — all green; `ruff check`/`ruff format` clean.
- Manual: live browser login, read inbox + a specific conversation, send SMS
  (received on the handset), and the CLI commands.

author: elijahkendrick04
body:
## What happened (PR #452)

PR #452 is the roadmap auto-update bot's refresh. It got stuck `dirty` (merge conflict) with auto-merge stalled — it never landed.

## Root cause

There is **one** automation path — `roadmap-autoupdate.yml` (PR → `main` via auto-merge). What *looked* like a second, direct-to-main writer (`3fd3542`, no PR number) was just a `gh pr merge --merge` artifact: a non-squash merge lands **two** commits per refresh (the bot branch's commit + the merge commit).

The actual conflict cause: every refresh rewrites the **same lines** (the `LAST_UPDATED` stamp + the top of the `ACTIVITY` table), but the bot branch was generated from the **stale commit that triggered the run**. When feature merges land in quick succession, their roadmap runs interleave with the async auto-merges, so a bot PR could be computed against a `main` that didn't yet include the previous roadmap landing → `dirty`.

## Fix (keeps the single PR path, makes it conflict-proof)

- **Branch the refresh off the freshest `origin/main`** (re-fetch + `checkout -B … FETCH_HEAD`) before running the script, so the bot branch is always exactly *"latest main + roadmap delta"* and its PR can never conflict on those shared lines.
- **Land by squash** instead of merge, so each refresh is **one** `docs: auto-update roadmap (#N) [skip render]` commit on `main` — no sibling branch commit that reads like a second writer.

The loop guard, `[skip render]` marker, and fail-soft "leave the PR open" behaviour are unchanged.

## Verification

- Workflow YAML parses; steps ordered correctly (`Branch the refresh off the freshest main` → `Refresh ROADMAP.md` → `Land …`).
- `tests/test_roadmap_autoupdate.py` — **40 passed** (script untouched).

## Note on PR #452

Once this lands on `main`, the merge is itself a push to `main` that triggers the (now-fixed) workflow: it rebuilds the bot branch from the latest tip, refreshes the still-open PR #452, and lets it auto-merge cleanly — so #452 self-heals without manual intervention.

## Summary
Council-ruled Fix-B/P0 from recycle-spiral remediation (grid#847). Breaks the boot-reload spiral by preventing STATUS/RESULT report-tasks from accumulating in the `created` pool.

## Changes
- **STATUS tasks** (`message_type:STATUS`): `auto_archived:true` on create — never enter `created` pool (ALAN ruling: informational, latest subsumes prior)
- **RESULT tasks** (non-failed, `message_type:RESULT`): `status:done` + `completed_status:SUCCESS` auto-set on create — preserves `get_task_lineage`/audit history while draining boot query (ALAN gate condition: archive would destroy lineage)

body:
## Summary

- Adds `compute_multi_leg_limit_price(legs, quotes)` to `execution/orders.py`: sign-aware net combo mid (buy=+mid×ratio, sell=−mid×ratio), floored conservatively to tick size
- Adds `build_multi_leg_request(proposal, qty, limit_price)` to `execution/orders.py`: builds `LimitOrderRequest(order_class=MLEG)` — type is statically LIMIT, no code path produces a market order
- Adds `submit_multi_leg()` and `_build_order_multi_leg()` to `execution/broker.py`: mleg submission + poll, same retry/poll infrastructure as `submit()`
- Adds 34 tests in `tests/test_multi_leg.py` covering pricing arithmetic, rounding, ratio handling, request structure, and broker submission outcomes

## Decisions resolved

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Spread limit price formula | Option (a): sign-aware sum of per-leg mids | Alpaca doesn't surface a spread-level quote; (b) isn't available. Internal sign convention (positive=debit) matches Alpaca's mleg `limit_price` — no translation needed. |
| Rounding direction | `math.floor(net / tick_size)` for both debit and credit | Floor is conservative in both cases: debit → pay slightly less; credit → receive slightly more. `round(net / tick_size, 8)` applied first to suppress FP noise at boundaries. |
| Leg ratio handling | Pass `Leg.ratio` directly as `ratio_qty`; Alpaca multiplies by `qty` | Alpaca's multi-leg API takes a per-leg `ratio_qty`; actual contracts per leg = `qty × ratio_qty`. Never pre-multiply. |
| Re-pricing strategy | Option (a): leave WORKING orders for reconcile | Simpler; safe failure (missed trade, not bad fill); no data yet to set step parameters. Disposition is a named policy in the contract docstring, owned by WP-1.4/WP-8. |
| Per-leg fill data | Empty at submit+poll | `filled_avg_price` on parent order = net combo fill price. Per-leg prices need a nested Alpaca fetch; left for WP-1.4 reconcile to populate via `get_order_by_id(nested=True)`. |
