author: heyoub
body:
## Post-Substrate Productionization Wave (pre-0.2.0)

Makes the **casting side production-grade** on top of the merged substrate (#37): every cast becomes a real artifact, the last pre-cut hygiene is cleared, and the cast family is completed (CSS/SVG/GLSL/WGSL/ARIA/video). **0.2.0 is cut when this merges.**

Per the pre-0.2.0 correctness directive, breaking changes are taken at the root — the edge-KV `CompiledOutputs` format and `CompositeState.outputs` shape are settled now, before the cut freezes them.

### What landed (8 parallel work-items + integration)
- **D0 — cast plumbing spine:** per-arm `dispatch` collapsed into a target-driven loop; `glsl`/`wgsl` threaded through authoring → manifest → edge KV → compositor.
- **GLSL cast (live):** authored `@glsl{}` per-state uniforms ride the satellite payload → live `czap:uniform-update` on every crossing (`gpu.ts` consumer completed).
- **WGSL cast (live):** new `emit-wgsl` phase (escalation-gated), `wgslIdent` twinned with `glslIdent`, net-new `wgpu.ts` uniform-binding loop (WebGPU-guarded).
- **SVG egress:** ECS render-sink reading P3's `_svgAttrs` dual-write (the missing reader), `PassThroughMixer` pattern, scene-only.
- **B — headless encoder + `@czap/stage` promotion:** real ffmpeg `FrameEncoder` behind the injectable `encode?` seam (validatable MP4; env-gated, honest skip), stage flipped public with full roster sync.
- **E — escalation:** `chooseRung` now gates compositor projection targets per `PolicyNode` budget/rung (proven to drop `glsl`/`wgsl` under tight budgets).
- **F — GraphPatch round-trip capsule:** `encode→decode→diff→patch→re-encode` identity locked; surfaced + fixed a real equality-semantics finding (graph is a content-addressed multiset, not positional).
- **C — coverage debt cleared, floors deleted:** astro 86/86/90/88 (merge-filter fix for browser-only files, no padding), genui 98/98/100/97, stage 100/100/100/94 — all clear the global 85/85/85/75 bar with `PACKAGE_THRESHOLD_OVERRIDES` removed.

### Integration
Fanned out as worktree-isolated agents, integrated by sequential cherry-pick. Two real merges resolved by hand: the `applyBoundaryState` detail block (glsl+wgsl+aria compose together) and `dual-export` (B's encoder + C's crossing-track digest coexist). Build green across 22 packages, full suite **4441 pass / 0 fail**, `docs:check` clean.

### Follow-up (queued, not in this PR)
The **AI Cast Primitive** mini-wave runs next (after this merges, before 0.2.0): wire the AI cast as a framework primitive (graph → context/tool-schema → validated GraphPatch proposal, host owns authority). The AI *producer* stays downstream by design.

body:
## Stage 3 fix — the last narrow rows

Your console output proved the new build was live (`5549d5a`) and that most dropdowns were already full-width (526–560px) — but the **top three rows** (Max Consecutive Days, Max Days Per Week, 5th Day) were still ~152px.

**Root cause:** the editor body is a flex column that sizes children to their content. A row whose only content is a small dropdown collapsed to the dropdown's intrinsic width (~152px), while nested sections with wide content stayed wide. That's why those three never went full-width no matter what I set on the select itself — the *container* was narrow.

**Fix:** `align-items:stretch` on the body + force `.rr-pol-rows` / `.rr-pol-row` / `.sf2-row` to full width. Now every row — and every dropdown — spans the panel uniformly.

CSS only, page-scoped.

author: sirmaelstrom
body:
## Feedback addressed

When a chore was already picked up by another member, the only available action was **Done** — there was no way to take it or reassign it without coordinating with the current holder. Real case: *"I saw an overdue task, did it, but I could only mark it done, not assign it to myself."* And the broader one: covering a chore for someone who's out/sick.

## What this adds

A chore held by **someone else** now shows two actions on the card (in addition to Done):

- **Take it** — grab it in one tap as a self-**claim**. It displaces whoever currently holds it (claimed *or* assigned), no coordination needed, and lands a `Claimed` — **not** a sticky `Assigned` — so a recurring chore returns to the pile after you complete it (you covered it once; it isn't permanently yours).
- **Reassign** — opens the existing hand-off picker to pass it to another member or release it to the pile.

### Action semantics (now cleanly separated)

| Action | Precondition | Result | Recurring chore after completion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claim | must be unheld (pile) | Claimed by you | returns to pile |
| **Take it** | *any* holder — displaces them | **Claimed by you** | **returns to pile** |
| Reassign / Hand off | any | Assigned to target (or pile) | stays with the assignee |

## Implementation

- **Backend**: `IChoreService.TakeAsync` + `ChoreService.TakeAsync`; route `POST /api/chores/{id}/take` (mirrors the claim endpoint). `TakeAsync` is allowed to displace a holder (unlike `ClaimAsync`, which stays pile-only — council MN8 intact) and lands a self-claim (unlike hand-off, which assigns). A stale prior claim still auto-releases first, recording the lapsed claimer (M16). Completion already credits the completer (council M8), so Take-then-Done attributes the work to the taker.
- **Island**: `takeChore()` api + `store.take()` (optimistic) wired through all four lenses; the card's "Take it" / "Reassign" affordances are gated on `heldByOther`. Also corrected the hand-off optimistic patch to `assigned` so a reassign no longer flashes a "Drop" button before the board reconciles.

## Verification

- 3 new claim-state-machine unit tests (take a claimed / assigned / stale chore held by another).
- **451** Services unit tests + **26** wiring tests green.
- Backend build: 0 errors. Island `svelte-check`: 0 errors; `vite build`: OK. Changed C# files format-clean.

## Deploy note

The island changes are source-level — they take effect once the Docker image rebuilds `wwwroot/islands`; hard-refresh busts the cached island. The backend (new endpoint + `TakeAsync`) ships with the normal build.

author: bypabloc
body:
## Problema

Promoción de `dev` a `main` (producción). Incluye 46 commits acumulados desde la última promoción (PR #277), entre ellos:

1. **Consolidación del CV** (PRs #280, #284, #285): el Lambda `cv` absorbe las operations `content` + `publish` del eliminado `cv_admin` (9 lambdas, POST /cv); fase Authorize declarativa en `lambda_kit`; editor de CV en el admin.
2. **Piso de memoria 1024 MB** en todos los lambdas (PR #283).
3. **Fix del correo de login/registro en prod** (PR #286): el pipeline ahora reconcilia `email-config` (S3 + DynamoDB) en cada deploy, evitando el drift `register-* -> login-unified` que dejaba a `send_email` rechazando con `EMAIL_KIND_NOT_FOUND`.

## Solución

Merge directo `dev -> main` (merge commit, sin rebase — preserva los SHAs y evita divergencia, según git-workflow.md). Al mergear se disparan `deploy-backend.yml` y `deploy-apps.yml` sobre `main` (stage `prod`).

## Cómo probar

Tras el merge, el deploy de backend en prod:
- corre las migraciones de DB + seed del CV + **el nuevo seed de email-config** (reconcilia login-unified/password-changed en prod).
- redeploya los lambdas afectados (cv, etc.).

Verificación post-deploy:
- `gh run list --workflow=deploy-backend.yml --branch=main` -> success en todos los jobs.
- el correo de registro/login en prod ya llega (el fix de datos se aplicó manualmente y se verificó E2E con SES message_id; este PR lo hace permanente vía pipeline).
- `curl` a las URLs canónicas de prod -> 200.

## TODO

- (opcional) métrica/alarma `EmailInvokeFailed` para detectar drift de kind futuro.

author: matthighlife-creator
body:
## Summary

- Replaces raw GPS coordinates in the location bar with a clean two-mode system: 📍 live GPS (shows nearest station name once data loads) and 📌 pinned daydream spot
- Adds a full-screen Leaflet map picker — tap anywhere to drop a pin, or search by name; daydream spot persists in localStorage across refreshes
- Leaflet 1.9.4 vendored locally so the picker works offline via the service worker

## How the location bar works

- **Apple-style location arrow** (CSS ↗) prefixes the location name — blue when live GPS, gray when daydream
- **📍 / 📌 toggle button** (Android-style pin icons) switches between modes
  - 📍 (GPS): tap to switch to saved daydream spot, or open picker if none saved yet
  - 📌 (Daydream): tap to switch back to live GPS
- **Tapping the location name itself** always opens the picker (so you can replace a saved spot)

## Daydream picker details

- Search fires on Enter/button tap only — no live autocomplete, respects Nominatim's 1 req/sec limit
- Results filtered to water features (`waterway`, `natural`, `water` OSM categories) with fallback to all results if none match
- Map taps reverse-geocode via Nominatim to show the waterway name or nearest town
- Confirm saves the spot; X cancels without changing anything

## Changes from original spec

- "Autocomplete" → search-on-submit (Nominatim ToS)
- Tapping location name text also opens picker (to replace a saved spot — original spec had no path for this)
- GPS mode label uses nearest station name from existing nearby-waters data instead of "My Location"
- Old manual lat/lon modal removed (superseded by picker)
- Leaflet vendored locally instead of CDN (offline support)

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh load → loc-bar shows 📍 arrow + "Locating…", resolves to nearest station name
- [ ] Tap 📍 button with no saved spot → picker opens
- [ ] Search "Lake Pontchartrain" + Enter → water results appear; tap one → pin drops on map, name shown
- [ ] Tap map → pin drops, name reverse-geocodes from Nominatim
- [ ] Tap "Set This Spot ✓" → modal closes, loc-bar shows 📌 + spot name, all data reloads from that location
- [ ] Tap 📌 button → switches back to GPS, data reloads for real position
- [ ] Tap loc name while in GPS mode → picker opens pre-loaded with existing spot
- [ ] Hard-refresh page → daydream spot still set (localStorage)
- [ ] Go offline → Leaflet JS/CSS still loads (vendored + SW precache); tiles won't load (expected)

body:
## Summary

Reworks the original *good-first-issue → Telegram* tool (PR #1) into **dev-feed-agent** — a personalized, **agentic news feed for developers / ML engineers**. Users sign in with **GitHub OAuth**; an agent (pydantic-ai over OpenRouter) profiles their interests from their GitHub activity, then curates a feed across **GitHub, HuggingFace, Hacker News, arXiv and Reddit** and delivers it to **Telegram**. Relevance is judged by the LLM over the profile — **no embeddings**.

Supersedes #1.

## What changed vs PR #1

- **GitHub OAuth** instead of pasting a token — "Connect with GitHub" is the entire web UI. The OAuth access token is captured for GitHub API calls.
- **Profile is the agent's self-managed memory**, not a rigid table: a sectioned `profile.md` the agent patches via an `update_profile_section` tool whenever it learns something new. Plus conversation history and a generalized `feed_items` dedup ledger (across all sources, not just issues).
- **Multi-source feed**, not just good-first-issues: projects, issues, help-wanted, papers, models, discussions — with an **explore/exploit** mix.
- **MCP sources as gateway containers**: HN/arXiv/Reddit via `supergateway` (Reddit keyless), HuggingFace as a remote HTTP MCP — wired directly into the agent.
- **Single build-based deploy surface**: one `docker-compose.yaml`, one `.env.example`, one `nginx.conf`, prefix-less `make` targets. The dev/prod split is gone.
- Removed the interest-table UI, the `PUT /interests` endpoint, and web chat — all interaction happens in Telegram.

## How it works

1. **Connect with GitHub** (OAuth) → JWT minted, GitHub token stored.
2. An Explore-style **sub-agent** builds the interest profile by walking your repos + scanning their dependency manifests.
3. **Link Telegram** with one tap (`/start <code>`). From then on everything is in Telegram.
4. An hourly **APScheduler** job curates a feed (explore/exploit), de-dups against what you've seen, and delivers the top matches. Chat with the bot to steer it (`/init` rebuilds the profile).

The agent, Telegram delivery, and each MCP source are all **opt-in** via config.

## Layout

- `server/src/agent/` — `prompts/`, `tools/` (github/feed/memory), `mcp.py` (toolsets), `agents.py` (factories + `FeedOutput`), `runtime.py` (`build_profile` / `chat` / `curate_feed`).
- `server/src/services/` — `github_oauth`, `feed`, `scheduler`, `telegram_bot`, `notifier`.
- Models: extended `users` (GitHub identity), new `connections`, `profiles`, `chat_messages`, `feed_items` (+ one Alembic migration).
- `client/src/` — `LandingView`, `AuthCallbackView`, `ConnectedView`; trimmed router/nav.
- `deploy/mcp/Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.yaml` MCP gateway services.

## Review & fixes

Reviewed by three subagents (correctness / security / infra+frontend). Fixed in this PR:

- **Telegram link codes are single-use** (rotated on link) and refuse silent relink → prevents feed/agent hijack if a link URL leaks.
- **App JWT delivered via URL fragment** (`#token=`), scrubbed from history → no leak via logs/Referer.
- **`supergateway` pinned to 3.4.3** with explicit `--streamableHttpPath /mcp`.
- **Client healthcheck gates nginx** → no empty-dir serving on cold boot.
- GitHub path validation (`owner/name` regex + filename encoding); shared-bot session reset on stop; profile-build username guard.

Accepted as follow-ups (tracked): #2 encrypt tokens at rest · #3 bind OAuth state to browser · #4 rate-limit poll-now/rebuild · #5 prompt-injection hardening · #6 tolerate an unreachable MCP source.

## Testing

- Backend: **42 pytest** green; `ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy --strict` clean.
- Frontend: `vue-tsc` type-check, `eslint`, `vitest` unit, production build all green.
- `docker compose config` validates.
- **Not run:** the full stack against live GitHub/OpenRouter/Telegram/MCP (needs real keys).

## Summary

Provisioning now avoids the blocking Hammerspoon CLI launch prompt and the integration workflow gives mise a GitHub token for release downloads.

## Why

Provisioning was observed hanging at the Reload Hammerspoon configuration task. The stuck child process was the Hammerspoon CLI, and sampling showed it inside an NSAlert modal because plain hs invocation prompts when it cannot reach the Hammerspoon IPC port. After the PR opened, CI also failed while installing aube via mise because unauthenticated GitHub API requests hit the rate limit.

- Plain hs -c probes timed out while waiting on the modal prompt.
- The same reload path with hs -A exited successfully in a bounded live run.
- The failed CI log showed mise receiving a 403 rate-limit response with no GitHub token available.

## Approach

Add the Hammerspoon CLI -A flag to the reload task while preserving the existing delayed hs.reload() behavior. Pass github.token as GITHUB_TOKEN to the integration provisioning step and add a policy regression check for that workflow contract.

## Verification

- The task command now resolves to the autolaunch hs -A form.
- The exact replacement reload command exited successfully in a bounded live run.
- The integration workflow policy checks pass, including the new GITHUB_TOKEN assertion.
- Ansible accepted the playbook syntax.

body:
## Handoff 16083ab3

`stdlib/signal/core_fft.hexa` `fft3_real`/`ifft3`: repeated large-grid calls accumulate memory → OOM (handoff: `nz=1024@reps150` and `nz=4096@reps30` were *killed*; single/bounded-reps were clean). Surfaced by QFORGE-PERF.bench.md §7a.

## Root cause

The working `re`/`im` buffers and the packed intermediates were `[float]` push-arrays. On grow they heap-promote (runtime arena → malloc), and a malloc-promoted buffer is **orphaned on scope-pop** — `hexa_val_arena_scope_pop` only rewinds the bump pointer; it never `free()`s a promoted buffer (`self/runtime_core.c`). So **every transform LINE leaked O(n)**, and `fft3` runs thousands of lines per call. Repeated `fft3_real`/`ifft3` thus accumulated memory linearly → OOM under load.

A secondary latent bug: `_fft3_run` did `let mut wre = re` and then mutated `wre` in place, which **aliased and corrupted the caller's input array** across repeated calls (the qforge caller worked around it with a defensive `drho_cp`).

## Fix (single file, scoped refactor: +130/−117)

- Route every transform through one in-place radix-2 butterfly core `_cf_fft_inplace` operating on **reclaimable `farr` scratch** (fixed-size, no push-growth, explicit `farr_free`).
- The 3D path keeps `re`/`im` as `farr` end-to-end — no `[float]` intermediate escapes/leaks — with **one reusable per-axis line scratch**.
- `fft3_real` synthesizes the zero imaginary part directly into the `farr` (no `zim` array built/leaked).
- Public `[float]` signatures unchanged; `fft3`/`ifft3`/`fft3_real` now copy input into scratch → **no longer mutate the caller's array** (strictly more correct).

The FFT math is unchanged: same bit-reversal permutation, same twiddles, same butterfly write order → output bit-identical (in-place bit-reversal swap is the textbook involution-equivalent of the prior gather).

## Verification on pool host `summer` (linux x86_64, CPU-only; native C-backend `hexa build -o`)

### Correctness — bit-identical output (BEFORE = origin/main inlined body, AFTER = fix)

Full `fft3_real` spectrum + `ifft3` round-trip on a 2×2×4 grid, every element dumped:
```
=== ORIG ===
SPEC 76.0,0.0,-4.0,4.0,-4.0,0.0,-4,-4.0,-16.0,0.0,...,-32.0,0.0,0.0,...,0.0,
BACK 1.0,0.0,1.5,2.86059e-18,2.0,0.0,2.5,-2.86059e-18,...,8.5,-2.86059e-18,
=== FIXED ===
SPEC 76.0,0.0,-4.0,4.0,-4.0,0.0,-4,-4.0,-16.0,0.0,...,-32.0,0.0,0.0,...,0.0,
BACK 1.0,0.0,1.5,2.86059e-18,2.0,0.0,2.5,-2.86059e-18,...,8.5,-2.86059e-18,
```
Byte-for-byte identical, down to the `2.86059e-18` round-off residuals.

Official regression suites run against the FIXED body — all green:
```
PASS A_delta_flat_spectrum     PASS T1_impulse_flat_spectrum
PASS B_planewave_single_bin    PASS T2_dc_single_bin
PASS C_gaussian_dc_and_peak    PASS T3_4point_dft_hand_computed
PASS D_parseval_energy         PASS T4_ifft_roundtrip
PASS E_roundtrip_identity_1e10 ALL PASS — stdlib/signal/core_fft (1D)
PASS F_separability_outer_product
PASS G_malformed_dims_guard
ALL PASS — stdlib/signal fft3 (3D FFT)
```

### Memory — accumulation eliminated

Peak RSS (`/usr/bin/time -v`), `nz=256`, forward+inverse FFT per rep (the qforge Poisson hot pattern):

| reps | ORIG RSS (KB) | FIXED RSS (KB) |
|------|---------------|----------------|
| 50   | 76,736        | 7,144          |
| 150  | 222,276       | 13,600         |
| 300  | 440,648       | 23,264         |
| 600  | 877,688       | 42,500         |

ORIG grows **~1.46 MB/rep, perfectly linear → unbounded (OOM)**. FIXED grows ~23× slower (the small residual is the *harness's own* `[float]` split arrays, outside `core_fft`'s control). At `nz=1024`: ORIG = 5.8 MB/rep (reps5→33MB, reps20→120MB).

The two exact handoff OOM cases now run trivially (FIXED):
```
nz=1024 reps=150  checksum=149.994   wall 0:00.25   peak RSS 42,460 KB
nz=4096 reps=30   checksum=29.9999   wall 0:00.22   peak RSS 34,720 KB
```
(Handoff said both were *killed* by OOM.)

### Bonus correctness signal
At `nz=256`: 1-rep checksum identical (ORIG=FIXED=0.999398); at 10 reps ORIG diverges (4.3e9 → NaN) because it corrupts its `drho` input in place, while FIXED stays correct (9.99398 = 10×). The fix also cures that input-mutation aliasing bug.

author: rbaumier
body:
## Problem

`prefer-type-over-interface` flagged an interface with no `extends` clause that no class `implements`, but it never checked whether *other* interfaces in the same file `extend` it. An interface used as an extends base must stay an `interface`: it enables extension and declaration merging, neither of which a `type` alias provides.

Real-world impact: 35,650 findings across azure-sdk-for-js (e.g. `Resource` extended by `TrackedResource` / `ProxyResource`).

## Fix

Collect interface names referenced in sibling `extends` clauses in the same first pass that already collects `implements` references (renamed the set to `referenced_as_base`), then skip flagging any interface whose name appears there. Heritage `extends` expressions are `Expression` (not `TSTypeName`), so a small `heritage_base_name` extractor pulls the base identifier; qualified bases (`extends a.B`) reference an imported namespace, not a sibling interface, and are ignored.

## Tests

- `allows_interface_extended_by_other_interface` — reproduces the issue example; `Resource` is no longer flagged (fails before the fix).
- `flags_standalone_interface_not_extended_by_anyone` — a plain interface that nothing extends or implements is still flagged.

`cargo test rules::prefer_type_over_interface` (22 pass) and the full `cargo test` suite are green.

Closes #1168

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive set of concurrency safety features to the MemoizR project, including both runtime and compile-time data-race protection, a new Roslyn analyzer suite, and an experimental actor engine. It also adds a new analyzer test project with extensive coverage for the new diagnostics. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Concurrency Safety and Runtime Features:**

* Introduced the first data-race safety layer at the user boundary: added a `[Sendable]` attribute, a structural `SendableChecker`, and a strict factory mode (`MemoFactoryOptions.StrictSendableChecks`) that enforces immutability/thread-safety at node creation.
* Added dynamic isolation assertions and runtime checks to ensure evaluation isolation, including methods such as `AsyncAsymmetricLock.IsHeldByCurrentFlow`, `Context.IsEvaluationIsolated`, and `MemoFactory.AssertEvaluationIsolated()`.
* Added support for custom executors for reactive side effects, including `IExecutor`, `SynchronizationContextExecutor`, and `DedicatedThreadExecutor`, with integration into `MemoFactory` and `ReactionBuilder`.
* Introduced an experimental actor engine (`CreateActorSignal`, `CreateActorMemoizR`, `GraphActor`) for serializing graph bookkeeping without locks, providing stronger safety guarantees and closing known race conditions.

**Analyzer and Diagnostic Infrastructure:**

* Added a new Roslyn analyzer package (`MemoizR.Analyzers`) with three new rules: MZR001 (non-Sendable value type at factory creation), MZR002 (mutating captured/shared state inside a computation), and MZR003 (`Signal.Set` inside a computation). Reference types with non-private settable properties now count as non-Sendable. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR6-R54) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-814605c3af64bfe4a928c5daa58f456bd3c2ef493c90a0e1aafdcec69129fb02R1-R10)
* Added analyzer release tracking files (`AnalyzerReleases.Shipped.md`, `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md`) to document analyzer rules and their shipped status. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-11a75d109d931661b07c45fb74ea394fb8d3a5a7797d5d69e2de0cb488d8afccR1-R2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-814605c3af64bfe4a928c5daa58f456bd3c2ef493c90a0e1aafdcec69129fb02R1-R10)

**Testing and Validation:**

* Added a new test project `MemoizR.Analyzers.Tests` targeting .NET 9, referencing all relevant MemoizR projects and using the real runtime assemblies for analyzer validation.
* Implemented an analyzer test harness (`AnalyzerTestHarness.cs`) for in-memory compilation and analyzer execution, ensuring diagnostics are only asserted on compilable code.
* Added comprehensive analyzer test suites for each rule: `SendableTypeArgumentAnalyzerTests`, `CapturedMutationAnalyzerTests`, and `SetInsideComputationAnalyzerTests`, covering positive and negative cases for each diagnostic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0c4f4238ef997cf37b865b61afcac30893b92fa690f5ea6b4018233ede41f72bR1-R195) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-12b298730e6b19f8066ad77c6db2a8af5406129e57cdf8d027a872583c26a8a5R1-R173) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2fd9f8181e2cd67951e1a2979c1b6d63a69bc3b068a1f7e17c0afe7540c29e1dR1-R124)
* Enabled global using of Xunit for concise test code.

**Documentation:**

* Updated `CHANGELOG.md` with detailed entries for all new features, changes, known issues, and fixes related to concurrency safety and analyzers.

body:
# Grafana Panel Health Monitoring System

Comprehensive monitoring solution for detecting and alerting on Grafana panel issues ("No Data" panels, query errors, InfluxDB connection failures).

## Summary

- **7 new scripts** — Panel health checker (Python), query debugger, repair orchestrator, Slack integration, enhanced sensor validator, systemd automation, installer
- **Automated monitoring** — Runs every 5 minutes via systemd timer
- **Slack integration** — Real-time alerts to `#soil-sensor-alerts` channel
- **Comprehensive documentation** — 495-line troubleshooting runbook with step-by-step fixes

## Key Features

### 1. Automated Panel Health Detection
- `check-grafana-panels.py` — Queries Grafana API, enumerates all dashboards/panels, tests Flux queries against InfluxDB
- **Exit codes:** 0=healthy, 1=no_data, 2=query_error, 3=datasource_error
- **Output formats:** JSON (for scripts) or human-readable (for terminal)

### 2. Query Debugging & Repair
- `debug-grafana-query.sh` — Extracts panel queries, tests against InfluxDB, provides fix suggestions
- `repair-grafana-panels.sh` — Orchestrator script (runs health check, logs issues, sends Slack alerts)
- **Auto-repair mode** — Optional automated fixes for common issues

### 3. Enhanced Sensor Health Validation
- Auto-detection from `sensors-config.json` (no manual sensor IDs required)
- Multi-timeframe checks (5min, 1h, 24h)
- Data quality validation (stddev check for stuck sensors)

### 4. Slack Integration
- `send-slack-alert.sh` — Generic webhook sender with rate limiting and retry logic
- Severity levels: info, warning, error, critical
- Secure storage: `/mnt/sensor-data/config/slack_webhook_url` (chmod 600)

### 5. Systemd Automation
- Timer runs every 5 minutes (starts 2 min after boot)
- Logs to `/mnt/sensor-data/logs/grafana-panel-issues.log`
- One-command installation: `./rpi-setup/install-panel-health-monitor.sh`

## Components

| Component | Type | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `check-grafana-panels.py` | Python | Main health checker (Grafana API, query testing) |
| `debug-grafana-query.sh` | Bash | Query extraction and debugging |
| `repair-grafana-panels.sh` | Bash | Orchestrator (detection, logging, alerts) |
| `send-slack-alert.sh` | Bash | Slack webhook integration |
| `check-sensor-health.sh` | Bash | Enhanced sensor validator |
| `grafana-panel-health.{service,timer}` | Systemd | Automation (every 5 minutes) |
| `install-panel-health-monitor.sh` | Bash | One-command installer |

## Documentation

- `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING_NO_DATA.md` — 495-line comprehensive runbook
  - Step-by-step fixes for InfluxDB connection errors
  - "No Data" panel troubleshooting (time range, device ID, measurement mismatches)
  - Query syntax error debugging
  - Manual investigation workflow (6-step process)
  - Diagnostic command reference
  - Preventive monitoring setup
- `AGENTS.md` — Updated with new diagnostic commands section
- All scripts include `--help` flags with usage examples

## Testing

Tested on Raspberry Pi 5 (192.168.99.134) with:
- 7 active sensors (all online, all reporting data)
- 6 Grafana dashboards (soil-moisture-main-v2, watering-history, sensor-details, system-health, alerts-overview, rpi-health)
- InfluxDB 2.7.12 (org: soil-monitoring, bucket: sensor-readings)
- Grafana 11.4.0

## Installation

```bash
# On Raspberry Pi
cd ~/soil-sensor/rpi-setup
./install-panel-health-monitor.sh

# Configure Slack webhook
echo "https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/WEBHOOK/URL" \
  > /mnt/sensor-data/config/slack_webhook_url
chmod 600 /mnt/sensor-data/config/slack_webhook_url

# Verify installation
systemctl status grafana-panel-health.timer
journalctl -u grafana-panel-health -f
```

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Quick health check
./scripts/check-grafana-panels.py

# Debug specific panel
./scripts/debug-grafana-query.sh --dashboard soil-moisture-main-v2 --panel 3

# Run repair with Slack notification
./scripts/repair-grafana-panels.sh --notify

# Send test alert
./scripts/send-slack-alert.sh --severity info --title "Test" --message "Monitoring is active"
```

### Added
- Grafana panel health monitoring system (7 new scripts)
- Automated Slack alerting for panel issues
- Enhanced sensor health validation (auto-detection, data quality checks)
- Comprehensive troubleshooting documentation (495 lines)

### Changed

### Fixed

## Migration Notes

No breaking changes. Existing functionality unchanged.

New dependencies:

author: sbriggssjc
body:
## Summary

Adds owner-name plausibility validation to prevent two failure modes in CRE owner extraction:
1. Bare field labels ("Ownership", "Seller", "L. BROKER") grabbed from master sheets instead of adjacent values
2. The folder's tenant/occupant brand incorrectly minted as the owner

The guard runs at every CRE owner-mint boundary (xlsx scan, PDF AI extraction, and the mint boundary itself) so no extraction path can bypass it.

## Key Changes

- **`entity-link.js`**: Added two new validation functions:
  - `isFieldLabelName(name)` — detects bare field-label cells by matching against a regex of common owner field headers (Ownership, Owner, Seller, Buyer, Landlord, Broker, Tenant, etc.). Strips trailing colons and normalizes whitespace.
  - `isImplausibleOwnerName(name, { tenantBrand })` — rejects bare labels OR the tenant brand via three matching strategies: exact normalized equality, substring containment ("Mavis" ⊂ "Mavis Tire"), and multi-token overlap ("Mavis Tire" ⊂ "Mavis Discount Tire"). Single-token matches are excluded to avoid false-rejecting legitimate owners that share a common word with the tenant.

- **`cre-owner-extract.js`**: 
  - `scanLoadedWorkbookForOwner()` now accepts `tenantBrand` parameter and rejects scanned values that fail `isImplausibleOwnerName()` before returning them
  - `extractCreOwner()` threads `tenantBrand` into the scan path

- **`cre-registry.js`**:
  - `ensureCreOwnerEntity()` now accepts `tenantBrand` parameter and validates the name at the mint boundary (before the reuse gate) so no extraction path can mint or reuse a label/tenant
  - `performCreRegister()` threads `tenantBrand` from the property key into the owner entity creation

- **`cre-owner-backfill.js`**: Threads `tenantBrand` from the property record into the mint context

- **Tests**: Comprehensive coverage in three test files:
  - `entity-link.test.js`: Tests for `isFieldLabelName()` and `isImplausibleOwnerName()` with label rejection, tenant matching (equality/substring/token overlap), and real owner acceptance
  - `cre-owner-extract.test.mjs`: Tests for scan-path rejection of blank values, adjacent labels, and tenant brands
  - `cre-registry.test.mjs`: Tests for mint-boundary rejection of labels and tenants, with real owners still passing through

## Implementation Details

- The field-label regex is anchored to exact-ish matching (case-insensitive, trailing colon stripped, whitespace normalized) so a real owner containing a label token ("Seller Properties LLC") still passes
- Tenant matching is conservative to avoid false-rejecting legitimate owners: requires exact normalized equality, substring either way, or ≥2-token tenant overlap
- The guard runs at both the scan level (xlsx) and the mint boundary (shared across all extraction paths), ensuring defense in depth

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Systematic review and improvement of error handling across `fiu.py`. The codebase had several categories of issues where errors were silently swallowed, connections leaked, or user-facing errors were unhandled.

**Structured logging** — Replaced all `print()` calls with `logging` module (`logger.info/warning/error/exception`). `logger.exception()` captures full tracebacks automatically, making error diagnosis much easier than bare `print(f"error: {e}")`.

**Bare `except:` → `except Exception`** — Three bare `except:` clauses (in `storage_info` and `health`) caught `SystemExit`/`KeyboardInterrupt`, preventing clean shutdown. Now scoped to `Exception`.

**Global `on_command_error` handler** — Only `force_add` had an error handler. All other owner-only commands (`invite`, `roster`, `remove`, `deploy`, `create`, `getid`, `storage_info`, `migrate_tokens`) would show raw tracebacks when used by non-owners or with bad arguments. The global handler now catches `NotOwner`, `UserNotFound`, `MissingRequiredArgument`, `BadArgument`, and `CommandNotFound`.

**DB connection leaks** — `get_user_access_token_db`, `save_user_token_db`, `delete_user_from_db`, `init_database`, `migrate_tokens`, and `storage_info` could leak connections on error paths. Restructured with `finally: conn.close()` blocks. Also fixed leaks in `on_ready`, `index()`, and the OAuth `callback` route where `get_db_connection()` was called without closing.

**Silent interaction drops** — `GetChannelIdView` callbacks silently `return`-ed for unauthorized users without responding to the Discord interaction, causing "This interaction failed" errors. Now responds with an ephemeral message.

**OAuth callback crash** — `token_data['access_token']` and `user_data['id']` would crash with `KeyError` if Discord returned an unexpected response. Now uses `.get()` with explicit validation and error messages.

author: dancinlife
body:
Handoff **d7b69397** — security-sensitive.

## What it gates
`tool/escalator.hexa` is an unsandboxed escalation daemon. It polls a `/tmp` queue and executes privileged ops on behalf of a sandboxed Claude Code session. The hardcoded allowlist root `/Users/ghost/core/` (and `.../hexa-lang/` for `invoke_tool`) restricts:
- `write_file` destination + content_file source paths (`_path_ok`)
- `invoke_tool` `argv[0]` binary path (`_argv_first_ok`)
- `launchctl_bootstrap` plist path (`_path_ok`)

## Change
Derive the root instead of hardcoding it:

```
$HEXA_ESCALATOR_ROOT (explicit)  →  $HOME/core/  (per-user default)
```

## Security reasoning — the resolved path is *exactly as narrow* as before
1. **Default = byte-identical on the author host.** `$HOME = /Users/ghost` there, so `$HOME/core/` resolves to `/Users/ghost/core/` — the old literal exactly. The allowed set is unchanged.
2. **Fail-closed on empty `$HOME`.** If `$HOME` is empty and no override is set, `_allow_root()` returns a sentinel (`__hexa_escalator_no_root__/`) that does **not** begin with `/`, so it can never prefix an absolute request path. `_path_ok`/`_argv_first_ok` then reject **everything** — strictly narrower, never the dangerous wide `/core/`.
3. **No sibling-prefix bypass.** The root always ends in `/`, so `starts_with()` cannot match `/Users/ghost/core-evil/`.
4. **The env override grants no new capability.** The daemon **already** has a `raw_exec` op that runs arbitrary unsandboxed shell commands with **no path check at all**, and its real trust boundary is "who can write the `/tmp/hexa_escalate/` queue". Setting `HEXA_ESCALATOR_ROOT` requires controlling the daemon environment, which already implies `raw_exec` access. So the override cannot widen the *effective* attack surface.

Because the worst case (empty `$HOME`) fails **closed** and the override is bounded by pre-existing `raw_exec`, the no-wider guarantee holds — so this is changed rather than left for human review.

## Verification
- **grep**: ZERO *functional* `/Users/ghost` literals remain — only doc-comments documenting the byte-identity are retained (load-bearing for this reasoning).
- **`hexa parse tool/escalator.hexa`** → clean (local `~/.hx/bin/hexa` is a stale oracle → SYNTAX check only, not a full build/run).
- Diff +48 / -7 (no wipe_guard concern).

author: vigneshsubbiah16
body:
## Summary - We're productizing install so the user-facing command becomes a one-liner: `sudo bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://getunbound.ai/setup/mdm/onboard.sh)" -- --api-key …`. getunbound.ai proxies `/setup/mdm/onboard.sh` to a stable "latest" S3 object — but today every release only writes the immutable, versioned path `s3://unbound-release-artifacts/macos//`, so that stable object never gets refreshed. - This adds one step to `release-macos-runtime.yml` that, on a real (tag) publishing release only, copies the just-uploaded versioned `onboard.sh` to a stable `macos/latest/onboard.sh`. ## Behavior - **Gating:** `if: steps.cfg.outputs.publish == 'true'` — identical to the existing "Upload to S3" step. `workflow_dispatch` dry-runs never write `latest`. - **Placement:** immediately AFTER "Upload to S3 (immutable, no-overwrite)" (which uploads the versioned `onboard.sh` strictly last) and BEFORE "Create GitHub Release", so the alias source provably exists before the copy. - **No-cache:** the alias is written with `--cache-control "no-cache, max-age=0"` and `--metadata-directive REPLACE` so a new release is never masked by a stale cached copy. Without REPLACE the `cp` would inherit the versioned object's cacheable headers. The versioned objects keep their immutable/cacheable headers — only `latest` is no-cache. - **Content-type:** set to `text/x-shellscript; charset=utf-8` because `latest` is the browser-reachable URL the proxy serves; the default `binary/octet-stream` can trip content-sniffing/attachment behavior. - **Scope:** only `onboard.sh` gets a `latest` alias. The pkg/tar.gz are NOT aliased — the rendered `onboard.sh` already bakes the versioned pkg `ARTIFACT_URL`, so the payload stays correctly version-pinned. - Auth/env mirror the existing S3 upload step (`ARTIFACTS_AWS_*` secrets, bucket `unbound-release-artifacts`, region `us-west-2`). ## Test plan - [x] `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` — workflow parses as valid YAML - [x] `shellcheck -x` on the new `run:` block — clean - [x] Eyeballed step ordering + gating: alias step sits between the versioned S3 upload and the GitHub Release, with the same publish gate - [ ] First real verification lands on the next `runtime-v*` tag release: confirm `s3://unbound-release-artifacts/macos/latest/onboard.sh` updates with `Cache-Control: no-cache, max-age=0` ## Notes - The one-time backfill of `macos/latest/onboard.sh` for the current `0.1.1` release is handled separately by a human; this PR only changes the workflow so future releases self-publish the alias. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a single step to `release-macos-runtime.yml` that, on every real tag-triggered release, copies the just-uploaded versioned `onboard.sh` to `macos/latest/onboard.sh` in S3 with no-cache headers, making `getunbound.ai/setup/mdm/onboard.sh` always point at the latest release. - The step is correctly gated with `if: steps.cfg.outputs.publish == 'true'` (identical to the existing S3 upload guard), placed after the versioned upload and before the GitHub Release, and uses `--metadata-directive REPLACE` to avoid inheriting the versioned object's immutable cache headers. - `ARTIFACTS_BUCKET` and `ARTIFACTS_REGION` are consumed from the workflow-level `env:` block (consistent with the existing upload step); `set -euo pipefail` ensures failures are loud rather than silent.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge once the IAM policy for the deployment credentials is confirmed to include GetObject on the source bucket path. The workflow change itself is well-structured — gating, ordering, and cache-header flags are all correct. The one concern is that `aws s3 cp` from S3 to S3 uses the CopyObject API and requires read permission on the source, which a write-only deployment key would not have. If the IAM policy hasn't been updated, the alias step will fail loud on the first real tag release and block the GitHub Release creation. Everything else is sound. .github/workflows/release-macos-runtime.yml — verify the IAM policy for ARTIFACTS_AWS_* credentials grants s3:GetObject on macos/* before the first runtime-v* tag fires.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | .github/workflows/release-macos-runtime.yml | Adds a post-upload step to copy onboard.sh to macos/latest/ with no-cache headers; gating, ordering, and metadata flags are correct, but the CopyObject API requires GetObject on the source which existing write-only credentials may not have. |

author: natb1
body:
Closes #1313

## What

Hardens `dispatch-sweep`'s per-worktree reconcile loop against the two
remaining defects from #1313:

- **Defect 2 — per-worktree gh failures no longer abort the whole sweep.** The
  `gh issue view` failure branch and the unexpected-issue-state branch each used
  `exit 1`, violating the script's own "per-worktree errors should not abort"
  contract. Both now log `ERROR_ISSUE_STATE_FETCH` and `continue`, so one bad
  worktree no longer strands every worktree after it. The same isolation now
  covers the PR fetch (`ERROR_PR_STATE_FETCH` + `continue`).
- **Defect 3 — the merged backlog tail is now reachable.** The sweep built its
  merged/open map from one creation-ordered `gh pr list --state all --limit 200`
  call. With hundreds of merged PRs, any fixed window misses the tail: a branch
  whose PR was created early but merged late falls outside the window and its
  worktree is never reaped. The bulk query is replaced by a per-worktree
  `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all` lookup — unbounded by construction (a
  branch has a handful of PRs, so it cannot truncate), wrapped in `gh_retry`, and
  only reached after the reservation and (for the merged path) liveness gates
  prune the candidate set. Precedence per branch: any OPEN PR keeps the worktree;
  else any MERGED PR takes the remove path; else the issue path runs.

## Scope note — overlap with work that landed during this change

This issue's title also covered "dispatch-sweep has no caller" and a missing
closed-path live-session guard. Both were handled by #1475 (for #1451), which
wired the sweep via `dispatch-spawn-sweep` from the worker Stop-hook, added the
closed-path `SKIP_CLOSED_LIVE_SESSION` guard, and introduced the loop-top
reservation gate. #1455 (for #1312) separately set the `--limit`/truncation
discipline for *open*-PR fetches across the pipeline; the unbounded merged
backlog addressed here is a distinct concern that a louder window cannot solve.

So this PR is the residual delta: it layers defects 2 and 3 onto main's
reservation-gated loop and leaves every gate #1475 added untouched —
`SKIP_RESERVED`, `SKIP_CLOSED_LIVE_SESSION`, `SKIP_MERGED_LIVE_SESSION`, and the
`REMOVE_*` / `SKIP_*` removal vocabulary are all preserved. No tick-level caller
is added (the Stop-hook caller from #1475 is the intended one).

## Tests

`test-dispatch-scripts.sh` (the sweep section):

- gh stub migrated from the bulk `gh-pr-list-all.json` fixture to per-branch
  `pr-state-<branch>.json` fixtures matching the `--head` query, plus a
  `SWEEP_GH_PR_FAIL` knob.
- The two `exit 1` assertions (gh-issue-view failure; unexpected issue state)
  inverted to the new contract: the sweep exits 0, logs the `ERROR_*` line, and a
  sibling worktree registered alongside the failing one is still removed —
  proving the failure was isolated.
- New cases: `gh pr list --head` failure isolation, and unexpected-state
  isolation.

Full suite: 2440/2440 passing. `shellcheck` clean on both files (only
pre-existing source-follow/info findings). The suite is not wired into CI
(intentional), so it was run locally.

author: lucvanrhyn
body:
## Summary

Two backlog-closeout changes so the only work left is genuinely new features or Luc's external/ops actions. Verified by TDD (RED→GREEN) + full local gates.

### 1. Einstein semantic retrieval — window date queries on the event axis (`observedAt`), closing the deferred fork of #516

The semantic/vector path windowed date ranges on `EinsteinChunk.sourceUpdatedAt` — the record-**mutation** axis (the source row's `updatedAt`/`editedAt`, which also drives stale detection). The structured path already used the correct per-entity **event** axes (`observation.observedAt` / `task.dueDate` / `notification.createdAt`, shipped #547). So a "what happened in the last two weeks?" question matched the wrong chunks on the semantic path whenever a row's edit date diverged from its event date (e.g. a back-filled observation).

The blocker that kept this deferred was always the **backfill** — `sourceUpdatedAt` isn't the event date for existing chunks. A **COALESCE-transition** dissolves it:

- New nullable `EinsteinChunk.observedAt DateTime?` (migration `0028`, additive `ADD COLUMN`, **no backfill UPDATE**).
- Chunker resolves the event axis per entity (`resolveEventDate`): observation→`observedAt`, task→`dueDate`, notification→`createdAt`; `null` for camp/animal/task_template/it3_snapshot.
- Ingestion persists it on every upsert.
- Semantic retriever windows on `COALESCE(observedAt, sourceUpdatedAt)` and surfaces the chunk date on the same axis.

**Zero regression, no re-embed cost:** existing chunks have `observedAt = NULL` → COALESCE falls back to `sourceUpdatedAt` → byte-identical to today. New/changed chunks populate `observedAt` going forward, so the event axis fills in naturally — no `chunkerVersion` bump, no forced re-embed, no risky re-join backfill. `sourceUpdatedAt` stays for stale detection (additive, not a replacement). Full rationale + rejected alternatives in [ADR-0009](docs/adr/0009-einstein-observedat-event-axis.md).

`EinsteinChunk` is operator-provisioned (excluded from `lib/farm-schema.ts`); column ALTERs flow through the numbered migration pipeline exactly like `0014`/`0027`. `lib/farm-schema.ts` regen only appends `0028` to `BASELINE_MIGRATION_NAMES` (still 42 tables — the table DDL stays excluded).

### 2. `scripts/setup-worktree.sh`

A new worktree has no generated Prisma client, so `tsc`/`next build` fail with cryptic errors until `prisma generate` runs — a recurring gotcha (memory `feedback-worktree-path-and-edit-disk-sync`). The script runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm prisma generate` + clears `.next/cache`; CLAUDE.md's worktree convention now points to it.

## Test plan
- New TDD coverage: chunker `observedAt` event-axis (per-entity + null cases), retriever `COALESCE(observedAt, sourceUpdatedAt)` window, ingestion persists `observedAt`. RED→GREEN.
- `pnpm vitest run` — full suite green (einstein: 304 pass; migrator/parity: 71 pass).
- `tsc --noEmit` at the **42 baseline** (zero new).
- `pnpm db:gen-schema:check` — up to date.
- `eslint` on changed files — clean.
- `pnpm build` — OK.

## Promote note
Carries **ADR-0009** + an all-tenant schema migration (`0028`) on the flagship Einstein retrieval path. Behaviour is COALESCE-guarded for zero regression. Promoting per Luc's explicit in-conversation go-ahead this cycle.

body:
🔗 **Jira:** [ENG-91318](https://creatio.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-91318)

## What & why

ENG-91318 (epic ENG-85256 "AI no-code agents") asked: **how does the agent read default column values, and should we adopt the OData approach other teams use?** This PR answers it through the BMAD pipeline and ships the resulting implementation.

The work has two phases on one branch.

### Phase A — investigation (documents only, `spec/**`)

Verified on a live Creatio 8.x instance:

- clio reads defaults via the **design-time** service `EntitySchemaDesignerService.svc/GetSchemaDesignItem` — **not** OData.
- OData v4 `$metadata` carries **zero** `DefaultValue` facets for any column (0 in 1.43 MB CSDL) → unusable for reading defaults.
- Live ticket-case E2E (create lookup → insert record → add lookup column → set `Const` default → readback → runtime insert): readback returns the **GUID only, no display value**; the runtime **correctly auto-applies** the `Const` default on insert.
- **Decision: HYBRID** — keep the designer-service readback backbone and enrich the display value inside clio. Gap confirmed → Phase B in scope.

Artifacts: PRD, ADR (Accepted), 8 stories, test plan, and the evidence docs under `spec/read-column-default-values/`.

### Phase B — implementation

**Readback enrichment (FR-05):** new `ILookupDefaultDisplayValueResolver` resolves a lookup `Const` default's referenced-record display value (display column via `IRuntimeEntitySchemaReader`, read via DataService `SelectQuery` through `IApplicationClient`). `EntitySchemaDefaultValueConfig` gains additive `display-value` / `record-resolution` fields; `GetColumnProperties` enriches `Const`+lookup columns only. Fully **fail-soft** — expected failures map to honest markers (`no-access`, `not-found-or-no-access`, `display-column-unavailable`), never an exception.

**Write-side validation (FR-06):** `EntitySchemaDefaultValueSourceResolver.Resolve` gains a `Const` branch + optional `referenceSchemaName`; a lookup `Const` GUID is validated to exist (new `IRemoteEntitySchemaDesignerClient.CheckRecordExists`) before save. Unknown GUID is rejected; unverifiable checks (no read access) pass through. Point-in-time (TOCTOU, documented).

**MCP + docs (FR-07):** tool descriptions, prompt guidance, tool contract (+ example), `help/en` and `docs/commands` updated. `Commands.md` reviewed, no change required.

## Reviewer notes

- **No new CLI flags** — all changes live inside the existing `default-value-config` JSON object and existing verbs (CLIO001 surface unchanged).
- **Additive & fail-soft** — no regression to the released 8.0.2.47 `default-value-config` contract.
- The new resolver is registered via the existing convention auto-registration (`BindingsModule.RegisterAssemblyInterfaceTypes`), not an explicit line.
- The resolver realizes the ADR D7 "SelectQuery" option (always-available, matches the module precedent) rather than the nominal OData-data primary — both are valid behind the interface; recorded in the comparison doc.

## Validation

- `dotnet test --filter "Category=Unit&(Module=Command|Module=McpServer)"` → **2584 pass, 0 fail**. New unit tests: `LookupDefaultDisplayValueResolverTests` (6), resolver `Const` validation (4), `CheckRecordExists` client (3), manager enrichment (2).
- Release build: **0 errors, 0 CLIO warnings**.
- **MCP E2E is not in CI** — `clio.mcp.e2e` gains a lookup `Const`-rejection scenario; run it manually before merge (the positive enrichment path was already verified live during Phase A).

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

- A separate clio bug: `call-service` fails (`Sequence contains more than one matching element`) on an `appsettings.json` with duplicate environment URIs.

author: noahgift
body:
## Summary — correctness fix

`sum(range(n))` (textbook!), `sum/max/min(set(xs))` previously emitted **undefined `range(...)`/`set(...)` Rust calls** — silent miscompiles (found via a rustc-verified probe): the reduction builtins handle a list arg, but a `range(...)` (not first-class) or `set(...)` arg fell through to context-free lowering, losing recognition.

## How
- New shared `materialize_iterable_arg(ctx, arg)`: `range(...)` → `lower_range_list`
  (Vec); a set-typed value → `Expr::SetToList`; a list-typed value → as-is; else
  `None`. The `sum()` and `min/max()` handlers route their iterable arg through
  it before reducing. **No new IR** (reuses `RangeList` + `SetToList`).

## Test
- `reduce_over_iterable.py` — rustc round-trip **cross-checked vs python3**
  (`sum(range)`, `sum(range(a,b))`, `sum/max/min(set)`).
- e2e 282 → **283**. Full gate green (`fmt`, `check`, `clippy -D warnings`,
  workspace tests, `pv lint` 0 errors).

author: venkata-pavani
body:
## Summary

- Add `deferrable` parameter to `SFTPOperator`, allowing `get` and `put` transfers of a single file (or list of single-file pairs, when `concurrency == 1`) to be deferred to a trigger instead of blocking a worker slot while the transfer is in progress.
- Add `SFTPOperatorTrigger` (in `airflow.providers.sftp.triggers.sftp`) which performs the async file transfer via `SFTPHookAsync` and yields a `TriggerEvent` on success or failure.
- `deferrable=True` raises `ValueError` at execute-time for unsupported configurations:
  - `operation == "delete"`
  - `concurrency > 1`
  - no `ssh_conn_id` available (neither explicit `ssh_conn_id` nor an `sftp_hook` with one set)

This re-implements the design from #65480 (closed unmerged due to a rebase issue), scoped down per discussion on #65475.

Closes #65475

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests added in `providers/sftp/tests/unit/sftp/triggers/test_sftp.py` (`TestSFTPOperatorTrigger`) covering serialization, get/put success, intermediate directory creation, and failure events.

author: panyam
body:
## What changes

Mechanical rename per issue 770. Zero behavior change. Renames the relay publish-side interface and the multiplex receiver to names that say what's relayed (notifications) and how the router routes (by method).

Before:
```go
type BroadcastRelay interface { PublishBroadcast(...) }
mux := server.NewMultiplexRelayReceiver().Handle(...)
bus, _ := redisstore.NewCapabilityBus(opts, mux)
srv := server.NewServer(info, server.WithBroadcastRelay(bus))
```

After:
```go
type NotificationRelay interface { Publish(...) }
router := server.NewNotificationRouter().Handle(...)
bus, _ := redisstore.NewCapabilityBus(opts, router)
srv := server.NewServer(info, server.WithNotificationRelay(bus))
```

`NotificationRelayReceiver` keeps its name (singular noun) and its method shrinks: `Receive` instead of `ReceiveRelay` (the `Relay` context is now carried by the type name itself, not duplicated on the method).

Issue 770's second half (store infra lift from `experimental/ext/events/stores/redis/` to root `stores/redis/`) lands as a separate PR on top of this one.

## Reviewer's guide
Read in this order:

1. [server/relay.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-6e1faa6c56182c2ea76b641b8d226799639d62a02d1349daa77988535f08668f) — start here. All the renamed types + reference receivers. The diff reads as a structured rename: same shape, new names. Doc-comments updated to reference the new symbol names.
2. [server/server.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-78f42ba40d0f10b08c73b7e6bb8376f398e249c963cf549e89591d6b6826b9a4) — three field/option references updated: `serverOptions.notificationRelay`, the `Broadcast` dispatch fork in `Server.Broadcast`, and `subscriptionRegistry.notificationRelay`. Cross-references in doc comments swept.
3. [experimental/ext/events/yield.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-1a35574e62fe51d6eb94df43ccdbf8519abbc134033627d9020fe30dbec06cf3) — `YieldingSource.Receive` method (renamed from `ReceiveRelay`) implements the renamed interface. Body unchanged.
4. [experimental/ext/events/stores/redis/capability_bus.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-99c675bb90ed0314ff756248e4b6eb740901a5c5c5f14da16c8179d81c22e498) + `bus.go` + [experimental/ext/events/stores/memory/bus.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-8c2453e1ccb566472aae4b2d950d36a2392cae1c90cd3a1beeae739ae29fe815) — Bus types implement the renamed interface; `Publish` instead of `PublishBroadcast`; `receiver.Receive` call sites updated.
5. [examples/whole-enchilada/events/event-server/redis.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-bdfe6a3c5d30e0ba0c34c3e73ae1b4a4a24f1ba17a8fab61316d4c34f0db523a) — adopter wiring uses the renamed option + types.
6. [docs/MULTI_REPLICA.md](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-17934e88ae4afd4b6c4f80b1734fdf574ce8e4fe79cbdc2374fd93e12bb29a30) — every reference renamed (mermaid diagrams, callstacks, recipes, tables). Line-number references in the "life of a notification" callstack section updated to match the new line numbers in [server/relay.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-6e1faa6c56182c2ea76b641b8d226799639d62a02d1349daa77988535f08668f) + [experimental/ext/events/stores/redis/capability_bus.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-99c675bb90ed0314ff756248e4b6eb740901a5c5c5f14da16c8179d81c22e498).
7. [CONSTRAINTS.md](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-f2043ef583480706f62a74d47dae3d7ae2402f1b42cff01383b08fe8b37fdf3b) § C5 + [experimental/ext/events/README.md](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-9222f2c9c82e15be71e1b286719f2d44d107c3ea315805c64c3d617ab960d4b3) + [experimental/ext/events/stores/redis/README.md](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-4309c899768e545e244ce0f504bcc4fd8e55b6fd0e58205a0e8531c2695119fa) + [experimental/ext/events/STORAGE_SEAMS.md](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-ceea0a5339d9583578ba93a8fd23a5cc2cc61ae832839b943f6d8e02b0bf6954) — naming references updated.
8. Tests — [server/relay_test.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-2bdce2c63b8b248c49eac7bf8f25ed3117f43e4afb90c819000534681d6e923d), [server/relay_inmemory_test.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-e84d05eb3b08b52b7bb21421bfc3ab3866c68a4785bab10c033fdc209ccd0d80), [server/listchanged_relay_test.go](https://github.com/panyam/mcpkit/pull/771/files#diff-a2fc396d77a5ac93a90383ddd1f38168e7430738d05afa4f439cf68de4daa9a8), `redisstore/capability_bus_test.go`. Test names also renamed for consistency (e.g., `TestMultiplexRelayReceiver_*` → `TestNotificationRouter_*`).

Skim or skip: nothing meaningful — every diff line is part of the rename.

## Decision log

- **`NotificationRelayReceiver` keeps its name.** Already singular; the `XYZRelay` / `XYZRelayReceiver` pairing reads cleanly with the new `NotificationRelay`. The method shrinks from `ReceiveRelay` to `Receive` because the `Relay` context is now carried by the type name itself.
- **`NotificationRouter` instead of `MethodRouter`.** Discussed in issue 770 — `Router` is the noun; routing-by-method is obvious from the `Handle(method, receiver)` signature. Future `RequestRouter` companion (if cross-replica request relay ever materializes) reads naturally with no namespace conflict.
- **No backwards-compat aliases.** User approved full break for the 755 stack; same posture here. The renamed types only existed in main for the duration between PR 768 merge and this PR; no external consumers possible.
- **Test names renamed for consistency.** `TestMultiplexRelayReceiver_RoutesByMethod` → `TestNotificationRouter_RoutesByMethod`. Code references in test bodies were already renamed by the type sweep; the function names trailing in tests would have been the only stale-naming residue.
- **Line-number references in the "Life of a notification" callstack section adjusted.** Rename added/removed bytes in the relay.go bodies; the callstack section's `file.go:line` annotations needed to track the new positions. Spot-checked each by grepping the current code.

- **Interface contract change for every implementer.** `NotificationRelayReceiver.Receive` (not `ReceiveRelay`) — every implementation simultaneously updated: `CapabilityBroadcastReceiver`, `ResourcesUpdatedReceiver`, `NotificationRouter`, `YieldingSource`, all test-file mocks. The build proves the rename is complete (unrenamed references break compile).
- **Adopter call sites change names.** `srv.NewServer(info, server.WithBroadcastRelay(bus))` won't compile after merge; must read `WithNotificationRelay(bus)`. Same for `NewMultiplexRelayReceiver` → `NewNotificationRouter`. Only the whole-enchilada demo wires these; updated in the same PR.

- **Race tests clean.** `go test -race -count=1` passes across server, events, redisstore, memorystore, event-server demo. Sole pre-existing failure is `TestMatchTransform_CrossModeParity` (issue 758) — not introduced by this PR.

author: jeremysnr
body:
Closes #30 (the top-tier "real planning" roadmap item).

`engines/planner.py` rendered "Satisfy acceptance criterion: X" boilerplate with no file-level analysis. This feeds the code-aware context engine's output into an **LLM planner** so dispatched agents receive named files, test locations, and verify commands — directly cutting retries and failed runs.

## What changed

**`LlmPlanner` behind the existing `DeliveryPlanner` seam** (`engines/llm_planner.py`), mirroring the `OpenAITicketAnalyzer` / `LlmRiskClassifier` degrade-to-floor design:

- Consumes the code-aware context (`candidate_files`, `RepoCodeFacts` from `context.provider: code`) and produces **file-level** `implementation_steps`, `unit_tests` / `integration_tests` locations, `verify_commands`, and a populated **`DeliveryPlan.expected_files_or_areas`** (enabling a future plan-vs-diff gate).
- Schema-validated output (`LlmPlanOutput`) with corrective-feedback retries; a fake LLM for offline tests.

**Safety discipline — the model enriches the plan but can never relax a guardrail:**

| Concern | How it's held |
| --- | --- |
| No `agent_instructions` unless buildable | The LLM is only consulted for runs the template planner would dispatch (ready ticket **and** a confident repo). Everything else returns the template plan **verbatim — no model call** — so the hard rule holds without trusting the model. |
| Identity / scope | `goal`, `scope`, `affected_repositories`, `branch` come from the analysis/context, never the model. |
| Forbidden paths / no migrations / stop conditions | The `agent_instructions` constraint block + PR-handoff closing are rendered by Foundry from shared `CONSTRAINTS_BLOCK` / `CLOSING_BLOCK` constants (extracted from `planner.py`), never delegated to the model. The system prompt tells the model *not* to restate them. |
| LLM outage / invalid / empty output | Degrades to the deterministic template plan, recorded honestly in the plan's `open_questions` (`"LLM planning unavailable (…); template plan used."`). |
| Grounding | The prompt feeds candidate files + code facts and instructs the model never to invent a path it has no evidence for. |

**Wiring.** New `planner.provider` config knob (`"template"` default | `"llm"`), parsed from YAML (`planner:` block) and env (`FOUNDRY_PLANNER_PROVIDER` / `FOUNDRY_PLANNER_MODEL`), validated in `Settings._validate`, and constructed in `build_orchestrator`. The template planner remains the no-key default.

**Secret-leak guard (invariant #6) still covers the enriched payload.** `agents/provider.py::assert_no_secrets` already scans the whole serialized job input (including `agent_instructions` and `delivery_plan`), so an LLM-generated plan passes through it automatically — a regression test confirms a secret slipped into a step is caught before dispatch.

## Why this is safe under the invariants

- **No gate, policy rule, or `foundry.rego` touched** — pure intelligence-layer addition behind an existing seam, so no Python/Rego lock-step concern and `opa` isn't needed to validate this PR.
- **No audit write added or removed.**
- **No network in tests** (invariant #3): the planner is exercised entirely with `FakeStructuredLLM`.
- `AGENTS.md` (Planning row + engines/ module row + known-limitations line), `README.md` (project layout + code-aware planning prose), and `foundry.example.yaml` (commented `planner:` block) updated per the maintenance rule.

## Tests

`tests/test_llm_planner.py` (new): enriched file-level steps + `expected_files_or_areas`; deterministic identity/scope; the **guardrail block is rendered regardless of model output**; the prompt carries candidate files / code facts and the untrusted-data framing; the floor discipline (not-ready and ambiguous-repo cases make **no** model call and yield `agent_instructions=None`); degrade-to-template on LLM failure / empty / persistently-invalid output, with the audit note; retry-then-succeed; the secret-leak guard catches a leaked token in a step; and a drop-in orchestrator integration test reaching `waiting_approval`. `tests/test_config.py`: defaults, YAML parse, env-overrides-YAML, and invalid-provider rejection.

Full offline suite: **515 passed, 5 skipped**. `ruff check src tests` clean.

## Risks / follow-up

- **Additive and default-off.** With `planner.provider: template` (the default) behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. The `planner.py` refactor only extracts the constraint/closing text into named constants; the rendered template-planner instructions are identical (covered by the existing `test_ready_plan_has_agent_instructions`).
- **Best paired with `context.provider: code`.** With `static`/`catalog` context there are no candidate files/code facts, so the LLM produces area-level rather than file-level steps (the prompt forbids inventing paths). File-level richness scales with the context provider — documented in the example config.
- **`expected_files_or_areas` is populated but not yet *consumed*.** The plan-vs-diff gate that would use it is deliberately out of scope for this slice (it's a gate change with its own Rego lock-step) — left as a follow-up sub-issue on #30.
- The C#/.NET port (`dotnet/`, unmerged PR #1) is **not** touched — this is a new feature and the Python implementation is canonical.

## What

Completes the full Cyfrin test taxonomy for **`OracleLib`** (the Chainlink staleness-guard library, `src/libraries/OracleLib.sol`) by adding only the **missing** test types, in new non-colliding files. No existing test, mock, or config was touched.

## Cyfrin taxonomy — before vs after

| Type | Status at branch | This PR |
|------|------------------|---------|
| **Unit** (per-function AAA) | covered — `test/unit/OracleLib.t.sol` (happy path, 3 revert branches, `age == TIMEOUT` boundary) | + `test/unit/OracleLibEdge.t.sol` adds the omitted edges |
| **Stateless fuzz** | missing | + `test/fuzz/OracleLibFuzz.t.sol` |
| **Integration (real script)** | partial — `EndToEnd.t.sol` wires by hand; fork test needs a live RPC | + `test/integration/OracleLibIntegration.t.sol` deploys via the **real `DeployAll`/`HelperConfig`** |
| **Attack** | covered — `test/attack/Access0x1Router.attack.t.sol::test_attack_stalePriceBlocksSettlement` (+ Bookings/Invoices stale-price attacks) | not duplicated |
| **Stateful invariant** | n/a | intentionally skipped — `OracleLib` is a pure stateless view guard with no persistent state to drive handler properties over (noted in the fuzz file's NatSpec) |

## New files

- **`test/fuzz/OracleLibFuzz.t.sol`** (stateless fuzz, 6 tests) — fuzzes the guard's accept/revert decision across the full round 5-tuple against a `bound()`-derived spec predicate: the master `guardDecisionMatchesSpec`, the carried-over and staleness boundaries isolated, byte-for-byte pass-through fidelity, answer-sign independence (single responsibility — `answer > 0` is the caller's job), and the future-`updatedAt` underflow-panic corner.
- **`test/integration/OracleLibIntegration.t.sol`** (integration, 5 tests) — `setUp` deploys the whole estate through the **real `DeployAll.run()`** on the local-mock chain (so the deploy path is under test too), then exercises `OracleLib` exactly where it lives in production — inlined into `Access0x1Router.quote()`: a fresh feed prices through the guard, a warped-stale and a carried-over round both revert end-to-end through the public `quote()` selector, and the native vs USDC feed slots are proven independently guarded.
- **`test/unit/OracleLibEdge.t.sol`** (unit edge cases, 7 tests) — the corners the main unit suite omits: `answeredInRound == roundId` accept boundary, `age == 0`, `age == TIMEOUT - 1`, negative/zero answer pass-through, byte-for-byte pass-through of an accepted round, and multi-condition revert precedence (the typed `OracleLib__StalePrice` always surfaces).

Reuses the existing `MockV3Aggregator` — no duplicate mocks added.

- `forge build` — clean
- `forge test` — **597 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (46 suites; +18 new OracleLib tests)
- `forge fmt --check` — clean

## Finding fixed
**[UX#2]** Anonymous visitor → "Sign in to register/accept" → after OAuth landed on `/dashboard`, not back on the event. The CTAs passed the return path via `location.state.from`, which the sign-in flow never read.

## Changes
- **`lib/safeNext.ts` (new, unit-tested open-redirect guard):** `getSafeNextUrl` (origin allowlist — this origin + known codescriet subdomains, so the playground handoff still works) and `getSafeRelativePath` (strict `^/(?!/)` single-leading-slash, rejects `//host`, backslash-normalization `/\evil.com`, and control chars). `import.meta.env.DEV` access made node-safe so the test runs under `node --test`. SignInPage now imports it instead of its inline duplicate.
- **`AuthCallbackPage`:** consumes `sessionStorage.post_login_next` (stashed by SignInPage before the OAuth round-trip, re-validated, **same-origin only**) and redirects there before the `/dashboard` fallback — closing the OAuth-from-event gap. Wins over the older `pendingEventRegistration` hint and clears it to avoid a double redirect.
- **`EventDetailPage`:** invitation + register CTAs pass `?next=/events/:slug[?register=1]`.

Email/password login already honored `?next=` via the logged-in effect; this makes OAuth match and gives the guard a tested home.

author: eumemic
body:
## What

Adds a required, derived `pending_since: datetime` to `AwaitingToolCall` = the declaring assistant event's `created_at` (tz-aware UTC).

## Why

`Session.awaiting` entries carried only `{tool_call_id, name, kind}`. For `kind == "custom"`, an entry exists from the moment the assistant declares the call until the executor posts a result — so a healthy in-flight connector call (e.g. `signal_react`, ~2s) was indistinguishable from a stuck one whose client died. Consumers (the console tool-confirmation surface) need an age signal everywhere, including the sessions list where no transcript is loaded.

With `pending_since`, clients can do age-based presentation: fresh custom = in-flight (quiet), stale custom = stuck (alert); builtin/mcp remain approval-gated (alert immediately).

## How

Threaded through the read-model in four hops (zero new DB state — `events.created_at` already exists):

- `_unresolved_tool_calls` now `SELECT`s `created_at` and stamps each unresolved call via a **shallow copy** (`{**tc, "_pending_since": row["created_at"]}`), never mutating the parsed source dict.
- `list_unresolved_tool_calls_batch` surfaces `pending_since` per entry (docstring updated).
- `_classify_awaiting` propagates it onto all three `AwaitingToolCall` variants (custom/builtin/mcp).
- `AwaitingToolCall` gains the required field.

The two connector-SSE paths (`list_pending_calls_for_connector`, `list_pending_calls_for_session_and_connection`) build their own explicit output dicts, so the extra `_pending_since` key is inert there — guarded by a new key-set regression assertion.

The model docstring notes this is the **same clock** the sweep's `client_tool_call_max_age_seconds` abandonment bound (#752) keys off; the two thresholds are intentionally different timescales (seconds-scale UI hint vs. 24h irreversible abandonment), not an inconsistency. Also corrected the stale "latest assistant message" docstring → "any assistant turn (#741)".

Regenerated `openapi.json` + the generated SDK (`awaiting_tool_call.py`) via `scripts/regen-client.sh`.

## Tests

- **New** `tests/unit/test_classify_awaiting.py`: `pending_since` propagates onto each custom/builtin/mcp variant; field is required (constructing without it raises `ValidationError`). Mutation-checked.
- **Extended** `test_awaiting_spans_all_assistants.py`: per-turn `pending_since` (tc_X earlier turn < tc_Z later turn), full `compute_awaiting` service path, and two-calls-in-one-event share the same `pending_since`.
- **Extended** `test_stale_connector_backfill.py`: connector backfill output dict shape is exactly the documented set (no leak).
- All 2713 unit tests pass; mypy + ruff clean; openapi/sdk snapshot tests green. Integration tests collect cleanly (require Docker Postgres; run in CI).

Closes #816

body:
bdo authored a v0.2.0 of the /goal skill and asked to land it; this is his content, applied faithfully as a governed config-as-code increment (skills are prompt-as-code per .claude/CLAUDE.md, landed as stamped increments, never hand-tuned silently).

The change corrects the exact failure this session surfaced: the old skill always minted a single-session done-line, so a multi-session outcome got crammed into one frozen line and the assistant then treated completing that line's documents as completing the goal. v0.2.0 makes the ritual ask first whether bdo is defining an outcome (a desired reality that spans sessions) or the next session-sized move that reduces pressure toward it, and then write the correct artifact: a probe-set or proposal for an outcome, a frozen done-line only for genuinely session-scoped work. It adds the core Outcome/Probe/Session-work/Task distinction, an evidence-bearing-probe discipline (refuse any probe that cannot be checked; aspirational prose is horizon, never a probe), a classify-intent step, a candidates-by-type step, a pressure-test, and an output-format-before-writing gate. The hard refusals now include the one drawn straight from this session: do not say done when the artifact is unlanded, unmerged, or only local.

Three honest reconciliations with the repo as it stands today, none blocking (the skill degrades gracefully): loop.pressure is referenced in Step 0 but does not exist yet — it is the outcome-pressure fold proposed in PR #122 and the skill already says to infer provisionally when it is absent; the done-line body the skill mandates now carries five sections (Done when, Non-example, Pressure reduced, Does not complete, Evidence expected) while the done-dir .pen.json still only enforces two, so the skill is stricter than the pen floor (the pen accepts the richer body) — raising the pen floor to match is a separate, optional increment; and the outcome/probe artifact locations it lists (outcomes/, pressure/, proposals/) do not exist yet, so a canonical home for outcome artifacts is itself an open question (the proposal in #122 currently lives at repo root).

author: rbaumier
body:
## Problem

`filename-naming-convention` flags Next.js Pages Router filenames that the framework *mandates*:

- `apps/nextjs-pages/src/pages/app/discussions/[discussionId].tsx` — dynamic route segment
- `apps/nextjs-pages/src/pages/404.tsx` — custom error page (must be named exactly this)

These names follow Next.js file-based routing and cannot adopt kebab/camel/Pascal case without breaking the route, so they are false positives.

## Fix

Add an `is_nextjs_pages_router_file` exemption in the rule's own module, mirroring the existing TanStack Router (`$param.tsx` under `routes/`) and SvelteKit (`+page.svelte`) carve-outs:

- bracket-wrapped routing base — `[id].tsx`, `[...slug].tsx`, `[[...slug]].tsx`
- purely numeric stem — `404.tsx`, `500.tsx`

both gated on a `pages/` ancestor directory. The routing base is derived from the text before the file extension rather than the dot-split stem, so catch-all segments (whose brackets contain dots) are handled correctly.

## Tests

Regression tests reproduce the issue's exact examples plus catch-all / optional-catch-all / `500.tsx`, with guards that numeric/bracket stems **outside** a `pages/` tree still fire.

- `cargo test rules::filename_naming_convention` — 65 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test` — 14573 passed, 0 failed

Closes #1758

author: noahgift
body:
## Pillar-3 (Unsloth) correctness beat #2 — completes the "replace Unsloth" pipeline

Unsloth's value is fast QLoRA fine-tuning → **merge** → export. apr's correctness beats now cover both stages: NF4 quantization ≡ bitsandbytes (PMAT-745) and **LoRA merge forward-equivalence** (this). apr's `MergeEngine::merge` folds the LoRA delta `scale·(B@A)` into the base weight; this beat proves the merged weights produce a forward pass **numerically equivalent** to applying the LoRA factors unmerged — a faithful, contract-gated merge, where PEFT/Unsloth `merge_and_unload` ships no such guarantee.

### Not tautological
The reference forward is computed **independently from the A,B factors** via a different path (`x @ A @ B`), never from `W_merged − W_base`. A transpose/indexing bug in `merge` would diverge.

### Measured (2026-06-14, CPU, deterministic)
Fold `A:[4,2], B:[2,3], scale=2.0` into `W_base:[3,4]`, forward `x:[2,4]` two ways:

| metric | value |
|--------|-------|
| **max \|y_merged − y_factored\|** | **1.49e-8** (essentially bit-exact) |

Evidence: `evidence/pillar3-lora-merge-equivalence-2026-06-14/findings.md`.

### CI gate
`crates/aprender-train-lora/src/merge.rs::tests::beat_lora_merge_forward_equivalence` (threshold 1e-4) — deterministic, no external deps. Contract `apr-lora-merge-equivalence-beat-v1.yaml` (`pv validate` clean). Wired into `ci.yml`.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p aprender-train-lora --lib beat_lora_merge_forward_equivalence` → 1/1 pass (max\|Δ\|=1.49e-8)
- `pv validate` clean; `cargo test -p aprender-contracts --lib lint::` → 191 pass

author: dierodfer
body:
## Summary
This PR improves form handling across the application by wrapping input groups in semantic `<form>` elements with proper `onSubmit` handlers, and adds explicit table-level permissions to the database schema for Supabase RLS to function correctly.

## Key Changes

### Frontend (src/App.jsx)
- **AdminAuth**: Wrapped email/password inputs in a `<form>` with `onSubmit` handler; button now uses `type="submit"` instead of `onClick`
- **CreateRoom**: Converted time-per-question input to a `<select>` dropdown with predefined options (10, 15, 20, 25, 30 seconds); wrapped in a `<form>` with `onSubmit`; added `type="button"` to sign-out button to prevent form submission
- **QuestionForm**: Wrapped question builder in a `<form>` with `onSubmit` handler; button now uses `type="submit"`
- **ParticipantApp**: Wrapped username and room code inputs in a `<form>` with `onSubmit` handler; added `type="button"` to open rooms list buttons

All forms now properly prevent default submission and handle validation before calling their respective action functions.

### Database (supabase/schema.sql)
- Added explicit `GRANT` statements for table-level permissions on `rooms`, `participants`, `questions`, and `answers` tables to both `anon` and `authenticated` roles
- These grants are required by PostgreSQL before RLS policies are evaluated; without them, clients receive "permission denied for table" errors instead of RLS policy violations
- Permissions follow the principle of least privilege: `anon` can only SELECT/INSERT where needed (rooms, participants), `authenticated` has broader access for admin operations

## Implementation Details
- Form submission now uses semantic HTML patterns (preventing default, calling handlers in `onSubmit`)
- The time-per-question selector is now more user-friendly with explicit options instead of a numeric input with min/max constraints
- All buttons are properly typed (`type="submit"` for form submission, `type="button"` for other actions) to prevent unintended form submissions
- Database permissions are documented with comments explaining why they're necessary for RLS to work
